docs.title: OpenTag user guide
docs.text:
An evolving editor and guide

OpenTag is in development. This guide covers desktop workflows; mobile builds and simulator previews have different capabilities. Check the release notes for available packages and limitations. OpenTag is an independent project; complete Mp3tag compatibility remains a goal.

docs.title: Tag, rename and organize your music
docs.text:
OpenTag edits the metadata inside your audio files: titles, artists, albums, track numbers and cover art. Start with a copy of an album, learn to edit and save its tags, then give the files consistent names.

Start your first session Download OpenTag

docs.title: Learn by doing
docs.text:
• Your first tagging session

    Open an album, change tags on one file and a selection, rename the files, and undo a change.

    Start the tutorial

  • Give track numbers two digits

    Rename 2 Low Tide.mp3 to 02 Low Tide.mp3 so files sort in order.

    Zero-padded track numbers

  • Get tags from names

    Use your existing artist and album folders to fill empty tags.

    Tags from folder and file names

  • Keep guest artists in titles

    Build an action group that moves “feat.” names from the artist field into the title.

    Move guest artists to titles

docs.title: Look up the syntax
docs.text:
• Format strings: combine tags, text and functions to build a value or filename.
  • Placeholders: read tag values and file properties such as %artist%, %title% and %_filename%.
  • Regular expressions: match, extract and replace text, with worked examples.

For everyday lookup, see Options, keyboard shortcuts, filter syntax and field mappings. Context and helper menus explain cover commands, field suggestions and named history entries; the menu reference helps locate each control.

Use the search box (press S or /) to find a topic in this guide. More topics are being written; only completed pages appear here.

docs.title: Get help and follow changes
docs.text: Download installers and read changes on the GitHub releases page. If a step in this guide differs from your build, report it on GitHub, including your OpenTag version, operating system and the steps you tried.

docs.title: Actions and action groups
docs.text:
Actions turn a repeated tagging job into a saved workflow. An action can change a field, rename a file, adjust artwork or produce an output file. A group combines actions so that the next step can use the previous step's result.

Start with copies of a few files. Save or discard pending tag-panel edits, select the files to process, then choose one of these routes:

Route Use it for What the confirmation does Actions → Actions (Quick)… (Alt+Shift+6) One change, such as replacing underscores Apply action runs the action and saves immediately Actions → Actions… (Alt+6) A reusable sequence Save groups keeps the workflow; Apply checked groups saves it and processes the selected files A named group in the Actions menu Running a saved workflow again Runs that group on the selected files

Alt is ⌥ Option on a Mac. The menus show the available commands when files are selected and the current source permits writing.

A new installation starts with five unchecked groups under Examples. Review and enable only the examples wanted for a run. Saving an empty library keeps it empty; removing examples does not make them return at the next start.

docs.title: Choose an action
docs.text: Goal Action Change capitalization Case Conversion Repair a confirmed legacy encoding mistake Convert Codepage Calculate one field or a name from tags Format Value Extract several fields from structured text Guess Values Substitute exact text Replace Match varying text with a pattern Replace with Regular Expression Turn a delimited string into several values Split Field by Separator Join several field values into one Merge Duplicate Fields Retain the first value or remove equal values Remove Duplicate Fields Delete specified fields Remove Fields Delete everything except a keep list Remove Fields Except Embed an existing image Import Cover from File Copy embedded images to files Export Cover to File Resize or convert embedded images Adjust Cover Change picture roles and descriptions Set Cover Properties Fill a field from a text file Import Text File Write a text report Export Write playlists grouped by folder or another value Generate Playlists

docs.title: Try a quick action
docs.text:
1. Select one practice file whose title contains an underscore.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)….
  3. Choose Replace in Action type.
  4. Enter TITLE in Field, _ in Original string, and one space in Replace with.
  5. Leave Only as whole word and Case-sensitive comparison off.
  6. Choose Apply action, then check the title in the file list.

Low_Tide becomes Low Tide. This is a saved change; there is no extra Save tags step. OpenTag remembers the last quick-action type and its settings. Check them before the next application.

docs.title: Build a reusable group
docs.text:
1. Open Actions → Actions… and choose New… under Groups.
  2. Give the group a clear name, such as Titles: underscores and spaces.
  3. Select the group and choose Edit actions….
  4. Choose New…, select an action type, enter its settings and choose Keep action. Repeat to add more actions.
  5. Use ↑ Move up and ↓ Move down to put the actions in order.
  6. Keep the edited action list, then choose Save groups.
  7. Check only the groups needed for this run and choose Apply checked groups.

A group's name does not need to match a field or filename. Duplicate it with Duplicate… before adapting a workflow you want to preserve. Rename… changes its name; Remove removes the saved group, not your music files. Closing with unsaved group changes asks whether to discard them. Hold Alt while choosing a move button to send the selected entries to the beginning or end. The same controls arrange both groups and their actions.

docs.title: Understand the order
docs.text:
Checked groups run in their displayed order. Within a group, field and file changes feed the following actions. For example, copy the guest artist into TITLE before removing it from ARTIST.

Export and Generate Playlists are batch outputs: OpenTag produces them after the other actions in that group. They see the group's final values even if their row appears earlier. Use a separate group when an output must capture a particular intermediate state.

A failed action warns for that file, then the file's remaining actions and later groups continue. It still participates in batch exports and playlists. Earlier successful writes remain; read every warning and inspect the practice files before repeating. Use Edit → Undo for recorded file changes in the current desktop session; keep backups for recovery beyond that session. Export Cover includes created and replaced images in its undo step. Generated reports and playlists may need separate cleanup.

docs.title: Choose a field or a special target
docs.text:
Most field actions take a name such as TITLE, ARTIST or ALBUMARTIST. Use the Field helper to insert names. The available special targets depend on the action:

Target Meaning Available for _TAG Process every tag field Case Conversion, Replace, Replace with Regular Expression, Convert Codepage, Merge Duplicate Fields, Split Field by Separator _ALL Process tag fields and the filename Case Conversion, Replace, Replace with Regular Expression, Convert Codepage _ALL in Remove Duplicate Fields Process every tag field; does not rename files Remove Duplicate Fields _FILENAME Process or construct the filename Case Conversion, Replace, Replace with Regular Expression, Convert Codepage, Format Value _DIRECTORY Process or construct the containing folder's name Case Conversion, Replace, Replace with Regular Expression, Convert Codepage, Format Value _FIELDNAME Change field-name spelling, keeping its values Case Conversion, on APEv2 and Vorbis Comment tags

The regex action includes the extension in _FILENAME; the other text transformations operate on the name without it. Format Value builds a new name and preserves the audio extension. Read the action page before using a filename or folder target.

COVER and PICTURE have a separate meaning in Remove Fields and Remove Fields Except: they refer to embedded artwork.

docs.title: Organize, select and repeat groups
docs.text:
Use Sort by name to alphabetize groups, or Sort by state to put checked groups first. Sorting changes execution order, so review the result. Checking a group controls whether Apply checked groups runs it; selecting a row chooses which group to edit. Those are different operations.

A Selection preset remembers which groups are checked. Check the groups, choose Save preset…, and give the selection a name. Choose that name from Selection preset to restore the checks. Remove preset… removes the saved selection while keeping the groups themselves. Save groups after changing presets.

For nested menu entries, use # in a name: Cleanup#Titles places Titles inside a Cleanup submenu. A single & marks a mnemonic character; && displays a literal ampersand. Keep names descriptive even without the mnemonic.

For example, name a group &Cleanup#&Titles. Outside a text box, press Alt+A to open the Actions menu, then C and T to run that group. The letters come from the characters following &, not from a separate arbitrary shortcut assignment.

After a run, Edit → Repeat can run the last action selection again. The Redo/Repeat command depends on the current undo history; read its label before using Cmd+Y / Ctrl+Y.

docs.title: Import and export an action group
docs.text:
Choose Import .mta… and select an action-group file. UTF-8 and BOM-marked UTF-16 are accepted; for an older file, enter its original encoding when asked, such as Windows-1252. An imported name already in use receives a numbered suffix.

Inspect every imported action. An Unresolved imported action keeps the uninterpreted settings visible and prevents checked groups from running. Replace or correct that action explicitly; importing a file is not proof that every setting has an equivalent in OpenTag.

Choose Export .mta… for the selected group to write an exchange file. Only supported export mappings can be written; review any reported error rather than assuming a partial export is usable.

docs.title: Keyboard controls in the group list
docs.text:
Use Cmd on macOS and Ctrl on Windows or Linux for the primary modifier.

Key Effect Ins New group or action Del Remove the selected entries; Backspace also works on Mac keyboards Space Toggle checked groups Ctrl+A / Cmd+A Select all rows Ctrl+Shift+A / Cmd+Shift+A Invert the row selection Ctrl+E / Cmd+E Enable all groups Ctrl+D / Cmd+D Disable all groups Ctrl+S / Cmd+S Save groups Alt+Up / Alt+Down Move selected rows Alt+Page Up / Alt+Page Down Move selected rows to the beginning or end F2 in the group list Rename the current group F4 or Enter in the group list Edit the group's actions; double-clicking also opens them F4 in the action list Edit the current action

Cmd/Ctrl-click toggles individual row selections; Shift-click selects a range. These controls apply inside the relevant lists, not while typing a field value.

docs.title: Adjust Cover
docs.text: Use Adjust Cover to resize or change the format of pictures embedded in the selected audio files. It changes all embedded pictures in each file; it does not change a separate cover.jpg alongside the music.

docs.title: Shrink oversized covers
docs.text:
1. Keep original copies and select a few practice files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Adjust Cover.
  3. Keep Image format as Original.
  4. Check Resize cover, set Size in pixels to 600, choose Maximum size and Scale proportionally.
  5. Choose Apply action, then inspect the cover dimensions.

A 1200 × 800 image becomes 600 × 400. A 300 × 300 image keeps its size. The picture's cover type and description are retained.

docs.title: Format and quality settings
docs.text:
Setting Choices and effect Image format Original, JPEG, or PNG Quality Best = 100, High = 90, Medium = 75, Low = 50, or Custom Quality (0–100) A whole number used when encoding JPEG Resize cover Off initially; enables the size and scaling settings

Original retains a writable original format: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP or WebP. If OpenTag cannot write that original format, choose JPEG or PNG. PNG preserves transparency; JPEG does not. Quality does not control PNG compression or resize dimensions.

If the format and dimensions remain the same, the picture stays byte for byte unchanged. Changing JPEG quality alone therefore does not recompress an otherwise unchanged JPEG. Choose the format and resizing operation to match the actual goal, and check the resulting file size rather than assuming a particular quality number guarantees it.

docs.title: Size policy and scaling
docs.text:
Size in pixels accepts 1–32768. The policy selects which dimension is compared with that number; scaling selects the resulting shape.

Size policy Meaning Maximum size Reduce images whose larger side exceeds the size; leave images already within it unchanged Minimum size Match the smaller side to the size, enlarging or reducing as necessary Scaling What happens when resizing is needed Scale proportionally Keep the aspect ratio Scale to square Stretch to exactly the requested width and height Crop to square Keep proportions, fill the requested square, and crop the excess around the center

With a 1200 × 800 cover and size 600:

Policy and scaling Result Maximum + proportional 600 × 400 Minimum + proportional 900 × 600 Maximum + square 600 × 600, stretched Maximum + crop 600 × 600, cropped

Maximum size does not force a small image into a square: a 300 × 200 image already within a maximum of 600 keeps its shape in every scaling mode. Use the policy deliberately when a player needs a square image.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Enlarging cannot restore image detail. Keep a high-resolution original outside the audio file if it may be needed later.
  • Cropping and JPEG conversion can lose information. Copy the files first; inspect Edit → Undo for recorded changes in the current session.
  • An invalid image or unsupported output format reports an error. Check the operation result before processing the rest of the library.

docs.title: Case Conversion
docs.text: Use Case Conversion to make capitalization consistent in a field or filename. It applies a mechanical rule; it does not recognize artist names, abbreviations or words that should stay lowercase.

docs.title: Change a field's capitalization
docs.text:
1. Select a few copied files and save pending edits.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Case Conversion.
  3. Set Field to TITLE and Case to Mixed Case.
  4. Keep Words begin after as (-_ for this example.
  5. Choose Apply action and inspect the result.

NORTH PIER (LIVE) becomes North Pier (Live). Save the same settings in an action group for repeated use.

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text:
Case Input Result lower case NORTH PIER north pier Mixed Case NORTH PIER North Pier Sentence NORTH PIER. LOW TIDE North pier. low tide UPPER CASE North Pier NORTH PIER

Sentence uppercases the first character of the whole value and lowercases everything after it. It does not start again after a period. If the value begins with a space or quote, that character occupies the first position; trim or remove the prefix first when appropriate.

docs.title: Teach Mixed Case where words begin
docs.text:
Whitespace always begins a new word. Words begin after adds individual characters that should also begin a word. The initial setting (-_ means an opening parenthesis, hyphen or underscore starts the next word.

Input Words begin after Result in Mixed Case LOW-TIDE (-_ Low-Tide LOW-TIDE Leave empty Low-tide NORTH.PIER . North.Pier DJ NIMBUS (-_ Dj Nimbus

The setting is a set of characters, not a regex or a list of words. It does not preserve DJ, EP, III or an artist's chosen spelling. Restore those with a later Replace action when the rule is unambiguous.

docs.title: Special targets
docs.text:
Field What changes A field such as TITLE Every value of that field _TAG All tag fields _ALL All tag fields and the filename stem _FILENAME The filename stem; the audio extension is retained _DIRECTORY The containing folder name _FIELDNAME Field-name capitalization on APEv2 and Vorbis Comment tags

Changing a folder can affect files outside the selection. For naming targets, inspect the actual path after the action, especially for a change that alters only capitalization on a case-insensitive volume.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Apply a named field before trying _TAG: comments, URLs and identifiers may require exact capitalization.
  • Case conversion processes each multivalue item separately and preserves their order.
  • The action saves when it runs. Use practice copies and inspect Edit → Undo for the recorded change.

docs.title: Convert Codepage
docs.text:
Use Convert Codepage to repair text whose legacy bytes were interpreted with the wrong character encoding. It reinterprets the existing characters as bytes, then decodes those bytes with the selected codepage.

This is useful for a known encoding mistake. It is not a language detector or translation tool. Correct Unicode text can be damaged by applying it again.

docs.title: Repair one known mistake
docs.text:
1. Preserve an untouched copy and select one practice file.
  2. Open Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Convert Codepage.
  3. Set Field to the affected field, such as TITLE.
  4. In Codepage, choose the encoding that the original bytes used.
  5. Choose Apply action and compare with the intended spelling.

For example, the two characters Ã© preserve the UTF-8 bytes for é. Choosing Unicode (UTF-8) converts them back to é. This diagnosis depends on the original byte mistake; choosing a Windows codepage instead would not perform the same repair.

docs.title: Worked byte-to-text examples
docs.text:
Existing text Codepage Result Ã© Unicode (UTF-8), 65001 é Ïðèâåò Cyrillic (Windows-1251), 1251 Привет Plain ASCII Western European (Windows-1252), 1252 Plain ASCII

The action processes all values of the selected field. It does not change an audio codec, the tag format, or the encoding of a sidecar text file. For reading a text file, use Import Text File instead.

docs.title: Choose the codepage from evidence
docs.text:
The list offers Windows regional encodings, DOS/OEM pages, East Asian encodings, Mac encodings, ISO-8859 variants, KOI8 and UTF-8:

Family Examples in the list Windows 1250 Central European, 1251 Cyrillic, 1252 Western European, 1253 Greek, 1254 Turkish, 1255 Hebrew, 1256 Arabic, 1257 Baltic, 1258 Vietnamese, 874 Thai DOS/OEM 437, 720, 737, 775, 850, 852, 855, 857, 858, 860–866, 869 East Asian 932 Shift-JIS, 936 GBK, 949 Korean, 950 Big5, 54936 GB18030, 51932 EUC-JP Other 20866 KOI8-R, 21866 KOI8-U, 10000 Mac Roman, 10007 Mac Cyrillic, ISO-8859 variants, 65001 UTF-8

An imported action can retain a codepage identifier outside the normal list; unsupported codepages report an error when run. Do not select an encoding solely because the output happens to look plausible.

docs.title: Targets and limitations
docs.text:
Use a named field first. _TAG processes every tag field; _ALL also processes the filename stem. _FILENAME keeps the audio extension, and _DIRECTORY changes the containing folder name.

The conversion must recover a byte for every existing character. Values up to U+00FF map to those byte values; certain Windows-1252 glyphs such as € also have a recoverable mapping. Characters with no legacy-byte representation produce an error, as do invalid byte sequences for the chosen codepage. A replacement character � or a previous ? substitution usually means information was already lost; encoding conversion cannot reconstruct it.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Do not run the action twice without checking the first result.
  • Whole-library _ALL conversion can damage correct fields and names. Select files with the same confirmed problem first.
  • Keep the original copy. The action writes when run; inspect operation errors and Edit → Undo for recorded changes.

docs.title: Export Cover to File
docs.text: Use Export Cover to File to copy embedded pictures to separate image files. Exporting leaves the pictures embedded in the audio. It does not resize or convert the image data. This action works with local files; action groups are not available for provider documents yet.

docs.title: Write a front-cover file beside the album
docs.text:
1. Select copied practice files and save pending edits.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Export Cover to File.
  3. Set Output filename format (extension is added) to folder.
  4. Set Export covers of type to Front Cover.
  5. Leave Export duplicate covers off.
  6. Choose Apply action, then inspect the album folder.

For a reusable workflow, create the action in Actions → Actions… (Alt+6; ⌥ Option on macOS). A new installation includes the unchecked Examples → Save front cover as folder image group for this task.

A JPEG front cover becomes folder.jpg. A PNG becomes folder.png. A relative output path is resolved beside each audio file. The extension comes from the picture's actual format, not the audio file's extension.

docs.title: Settings and naming examples
docs.text:
Setting Meaning Output filename format (extension is added) Format string evaluated per audio file Export covers of type All cover types, or one role such as front or back Export duplicate covers Whether to attempt exports of repeated image content at the same requested destination Output format Embedded picture Output name folder JPEG folder.jpg cover.jpg PNG cover.png %album% with album Harbour Lights JPEG Harbour Lights.jpg Vol. 2 JPEG Vol. 2.jpg

An existing matching image extension is kept; a different recognized image extension is replaced. A suffix such as . 2 in the last example is part of the name, so the image extension is appended.

When several pictures in one audio file qualify, later pictures receive numbered names such as cover (1).jpg. The suffix follows the position among matching cover types, including earlier covers skipped as duplicates. Appending another embedded cover and exporting again keeps the first image and writes the new one to its numbered name. Prefer a type filter when one front cover is wanted rather than every embedded picture.

Use \ to create literal folder components on every platform. Ordinary tag values have separators and reserved filename characters cleaned. %_folderpath%, %_path% and %_workingpath% retain native path components, including a backslash inside a macOS or Linux folder name. See placeholders and format strings.

docs.title: Understand duplicates and existing files
docs.text:
With duplicate export off, OpenTag skips a picture when the same image bytes remain in an output for the same requested name after this action finishes. This is useful when every track in an album contains identical artwork. Reordering or replacing embedded pictures exports a repeated image again when a later numbered write would overwrite its only output.

Different pictures aimed at the same name are not duplicates. Nor does enabling duplicate export create a unique name for every track. Use a per-track expression such as %_filename%-cover when every track needs its own output file.

An existing destination with identical image bytes stays unchanged. A different image is replaced. Export duplicate covers controls repeated images in this run; it does not prevent replacement of existing files. An export that only finds identical images does not add an undo step.

Use Edit → Undo (Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z) in the same session to restore a replaced image or remove a new image created by the action. Redo recreates those images. Empty output folders can remain. Keep backups of images to retain beyond this session and inspect the available undo operation.

When recording undo, OpenTag checks the retained snapshot budget before copying an existing output. On macOS and Linux it also checks the journal's free-space reserve; that reserve check is unavailable on Windows. If the capture cannot fit, the export warns and leaves that destination unchanged. A later failure to retain the completed operation produces an undo notice; check which operation is actually available before relying on Undo.

When two selected files export different images to one name in a run, the later file gets a warning and the first image stays. A file can replace its own earlier output after another action changes its cover, including returning to an image exported earlier. A different file's equal-image no-op does not take ownership of the output name.

On macOS and Linux, exporting to an image symlink replaces the link entry; its target file stays unchanged. With the undo step available, Undo restores the original link and Redo restores the exported image. If link undo cannot be prepared, the action warns before replacing it. Dangling output links are refused. A later folder move carries output ownership and undo capture with the image; repeated exports retain the snapshot from before the first replacement. An export back into the old folder after a rename is tracked separately. Undo removes those later images and only their tracked empty parent folders before moving the album back. Extra files in that recreated folder are kept; if they block the move, Undo reports the obstruction and attempts to restore the side-file changes it had already made.

Output aliases that would replace an input audio file are refused. A warning does not stop the file's remaining actions or later groups. Inspect all warnings and earlier successful writes before repeating the group.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Running the same export again can encounter files created by the first run. Duplicate detection for a run is not a disk cleanup policy.
  • Pictures of different roles may contain identical image bytes. A type filter makes the intended export clearer.
  • An audio file without a qualifying picture produces no image for it.
  • Undo covers this action's created and replaced images. Other external exports use their own write/undo rules; it is not a general cleanup tool.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: Use the Export action to produce a text report from selected files as part of a saved action group. An export configuration defines the report's contents; an output filename format decides where to write it.

docs.title: Produce a small track report
docs.text:
1. In a plain-text editor, save this configuration as a UTF-8 file named practice-report.mte:

    $filename(tags.txt,utf-8)$loop(1)%artist% - %title%
$loopend()

  2. Save pending tag edits and select copied practice files in the order you want them listed.

  3. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Export.
  4. Next to Export configuration, choose Browse… and select practice-report.mte.
  5. In Output filename format, enter tags.txt.
  6. Leave Append data and Create one output file per partition off.
  7. Choose Apply action, then open the report beside the first selected audio file.

With two selected titles, the content can look like:

Juniper Vale - Paper Boats
Juniper Vale - North Pier

$filename declares an export destination and encoding, $loop(1) repeats its body in input order, and $loopend() ends the repetition. A constant loop key keeps the input order; a key such as %_path% sorts by that value. Field-key loops follow Options → General → natural sorting: enabled, numbered names compare as 1, 2, 10; disabled, they use text order. Constant loop keys retain input order. These are export-template commands, separate from ordinary tag-format functions.

docs.title: Configure the output
docs.text:
Setting Meaning Export configuration A saved configuration name, an .mte file path, or complete export-template text Browse… Choose an export configuration file Output filename format A format string overriding the configuration's output filename; leave empty to use its declaration Append data Append rendered data rather than replacing the output Create one output file per partition Enable grouping by Partition format Partition format A per-file format string whose equal results belong to the same output group

Export configuration is a single-line input. Use a saved configuration name or an .mte file path for templates containing line breaks; do not paste the multiline file contents into that box. A complete one-line template can be entered directly. Export settings control byte-order marks and whether missing output folders may be created.

docs.title: Partition a report
docs.text:
To write one report per album folder, enable partitioning and use:

Setting Value Partition format %_folderpath% Output filename format %_folderpath%tags.txt

All selected files with the same folder path enter the same report. The filename and the grouping key serve different purposes. Ensure each partition has a distinct output path; do not group by disc number while sending every disc to the same tags.txt.

The action uses the selected files' final values in its group. Export runs after the per-file actions even when its row is listed first. Files with an earlier action warning still participate. Use a separate earlier group if the report must capture values before cleanup.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Export writes a report; it does not create copies of the audio files.
  • Appending can repeat rows when the group is run again. Check the output before enabling it in a frequently used workflow.
  • A relative output path is based on the first input file's folder. Use an explicit destination for a selection spanning several folders.
  • Protect existing reports and check operation errors. Generated output may require separate cleanup, and earlier group effects can remain after a later error.

docs.title: Format Value
docs.text: Use Format Value to create or replace a field with a value calculated from other tags. It can also build a new filename or folder name. Use it when the result needs placeholders, conditions or scripting functions.

docs.title: Fill a field from other tags
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few practice files.
  2. Open Actions → Actions (Quick)… and select Format Value.
  3. Enter the destination in Field and the expression in Format string.
  4. Choose Apply action and inspect the result.

For a reusable workflow, add the same action to an action group and choose Keep action. Saving a group alone does not run it.

Setting Meaning Field A tag field, _FILENAME, or _DIRECTORY Format string Text, placeholders and functions evaluated for each selected file

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Field Format string Result ALBUMARTIST $if2(%albumartist%,%artist%) Keep an existing album artist; otherwise use the first artist YEAR $left(%year%,4) 2024-05-01 becomes 2024 TITLE $replace(%title%,_, ) Low_Tide becomes Low Tide; the last argument is one space COMMENT Tagged with OpenTag Set the same comment in every selected file TRACK $num(%track%,2) 2/8 becomes 02; the total is not retained by this expression

Try a small selection first. Format Value replaces the destination's whole value list; it does not append to an existing list.

docs.title: Write one or several field values
docs.text:
For an ordinary tag field, two consecutive backslashes (\\) in the evaluated result separate values. When that delimiter is present, surrounding whitespace is trimmed from each component and empty components are dropped. If none remain, the field is removed. One backslash is ordinary text. Without the delimiter, a nonempty result stays one value and keeps its surrounding whitespace.

In this table, · marks a space in a stored value; it is not a character to type. Each separately quoted result is a separate GENRE value.

Format string Values stored in GENRE Rock\\Pop Rock + Pop Jazz \\ \\ Blues\\ Jazz + Blues $char(32)Live$char(32) ·Live· AC\DC AC\DC \\ (field removed) $if(%missing%,unused,) (field removed)

A bare %artist% reads only its first value. To write all existing artists as separate values, use $meta_sep(artist,\\); a comma or & join instead produces one combined value. Read the multivalue syntax before replacing artist lists. A tag format may limit how separate values are stored.

These output-splitting rules apply to metadata fields. _FILENAME and _DIRECTORY use the naming rules below; their backslashes name folder levels, not several metadata values.

An empty result removes the destination field. A missing %albumartist% alone therefore removes ALBUMARTIST; $if2 is useful when a fallback is required. '' is a literal apostrophe, not an empty result.

docs.title: Build filenames and folders
docs.text:
For Field _FILENAME, try:

$num(%track%,2) - %artist% - %title%

With track 2/8, artist Juniper Vale and title Lanterns on the Water, the stem becomes 02 - Juniper Vale - Lanterns on the Water. The original audio extension is retained. A format result already ending in that extension does not need a second copy of it.

For _DIRECTORY, the result names the containing folder. That can affect other files in the folder, including files outside the selection. Practice on a copied folder before using this target.

Literal folder separators in a format string can create folder levels. Separators originating in tag values use the configured replacement; see file and folder rules. An empty filename or directory result is rejected.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• _TAG, _ALL, _FIELDNAME and information placeholders such as _BITRATE are not Format Value destinations. Choose a real tag field or one of the two naming targets.
  • An action writes when it runs. It does not leave the result waiting in the tag panel. Keep copies and check Edit → Undo for recorded changes.
  • Within a group, the expression sees earlier actions' results. Put a copy action before any action that clears its source field.
  • The preview in Convert → Tag → Tag… is useful for experimenting with the expression before putting it in a group.

docs.text:

docs.title: Generate Playlists
docs.text: Use Generate Playlists to write playlists for the selected files from an action group. A partition format decides which tracks belong together; a filename format names each partition's playlist.

docs.title: Create one playlist per album folder
docs.text:
1. Select a few copied files and put them in the desired file-list order.
  2. Save pending edits, then open Actions → Actions (Quick)….
  3. Choose Generate Playlists.
  4. Set Partition format to %_folderpath%.
  5. Set Playlist filename format to %_folderpath%playlist.m3u8.
  6. Choose Apply action and inspect each folder's playlist.

Tracks with the same folder path enter one playlist, preserving their relative order in the file list. The .m3u8 extension requests an M3U8 playlist; choose an extension supported by the playlist writer.

docs.title: Understand partitions
docs.text:
OpenTag evaluates Partition format for every selected track. Tracks with exactly equal results form a group. For each group, it evaluates Playlist filename format using that group's first track.

Goal Partition format Playlist filename format One playlist in every folder %_folderpath% %_folderpath%playlist.m3u8 One per disc in an album folder %_folderpath%-%discnumber% %_folderpath%disc-%discnumber%.m3u8 One for the entire selection all An absolute path chosen for the combined playlist

The partition value is a grouping key, not an output path. The filename must distinguish different groups: two partitions that resolve to the same destination report an error. Adding %discnumber% to the partition alone would not give each disc a distinct output filename.

A relative filename is resolved beside the first track in that partition. For a combined playlist spanning folders, choose an explicit absolute destination so the result does not depend on which track comes first.

The filename format uses literal \ as a folder separator on every platform. Separators and reserved filename characters in ordinary tag values are cleaned; native path placeholders such as %_folderpath% retain their path components. The partition format remains a grouping key, not a filename.

docs.title: Order and playlist options
docs.text:
This action uses the current playlist settings for entry paths, extended information, encoding where applicable, and writing behavior. Inspect the result in the player that will open it, especially when moving the music and playlists to another machine.

In an action group, playlist generation runs after the group's per-file actions. A preceding rename therefore appears in the playlist, and even a playlist action listed before that rename sees the final values. Files with an earlier action warning still participate. Put it in a separate earlier group if an intermediate state is required.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• The action includes selected files, not every track in the folder.
  • File-list order matters; the action does not automatically sort by track number.
  • Avoid filename collisions with audio files or other partitions.
  • Generated playlists may require separate cleanup. Do not assume session undo removes every output file, or that a failed batch rolled back all earlier file effects.

docs.text:
• Export

  • Placeholders

docs.title: Guess Values
docs.text: Use Guess Values to split a structured value into several fields. Supply a source format string to read the text, then a guessing pattern to say which parts belong in which fields. Despite its name, this action does not infer a layout: the entire source must match the pattern.

docs.title: Split an artist and title
docs.text:
Suppose TITLE contains Juniper Vale / Paper Boats, and the artist field is missing.

  1. Save pending edits and select a copied practice file.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Guess Values.
  3. Enter %title% in Source format string.
  4. Enter %artist% / %title% in Guessing pattern.
  5. Choose Apply action, then inspect both fields.

The result is ARTIST = Juniper Vale and TITLE = Paper Boats. The source is evaluated before either destination changes, so reading from TITLE while replacing TITLE works.

docs.title: Understand the two boxes
docs.text:
Setting What it does Source format string Reads tags and evaluates functions to produce one text value Guessing pattern Captures text between exact separators into named fields

In the pattern, %artist% names a destination. It does not read the existing artist value. The spaces around / are literal and must also occur in the source. Pattern text is case-sensitive.

Source text Guessing pattern Fields written Juniper Vale / Paper Boats %artist% / %title% ARTIST = Juniper Vale; TITLE = Paper Boats 2024 - Harbour Lights %year% - %album% YEAR = 2024; ALBUM = Harbour Lights 02 - Paper Boats - archive %track% - %title% - %dummy% TRACK = 02; TITLE = Paper Boats Juniper Vale / Mira Solberg %artist% / %artist% Two ARTIST values, in that order

Use %dummy% for a part that should be consumed without being stored. Repeated destination names create multiple values, replacing the field's previous values.

docs.title: Make the source predictable
docs.text:
Functions belong in Source format string, for example:

$trim(%comment%)

With COMMENT = 2024 - Harbour Lights, this produces 2024 - Harbour Lights. The pattern %year% - %album% can then capture the two values without surrounding spaces.

Captures themselves are not trimmed. A separator appearing inside a name can also change where the text splits: captures take the shortest text that permits the rest of the pattern to match. Choose a separator that is unambiguous for the selected files.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• No full match means no field changes for that file. Check both successful and unmatched files after a batch.
  • Adjacent placeholders such as %artist%%title% are rejected because there is no separator defining where the first value ends.
  • The pattern needs at least one complete %field% placeholder. It is not a regular expression or a place to call scripting functions.
  • _FILENAME and _DIRECTORY destinations can rename files or folders. Captured names are treated as values, with invalid naming characters replaced. Use ordinary tag destinations while learning the action.
  • This action saves changes immediately. Try copies first and inspect Edit → Undo for recorded changes.

docs.text:

docs.title: Import Cover from File
docs.text: Use Import Cover from File to embed an existing image in each selected audio file. A filename format lets one action find the right picture in each album folder. This action works with local files; action groups are not available for provider documents yet.

docs.title: Embed each album's cover
docs.text:
1. Put the intended image in each album folder as cover.jpg.
  2. Keep copies of the audio files, save pending edits and select a few practice files.
  3. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Import Cover from File.
  4. Enter cover.jpg in Image filename format.
  5. Choose Front Cover in Import cover as.
  6. Leave Delete existing covers off for this trial.
  7. Choose Apply action and inspect the embedded pictures.

For a reusable sequence, open Actions → Actions… (Alt+6; ⌥ Option on macOS), create a group and add the same action there. Applying either route writes the audio files immediately.

A relative image path is resolved beside each audio file. Thus files in different folders can use different cover.jpg images with the same action. Browse… can choose one specific image; an absolute path uses that image for every selected file.

docs.title: Choose the filename and cover type
docs.text:
Setting Meaning Image filename format A format string evaluated for each file, including the image's extension Import cover as The picture role to store, initially Front Cover Delete existing covers Remove all previously embedded pictures before adding the new one; off initially Image filename format Where it reads cover.jpg cover.jpg next to each audio file %_folderpath%folder.jpg folder.jpg in that audio file's folder %album%.png For ALBUM = Harbour Lights, Harbour Lights.png beside the audio file

Use * for any run of characters or ? for one character in the final filename component. For example, %_folderpath%front*.png finds the first importable matching image, while %_folderpath%cover?.jpg can find cover1.jpg. Candidates are considered in natural name order, ignoring filename case: front2.png comes before front10.png. Folders, non-images and formats the importer refuses are skipped. JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF and WebP are accepted. Folder components are used as literal existing paths; matching does not expand a folder pattern or search several folders. On macOS and Linux, * and ? in an actual source-folder name remain literal, including when that folder comes from %_folderpath%. Prefer a specific filename pattern; a broad * can choose unintended artwork.

Use \ to separate literal folders in the format on every platform. %_folderpath%, %_path% and %_workingpath% keep their native path components, including a backslash inside a macOS or Linux folder name. Ordinary tag values have separators and reserved filename characters cleaned: an album value AC/DC does not create an AC folder.

Cover roles include front, back, leaflet, media, artist, band and other standard picture types. Choose the role that describes the image; changing the role does not change the image itself.

docs.title: Decide whether to keep existing pictures
docs.text:
With Delete existing covers off, importing adds a picture and retains the existing pictures. Repeated runs can add repeated artwork.

With it on, every existing picture is removed, including back covers and booklet images, before the import. The source image is checked before removal, but a later write failure is still a reason to inspect the file and retain a backup. To replace only one particular picture, use the cover-management controls instead of clearing all covers.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• The audio format must support embedded artwork. A sidecar image existing on disk does not mean every selected tag format can store it.
  • A missing or invalid image reports an error; it does not trigger an online artwork search.
  • The action writes immediately. Inspect the pictures and Edit → Undo for recorded file changes before applying it to the whole album.
  • A missing or invalid match leaves the existing covers in place, even with Delete existing covers enabled. A warning does not stop that file's remaining actions or later groups; inspect earlier successful writes before running the group again.

docs.text:
• Export Cover to File

  • Set Cover Properties
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Import Text File
docs.text: Use Import Text File to replace one field with the complete contents of a text file. It suits lyrics, a long comment or album notes. It does not parse columns or assign different lines to different audio files.

docs.title: Load a text file into a field
docs.text:
1. Put a UTF-8 file named notes.txt beside your practice audio file. For this example, give it the text Recorded at the north pier.
  2. Save pending edits and select that copied audio file.
  3. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Import Text File.
  4. Set Field to COMMENT and Text filename format to notes.txt.
  5. Choose Apply action, then inspect COMMENT in Extended tags….

The comment becomes Recorded at the north pier.. Existing comment values are replaced with one value containing the imported text.

docs.title: Filename formats
docs.text:
Setting Meaning Field The destination tag field, such as LYRICS or COMMENT Text filename format A format string evaluated separately for each selected audio file Browse… Choose a specific text file

A relative path is resolved in each audio file's folder. An absolute path reads the same file for every selected track.

Literal \ separates folders on every platform. Ordinary tag values have separators and reserved filename characters cleaned, using the configured folder-separator replacement. %_folderpath%, %_path% and %_workingpath% retain native path components, including a backslash within a macOS or Linux folder name.

Filename format Example use notes.txt The album folder's notes for every selected track there %_filename%.txt For 02 - Paper Boats.flac, read 02 - Paper Boats.txt beside it %_folderpath%lyrics.txt Read one lyrics file from that audio file's folder

Use an exact path, including the extension. The filename expression does not expand wildcard searches. A missing file warns for that file; later actions and groups still run. It does not schedule an import for later.

docs.title: Text and encoding rules
docs.text:
The entire file becomes one value, including its line breaks and spaces. Use UTF-8 for new text files. A byte-order mark selects the corresponding Unicode decoding. Without one, valid UTF-8 is accepted; otherwise the configured ANSI/system codepage is used, with Windows-1252 as the fallback when none is configured.

Check accented characters after importing older files. Convert Codepage repairs some already-misdecoded field text, but choosing a known encoding for the source text before import is preferable.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• The action replaces all existing values of the destination field. It does not append the text.
  • An empty source file replaces the existing content with empty text. Use Remove Fields when the goal is to delete the destination field.
  • _FILENAME, _DIRECTORY and other underscore targets are not supported destinations for this action.
  • This action writes immediately. Keep copies and inspect operation errors and Edit → Undo for recorded changes.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Convert Codepage
  • Remove Fields
  • Format Value
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Merge Duplicate Fields
docs.text: Use Merge Duplicate Fields when a field contains several separate values and the target player expects one combined value. It joins the existing values with a chosen separator. It does not remove repeated text.

docs.title: Join a field's values
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few copied files.
  2. Open Actions → Actions (Quick)… and choose Merge Duplicate Fields.
  3. Set Field to ARTIST and Separator to ;, including the space.
  4. Choose Apply action and inspect the field in Extended tags….
Setting Meaning Field One tag field, or _TAG for every tag field Separator Literal text inserted between values; leave empty to concatenate them

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Separate values before Separator One value after Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Semicolon and space Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg & Juniper Vale & Mira Solberg Low, Tide One space Low Tide Juniper Vale, Juniper Vale ; Juniper Vale; Juniper Vale

The last example matters: duplicate fields means multiple values of one field, not necessarily equal values. To remove repeated values, use Remove Duplicate Fields with its same-content option instead.

A field with zero or one value is unchanged. Existing order is preserved. An empty separator joins directly, so Low and Tide become LowTide. The separator is text, not a format string: %artist% would be inserted literally between the values.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• _TAG can collapse every multivalue field, including ones whose separate values a player needs. Prefer a named field.
  • _FILENAME, _DIRECTORY and _FIELDNAME are not supported targets.
  • Merging changes the stored structure. A later split can only recover the original values if the separator never appeared inside any original value.
  • The action writes when run. Practice on copies and check Edit → Undo for the recorded file change.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Split Field by Separator
  • Remove Duplicate Fields
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Remove Duplicate Fields
docs.text: Use Remove Duplicate Fields to reduce a field's multiple values. Choose carefully: the default keeps only the first value, even when the later values are different artists or names that should be retained.

docs.title: Choose what to keep
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few copied files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Remove Duplicate Fields.
  3. Enter a field such as ARTIST, or _ALL for every tag field.
  4. Set Only duplicated fields with the same content as needed.
  5. Choose Apply action and inspect the values in Extended tags….
Option What survives Initial setting Same-content option off The first value of each affected field Off Same-content option on The first occurrence of each exactly equal value

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Values before Same-content option Values after Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Off Juniper Vale Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg On Both artists Juniper Vale, Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg On Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Juniper Vale, JUNIPER VALE On Both values: comparison is case-sensitive

Remaining values keep their original order. A missing field is not created. A field with one value stays as it is.

docs.title: Special targets
docs.text: _ALL means all tag fields for this action. It does not rename a file or remove artwork. Filename, directory and field-name selectors are not supported. Use a specific field to avoid reducing unrelated multivalue fields such as composers or genres.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Equal-looking strings may differ in case or whitespace. The same-content option compares the stored text exactly.
  • Turning the option off is a deliberate loss of additional values. Keep a backup until the result is verified in the player that will use it.
  • Actions save immediately. Check operation errors and the Edit → Undo entry for the recorded change.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Merge Duplicate Fields
  • Split Field by Separator
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Remove Fields Except
docs.text: Use Remove Fields Except to keep an explicit list of fields and remove all other fields. This is useful for a controlled export copy of your music; it can also remove useful identifiers, sort fields and artwork if they are missing from the keep list.

docs.title: Keep a chosen set of fields
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select copied files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Remove Fields Except.
  3. Enter the field names in Keep fields (separate with semicolons).
  4. Choose Apply action and inspect the full tag with Extended tags….

For example:

TITLE;ARTIST;ALBUM;ALBUMARTIST;YEAR;DATE;TRACK;TRACKNUMBER;DISCNUMBER;GENRE;COVER

This preserves the named fields if present. It does not add missing ones. COVER preserves embedded artwork; PICTURE can be used for the same purpose. Without either artwork selector, embedded pictures are removed.

docs.title: Build the list from actual files
docs.text:
Different formats can expose similar values under different names. For example, a file may use DATE rather than YEAR, or TRACKNUMBER rather than TRACK. Open Extended tags… before preparing the keep list, and include the names used in the files being processed.

Keep list Effect TITLE;ARTIST;COVER Keep only title, artist and embedded artwork TITLE;ARTIST Keep only title and artist; remove embedded artwork COVER Keep embedded pictures while removing all tag fields

The list is literal field names separated by semicolons. It does not accept placeholders or patterns such as MUSICBRAINZ_*. Add each field that must survive explicitly.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• An empty keep list removes every field and embedded cover. Review it before applying; keep an untouched copy of the files.
  • Identifiers, ReplayGain values, lyrics, sort names and totals are metadata too. Include them if another application depends on them.
  • The action writes immediately. Check operation errors and the session's Edit → Undo entry; do not rely on an unspecified whole-batch rollback.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Remove Fields
  • Remove Duplicate Fields
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Remove Fields
docs.text: Use Remove Fields to delete selected metadata fields while keeping the rest of the tag. It can also remove embedded artwork.

docs.title: Remove named fields
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few copied files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Remove Fields.

  3. In Remove fields (separate with semicolons), enter:

    COMMENT;ENCODEDBY

  4. Choose Apply action and check Extended tags….

COMMENT and ENCODEDBY disappear when present; other fields stay in place. A name not present in a file has nothing to remove.

docs.title: More examples
docs.text:
Enter Effect COMMENT Remove the comment field COMMENT;RATING Remove both named fields COVER Remove every embedded picture COMMENT;PICTURE Remove comments and every embedded picture

COVER and PICTURE are artwork selectors here. They do not refer to an image file alongside the music. This action does not delete folder.jpg.

The list accepts field names separated by semicolons. It is not a filter, regular expression or format string, and it does not support wildcard field-name patterns. Do not enter %comment% or an information placeholder such as _BITRATE to remove a tag field.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Field removal saves immediately. It does not blank the panel and wait for Save tags.
  • Removing a field differs from removing the entire tag format. The action only targets the names listed, plus artwork when explicitly requested.
  • Keep backups. For recorded file edits in the current desktop session, inspect Edit → Undo after applying.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Remove Fields Except
  • Remove Duplicate Fields
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Replace with Regular Expression
docs.text: Use this action when the text varies in a predictable way: leading track numbers, repeated spaces, a dated suffix, or a guest name to extract. The regular expression describes what to match; the replacement can reuse captured parts.

docs.title: Run the action
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few copied files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)….
  3. Select Replace with Regular Expression.
  4. Enter Field, Regular expression and Replace matches with.
  5. Set Case-sensitive comparison, then choose Apply action.

There is no separate save step. For a preview while designing a pattern, try the equivalent $regexp expression in Convert → Tag → Tag… first.

Setting Meaning Field One field or a supported target below Regular expression A Boost Perl-style pattern Replace matches with Replacement text and capture references such as $1; leave empty to remove matches Case-sensitive comparison Off initially; turn it on when case matters

The action transforms every value in a multivalue field independently. It replaces all matches; a value with no match remains unchanged.

docs.title: Patterns to try
docs.text:
Enter these patterns and replacements directly, without outer quotes:

Goal Field Regular expression Replace matches with Before → After Remove a leading track number TITLE ^\d+[\s._-]* Leave empty 03_Paper Boats → Paper Boats Collapse repeated spaces TITLE \s{2,} One space North Pier → North Pier Keep only a year YEAR ^(\d{4}).*$ $1 2024-05-01 → 2024 Put "The" after an artist ARTIST ^The (.+)$ $1, The The Lanterns → Lanterns, The Remove a dated remaster suffix TITLE \s*\(Remastered \d{4}\)$ Leave empty North Pier (Remastered 2021) → North Pier

For example, 03_Paper Boats becomes Paper Boats, and North Pier (Remastered 2021) becomes North Pier. Test the pattern on unexpected values too; a successful match on one example is not enough for an entire library.

docs.title: Quotes differ from format strings
docs.text:
The action boxes contain raw pattern and replacement text. Do not wrap a pattern in single quotes, and type $1 directly. By contrast, a $regexp function sits inside the format-string language and needs quoting around special syntax:

$regexp(%title%,'^\d+[\s._-]*',)

The final argument above is empty. '' would insert an apostrophe. See the regex reference for quoting, groups, lookarounds, case controls and replacement escapes.

docs.title: Special targets and extensions
docs.text:
Target What the action reads _TAG Every tag field _ALL Every tag field and each filename, including its extension _FILENAME The filename including its extension _DIRECTORY The containing folder name

For _FILENAME, \s+$ does not remove spaces just before .mp3, because those spaces are not at the end of the input. Use \s+(?=\.\w+$) for that specific case. Protect the extension when rearranging captured groups. Folder renames can affect unselected files in that folder.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Patterns can also match an empty string, producing replacements between characters. Preview deliberately before using an empty or optional pattern.
  • Invalid syntax reports an error. A valid pattern that finds nothing is not an error and leaves the value unchanged.
  • _FIELDNAME is not a supported selector for this action.
  • Keep backups and inspect Edit → Undo and operation errors after a run. Generated file effects are not a guarantee of whole-batch rollback.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Regular expressions
  • Literal Replace
  • Move guest artists to titles
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Replace
docs.text: Use Replace for literal text changes: underscores to spaces, an unwanted word, or a consistent spelling. The search text is not a regular expression; . means a dot and * means an asterisk.

docs.title: Make a replacement
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few copied files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Replace.
  3. Choose a Field, enter Original string and Replace with, then set the two comparison options.
  4. Choose Apply action and check the changed fields.

Add the same settings to a group when the change will be repeated.

Setting Meaning Initial value Field A field name or supported target below TITLE Original string The literal text to find; cannot be empty Empty Replace with The replacement text; leave empty to delete matches Empty Only as whole word Restrict the match to whole words as defined below Off Case-sensitive comparison Distinguish upper- and lowercase search text Off

All occurrences are replaced in each value of the chosen field. Unmatched values stay unchanged. The replacement is literal too: $1 is text here, not a captured group.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Field Original string Replace with Before → After TITLE _ One space Low_Tide → Low Tide ALBUM (Deluxe) Leave empty Harbour Lights (Deluxe) → Harbour Lights, with a trailing space TITLE Live Concert LIVE at the Pier → Concert at the Pier when case sensitivity is off ARTIST & and Kofi & the Tidewater Band → Kofi and the Tidewater Band

Enter the actual spaces around & and and; do not type quotes. For deleting a suffix and its preceding spaces, use the regex action with a pattern that includes those spaces.

docs.title: Whole-word matching
docs.text:
Only as whole word accepts a match at the start or end of a value, or next to whitespace or one of these punctuation characters:

. , ; : ! ?

A hyphen, underscore, slash or parenthesis does not count as that boundary. For example, a whole-word search for Live can change Live! but leaves Live-Version unchanged. Use regular expressions when a different word boundary rule is needed.

docs.title: Special targets
docs.text:
• _TAG changes every tag field.
  • _ALL changes every tag field and the filename stem.
  • _FILENAME changes the filename stem, keeping the audio extension.
  • _DIRECTORY changes the containing folder name.

The replacement can therefore have wider consequences than the field list suggests. Keep a folder backup when using a naming target, and avoid changing a directory merely to fix tag text.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Quick-action settings are remembered. Check them before each run.
  • Literal replacement does not trim the result. A deleted word can leave double or trailing spaces.
  • Changes are saved when the action runs. Check operation errors and the Edit → Undo label rather than assuming the whole batch is atomic.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Replace with Regular Expression
  • Format Value
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Set Cover Properties
docs.text: Use Set Cover Properties to change the role or description of embedded pictures. The picture data and dimensions stay the same. Use Adjust Cover when the actual image needs resizing or conversion.

docs.title: Label a front cover
docs.text:
1. Keep copies, save pending edits and select practice files whose embedded pictures you have inspected.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Set Cover Properties.
  3. Choose Front Cover in Cover type.
  4. Keep Keep existing description checked.
  5. Set Apply only to covers of type to the pictures' current role, for example Other.
  6. Choose Apply action and inspect the roles afterward.

In this example, pictures previously marked Other become Front Cover. Back covers and other roles remain unchanged because the filter checks each picture's original role.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Effect Cover type Set a new role, or keep the existing type Keep existing description Checked initially; retain each picture's description Cover description When keeping is off, replace the description with this literal text Apply only to covers of type Restrict changes to an original role, or select All cover types

Type and description are independent. Keeping the type still allows a description change, and keeping the description still allows a type change.

docs.title: Worked settings
docs.text:
Goal Cover type Description setting Apply only to Mark unclassified art as front covers Front Cover Keep existing Other Clear descriptions without changing roles Keep existing Uncheck keep; leave description empty All cover types Describe back covers Keep existing Uncheck keep; enter Album back cover Back Cover

Description text is literal: %album% is stored as those characters, not evaluated as a placeholder. An empty replacement clears the description; leaving Keep existing description checked preserves it.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• All cover types can turn a front cover, back cover and booklet into the same role. Use the role filter when only one kind should change.
  • Files without embedded artwork gain no picture from this action.
  • Role and description support varies by tag format and player. Inspect the saved file as well as its display in the target player.
  • Changes save when the action runs. Use practice copies and inspect Edit → Undo for recorded file changes.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Import Cover from File
  • Export Cover to File
  • Adjust Cover
  • Actions and action groups

docs.title: Split Field by Separator
docs.text: Use Split Field by Separator to turn text containing several names into separate field values. For example, one ARTIST value containing Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg becomes two artist values.

docs.title: Split a field
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select a few copied files.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Split Field by Separator.
  3. Set Field to ARTIST and Separator to ;.
  4. Choose Apply action, then open Extended tags… (Alt+T) to inspect the separate values.

For repeated use, keep these settings in an action group.

Setting Meaning Field A tag field, or _TAG for every tag field Separator A nonempty literal string; it can contain several characters

docs.title: Understand the result
docs.text:
Each existing value is split, with surrounding whitespace trimmed from each piece. The pieces keep their original order. The separator itself is not kept and is not interpreted as a regular expression.

Before Separator Values after splitting Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg ; Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Juniper Vale / Mira Solberg / Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Low Tide ; Low Tide

If a field already has two values, both are processed and their resulting pieces are collected in order. A separator at the start or end, or two separators together, can produce empty pieces. Clean the input first when those empty values are unwanted.

OpenTag's display may join values with \\. That is a display convention; do not use it as a separator unless those characters actually occur inside one value. Whether another player displays multiple values separately depends on the tag format and the player.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Splitting AC/DC on / would divide a single artist name. Select only the files that follow the intended convention.
  • _TAG applies the same separator to every tag field, including comments or lyrics. Use a named field whenever that is the actual goal.
  • _FILENAME, _DIRECTORY and _FIELDNAME are not split targets.
  • The action writes immediately. Use practice copies and check the recorded Edit → Undo operation before relying on it.

docs.title: Cover art
docs.text: Why can an album show artwork in one folder, then lose it when a track is copied elsewhere? An image beside the audio file and an image embedded in its tags are different objects. OpenTag labels its folder-image fallback so you can tell which one you are seeing.

docs.title: Where the picture lives
docs.text:
Picture location What travels when only the audio file is copied folder.jpg beside the tracks The image stays behind unless it is copied separately. Embedded picture in each track's tags Each copied track carries its own saved picture, where its format supports artwork. Pending or staged picture in an editor A visible preview alone does not establish that the audio file has been written.

A shared folder image avoids storing a copy in every track. Embedding makes each file self-contained. Those are storage choices, not guarantees about what a particular player displays. Some players prefer a folder image; others choose an embedded role, the first image, or cached artwork.

OpenTag can show Folder image / Not embedded in the file when the eligible local selection has no embedded or pending artwork. This fallback is a display convenience. Adding an embedded image does not delete the external source. Removing embedded images does not remove folder.jpg. The exact selection and option rules are in Working with covers.

docs.title: An embedded cover has more than pixels
docs.text:
A cover consists of image bytes, a picture type, a description and a position in the file's ordered cover list. Front Cover, Back Cover and Leaflet are roles. Assigning a role does not crop, rotate or rename the image. The description is separate text; it is not a filesystem path.

These selection examples use the same front image A and a different back image B. A label includes image, role and description; list order matters.

Label Image identity Picture type Description front image-A Front Cover Album front front-other-description image-A Front Cover Alternate note same-image-back-role image-A Back Cover Album front back image-B Back Cover Track list First file's ordered covers Second file's ordered covers Shared cover-window result front front Same front front-other-description Covers vary front same-image-back-role Covers vary front,back back,front Covers vary front None Covers vary None None No embedded artwork

Covers vary therefore does not necessarily mean that every image looks different. Inspect individual files or open Manage covers…. Its full circle marks an image present in every selected file; the partial circle marks one present in a subset. Keeping a partial entry normally preserves its membership. Apply to all deliberately adds it to other selected files. A newly added image is planned for the whole initial selection.

Not every format preserves these properties equally. MP4 artwork does not retain the same role distinctions as ID3v2; OpenTag reads its pictures as Other. ID3v1 cannot hold pictures. Read the file format capabilities before relying on a role or description surviving a conversion.

docs.title: Dimensions, bytes and encoding are different
docs.text:
A 1200 × 1200 image describes pixel dimensions, not its file size. Two images with those dimensions can have very different byte sizes and compression artifacts. Embedding a large image into eight tracks stores a separate copy in each; keeping an external high-resolution original can make later revisions easier.

JPEG compression trades image detail for size and does not retain a PNG's alpha transparency. PNG can preserve transparency but may be larger for photographic artwork. The best choice depends on the source and receiving software; no single pixel limit is guaranteed for every player.

Changing .jpg to .png in a filename does not convert the bytes. Use Adjust… or an Adjust Cover action for actual resize/conversion. A preview's Correct aspect ratio changes how it is shown, not the embedded pixels. Upscaling cannot restore detail missing from a small original. Settings that already match can leave image bytes unchanged; JPEG quality alone does not force OpenTag's adjustment path to recompress an otherwise unchanged image.

docs.title: What this means in OpenTag
docs.text:
Start with a copy and decide whether the task is display, embedding, extraction, reordering or image conversion. Manage covers… stages a list plan and writes it on OK; direct cover-window mutation commands write through their own operation. External extraction creates a separate file, which tag undo does not generally remove. Inspect operation errors and each saved track rather than assuming an entire selection changed together.

For a recorded cover edit, inspect Edit → Undo and its label. Keep the original images and audio files: a session history is not a permanent image archive. The detailed guide explains clipboard/platform limits and the separate handling of pending pasted artwork.

docs.title: Multi-value fields
docs.text: Why does a player show Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg as one artist when you expected two? A field can contain one text value with punctuation, or a list of separate values. Those are different structures even when a screen renders them similarly.

docs.title: One field can hold several values
docs.text:
Compare three possible ARTIST fields:

Stored structure What it says One value: Juniper Vale One credited artist One value: Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg One string containing a semicolon Two values: Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg Two separate artist values

A semicolon is ordinary text until an operation explicitly splits on it. The same is true of &, / and commas. Splitting every slash would damage names such as AC/DC; the punctuation alone cannot reveal whether it belongs inside one name or separates two names.

docs.title: Display separators are not stored punctuation
docs.text:
OpenTag can display multiple values as:

Juniper Vale \\ Mira Solberg

The two backslashes separate values in that editing/display convention. They do not mean that the raw tag stores those exact characters between the names. In the tag panel, entering Juniper Vale \\ Mira Solberg creates two values and trims surrounding whitespace from each piece.

Extended tags… (Alt+T; Alt is ⌥ Option on a Mac) makes the structure explicit with Value 1, Value 2 and ＋ Add value. Put one whole name in each value box. A semicolon typed inside one box remains part of that value.

Selecting several files introduces another kind of difference: the files may have different artists. Mixed values — keep existing values means the selection differs; it does not mean every file contains the union of all those artists. Leaving a mixed field unchanged preserves each file's existing values.

docs.title: Format strings choose which values to read
docs.text:
For two stored artist values, Juniper Vale followed by Mira Solberg:

Format string Result %artist% Juniper Vale $meta(artist) Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg $meta(artist,0) Juniper Vale $meta(artist,1) Mira Solberg $meta_sep(artist,' & ') Juniper Vale & Mira Solberg

A bare placeholder reads the first value. $meta without an index reads all values using comma-space; indexed $meta starts at 0. $meta_sep lets the expression choose how to join them. These functions calculate text; joining text does not preserve the original list structure if that result is written back as one field value.

docs.title: Storage depends on the tag format
docs.text:
OpenTag's editing model is a list of values per field. The writer must represent that list in the destination format:

Tag storage Representation relevant to multiple values Vorbis Comments in FLAC/Ogg-family files Repeated entries with the same field name APEv2 Text values separated inside the item by NUL characters ID3v2 Text-frame value lists and format-specific frames; some fields have a single-value restriction MP4 metadata Multiple data values; the advanced setting can keep them inside one item atom or write separate item atoms RIFF INFO One string per INFO identifier; OpenTag joins multiple values with semicolon-space ID3v1 Limited legacy fields; it cannot represent a general list of values

The two MP4 layouts can contain the same logical values while being interpreted differently by a player. ID3 revisions and special-purpose fields also have their own constraints. A field that supports several artists does not imply that a numeric field or identifier accepts several values. Read the saved file back and verify the intended player before applying a storage convention to a whole library.

docs.title: Splitting, joining and deduplicating are different jobs
docs.text:
Operation Input Result Split on ; One value: Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg Two values: Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Merge with ; Two values: Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg One value: Juniper Vale; Mira Solberg Remove equal duplicates Three values: Juniper Vale, Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Two distinct values

The Split Field by Separator action trims the resulting pieces. Merge Duplicate Fields joins every value, even when the values are different. Remove Duplicate Fields is more destructive with its same-content option off: it keeps only the first value, including when the discarded values were different people. Check that option carefully.

docs.title: What this means in OpenTag
docs.text:
Decide whether the destination player needs separate artists or one display credit. Preserve separate values when they carry useful structure; join them only for a specific display or compatibility goal. Work on copies until the saved tags and player agree.

Editing in Extended tags… stages pending changes; Save tags writes them. An action writes when run. A successful preview or a joined display is not proof that the final file still contains the intended value list.
