docs.title: Save embedded covers as folder.jpg
docs.text: Uses: Export Cover to File action · Works on: copied local audio files with embedded artwork · Time: about 5 minutes per practice album · Undo: this action can record external-image changes in the current desktop session; inspect the available operation and keep existing images

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
You have a front cover inside the audio files and want a separate album-folder image. Export copies the embedded bytes out; it leaves the embedded pictures and audio in place. A JPEG exports as .jpg; a PNG exports as .png. Naming the output folder.jpg does not convert a PNG to JPEG.

For this recipe's exact folder.jpg result, start with a JPEG Front Cover. If the picture has another encoding, keep its actual extension or deliberately make a converted copy using appropriate image tools. Changing embedded images with Adjust Cover is a separate audio-file mutation; keep originals and inspect its scope before choosing that route.

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Copy one album folder, including any existing folder images, and keep the original elsewhere. Save pending tag edits in OpenTag.
  2. Select one copied audio file with the intended embedded Front Cover. Inspect it in Manage covers… or the cover window. A Folder image / Not embedded in the file fallback is not an embedded source for this action.
  3. Inspect the copied folder's current image files. If an existing folder.jpg matters, keep a separate copy or choose another output basename for the trial.

  4. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Export Cover to File. Enter these settings:

    | Setting | Value | |---|---| | Output filename format (extension is added) | folder | | Export covers of type | Front Cover | | Export duplicate covers | Off |

  5. Choose Apply action and read the result and any warnings. This writes the external image immediately; it does not wait for Save tags.

  6. Open the copied folder and inspect folder.jpg. For a JPEG source, its bytes are copied without resizing or recompression. Check that the embedded Front Cover is still present in the audio file too.

A relative folder is resolved beside that selected audio file. The action adds an extension from the embedded picture's actual encoding. It is not a wildcard search for an existing external image.

docs.title: How filenames and image formats interact
docs.text:
Output format Embedded image Output name folder JPEG folder.jpg folder PNG folder.png folder.jpg PNG folder.png folder.jpeg JPEG folder.jpeg Vol. 2 JPEG Vol. 2.jpg

The extension comes from the image, not .mp3 or .flac. An existing matching image extension is retained; another recognized image extension is replaced. A dot elsewhere in the basename does not necessarily mean an image extension, which is why Vol. 2 receives .jpg afterward.

When several embedded Front Covers qualify, the first uses folder.jpg and later qualifying positions receive names such as folder (1).jpg. A repeated image can be skipped with duplicate export off, while later numbering still reflects its qualifying position. Inspect the source cover set if you want one particular image rather than several qualifying fronts.

docs.title: Existing files and repeated images
docs.text:
An existing output with identical image bytes stays unchanged. A different image can be replaced. Export duplicate covers controls repeated content during the run; turning it off is not an “avoid overwriting existing images” setting. A run that finds only identical outputs may add no undo step.

For an album in which every track has the same cover, one representative track is enough for this trial. If you select more tracks, repeated content at the same requested destination can be skipped. This does not compare musical album identities or choose the best image.

Different embedded pictures are not duplicates. When different selected files attempt different images at the same output name in one run, a later file can warn that it was already written for another file. Do not treat processing order as an artwork-selection policy; inspect the first output and all warnings, then choose the intended representative track explicitly.

docs.title: Export from several album folders
docs.text:
Select one representative copied track per album and use the same relative folder format. Each file writes beside its own audio. An absolute output instead points the selected files toward the same location.

There is no Create one output file per partition control in this action. The per-album behavior comes from your selection and each input's folder. File → Export… creates text-based reports with separate partition controls; it is not this image-export action.

docs.title: Give each track a separate output
docs.text:
Use this in Output filename format (extension is added):

%_filename%-cover

For 03 - Paper Boats.flac containing a PNG front cover, it requests 03 - Paper Boats-cover.png in that audio file's folder. The basename placeholder omits the audio extension. This distinguishes ordinary per-track names; it does not make every possible destination or filesystem alias unique.

docs.title: Store images in an explicit subfolder
docs.text: Use art\folder when you intentionally want an art subfolder below each input's folder. Literal backslashes separate folders in filename formats on supported desktop platforms. Tag-derived values and native path placeholders have their own handling; see the action reference before building more complex destinations.

docs.title: Recovery and limits
docs.text:
This image-export action can record created and replaced external images in session undo. After a successful recorded change, inspect Edit → Undo and its operation label: Undo can remove a created image or restore a replaced one, and Redo can recreate the export. Empty output folders can remain. This is specific to this action; it is not a promise that ordinary report exports or arbitrary external files have the same undo behavior.

Snapshot retention and available space can prevent preparing an undo capture. The action can warn before a write when that capture cannot be prepared; a later retention failure can also produce an undo notice. Read the actual result and available undo entry instead of assuming the previous operation label now represents this export. If history itself is unavailable, an export can still run without an undo entry. Keep any image you need beyond the session.

A file without a qualifying embedded cover produces no image for it. A missing image, unsupported bytes or file error is a reason to inspect that source; export does not download, invent or repair artwork. Save a copied result and test it with the receiving player or folder viewer when compatibility matters.

docs.title: Move “feat.” artists out of the artist field
docs.text: Uses filter, action group, regular expressions Works on any tag format Time 5 minutes, then one click each time Undo Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Guest artists are written into the ARTIST field, so your player lists Juniper Vale feat. Mira Solberg as an artist of its own, separate from Juniper Vale. You want the guest in the title instead, which is how most music databases and streaming services do it:

Before After ARTIST Juniper Vale feat. Mira Solberg Juniper Vale TITLE Paper Boats Paper Boats (feat. Mira Solberg) ARTIST Juniper Vale ft Kofi & the Tidewater Band Juniper Vale TITLE North Pier North Pier (feat. Kofi & the Tidewater Band) ARTIST Juniper Vale Juniper Vale (unchanged)

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
Try this on a copy of a few files first. Check the results before applying it to your library; use Edit → Undo in the same session to reverse the recorded changes. Keep the originals as a backup.

You'll find the affected files with the filter, then build an action group with two actions. Order matters: the title has to read the guest's name before the artist field loses it.

Find the files

  1. Show the filter with F3 and type:

    artist MATCHES "\s(feat\.?|ft\.?|featuring)\s"

  2. Only files with a guest in the artist field remain. Select them all (Cmd+A / Ctrl+A).

Create the action group

  1. Choose Actions → Actions… (Alt+6; Alt is ⌥ Option on a Mac).
  2. Create a new action group and name it Guests: artist → title.

  3. Add a Format value action:

    • Field: TITLE

    • Format string:

      %title% (feat. $regexp(%artist%,'^.*?\s+(?:feat\.?|ft\.?|featuring)\s+',))

  4. Add a Replace with regular expression action below it:

    • Field: ARTIST

    • Regular expression:

      \s+(feat\.?|ft\.?|featuring)\s+.*$

    • Replace matches with: leave it empty

    • Case-sensitive comparison: off

  5. Save the group, make sure only this group is checked, and run it.

The action group stays in the Actions menu. Next time, filter, select and pick it from the menu. Actions write immediately. If one action reports a warning for a file, its remaining actions and later checked groups still run. Review the warnings and the resulting fields before repeating a group.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The pattern (feat\.?|ft\.?|featuring) covers the common spellings: feat., feat, ft., ft and featuring. \.? makes the dot optional, and because case is ignored by default, Feat. and FT match too. \s on both sides requires whole words, so a name like Kraftwerk is safe.

Action 1 builds the new title from three parts:

Part Gives %title% Paper Boats (feat. plain text $regexp(%artist%,'^.*?\s+(?:feat\.?|ft\.?|featuring)\s+',) the artist with everything up to and including feat. removed: Mira Solberg ) plain text (outside a function, ) has no special meaning)

.*? is lazy: it takes as little as possible, so the match stops at the first feat.. The pattern and replacement are in single quotes because they contain characters that format strings treat specially. See Quote the pattern and the replacement.

Action 2 deletes everything from the first feat. to the end of the artist field. The action takes its pattern as plain text, so no quotes are needed here.

Why the filter comes first

$regexp returns its input unchanged when nothing matches. Run action 1 on a file without a guest, and its title becomes Low Tide (feat. Juniper Vale). The filter guarantees that every selected file has a guest. If you put the group on a toolbar for regular use, keep the filter step.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
Keep the guest as a second artist value instead

Some players handle multi-value artists well. Replace both actions with:

  1. Replace with regular expression on ARTIST: pattern \s+(feat\.?|ft\.?|featuring)\s+, replacement ;
  2. Split field by separator on ARTIST, separator ;

ARTIST then holds Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg as two values. Check that your player displays multiple artists as intended.

Use “ft.” or “with” in titles

Change the text in action 1, for example %title% (with $regexp(…)).

Guests that are already in brackets in the artist field

For Juniper Vale (feat. Mira Solberg), insert a Replace with regular expression action at the top of the group. Set Field to ARTIST, Regular expression to [()], and leave Replace matches with empty. This removes all round brackets from the artist field, so use it only on files where those brackets wrap the guest credit.

The complete group must run in this order; leave Case-sensitive comparison off for both replacement actions:

Order Action Field Pattern or format string Replacement 1 Replace with regular expression ARTIST [()] (empty) 2 Format value TITLE %title% (feat. $regexp(%artist%,'^.*?\s+(?:feat.?|ft.?|featuring)\s+',)) — 3 Replace with regular expression ARTIST \s+(feat.?|ft.?|featuring)\s+.*$ (empty)

Step 1 produces Juniper Vale feat. Mira Solberg. Step 2 then produces Paper Boats (feat. Mira Solberg), and step 3 leaves Juniper Vale in ARTIST. Putting bracket removal last cannot repair a closing bracket already copied into the title.

docs.title: Find files below a bitrate threshold
docs.text: Uses: Filter, %_bitrate%, numeric comparisons and an optional codec check. Works on: Loaded entries with technical information in the installed app. Time: About 5 minutes to inspect a small practice set. Undo: The filter writes nothing; clear it to show all loaded files.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
You want to review low-bitrate files without treating an unknown reading as a quality judgment. Bitrate is a rate of encoded data, not a listening test. Different codecs, source recordings and variable-rate encoding make a single cutoff a search aid rather than proof of quality. Use copied practice files before doing any later conversion or replacement.

These are invented technical snapshots, not measured tracks from the example album. Zero is included to show how an unavailable/zero reading affects the numeric query:

ID _BITRATE in kbps _CODEC A 128 MPEG-1 Layer III B 192 MPEG-1 Layer III C 320 MPEG-1 Layer III D 1411 PCM E 0 MPEG-1 Layer III F 128 AAC

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Load the files and review any read errors. Technical values must describe the loaded file, not a guessed value typed into an ordinary metadata field.
  2. Show the Filter with View → Show filter or F3.
  3. To find a positive measured rate below 192 kbps, enter:
"%_bitrate%" GREATER 0 AND "%_bitrate%" LESS 192
  1. Wait for automatic application, or press Enter when Auto-apply filter is disabled. A and F match the practice set. B is exactly 192, so it is outside this strictly lower-than threshold; E is zero and is excluded.
  2. Inspect a result's codec and technical details before deciding what it needs. A value of 128 for AAC is not an assertion of the same audible result as 128 for MPEG Layer III.
  3. Clear the query, then press Enter in manual mode, to restore the loaded list. No audio conversion or metadata save occurred.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
%_bitrate% supplies the loaded bitrate in kbps. Double quotes make the left operand a complete format-string selector. GREATER and LESS compare its leading integer with integer thresholds. AND requires both conditions. Type 192, not 192 kbps or a decimal threshold such as 191.5.

Scroll the table sideways on a narrow screen to read each complete query.

Query Matching IDs Why "%_bitrate%" LESS 192 A,E,F Zero is also less than 192. "%_bitrate%" GREATER 0 AND "%_bitrate%" LESS 192 A,F Positive readings below the cutoff. "%_bitrate%" EQUAL 192 B Exactly the boundary. "%_bitrate%" GREATER 0 AND "%_bitrate%" LESS 193 A,B,F Includes integer 192 as well. "%_codec%" IS "MPEG-1 Layer III" AND "%_bitrate%" GREATER 0 AND "%_bitrate%" LESS 192 A The positive low-rate MPEG subset.

The codec text is an exact example from OpenTag's MPEG-1 Layer III technical naming; inspect the actual %_codec% of other formats/versions instead of assuming their labels. A filename suffix alone does not prove the encoding. If a selector supplies no leading number, it does not satisfy a numeric comparison. An absent value and a displayed fallback zero can therefore produce different results; investigate the file rather than inventing a rate.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• Change the upper cutoff (192) when saving another search; keep GREATER 0 to exclude zero readings. “Below 192” excludes 192; for whole-number readings, < 193 includes it. The actual filter keywords remain LESS and EQUAL, not symbolic <.
  • Use the exact codec constraint when comparing like encodings. For a mixed library, inspect each codec family rather than applying one quality label to every result.
  • Search for "%_bitrate%" EQUAL 0 separately when investigating zero readings. A successful query with no matches is different from a file-read or filter syntax error.

Filtering does not select only its visible rows. Before a later write, rename or removal, Edit → Unselect all and deliberately select the desired results. Preserve pending tag edits intentionally before reloading files. A tag edit cannot recover information lost during lossy encoding; changing a metadata value or transcoding to a larger bitrate does not establish restored audio detail. The browser app preview has simpler substring search and is not a test of these installed filter expressions.

docs.title: Find files without embedded covers
docs.text: Uses: Filter and %_covers%. Works on: Loaded audio entries with cover information in the installed app. Time: About 5 minutes for a small copied album. Undo: Filtering writes nothing; clearing it restores the view.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
The cover window shows artwork, but you need to know which tracks actually carry an embedded image. A folder.jpg fallback can make a track look illustrated even when its embedded-cover count is zero. Use copied files before following the results with an import or removal operation.

This practice snapshot separates the count from the external image:

ID ALBUM _COVERS Folder image available A Harbour Lights 0 Yes B Harbour Lights 1 No C Harbour Lights 2 Yes D Harbour Sessions 0 No

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Load the copied album and wait for its entries to finish loading. Resolve any file-read errors instead of treating a failed read as proof of no art.
  2. Show the Filter using View → Show filter or F3.
  3. Enter:
"%_covers%" EQUAL 0
  1. Wait for automatic application, or press Enter if Auto-apply filter is disabled in the helper menu. A and D match the table above. A still matches when OpenTag can display its folder fallback.
  2. Select one result and inspect the cover window's label. Not embedded in the file explains a folder-image preview; it is not an embedded cover. For mixed selections, inspect individual files or Manage covers….
  3. Clear the filter to restore the list; press Enter in manual mode.

The query does not embed the available folder image. To do that deliberately, use Embed a folder image. Before any batch cover change, choose Edit → Unselect all, then select only the intended visible files. Hidden selected rows remain a separate selection concern.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
%_covers% is a computed information placeholder. In this recipe it counts embedded cover entries, not external images, distinct colors, pixels or front cover roles. The filter evaluates the quoted selector, then EQUAL compares its leading integer with zero.

Scroll the table sideways on a narrow screen to read each complete query.

Query Matching IDs Meaning "%_covers%" EQUAL 0 A,D No embedded cover entries. "%_covers%" GREATER 0 B,C At least one embedded cover entry. "%_covers%" GREATER 1 C More than one embedded entry. "%_covers%" EQUAL 0 AND ALBUM IS "Harbour Lights" A The missing-cover subset of this album.

A count of two does not prove that one is Front Cover and the other Back Cover, or that their image bytes differ. A nonzero count also does not prove that every embedded image can be decoded or that a receiving player supports its encoding. Conversely, lack of embedded art need not be a mistake: some collections intentionally use only folder images.

Do not use _COVERS MISSING to ask for zero covers. Zero is a supplied count, so a presence query asks a different question. Renaming a metadata field to _COVERS is not a way to embed artwork; information fields are derived from the loaded entry and its actual file measurements.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• Use the positive-count query to review files before removing oversized or unwanted artwork. Inspection does not mean all covers should be removed.
  • Add an album/artist constraint to work through one group at a time. Keep boolean grouping explicit when mixing AND and OR.
  • If a folder image should travel with every track, embed a tested copy in supported tag formats. If it should stay external, copy that image along with the audio files instead.

Direct cover-window mutations and cover actions have their own write paths; Manage covers… stages a plan until OK. A filter itself needs no tag undo. After a subsequent recorded edit, inspect Edit → Undo and retain original files/images for recovery beyond the session. Clearing a query does not reverse an import, removal or external extraction.

docs.title: Find files with missing fields
docs.text: Uses: Filter, MISSING, PRESENT, IS, optional scripting. Works on: Loaded files in the installed app's full filter engine. Time: About 5 minutes to inspect a small practice set. Undo: Filtering writes nothing; clear the query to restore the view.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
You want to find tracks without an album artist before filling it in. A blank-looking cell can mean no value, an empty string, or whitespace. Those are different states to the filter engine. Work on a copied practice set before using the results for a tagging operation.

This table describes evaluation snapshots, not a promise that a tag format will preserve every empty value when saved:

ID ALBUMARTIST values Meaning A Absent No field/value. B [""] One present empty string. C [" "] One present value containing three spaces. D ["Juniper Vale"] A useful credit. E ["Juniper Vale",""] A credit plus an empty second value.

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Load the files you want to inspect. Resolve pending edits deliberately: save them if they are intended, or discard them before investigating the saved tags. Filtering can use the current pending metadata snapshot.
  2. Choose View → Show filter, or press F3 when it is hidden.
  3. Enter this query:
ALBUMARTIST MISSING
  1. With Auto-apply filter enabled, wait for filtering to finish. If it is disabled in the helper menu, press Enter. In the example above, only A matches. Check No matching files versus Invalid filter; these are different outcomes.
  2. Inspect one result in Extended tags before deciding what value belongs there. A compilation does not necessarily want the first track's artist copied into every album-artist field.
  3. Clear the query to show the original loaded list. In manual mode, press Enter to apply the empty query.

Filtering changes visibility, not the selected-file set. Before any later write, choose Edit → Unselect all and deliberately select the intended visible rows. A selected file hidden by the filter can otherwise still be part of a batch operation.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
ALBUMARTIST names a field. MISSING asks whether it supplies no values. PRESENT asks the inverse; it does not require nonempty text. Write these keywords in uppercase. Field names themselves are case-insensitive.

Scroll the table sideways on a narrow screen to read each complete query.

Query Matching IDs ALBUMARTIST MISSING A ALBUMARTIST PRESENT B,C,D,E ALBUMARTIST IS "" B,E ALBUMARTIST MISSING OR ALBUMARTIST IS "" A,B,E "$trim(%albumartist%)" IS "" A,B,C

IS "" does not match three spaces. Also notice E: equality tests any value, so an empty second entry matches even when another entry contains a credit. A plain %albumartist% placeholder reads the first value, which explains why the last query does not match E. Choose the question that fits the cleanup; there is no universal “blank” test that silently means every one of these.

The final query encloses a format-string selector in double quotes. $trim calculates a result for comparison; it does not trim or save the field. Its whitespace rules are explained in Trim surrounding spaces.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
• Replace ALBUMARTIST with TITLE, ALBUM or another actual field name. Add OR between missing-field checks to find files missing either field; use AND when both must be absent.
  • Limit the task to one album with (ALBUMARTIST MISSING) AND ALBUM IS "Harbour Lights". Use the real loaded album value and quote a complete multiword operand.
  • Use ALBUMARTIST ABSENT as an equivalent spelling of MISSING. Prefer one convention in saved favorites so the intent stays clear.

A numeric zero is still a value, not a missing field. A tag reader/save path can also remove empty metadata rather than preserving this synthetic snapshot. Reload and inspect the actual saved result when investigating a container-specific issue. The browser-only app preview uses a simpler search; these expressions describe the installed backend's filter engine.

docs.title: Normalize title case and restore chosen exceptions
docs.text: Combine mechanical Mixed Case with a short, explicit exception policy. This recipe keeps DJ and EP uppercase and lowercases interior and and the when surrounded by spaces/tabs. It is a practice style, not an English grammar engine or a recognizer of every artist's preferred spelling.

docs.title: Inspect what the policy would do
docs.text:
Work on copied files with single-line title values. In the table, · marks an ordinary space; do not type that visible marker literally.

TITLE before TITLE after the complete group THE DJ AND THE SEA (EP) The DJ and the Sea (EP) ··DJ KOFI AND THE TIDEWATER BAND·· DJ Kofi and the Tidewater Band ADJACENT EPISODE Adjacent Episode THE END AND The End And AND THE TIDE And the Tide iOS AT THE HARBOUR Ios At the Harbour AC/DC LIVE Ac/dc Live

The last two show why review is essential. If iOS or AC/DC must keep that spelling, exclude those files or add a separately tested exception. This group's two acronym rules do not protect every brand or proper name.

Repair a confirmed encoding error before capitalization: changing the case of garbled surrogate characters can destroy clues to their original bytes. See mojibake repair. Do not put unrelated artist names, identifiers or URLs through this title policy with _TAG or _ALL.

docs.title: Build the ordered action group
docs.text:
1. Save or discard pending edits and select one copied practice file.
  2. Open Actions → Actions…, create Practice title case exceptions, and open Edit actions….
  3. Add the rows below. For every regex row, set Case-sensitive comparison to Off. For Mixed Case, Words begin after is the literal set (-_.
  4. Keep each action and the group, then Save groups.
  5. Check only this group and choose Apply checked groups. Compare the saved title and any operation errors before trying the remaining copies.
Step Action Field Pattern or case Replacement or word separators 1 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE \A[ \t]+ Leave empty 2 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE [ \t]+\z Leave empty 3 Case Conversion TITLE Mixed Case (-_ 4 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE \bDj\b DJ 5 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE \bEp\b EP 6 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE ([ \t])And(?=[ \t]) $1and 7 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE ([ \t])The(?=[ \t]) $1the

In the action boxes, patterns and replacements are entered directly, without format-string quotes. The two trim rows leave no unwanted edge spacing. They matter because the interior-word rules use surrounding whitespace to distinguish the first and last words from interior ones.

docs.title: Why this order works
docs.text:
Mixed Case lowercases the rest of each word and starts words after whitespace or a configured character. (-_ adds an opening parenthesis, hyphen and underscore as word starts. It is a character set, not a regex or an exception list. The first practice title becomes The Dj And The Sea (Ep) at this stage.

The following acronym rules restore exact whole words. \b prevents the Ep rule from changing the beginning of Episode, or the Dj rule from changing letters inside Adjacent.

For a small word, ([ \t]) captures its preceding space/tab. The lookahead (?=[ \t]) requires following whitespace without consuming it. $1and or $1the puts the leading whitespace back with the chosen lowercase word. First words have no leading whitespace after trimming, and last words have no following whitespace, so those words keep their capitals.

Putting Mixed Case after the exception rows would turn DJ back into Dj and EP back into Ep. A rule that depends on a previous result belongs after the action that creates that result.

docs.title: Add exceptions carefully
docs.text:
An acronym list is an editorial choice. Restore III, a specific place name or an unusual artist spelling only when that rule fits the selected material. Match whole words or an intentionally narrower context, not an unreviewed substring everywhere.

Words touching punctuation are not all handled by the whitespace-only small word rules. The group does not parse sentence structure or guarantee a house style for quotations and parentheses. Inspect those cases and keep them for manual editing when a general rule would alter meaning.

Every current value of TITLE is processed independently. A file with several title values retains a list rather than being reduced through a bare %title% placeholder. This does not override native format/value restrictions.

docs.title: Check writes and recovery
docs.text:
There is no full group dry-run in this recipe. The group writes when applied; Save groups only stores it. Use one copy, compare expected results, then expand the selection. An action warning does not stop later actions/groups, so inspect the full reported result before repeating the workflow.

Use Edit → Undo … for the recorded operation during the current desktop session, and keep original files for recovery beyond it. A capitalization rule cannot reliably reconstruct spelling that an earlier cleanup discarded.

docs.title: Repair a confirmed UTF-8 decoding mistake
docs.text: Repair text whose UTF-8 bytes were once read as legacy characters, such as MarÃ© Serena instead of Maré Serena. Choose the repair from evidence about the mistake, then test it on one copied file. The action cannot infer a language or recreate characters already replaced with ?.

docs.title: Recognize the byte path
docs.text:
The intended é has UTF-8 bytes C3 A9. Reading those bytes as Western legacy characters can produce the two visible characters Ã©. The repair recovers those byte values and decodes them as UTF-8 again.

That is why this case uses Unicode (UTF-8), codepage 65001: it names what the original bytes should have meant. It does not mean “save this tag using an arbitrary UTF-8 switch,” and it does not change the audio codec. A different original byte encoding needs its own diagnosis and codepage.

docs.title: Try one affected field
docs.text:
1. Keep an untouched original and select one copied practice file.
  2. Inspect Extended tags… and identify the affected field and values.
  3. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Convert Codepage.
  4. Use these settings and choose Apply action.
  5. Compare the resulting title with a known correct spelling and read any operation error before selecting more files.
Setting Value Field TITLE Codepage Unicode (UTF-8), 65001 TITLE before Result using codepage 65001 MarÃ© Serena Maré Serena Mira â€“ live Mira – live Harbour â™¥ Harbour ♥ North Pier North Pier Maré Serena Conversion error Mar� Serena Conversion error Mar? Serena Mar? Serena

The correctly accented title is intentionally an error case for this particular byte repair. Its characters do not encode a valid UTF-8 byte sequence through this reconstruction. An error is a reason to stop and inspect, not to try every encoding until one result looks plausible.

The last row remains readable ASCII but does not regain the lost accent. A previous replacement with ? or � can mean that the original character information is already gone. Compare an original backup or another reliable source instead of accepting a guessed name as an encoding conversion.

docs.title: Keep the repair narrowly targeted
docs.text:
The action processes every value of the chosen field. A field containing already-correct and incorrectly decoded text can refuse conversion; it is not a per-character language detector. For this action, unrepresentable characters or invalid byte sequences report an error rather than silently returning replacement glyphs.

Use TITLE first. _TAG includes all tag fields; _ALL also includes filenames, and _DIRECTORY targets a folder name. Those scopes can affect correct text and paths. They are unsuitable for an unconfirmed whole-library experiment.

The byte recovery accepts characters up to U+00FF directly and supported Windows-1252 glyphs such as the punctuation in the practice cases. It is not a universal inverse of every historical mis-decoding. More complicated multi-stage damage needs a separately tested diagnosis.

docs.title: Separate text repair from storage settings
docs.text:
Correcting a value does not choose ID3v2.3 versus ID3v2.4, change a sidecar file's encoding, or prove that a target player supports its eventual native tag. Review tag write options and text encodings for those separate choices.

$ansi evaluates with the application's ANSI context; it is not a replacement for selecting the known original byte encoding in this action. When importing new text, choose the correct source encoding instead of deliberately loading bad text and repairing it afterward.

docs.title: Check timing and avoid a second repair pass
docs.text:
The action writes immediately. Saving it in a group stores a workflow without running it; applying that group writes the selected files. Do not run the same repair again just because the spelling was corrected once—the corrected accented text can now fail this same conversion.

A warning from one action does not stop later actions/groups. Avoid appending case conversion or deletion until this repair has been inspected; those can make diagnosis harder or change other data after a repair warning. Use Edit → Undo … for a recorded write in the current desktop session, and retain the original file for recovery beyond it.

docs.title: Keep each file's front covers and remove the others
docs.text: Remove back/leaflet pictures while retaining the front artwork that already belongs to each file. Use Manage covers… to review the whole selection's cover list. A quick Remove-cover command on a varying selection can remove all artwork, which is not this task.

docs.title: Use role-aware practice files
docs.text:
Start with copied local MP3 files whose writable ID3v2 artwork roles have been checked. In this example, labels identify the picture contents for the exercise; they are not filenames the app must display:

Picture label Cover type Description front-A Front Cover Harbour front front-B Front Cover Low Tide front back Back Cover Rear booklet Leaflet Booklet

Use the role labels shown in the dialog, and inspect the actual pictures as well: a stored role can be wrong. The three practice files contain these lists:

File Pictures before Pictures after this cleanup Paper Boats.mp3 ["front-A","back"] ["front-A"] Evening Ferry.mp3 ["front-B","booklet"] ["front-B"] Archive.mp3 ["back"] []

The archive file has no Front Cover to keep, so removing its back picture leaves it without embedded art. Exclude such a file if that is unwanted. This recipe does not recognize a front image visually or invent a missing one.

docs.title: Remove only the unwanted cover rows
docs.text:
1. Save or discard pending edits and select the three copied audio files.
  2. Choose Edit → Manage covers… (Cmd+Alt+M on macOS; Ctrl+Alt+M on Windows/Linux).
  3. Inspect every listed cover's role, description, picture and membership. Cancel and resolve read errors before interpreting unavailable art as empty.
  4. Select the Back Cover and Leaflet rows for this exercise. Use Command/Ctrl-click to select separate rows, or Shift-click for a range; check the actual highlighted rows before removing them.
  5. Choose Remove inside Manage covers. Leave the two Front Cover rows.
  6. Inspect the remaining rows and choose OK only when the plan is right.
  7. Select each practice file separately and verify its saved artwork.

Remove edits the dialog's planned set. OK writes it to the audio files; Cancel before OK abandons this unconfirmed removal plan. It is not an ordinary text edit waiting for Save tags after OK. Inspect any per-file write errors.

docs.title: Preserve partial membership
docs.text:
A full circle ● means the same cover is present in every selected file. A partial circle ◐ means only some contain it. This describes membership, not quality or whether it is a front cover.

Remaining cover Membership without Apply to all front-A In 1 of 3 files front-B In 1 of 3 files

Leave Embed in all selected files unchanged/off for these partial rows. Merely keeping a partial cover retains it only where it was already present. Do not choose Apply to all just to turn the circle solid: applying front-A to all would add Harbour's front to Evening Ferry as well as to Archive. Evening Ferry would then have both front-A and its own front-B in this plan. That is a different, intentional redistribution task.

If several Front Cover rows belong to one file, this recipe keeps those front pictures, not necessarily exactly one picture. To keep only one, inspect that file alone and select the other front occurrence(s) for removal too. A picture role does not establish which scan or edition is correct.

docs.title: Respect formats without Front/Back roles
docs.text:
MP4 artwork does not retain Front/Back type and description distinctions; OpenTag normalizes it to Other. Do not remove every Other picture while expecting this role-based recipe to discover a front automatically. For such a file, inspect images individually and keep the chosen image by its content. Other tag formats can also restrict roles, descriptions or repeated pictures. See format capabilities.

A folder image can appear after embedded artwork is removed. Its Not embedded in the file label is not proof that the old cover survived or was restored. Use the embedded cover list and individual files to verify results.

docs.title: Recover a mistaken cleanup
docs.text: Before OK, Cancel abandons the plan. After a recorded write, inspect Edit → Undo … and its operation label in the current desktop session. Keep the original audio and images for recovery after quitting. A failed multi-file write can leave some files changed; check the operation errors before retrying or applying another cleanup.

docs.title: Import lyrics from .txt files
docs.text: Uses: Import Text File action · Works on: selected writable whole-file tracks with matching text sidecars · Time: about 5 minutes for a practice pair · Undo: recorded tag writes in the current desktop session; keep originals

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
You have written lyrics in separate text files and want to embed the text in each corresponding audio file. A sidecar is a separate file kept beside the audio; importing it copies its current contents into a tag field. It does not create an ongoing link to the text file.

Audio file Text file beside it Destination 01 - Paper Boats.flac 01 - Paper Boats.txt That audio file's LYRICS field 02 - Lanterns on the Water.flac 02 - Lanterns on the Water.txt That audio file's LYRICS field

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Work on copies of these two audio files. Save pending edits and keep copies of any existing lyrics you want to retain.

  2. Create the matching .txt files as UTF-8 text. Put this invented practice text in 01 - Paper Boats.txt:

    Paper boats drift past the pier.
We keep a lantern burning here.

    Give the second sidecar different practice text, so a wrong association is visible. Check the actual extension: 01 - Paper Boats.txt.txt does not have the name this recipe expects.

  3. Select the two copied audio files. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)… and select Import Text File.

  4. Set Field to LYRICS. Set Text filename format to:

    %_filename%.txt

  5. Choose Apply action. This writes immediately. Read the result and any per-file errors; there is no separate reviewed text-import preview in this action.

  6. Select each file separately and open Extended tags…. Check that LYRICS contains that file's complete text, with the intended line breaks and accents. Check the player afterward if displaying embedded lyrics is your goal; field storage alone does not prove player support.

The action replaces all previous values of LYRICS with one value. It does not append a verse. An empty sidecar supplies empty text and can replace existing lyrics. Use a small copied selection before a larger run.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
%_filename% is the audio filename without its extension. Appending .txt gives the matching sidecar name. The format is evaluated separately for every selected file, and a relative result is read from that file's folder.

Audio basename Evaluated text filename 01 - Paper Boats.flac 01 - Paper Boats.txt 02 - Lanterns on the Water.mp3 02 - Lanterns on the Water.txt 03 - Café.ogg 03 - Café.txt

The complete decoded file becomes one field value. Individual lines do not map to individual tracks, and punctuation is not treated as a separator. Spaces, blank lines and a final line ending belong to the imported text. Changing the sidecar afterward does not change the embedded value; rerun the action when you intentionally want to replace it.

This uses a filename format, so normal tag-derived names have reserved characters cleaned according to filename rules. Basing the sidecar on the actual %_filename% avoids relying on a title that differs from the file's name. Use an exact name, including .txt; *.txt is not a wildcard search.

docs.title: Use one notes file for the whole folder
docs.text:
Set Field to COMMENT and Text filename format to notes.txt. Every selected track reads the notes.txt in its own folder. This is useful for album recording notes, but it deliberately gives the same text to all selected tracks in that folder. It also replaces existing comments.

An absolute filename reads that same file for every selected track, regardless of their folders. Browse… can select such a file; inspect the resulting format before applying it to several tracks.

docs.title: Keep sidecars in a lyrics subfolder
docs.text:
Use this when a Lyrics subfolder exists beside every selected track:

Lyrics\%_filename%.txt

The literal backslash separates folders in filename formats on supported desktop platforms. Each text file must already exist. Importing does not create sidecars, search other folders or download missing lyrics.

docs.title: Import an older text encoding
docs.text: Use UTF-8 for new files. A Unicode byte-order mark selects its decoding; without a BOM, valid UTF-8 is used first. Otherwise the configured ANSI/system codepage is used, with Windows-1252 when none is available. Unlike Text File → Tag, this action has no per-import legacy-encoding box. Convert a copy of an older sidecar to known UTF-8 in a suitable text editor before importing, then inspect accents and symbols in one test track.

docs.title: If the result is missing or wrong
docs.text:
Symptom What to inspect A file reports that the text could not be read Check the exact basename, extension, folder, case and read permission All selected tracks receive the same lyrics Look for an absolute filename or a constant lyrics.txt shared in one folder Existing lyrics disappeared The import replaces values; use recorded Edit → Undo or your original copy Text is garbled Check the source encoding before repeating the write The player shows no lyrics Verify the embedded field in OpenTag first, then that player's format/lyrics support

A missing or unreadable sidecar reports an error for that operation; it is not an instruction to clear the field or to retry later. Action processing can continue with later work. Do not put a destructive “cleanup” action after the import on the assumption that every sidecar was read successfully. Keep this practice action alone until you have checked its results.

Timestamped text imported this way remains text in one field. The action does not interpret timing markers, synchronize playback, or verify that a player will treat the field as timed lyrics.

docs.title: Number tracks separately in each folder
docs.text: Give each album folder its own sequence, starting at 01. The per-folder shortcut can also store each contiguous run's final number as its total. It uses the selected files' current list order, not filename guessing or an audio-based track-order lookup.

docs.title: Arrange and select the intended tracks
docs.text:
Work on copied local files. Sort or manually arrange them so each folder's tracks are together and each track is in the intended playing order. Select every file that belongs in the run. The numbers below illustrate five files in this order:

File in list order Existing TRACK Pending TRACK after staging /Practice/Harbour Lights/Paper Boats.mp3 9 01/3 /Practice/Harbour Lights/North Pier.mp3 4 02/3 /Practice/Harbour Lights/Quiet Harbour.mp3 7 03/3 /Practice/Low Tide/Evening Ferry.mp3 8 01/2 /Practice/Low Tide/Lantern Wake.mp3 2 02/2

The paths illustrate folders, not paths to create verbatim. On Windows, use the files' actual drive/folder paths. Existing track values do not decide the new order: this example intentionally starts with inconsistent numbers.

docs.title: Open the per-folder run
docs.text:
1. Save or discard existing pending edits and check the selected count.
  2. Press ⌘+Shift+K on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+K on Windows/Linux to open the per-folder Auto-numbering run for local files.
  3. Set the controls below. Check both field-change controls even if this is a familiar wizard: remembered settings can otherwise introduce resets.
  4. Choose Preview and inspect the first and last row of each folder.
  5. Choose Stage numbers, inspect the pending tags, then File → Save tags.
Control Value Begin at track 1 Minimum digits under Track numbers 2 Save total track count On Disc numbers Off Next disc on change of directory On Next disc on change of field Do not change counter Reset track counter on next disc On Reset disc counter on change of field Do not change counter

The shortcut presets directory transitions, track resets and no disc writing. This can restart tracks without changing an existing DISCNUMBER. With Save total track count on in this shortcut mode, the entered Total tracks box is disabled: the run determines the total.

Stage numbers is not a disk write. Discard the selected files' pending changes if the sequence is wrong, or rerun a reviewed preview before saving. An enabled selection-change saving preference can write pending values when moving on; review saving behavior.

docs.title: Understand what “total” counts
docs.text:
The total is the last track number assigned before the counter restarts, not always the number of selected files. Each example here is a separate run in one folder with the same width/total settings:

Begin at track Selected files First result Last result 1 3 01/3 03/3 5 3 05/7 07/7 1 1 01/1 01/1

A single selected bonus track does not inherit a twelve-track album's total. A start of 5 with three selected tracks ends at 7. If an entered fixed total is required, use the regular Convert → Auto-numbering… dialog and review its total separately; recreating its directory/reset switches does not enable the shortcut's per-run total mode.

docs.title: Check folder boundaries and order
docs.text:
Grouping detects a change between adjacent selected files. It does not first collect all equal folder paths. An order of Harbour, Low Tide, Harbour creates three counter runs. The last Harbour item can therefore restart at 01 with total 1 even though other Harbour files occurred earlier. For example:

File in list order Pending TRACK /Practice/Harbour Lights/Paper Boats.mp3 01/1 /Practice/Low Tide/Evening Ferry.mp3 01/1 /Practice/Harbour Lights/North Pier.mp3 01/1

A filter or partial selection can omit tracks from a run. Preview shows at most 100 rows while the plan covers the selection; use smaller batches when an important boundary is beyond those visible rows. Changing selection or settings invalidates the previous preview; run Preview again.

Local folder grouping requires known local paths. Provider-backed documents without those paths cannot use the directory control. Use the supported regular grouping workflow or number each intended album selection separately. Do not infer provider rename or full action support from this wizard.

docs.title: Check storage and recovery
docs.text:
Numbering updates metadata, not filenames. Some formats store track/disc components as integers and can lose leading-zero padding on read-back. For padded filenames, use $num(%track%,2) in a separate reviewed Tag → Filename conversion.

After saving, inspect errors and the saved tags. A partial failure can leave some numbers pending. Use Edit → Undo … for recorded saved changes in the current desktop session, and keep the original files for recovery afterward.

docs.title: Write one playlist in each album folder
docs.text:
Uses: Generate playlists, folder-path partitioning and M3U8 output.

Works on: Copied ordinary local audio files already organized into album folders.

Time: About 10 minutes for two practice albums.

Undo: Playlists are external outputs written on OK. Keep existing lists and clean up practice outputs deliberately; tag undo is not a playlist backup.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Your visible list spans two album folders. You want a separate playlist in each folder, with tracks following their current list order. Equal album titles alone are not a reliable partition: different releases or locations can share a title. This recipe groups by containing folder.

Keep originals, save intended tag edits, and use fresh practice output names. Return to whole audio-file rows before starting; chapter/CUE-track rows are not independent playlist files. Clear a filter if hidden tracks should be included, and arrange the file-list order deliberately.

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Load two copied album folders. For this example, the visible rows have this order. Paths below are relative to a common practice root:

    Order Folder File Disc 1 Harbour Lights 01 - Paper Boats.wav 1 2 Harbour Sessions 01 - North Pier.wav 1 3 Harbour Lights 02 - Low Tide.wav 2

  2. Choose Edit → Unselect all if the generator should use the whole visible list. Otherwise, select exactly the subset wanted: a nonempty selection takes precedence over all-visible scope.

  3. Choose File → Generate playlists…. Set Partition format to:

    %_folderpath%

  4. Set Playlist file name to:

    %_folderpath%listening.m3u8

  5. Inspect the live preview. It should show two playlists; the full output paths end in the following relative names:

    Playlist Members in their playlist order Harbour Lights/listening.m3u8 01 - Paper Boats.wav, 02 - Low Tide.wav Harbour Sessions/listening.m3u8 01 - North Pier.wav

  6. Check that the outputs are new practice names in the intended folders, rather than audio files or existing valuable playlists. Review playlist options for extended labels, relative entries and BOM.

  7. Choose OK to write. Read errors, inspect each output and load a playlist back. No later Save tags step creates these external files.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
%_folderpath% supplies a path including its trailing separator. Identical partition results group files together even when another folder's row appears between them in the list. The generator keeps each group's relative list order; it does not sort the filenames or track tags independently.

The filename format is evaluated against the group's first readable file. Here its folder path plus the literal listening.m3u8 gives a distinct output inside each folder. The grouping key and filename are separate decisions: changing the partition alone does not automatically make output names unique. The .m3u8 suffix chooses UTF-8 M3U output, not a copy of the audio.

The preview displays the total and at most its first 50 output paths. Changing inputs updates that planning display; OK performs the current write request. It is not a reservation of filesystem names. A later error is not proof that no earlier output was written. Keep the original lists and inspect actual results without assuming universal alias/overwrite protection.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
File → Playlist per folder (all files) is a direct alternative for the current visible whole-file list. It uses the configured Filename of playlist from Playlist options without individual filename-confirmation dialogs. A relative configured name is resolved inside each group's folder; an absolute name overrides that base and can cause different groups to share one output name. Check the configuration before using this direct command. Its shortcut is Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P; this shortcut invokes the per-folder command in OpenTag, not the generator dialog. Try the previewed recipe first when destinations are unfamiliar.

For one list per disc within each folder, use these two coordinated formats:

%_folderpath%-%discnumber%

%_folderpath%disc-$num(%discnumber%,2).m3u8

For the three practice rows, expect:

Source row Relative disc playlist 1 Harbour Lights/disc-01.m3u8 2 Harbour Sessions/disc-01.m3u8 3 Harbour Lights/disc-02.m3u8

Check disc tags first: a missing/nonnumeric disc can create an unintended disc-00 name. Two distinct partition values can still converge on one filename if their numeric formatting discards differences.

For an action-group workflow, use Generate Playlists. It includes selected files and executes after that group's per-file actions, so preceding renames/field changes can affect the playlist. A recipe that needs an earlier intermediate state should use a separate group.

docs.title: If a playlist is incomplete or in the wrong place
docs.text:
• Check selected versus visible scope, the active filter and ordinary-file versus chapter rows. The generator does not scan every unlisted file in a folder just because one listed track came from it.
  • Check actual list order and readable-file errors. A count of selected paths does not prove every file was read successfully.
  • Relative output names without %_folderpath% use the working-directory context. This recipe makes each target explicit with its folder placeholder.
  • Relative entries are calculated from each output's folder, subject to the configured working root and filesystem roots. Test after moving an album with its playlist as a unit; moving the audio independently can break it.
  • Don't create directories requires existing parent folders; turning it off is not permission to overwrite valuable files.

docs.title: Keep a reviewed field list on a cleanup copy
docs.text: Use Remove Fields Except when the remaining field set is known and every other exposed field should be removed. Build the list from the actual files; OpenTag does not decide which identifiers, comments or custom fields are junk. Use Remove Fields instead when only a few unwanted names are known.

docs.title: Inventory a copied file first
docs.text:
Open Extended tags… on a copied practice file and note the fields that must survive. Include values needed by the intended player or library: identifiers, sort names, original dates, lyrics, ReplayGain and totals can all be useful metadata.

The example below keeps core album data and one chosen identifier, and intentionally drops the shown comment and encoder annotation. It is a practice policy for that known copy, not a universal master-library cleanup.

docs.title: Enter an explicit keep list
docs.text:
1. Save or discard pending edits and select one copied practice file.
  2. Choose Actions → Actions (Quick)…, then Remove Fields Except.
  3. In Keep fields (separate with semicolons), enter the following list.
  4. Review it against the full field inventory before choosing Apply action.
  5. Inspect Extended tags…, embedded pictures and any operation errors.
TITLE;ARTIST;ALBUM;ALBUMARTIST;YEAR;DATE;TRACK;TRACKNUMBER;TRACKTOTAL;TOTALTRACKS;DISCNUMBER;TOTALDISCS;GENRE;MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID;PICTURE

These are literal names, not format strings. Do not add percent signs or patterns such as MUSICBRAINZ_*. Each needed field must be named explicitly. The action keeps a named field only when it already exists; it does not create missing album artists or empty date fields.

The list includes several date/track spellings because native formats or custom mappings can expose related data under different names. Inspect the actual selection rather than assuming aliases are universally interchangeable. For MP4, keep native total fields when the total is wanted: TOTALTRACKS and TOTALDISCS share native pairs with their current-number fields. A custom TRACKTOTAL field is a separate choice.

docs.title: Compare the practice inventory
docs.text:
Each row is one value in the copied file before the action. The kept names retain their existing values; the other two fields disappear from the editing model.

Field before Value before Kept by the example list TITLE Paper Boats Yes ARTIST Juniper Vale Yes ALBUM Harbour Lights Yes TRACK 3/8 Yes TOTALTRACKS 8 Yes DISCNUMBER 1/2 Yes TOTALDISCS 2 Yes YEAR 2024 Yes MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555 Yes COMMENT Practice-only note No ENCODEDBY Old test encoder No

If an unlisted lyrics, rating, original-date or ReplayGain field is needed, add its actual name before running the action. A successful run is not proof that the chosen policy was appropriate.

docs.title: Preserve artwork deliberately
docs.text:
PICTURE in this action is an artwork selector. COVER is an alternative. It preserves embedded pictures; it does not refer to folder.jpg or rename an image file. Without either selector, the action also removes embedded artwork.

The following effects use the practice inventory above.

Keep list Metadata result Artwork request TITLE;ARTIST;PICTURE Keep TITLE and ARTIST only Keep embedded pictures TITLE;ARTIST Keep TITLE and ARTIST only Remove embedded pictures COVER Remove all exposed tag fields Keep embedded pictures Leave empty Remove all exposed tag fields Remove embedded pictures

An empty keep list is a destructive operation, not “leave everything alone.” A folder-image fallback can appear after artwork removal; check the Not embedded in the file label rather than interpreting the visible picture as proof that embedded art survived.

docs.title: Check native storage and write timing
docs.text:
The action operates on exposed fields and artwork. It is not a general container-data eraser: opaque or unsupported structures have format-specific preservation/removal rules. Native writers also have their own field mappings and tag-type policies. Read back the file and inspect the supported format limits after applying a cleanup copy.

The action writes when run; it does not wait for Save tags. A stored group is only a workflow until applied. Start with one copy, inspect what remained, then expand the selection only when the policy is confirmed. An action warning does not stop later actions/groups, and a batch can partly succeed. Read every reported file result before repeating it.

Use Edit → Undo … for a recorded change in the current desktop session. Keep original files and wanted metadata outside that session's history. A later metadata field cannot restore information that the cleanup discarded.

docs.title: Remove a trailing remaster annotation
docs.text: Remove a known Remastered suffix while retaining parentheses that belong to a title. A rule that deletes every bracketed phrase would also remove useful information such as (Live) or part of a work's name.

docs.title: Start with known practice titles
docs.text:
Each row below starts from a separate copied file with one title value. The recipe accepts parentheses or square brackets around Remastered, optionally followed by a space and a four-digit year. Matching ignores case. ↵ represents a line break within one title value.

TITLE before TITLE after Paper Boats (Remastered 2021) Paper Boats North Pier [remastered] North Pier Quiet Harbour (Live) Quiet Harbour (Live) Remastered Memories Remastered Memories Paper Boats (Remastered edition) Paper Boats (Remastered edition) Quiet Harbour (Part (One)) Quiet Harbour (Part (One)) Paper Boats (Remastered 2021)↵Notes Paper Boats (Remastered 2021)↵Notes

The last five are intentional nonmatches. Inspect a sample of the titles that should stay unchanged as well as those that should change.

docs.title: Build the two-action group
docs.text:
1. Save or discard pending edits and select one copied practice file.
  2. Open Actions → Actions…, create Practice remove remaster suffix, and open Edit actions….
  3. Add these rows in order. Set Case-sensitive comparison to Off in both regex actions. Leave the replacement box completely empty.
  4. Keep the actions and group, then Save groups.
  5. Check only this group and choose Apply checked groups. Inspect the saved title before trying the remaining practice copies.
Step Action Field / source Pattern / format / separator Replacement / option 1 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE [ \t]*\(Remastered(?: [0-9]{4})?\)\z Leave empty 2 Replace with Regular Expression TITLE [ \t]*\[Remastered(?: [0-9]{4})?\]\z Leave empty

Type the pattern directly in the action's regex box, without wrapping it in format-string quotes. A regex action's replacement box is also literal: '' would insert apostrophes rather than requesting an empty replacement.

docs.title: Understand what the patterns permit
docs.text:
• [ \t]* includes spaces/tabs immediately before the annotation, so the deletion does not leave an extra trailing space.
  • \( and \) match literal parentheses. The second row uses \[ and \] for literal square brackets; the pairs must match.
  • Remastered is the exact annotation word, with case ignored by the setting.
  • (?: [0-9]{4})? allows either nothing or one space followed by exactly four digits. (?:…) groups those pieces without a capture number.
  • \z restricts the annotation to the end of the whole value, including values containing a line break. $ would also match at line ends here. Remastered Memories therefore does not match the suffix pattern.

Normalize unwanted trailing spaces first with the spacing recipe, or a space after the closing bracket can prevent this end-anchored match. These are two ordered replacements, not a repeated “remove all annotations” loop. For example, removing a final parenthesized annotation can expose a square-bracketed one for the next row; two consecutive parenthesized suffixes need a separate decision before repeating the group.

docs.title: When removing any parenthesized suffix is intended
docs.text:
For a carefully reviewed selection, a broader pattern is:

Pattern Input Result [ \t]*\([^()]*\)\z Paper Boats (Live) Paper Boats [ \t]*\([^()]*\)\z Quiet Harbour (Part (One)) Quiet Harbour (Part (One)) [ \t]*\([^()]*\)\z Paper Boats (Remastered 2021)↵Notes Paper Boats (Remastered 2021)↵Notes

Use this as a separate regex action with an empty replacement, not as a silent substitute for the remaster rule. [^()]* permits characters other than parentheses, so it does not parse nested parentheses. A broad .* can instead span from an earlier opening bracket to the final closing one and remove more of the title than expected.

docs.title: Verify and recover
docs.text:
A regex action runs immediately; there is no full-group dry-run preview in this recipe. Start with one copy, compare the before/after title, and check warnings. A no-match file remains unchanged by these replacements. An annotation-only title can leave no useful title; inspect those cases before using a cleaned value to rename files.

Use Edit → Undo … promptly for a recorded action write. History belongs to the current desktop session; a file backup remains the recovery route beyond it. Do not combine this cleanup with a destructive field-removal action until its intermediate result has been reviewed.

docs.title: Keep compilation tracks together when renaming
docs.text:
Uses: Tag → Filename, ALBUMARTIST fallback and explicit track credits.

Works on: Copied local album tracks with reviewed artist/album metadata.

Time: About 10 minutes for a small compilation.

Undo: Apply changes paths immediately; inspect recorded session Edit → Undo and retain untouched copies.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
A compilation has a common album title but different artists on its tracks. An outer %artist% folder can scatter those tracks across several folders. Choose an album-level folder credit while retaining each track's own artist in the filename. A compilation flag and an album-artist credit are separate fields; one does not automatically supply the other.

Use copies, check the selection and resolve pending tag edits first. This practice album is Harbour Sessions. Where it represents your intended credit policy, give all its tracks ALBUMARTIST = Various Artists while keeping their different ARTIST values. That text is a chosen credit, not a special command or a guarantee about player grouping.

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Inspect and deliberately save the chosen ALBUMARTIST, ARTIST, ALBUM, TRACK and TITLE values on the copied album. Do not change credits just to force a filename convention without deciding what those fields mean.
  2. Select the intended copies. Hidden selected rows can remain in a batch, so use Edit → Unselect all first if the active filter obscures scope.
  3. Choose Convert → Tag → Filename… (Alt+1; Alt is ⌥ Option on macOS).

  4. Enter:

    $if2(%albumartist%,%artist%)\%album%\$num(%track%,2) - %artist% - %title%

  5. Choose Preview. All rows below use ALBUM = Harbour Sessions. Relative paths resolve under each source file's current containing folder; / shows folder levels. The rows without album artist demonstrate fallback splitting even when COMPILATION is set.

    Scroll the table sideways on a narrow screen to read the complete destinations.

    Artist Album artist Compilation Track Title Source name Relative destination Juniper Vale Various Artists 1 1 Paper Boats old.mp3 Various Artists/Harbour Sessions/01 - Juniper Vale - Paper Boats.mp3 Mira Solberg Various Artists 1 2 Low Tide old.mp3 Various Artists/Harbour Sessions/02 - Mira Solberg - Low Tide.mp3 Juniper Vale Absent 1 1 Paper Boats old.mp3 Juniper Vale/Harbour Sessions/01 - Juniper Vale - Paper Boats.mp3 Mira Solberg Absent 1 2 Low Tide old.mp3 Mira Solberg/Harbour Sessions/02 - Mira Solberg - Low Tide.mp3 Mira Solberg Various Artists Absent 2 Low Tide old.flac Various Artists/Harbour Sessions/02 - Mira Solberg - Low Tide.flac

  6. Verify the common album folder, individual filenames, source extension, destination root and existing destination contents. Correct any missing album/artist/title data or repeated names before applying.

  7. Choose Apply to … files for the checked practice plan. Inspect the results and errors. The converter changes paths immediately and leaves metadata credits as supplied; it does not need a second Save tags step.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
$if2(%albumartist%,%artist%) chooses the first album-artist value when it contributes text. If it does not, the first track artist becomes the outer folder. It is a per-file fallback, so a compilation with missing album artists can split exactly as the third and fourth rows show.

The rest of the format creates the album folder, a padded track number and an explicit track credit/title. COMPILATION does not appear in this format, so changing that flag does not change these calculated destinations. In its constrained ID3/MP4 representations, enable the flag with 1 or remove it; see sort fields and compilations before editing.

A field with several values contributes its first value to a plain placeholder. Do not expect the filename to list every artist unless you deliberately choose and test an explicit join. Slashes inside ordinary values use the configured folder-separator replacement; literal separators in the format create folders.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
If you want one fixed outer folder independent of any album-artist spelling, use this complete alternative after checking that the whole selection belongs there:

Compilations\%album%\$num(%track%,2) - %artist% - %title%

The first practice row becomes

Compilations/Harbour Sessions/01 - Juniper Vale - Paper Boats.mp3. This literal path policy does not write a compilation flag or album artist.

For a multi-disc compilation, retain disc identity too:

$if2(%albumartist%,%artist%)\%album%\CD$num(%discnumber%,2)\$num(%track%,2) - %artist% - %title%

With the first practice row and DISCNUMBER = 2/2, expect

Various Artists/Harbour Sessions/CD02/01 - Juniper Vale - Paper Boats.mp3. Check disc tags first: missing/nonnumeric values can produce CD00. The multi-disc recipe explains optional disc folders.

docs.title: Recovery and common mistakes
docs.text:
All tracks sharing this relative format only meet in one destination when their starting roots also suit that plan. Files from different source folders can create parallel layouts; choose a real absolute archive root deliberately when consolidation is intended. Reapplying a relative expression after a move can nest the same hierarchy again.

A numbered filename is not proof of correct album order. $num reads each stored track; it does not run auto-numbering or infer totals. Identical metadata can produce identical target names. Inspect the preview and actual folder contents without assuming every filesystem alias or collision is covered by one naming convention.

Sidecar art, playlists and old empty folders are separate from this audio-file move. Check Keep moved files when an entry leaves the list. Review any partial operation errors, inspect recorded Edit → Undo while available, and keep originals for recovery if paths later become occupied.

  • Multi-disc layout
  • Multi-value fields

docs.title: Move tracks into artist and album folders
docs.text:
Uses: Tag → Filename, optional year text and padded track numbers.

Works on: Copied local audio files with checked artist, album and title tags.

Time: About 10 minutes for a small album.

Undo: Apply changes paths immediately; inspect recorded Edit → Undo in the same desktop session and keep originals.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Your copied tracks sit together in an incoming folder. You want an artist folder, an album folder and numbered filenames. This recipe builds each relative destination under that track's current containing folder. It does not gather files from several source folders into one archive automatically.

Check the tags first. Keep originals outside the practice folder, resolve pending edits deliberately, and choose an album with useful ARTIST, ALBUM, TRACK and TITLE values. The optional YEAR can be absent.

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
1. Select only the practice audio files. If a filter is active, inspect the selection count; hidden selected files can still belong to an operation.
  2. Choose Convert → Tag → Filename… (Alt+1; Alt is ⌥ Option on macOS).

  3. Enter this Format string, without adding an audio extension:

    %artist%\%album%[ (%year%)]\$num(%track%,2) - %title%

  4. Choose Preview. Check the full destination, including the root, every folder and the final filename. The following paths are relative to each input's containing folder; / shows folder levels for readability.

    Scroll the table sideways on a narrow screen to read the complete destinations.

    Artist Album Year Track Title Source name Relative destination Juniper Vale Harbour Lights 2024 3/8 Paper Boats old.mp3 Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights (2024)/03 - Paper Boats.mp3 Juniper Vale Harbour Lights Absent 3 Paper Boats old.mp3 Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/03 - Paper Boats.mp3 Kofi/Mira Harbour Lights 2024 3 Paper Boats old.mp3 Kofi_Mira/Harbour Lights (2024)/03 - Paper Boats.mp3 Juniper Vale Harbour Lights 2024 3 Low Tide: Dawn old.mp3 Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights (2024)/03 - Low Tide_ Dawn.mp3 Juniper Vale Harbour Lights 2024 100 Last Harbour old.flac Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights (2024)/100 - Last Harbour.flac

  5. Inspect the destination folders in the file manager if they already exist. Ensure your intended names are distinct and account for existing files. A preview is not a reservation or a guarantee about every filesystem alias.

  6. When the small practice plan is correct, choose Apply to … files. The audio files move/rename immediately; no second Save tags step is needed for the paths. Inspect operation errors and the saved destinations.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• %artist% supplies the artist folder. A literal backslash in the expression starts the next folder on all supported desktop platforms.
  • %album%[ (%year%)] keeps the album, adding a space and parenthesized year only when the year field contributes a value. An absent year does not leave empty parentheses.
  • $num(%track%,2) reads the leading track number and pads to at least two digits. It turns 3/8 into 03 and leaves 100 at three digits; it does not preserve a vinyl-side label such as B2.
  • %title% supplies the final title text. The host retains the source audio extension. A FLAC input remains a FLAC file; this is not audio conversion.

A separator inside a tag value does not create the literal folder level: with the default replacement, Kofi/Mira becomes Kofi_Mira. The setting is Options → Files → Replace folder separator in tag values with. Other forbidden value characters such as the example colon become underscores. These rules do not certify that every generated component is suitable for every target filesystem, network share or device. Preview and test the actual destination.

Required empty fields need attention before applying. A missing artist can leave a leading separator and change the destination root: stop and correct that field rather than applying the unexpected path. A missing album can leave an empty component, or only the optional year suffix when YEAR is present. A missing title can produce an incomplete name, and a missing/nonnumeric track can become 00. Do not treat a syntactically valid format string as proof of correct metadata.

docs.title: Variations
docs.text:
For an artist folder based on album credit, use this expression only after checking the album artist policy for the selection:

$if2(%albumartist%,%artist%)\%album%[ (%year%)]\$num(%track%,2) - %title%

$if2 uses the album artist when present, otherwise the first track artist. With album artist Various Artists and the first practice row's other values, the relative destination is Various Artists/Harbour Lights (2024)/03 - Paper Boats.mp3. The compilation recipe explains why per-track fallback can split one album across several artist folders.

To use a shared archive root, prepend the intended absolute root and preview it on that platform. A Windows drive path is not a portable absolute path on macOS/Linux. Choose a real writable location; do not copy another machine's root blindly. A complete date in YEAR remains a complete date here; use the year-only recipe if a deliberate extraction is needed.

Reapplying this relative expression after moving files can nest the structure again under their new folders. It does not promise to move sidecar pictures, playlists or text files, or to remove old empty folders. Keep moved files controls whether moved entries remain listed. Undo can meet newly occupied paths, so verify the result and retain originals beyond the session.
