docs.title: The main window
docs.text:
Use the main window to answer three questions before changing files: what is loaded, what is selected, and what still needs saving. The tag panel and the file list show the same files from different angles; neither is a permanent backup of the metadata on disk.

Desktop orientation example from the existing reviewed screenshot set. Configured columns, toolbars, placement and platform controls can differ.

docs.title: Find each part
docs.text:
Area What to look for What it means for your work Menu bar File, Edit, View, Convert, Actions, Tag Sources, Tools, Help Find named commands even when a toolbar button is hidden Toolbars Main buttons and optional custom buttons Shortcuts to operations; a disabled icon can have a reason Location strip Current location and loaded-file count How many entries are in the workspace, including rows hidden by a filter Tag panel Fields such as Title, Artist, Album, plus cover controls Values for the selected files; differing fields can show < keep > File list One row per loaded file or expanded chapter Select targets, inspect columns, sort and edit supported cells Filter Text box and visible/selected counts Restrict the visible rows without assuming hidden selections disappear Selection summary below the list Selected duration/size, listed totals and single-file technical details Compare the intended selection with the visible list; filtered totals describe listed files Status/footer Operation message, progress, unsaved-file count Inspect the result and whether pending edits remain File-error area Individual paths, messages and Dismiss Investigate each failed file; dismissing only clears the displayed errors

The title area's Local files, Provider documents or Browser preview mode identifies the access environment. A familiar-looking window does not make every command available in every mode.

docs.title: Loaded, visible, selected and unsaved are different
docs.text:
A filter changes visibility. Selection determines targets for selected-file commands. Pending edits record changes still waiting to be saved. These are independent states: a hidden row can remain selected, and an unselected row can still have pending edits.

The count beside the filter illustrates this distinction:

Loaded rows Visible rows Selected rows Filter-area count text While filtering 8 8 1 1 selected Filtering… · 1 selected 8 3 2 3 visible · 2 selected Filtering… · 2 selected

The second line does not tell you which two rows are selected. One could be hidden. Clear the filter and inspect/reselect the intended files before a batch write. The unsaved-file count covers the loaded workspace; saving one selection does not necessarily clear all pending edits.

While a filter is being evaluated, the count shows Filtering… and the selected count; the visible count returns after evaluation. An invalid filter is different from a valid query with no matches. Use the filter guide for expressions and error handling. F3 hides a shown filter and clears its applied restriction; showing it again restores the remembered text. It does not delete any audio files.

docs.title: Read and edit a selection
docs.text:
Select one row to inspect its fields. Select several only when a change is intended for all of them. A shared value appears in the tag panel; differing values can show < keep >. Leaving that state alone preserves the different values. Replacing it assigns the new value across the selection, and clearing a field requests removal.

A column can show a stored field, a calculated expression or a technical property. Seeing text in a column does not mean that cell is writable. Filename/path editing changes a filesystem name, while Title changes metadata. Read The file list before using F2 or custom columns. Use Extended tags to inspect fields that the current panel does not display.

For an ordinary metadata edit, look for the pending marker and unsaved files, then use File → Save tags on the intended selection. Actions, applied converters and direct artwork commands have different write timing. Editing, saving and undo explains those boundaries, partial success, cancellation and session history.

docs.title: Arrange a wide desktop window
docs.text:
Use View → Show tag panel if the panel was hidden (Hide tag panel is the inverse command). Its shortcut is Ctrl+Q: Control on every platform, including macOS. View → Tag panel position offers Left, Right, Top, Bottom and Floating on a wide layout. Resize its border or move the floating panel to keep the fields reachable.

View → Filter position places the filter above the list or on either side of the toolbar. View → Toolbars controls the main/custom toolbars. Use Columns and Tag-panel customization for detailed field layouts; rearranging the workspace does not rewrite tags.

If the view becomes confusing, show the panel, choose a docked position such as Left, show the filter with F3 if hidden, and clear its text before checking the loaded list. Do not load an old configuration merely to find a hidden panel: that replaces broader settings and reloads the window.

docs.title: Use a narrow window
docs.text:
At compact widths, Files and Tags switch between the list and the tag panel. Select a file before opening its tags; selecting a row can move to the Tags pane. Compact layouts show the first three visible columns and keep the filter with the list. Widen a desktop window when a full column comparison or docking controls are needed.

This responsive layout is separate from mobile filesystem support. A phone preview can display fields while access or save-back is restricted. Read the mode and source-access messages rather than inferring capabilities from the layout alone.

docs.title: Diagnose a disabled command or a failed operation
docs.text:
First check whether an operation is still running, whether the right files are selected, and whether the row is an ordinary file, chapter row or provider-backed document. Hover or focus a disabled control when possible to read its reason. A temporary Wait for the current operation reason is different from an unsupported source or a read-only file.

After an operation, inspect the status and each file error. A success for one file does not prove the rest were written. Dismiss removes the error messages from view; it does not retry a write or repair the file. Keep the exact message and test a corrected operation on copied files before returning to a large batch.

For appearance, use the title-area System, Light or Dark choice. Changing appearance does not change audio or metadata. Keep a configuration backup before broader customization experiments; installation and updates explains what that JSON bundle includes.

docs.title: Opening files
docs.text: Loading files puts their current metadata into the file list. Start with a copied album, then decide whether the next location should replace the list or add to it. Loading is not a tag save, an audio conversion or a backup of the originals.

docs.title: Open one practice folder
docs.text:
1. Choose File → Change directory… (Cmd+D / Ctrl+D on desktop). From an empty window, Open folder… offers the same starting task.
  2. Select the copied folder. Resolve any pending edits before accepting a replacement/discard prompt.
  3. Wait for scanning to finish. Check the loaded count and any file errors.
  4. Select one row and compare its filename with Title and Album in the tag panel. They need not match: names and stored fields are independent.

Change directory… replaces the list and sets the working directory. The working directory supplies context for commands and placeholders; it is not necessarily every loaded file's parent after other folders are added. Options → Directories → Read subfolders controls folder recursion and is on by default. Changing the setting does not rebuild the existing list; open the folder again to apply it.

docs.title: Replace or add deliberately
docs.text:
Command or gesture List behavior Working directory Change directory… Replace The chosen folder Add directory… Append Keep the existing working directory Add files… Append Keep the existing working directory Plain file/folder drop onto the file list Replace Does not establish a new working directory by itself Cmd-drag on macOS / Ctrl-drag on Windows or Linux Append Keep the existing working directory

Add directory… uses Ctrl+H (Control on every platform, including macOS). An append is useful for editing two albums together, but check the selection before assigning shared values. Already loaded files are not intended to become duplicate rows merely because the same file is added again; this does not establish a guarantee about every filesystem alias.

Drop onto the file list, away from the cover area: dropping an image on artwork controls is a different task. Hold the add modifier during the drop. If the result's scope is uncertain, stop and inspect the loaded/selected counts before running a write operation.

Replacing the list can discard pending edits. Confirmation is controlled by Options → Messages and is not an automatic save. A scan can also report individual unreadable files; do not assume that a completed load means every requested file was accepted or that an empty result preserves the old list.

docs.title: Control which files a folder scan finds
docs.text:
Under Options → Files → Restrict incoming files to, enter extensions such as *.mp3;*.flac. The restriction applies to files discovered inside folders. An explicitly added file can still be read even when its extension is outside that restriction. An empty restriction allows the supported audio extensions. Filename patterns such as album*.mp3 are not extension entries.

For a concrete practice folder, suppose these supported, readable files exist:

Practice/01 - Paper Boats.mp3
Practice/bonus.wav
Practice/Disc 2/01 - Intro.mp3

The expected results are:

Input Read subfolders Restriction Loaded paths relative to Practice Folder Yes mp3 01 - Paper Boats.mp3; Disc 2/01 - Intro.mp3 Folder No mp3 01 - Paper Boats.mp3 Folder Yes (empty) 01 - Paper Boats.mp3; bonus.wav; Disc 2/01 - Intro.mp3 Explicit file bonus.wav No mp3 bonus.wav

Folder restrictions do not remove files already in the list. If an album is missing, check the folder chosen, recursion, extension restriction, any active filter, and the file errors. A recognized extension does not make a damaged file readable. Review supported formats for the difference between reading a container and writing its metadata.

docs.title: Return to a directory
docs.text:
File → Favorite directories… manages a saved ordered list. Add the current folder or browse to another, use Make first for the default favorite, then Save. Removing a favorite removes the shortcut, not the folder or music. Favorite directory (Ctrl+M, Control on every platform) opens the first favorite and replaces the list. The File menu also offers individual favorites and recent directories when present.

Previous directory and Next directory use the working-directory history; they are not track navigation and are not the same as the recent list. Upper directory opens its parent when one exists. These operations can replace the list, so resolve pending edits first. Alt is Option on macOS; Alt+Left / Alt+Right navigate directory history when not editing text.

Under Options → Directories → Startup, choose an empty list, the previous directory, or the first favorite. An unavailable previous/favorite entry is not a saved snapshot of your old selection. A queued launch request takes priority over startup restoration. Keep Empty file list while learning if automatic opening makes it hard to see which folder was requested.

docs.title: Open from outside the window
docs.text:
The desktop executable accepts file/folder launch requests, including requests to an already running instance; the command-line reference explains append versus replacement flags. macOS file-open requests are handled when the system delivers them. This does not mean the v0.2.12 installer registers OpenTag for every audio extension or adds an Explorer context menu. Use Add files… if the file manager's Open With route is unavailable.

File → Load playlist/cue sheet… loads supported local playlist entries or CUE track rows and replaces the list after the pending-edit decision. A playlist is a list of references, not embedded audio. Missing files and remote URLs can produce errors. CUE/chapter rows have different write and command limits; read Playlists and Chapters before treating them as ordinary files.

docs.title: Understand platform access
docs.text: Desktop folder loading describes local filesystem paths. In a document-provider build, Add files… selects documents and folder commands can be unavailable. The menu can say Folder access is not available here. Use Add files. Access, writability and recovery are separate from whether a row is visible. A mobile preview or browser preview is not evidence of desktop save-back capability. Read the source/access message before editing important material.

docs.title: Chapters and cue sheets as rows
docs.text:
A chapter row represents part of a containing file. A CUE-track row represents a track described by a cue sheet. Neither is a newly split audio file. This distinction matters when editing a title, creating playlists, or choosing a command that acts on the whole containing file.

Use copied local files and sheets first. These instructions describe current OpenTag source behavior; they do not establish every container/player's support or a native application test on each platform.

docs.title: Show embedded chapters as rows
docs.text:
1. Keep a copy of a file with recognized chapter information. Save or discard pending edits deliberately before changing the view and reloading.
  2. Open File → Options… → Tags → Advanced and enable List chapters as separate files, which is off by default.
  3. Apply the options and reload the directory. OpenTag expands files with at least two recognized chapters into chapter-order rows. A file with fewer than two stays an ordinary file row.
  4. Inspect a row's title and length, then compare the whole-file view by disabling the option and reloading again.

Recognized sources include MP4 Nero/QuickTime chapters, Matroska chapters, ID3v2 CHAP frames, and cue sheets embedded in a CUESHEET field where supported. Each row starts from file fields, overlays that chapter's own fields and uses its chapter title. The same physical filename can therefore appear on several rows. A row duration describes its segment, not a separate file size.

The information placeholders %_subsong% and %_subsong_count% help identify these rows. The index is zero-based; the first of two rows has index 0 and count 2. MP4 rows without explicit track numbers can be given row-based TRACK/TOTALTRACKS values by the read model. Do not infer that new physical tracks were created or that every format stores those synthesized values.

docs.title: Edit a chapter title deliberately
docs.text:
1. Select one copied chapter row and open Extended tags… (Alt+T; Alt is ⌥ Option on macOS).
  2. Change TITLE, then choose Keep changes. That stages text edits.
  3. Choose Save tags to write the appropriate chapter metadata, inspect errors, and read the saved file back.

A title edit uses the existing chapter positions; it is not a timing editor or an audio split. Check read-back positions alongside the title. Clearing the title does not mean deleting the chapter. Other field changes can affect shared storage: for supported chapter formats, equal values across every row consolidate as a file field, while differing values belong to the individual chapters. Only changed fields are considered for that redistribution; format-specific constraints can still reject a requested field or value.

CHAPTERS and CUESHEET are structural whole-file fields. A chapter row refuses editing them as though they were an ordinary chapter label. Return to the whole-file view for supported structural editing. MP4/Matroska CHAPTERS values use time-and-title entries such as 00:00:01.000 Low Tide; this is not a universal way to create ID3 CHAP frames in every audio format.

docs.title: Load an external CUE sheet
docs.text:
Choose File → Load playlist/cue sheet… and select the copied .cue file. This loader lists its AUDIO tracks with INDEX 01 as rows, even when the embedded-chapter display option is off. A sheet with one audio file per track still represents cue-sheet tracks; it does not turn those rows into direct edits of the individual audio files.

Here is a complete small illustration for a three-second image.wav beside the sheet. INDEX uses minutes, seconds and 1/75-second CD frames, not milliseconds. This example's second track starts at one second.

REM COMMENT "Practice copy"
PERFORMER "Juniper Vale"
TITLE "Harbour Lights"
FILE "image.wav" WAVE
  TRACK 01 AUDIO
    TITLE "Paper Boats"
    INDEX 01 00:00:00
  TRACK 02 AUDIO
    TITLE "Low Tide"
    PERFORMER "Mira Solberg"
    INDEX 01 00:01:00

The expected rows are below. Index is %_subsong%, and Count is %_subsong_count%.

Scroll this example table sideways on a narrow screen for the information columns.

Track Title Artist Album Index Count Seconds 1 Paper Boats Juniper Vale Harbour Lights 0 2 1 2 Low Tide Mira Solberg Harbour Lights 1 2 2

The first row inherits the album performer because it has no track performer. The second uses its own. Timing ends at the next applicable INDEX 01 in the same source file, or at the source file's end. A pregap is not an additional file produced by this view. Missing FILE references and unsupported FILE URLs are reported. DATA tracks and AUDIO tracks without INDEX 01 are not listed; this view does not download or reconstruct their audio.

docs.title: Know which file a CUE edit changes
docs.text:
Changing the first row's TITLE to At the Pier, keeping changes and saving writes that TITLE line in the .cue file. It does not retitle image.wav. A shared ALBUM edit to Harbour Sessions changes the sheet's album TITLE line. After reloading, both rows read that shared value. Different requested album values for two rows cannot coexist in that one shared line.

CUE fields have defined storage, not arbitrary custom-field capacity:

Scope Supported field families Album lines ALBUM, ALBUMARTIST, GENRE, YEAR, COMMENT, DISCNUMBER, TOTALDISCS, album ReplayGain gain/peak. Track lines TITLE, ARTIST, COMPOSER, ISRC, track ReplayGain gain/peak. Track number Comes from TRACK lines. Requesting a different number through a tag edit is refused.

Unsupported field names are refused. Album-scope edits in one batch must agree. Original line order, unedited text and the detected encoding are preserved by the sheet editor; newly written values follow its line/quoting rules. Multi-line values are flattened for a cue line. New text that cannot round-trip in a legacy encoding can fail the staged write; inspect the error and retain the original rather than assuming the characters were stored. Keep the original sheet because this is a metadata editor, not a general text-history system.

docs.title: Commands that need the containing file
docs.text:
Some commands are unavailable for rows because they rename or list physical files. Other commands can affect the whole containing file, even when only one chapter row is selected. Read the operation label and scope first.

Row kind Command Scope or restriction Embedded chapter Tag → Filename… Unavailable for the selected row. Embedded chapter Playlist (selected files) Unavailable for the selected row. Embedded chapter Playlist (all files) Unavailable when a chapter row remains in the loaded list. Embedded chapter Remove tag… Acts on the containing file. Embedded chapter Manage covers… Acts on the containing file. CUE track Remove tag… Refused; the row edits the cue sheet. CUE track Play Resolves to the referenced audio file.

Return to ordinary whole-file rows before playlist creation, renaming, moving, copying or deleting audio. To do so for embedded chapters, disable the chapter option and reload the directory. For an external CUE view, load the actual audio files/directory instead of the sheet. A Play/reveal command resolving a CUE source does not export its segment as a new recording.

docs.title: MP4 Nero metadata and artwork
docs.text:
Chapter-row field changes use MP4 field mappings and also update or remove matching fields already present in the file's Nero global metadata. iTunes metadata takes precedence, with Nero filling missing values. This prevents a deleted value from reappearing from its Nero copy after saving.

Nero artwork is shown only when iTunes artwork is absent. A cover edit writes the resulting covers to the iTunes artwork box and removes the Nero artwork copy; a normal text-field edit preserves that copy. Unrelated MP4 index data is retained. These rules do not add a separate Nero artwork editing mode.

docs.title: Remove MP4 chapters only when intended
docs.text:
Tools → Strip chapters MP4… operates on selected MP4 files with recognized chapters and asks before writing. With chapter rows selected, the containing file is the target. CUE-track rows do not support that whole-file command. It removes chapter structures rather than merely hiding rows; the UI explains that their boxes become free space while audio, video and ordinary tags stay. This is not the same as clearing one chapter title or disabling the display option, and it does not apply to every chapter format.

Inspect the returned file/row state after any whole-file operation. A stripped file can replace its earlier chapter rows in the list. For recorded desktop file edits, inspect Edit → Undo and its label; keep copied files and sheets for longer-term recovery and failures. Do not assume generated external playlists or every side effect are included in that history.

docs.title: Cut, copy and paste tags
docs.text: Copying tags transfers structured fields, multiple values and available embedded artwork. It is useful when replacing one encoding of a recording with another. Pasting replaces the target's field set, so use copied practice files before transferring an album.

docs.title: Copy one file to several targets
docs.text:
1. Select one source file with the desired tags. Inspect Extended tags… and its artwork first.
  2. Choose Edit → Copy tags (Cmd+C / Ctrl+C with the file list focused).
  3. Select the destination files. Check the selected count.
  4. Choose Edit → Paste tags (Cmd+V / Ctrl+V) and confirm when asked.
  5. Inspect the pending fields and covers. Choose File → Save tags only for the targets that should receive them.

Copying reads the current displayed field values, including pending edits. It does not first save the source. The tag clipboard is held inside OpenTag; a textual version is also offered to the system clipboard when possible. Copying text elsewhere does not import a new structured tag clipboard.

docs.title: Understand replacement before saving
docs.text:
For this example, the source has TITLE=Paper Boats and ARTIST=Juniper Vale, with no COMMENT. The target has TITLE=Old title, ARTIST=Another artist and COMMENT=Device copy. After Paste, expect this pending result:

Field Source values Target values before Paste Target values after Paste TITLE ["Paper Boats"] ["Old title"] ["Paper Boats"] ARTIST ["Juniper Vale"] ["Another artist"] ["Juniper Vale"] COMMENT [] ["Device copy"] []

The missing source comment removes the target comment; Paste is not a merge that keeps target-only fields. Multiple source values stay separate values in OpenTag's editing model. The destination writer still has its own format limits. For copying only selected fields, use the field clipboard in Extended tags, or calculate a chosen field with Tag → Tag.

docs.title: Transfer several files in order
docs.text:
Copy sources in the intended file-list order, then select targets in the matching order. Sorting affects that order; the order in which rows were clicked is not a separate track-matching system.

Copied source count Selected target count Result 1 3 Same source tags for all targets 2 2 First source to first target; second source to second target 2 1 Refused: counts do not match 2 3 Refused: counts do not match

There is no automatic title/duration matching here. Sort both sets by a reliable track order and inspect the first and last results before saving. For an unfamiliar album, transfer one file at a time instead.

docs.title: Include or leave artwork deliberately
docs.text:
A successfully copied cover list replaces each target's embedded cover list when pasted tags are saved. A source known to have no embedded covers carries an empty list, so it can remove the target's covers. Cover roles, descriptions and order are copied with the image data when available.

If source artwork could not be copied, the operation reports that limitation and Paste leaves the target's covers alone. That is different from a verified empty cover list. Folder-preview images are not copied as embedded artwork. Inspect the status and cover states instead of assuming every text-tag copy included all pictures.

Pasted artwork stays pending until Save tags. Discard pending changes abandons it with the selected files' other pending edits. Provider-document sources and destinations have additional access/copy limits; Save a copy… currently carries edited tag fields, not pending artwork. Use supported local copies when an artwork transfer must be verified.

docs.title: Cut without deleting the audio
docs.text:
Edit → Cut tags copies the selected tags, then stages removal of their fields and supported covers. The source audio files remain in place. Saving the source selection commits that removal; pasting to a destination does not itself save either set.

If the cut was unintended, use Edit → Discard pending changes on the source before saving. After a recorded save, inspect Edit → Undo instead. If the status says artwork could not be copied, do not save the cut expecting the clipboard to recover that artwork. Keep the original files until the destination's tags and artwork have been saved and checked. Cut is not a move of the audio file, and Paste does not rename it from the copied source filename.

docs.title: Copy a readable text report
docs.text:
For an email, track list or spreadsheet note, use Edit → Copy as Text…:

  1. Select tracks and choose Copy as Text….
  2. Enter a format string, such as the example below.
  3. Inspect the preview, which shows up to 5 files.
  4. Choose Copy to calculate text for the whole selection.

For TRACK=3/8, ARTIST=Juniper Vale and TITLE=Paper Boats:

Format string Copied line $num(%track%,2). %artist% — %title% 03. Juniper Vale — Paper Boats

Each selected file contributes one evaluated entry, joined with a newline. A field value containing line breaks can itself produce several text lines. The remembered format history keeps the ten most recent distinct expressions. This command changes no tags and supplies text rather than a structured Paste-tags payload. Use Export for encoded files, headers, loops and a report that should be saved to disk.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Copy/Cut/Paste shortcuts inside a text-entry field operate on text. Focus the list or use the named Edit commands to transfer complete tags.
  • A one-source paste onto a whole album also copies its title and track; it is unsuitable for setting only a shared album artist.
  • Confirmations depend on Options → Messages. Disabling one does not change whether Cut and Paste are pending or whether Paste replaces fields.
  • Keep backups. In-session undo history concerns recorded file writes; it is not a permanent clipboard archive or an external-change backup.

docs.title: Working with covers
docs.text:
Embedded covers travel inside an audio file's metadata. A folder image such as folder.jpg is a separate file that a player or OpenTag can display. Use the cover window to inspect embedded images, and Manage covers… to review a selection's cover set before writing a batch change.

Start with copied practice files. Cover operations have their own write steps; they are not all ordinary pending text-tag edits.

docs.title: Identify what the window shows
docs.text:
The tag panel and Extended tags dialog share the cover window. It reports the current picture role, available dimensions, image size/type, description and position within a common cover set. Previous/next controls appear when there are several shared images.

Display Meaning A shared embedded image All selected files have the same ordered cover identities; the current image can be inspected individually. Covers vary The selected files have different cover sets, including files with no artwork. The app does not present the first file's cover as common to all. Folder image / Not embedded in the file A local image is being shown as a fallback; it is not inside the selected audio files. No artwork No embedded cover is available for the selection and no applicable folder fallback is shown. Loading/unavailable/error message Artwork has not been obtained successfully; do not interpret this as a confirmed empty cover set.

Image bytes, picture role, description and cover order all participate in a shared cover set. Two visually identical files with different descriptions can produce Covers vary. Select one file at a time to investigate.

docs.title: Add a front cover to two practice files
docs.text:
1. Save pending changes and select only the two copied audio files.
  2. Choose Edit → Manage covers… (Cmd+Alt+M on macOS; Ctrl+Alt+M on Windows/Linux).
  3. Choose Add… and select an image file. The list gains a new cover, initially Front Cover, to be embedded in every selected file.
  4. Inspect its dimensions, image type, picture type and description. Review the whole list so an unintended old cover is not left first.
  5. Choose OK to write the planned cover set. Inspect any file errors.
  6. Select each practice file separately and verify its saved artwork.

The shortcut respects text-entry/AltGr combinations on Windows; use the menu if the key combination types a character in the current input. The picker offers supported image files such as JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP and WebP. Its starting folder follows the configured cover-art directory and fallback order explained in the cover context reference.

Adding an image does not convert the audio format. Some tag formats cannot store embedded artwork or preserve every picture-role distinction; see file format capabilities.

docs.title: Understand the Manage covers list
docs.text:
The dialog combines the selection's distinct covers into one editable list. A full circle ● means a cover is present in every selected file. A partly filled circle ◐ identifies a cover present in only some files, with its file count shown. These indicators describe membership, not image quality or whether the cover is the front image.

For example, suppose a front cover is embedded in one of two selected files:

State Presence label original In 1 of 2 files apply-to-all In all 2 files

Select that partial cover and choose Apply to all from its right-click menu, or enable Embed in all selected files. The plan now adds it to the other selected file too. This is an intentional redistribution of artwork; merely selecting the partial cover does not add it anywhere.

An existing partial cover normally stays only in the files that had it. Replacing or adjusting that cover preserves its membership unless applying it to all is also chosen. A newly added cover targets all files selected when the dialog opened; choose the initial audio selection accordingly.

docs.title: Select and reorder covers
docs.text:
Click a cover to select it. Command/Ctrl-click toggles individual covers, and Shift-click selects a range. With the cover list focused, use arrow keys, Home/End, Shift for a range, Space to toggle the focused cover, and Command/Ctrl+A to select every cover in that dialog.

Use Move up / Move down, Alt+Up / Alt+Down, or drag selected covers to reorder them. A selected block retains its relative order. Moving an item at a boundary cannot move it beyond the list. For three cover labels Front, Leaflet, Back, selecting Leaflet and moving it up gives Leaflet, Front, Back.

The resulting first cover is often what a player initially displays, but the receiving player can use its own role/order rules. Reordering does not change a cover's picture type. For an existing partial cover, order changes affect the files in which it will actually be embedded, not files that lack it and are not part of an Apply-to-all plan.

docs.title: Change images, types and descriptions
docs.text:
Control What is planned Replace… Replace one selected cover's image, retaining its role, description and position. Adjust… Resize/convert the selected covers through the cover-adjustment settings, staging the results for the dialog's later OK. Remove Remove the selected cover entries from the planned set. Delete/Backspace in the focused cover list performs this list action. Cover type Assign a picture role to all selected covers. A mixed keep indication preserves current types until a real choice is made. Description Set one description on selected covers; empty text clears it. Extract… Save one unchanged original embedded image to an external file. New/replaced staged images are not available through this original-image extraction path.

For precise scaling policies and image encoding, see Adjust Cover. A status saying the selected covers already match those settings means no image replacement was needed. The available role names and their format limits are listed in the cover menu reference.

A new cover starts as Front Cover. If a cover already uses that type with an empty description, a new cover can receive the selected image filename as its description to keep the entries distinguishable. Inspect those descriptions before saving when a consuming player relies on them.

docs.title: Confirm or leave the dialog
docs.text:
Changing the Manage covers list creates a plan. OK writes changed plans to the selected audio files. Closing without OK drops those unconfirmed cover-list edits. A failed write shows the actual file errors; check which files were changed rather than assuming a multi-file operation is atomic.

Extraction is different: an image already written to an external destination remains there when the dialog is closed. Tag-edit undo is not a general cleanup operation for external files. For an applied recorded cover change, inspect Edit → Undo and its operation label.

docs.title: Use direct cover commands deliberately
docs.text:
The cover window's ⋯ or right-click menu offers Add, Remove, Replace, Extract, Adjust, Manage, type/description and clipboard commands. Direct cover mutations write through their own operation immediately. They do not wait for the Extended tags dialog's Keep changes button.

For an equal cover set, Remove cover acts on the current displayed occurrence. For Covers vary, it asks before removing all covers from the selected files. Replace, Extract, Copy and Cut require a common displayed image; use Manage covers for a mixed set.

Copy/Cut use the image clipboard, and Paste embeds a supplied image. This is separate from copying tag fields or all tags. Save tags first if the displayed artwork is pasted but not yet written: Copy, Cut and Extract require its saved form. Platform image-clipboard support can make commands unavailable.

docs.title: Drag, drop and inspect larger
docs.text:
• Drop supported image files onto the cover area to add embedded artwork. When Extended tags is open, its cover area is the target. A file dropped elsewhere can load files instead, so aim at the image area.
  • Where native desktop image drag-out is available, drag the displayed embedded image into a file manager to copy it externally. Use Extract cover… when drag-out is unavailable or an explicit destination is needed.
  • Double-click the displayed embedded image, press Enter while its window is focused, or choose View larger…. Previous/next changes the displayed cover, not the stored cover order. Close the viewer to return.
  • Correct aspect ratio changes how the image fits the preview/viewer. Stretching a display is not resizing or re-encoding the embedded image.

docs.title: Folder-image fallback
docs.text:
When none of the selected files has embedded or pending artwork, OpenTag can show a local image if every selected local file is in the active file's folder. Options → Tags → Don’t display first image from file directory as cover art disables this fallback. Provider documents without a browsable local folder use a different access path and do not gain folder browsing through this setting.

The fallback is labeled Not embedded in the file. It does not appear because a failed embed was magically repaired, and removing embedded art does not delete the external image. Add/embed the image explicitly when it should travel with the audio files.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Choose the audio selection before opening a batch cover dialog. Its presence counts and write targets refer to that selection.
  • A partial cover and an all-files cover are different plans; check the circle indicator and Embed in all selected files before applying.
  • Changing a file suffix from .jpg to .png does not convert image bytes. Use a real cover-adjustment operation when a different encoding is needed.
  • Confirm saved results and format limits in the receiving player. A common cover preview does not prove every tag format will retain its description or role after saving.

docs.title: Extended tags
docs.text:
Use Extended tags… to see fields that are not on the tag panel, edit separate values and work with cover art. Open it through View → Extended tags… or Alt+T with files selected. Alt is ⌥ Option on macOS.

For one file, the heading identifies its filename and available tag type. For a selection, the heading gives the number of files. A field's values can contain several lines without becoming several separate field values.

docs.title: Add a practice field and save it
docs.text:
1. Select one copied practice file and open Extended tags….
  2. Choose ＋ Add field.
  3. Enter COMMENT as the field name, or choose it through the ► helper. Do not add a second COMMENT row if one already exists; edit that row.
  4. Choose ＋ Add value, then type Checked for the catalogue in its value box.
  5. Choose Keep changes. Back in the main window, the change is pending.
  6. Choose File → Save tags (Cmd+S / Ctrl+S) to write it.
  7. Reopen Extended tags and confirm the saved value.

Keep changes stages text-field edits; it does not itself write all tags. Until saving, Edit → Discard pending changes can discard staged field edits. Keep an original copy and inspect the actual errors after a save.

docs.title: Read a selection without overwriting differences
docs.text:
Suppose two selected files have these values:

Field Paper Boats North Pier Dialog state ALBUM Harbour Lights Harbour Lights One shared value is shown TITLE Paper Boats North Pier Mixed values — keep existing values ARTIST Juniper Vale plus Mira Solberg Juniper Vale Mixed separate-value lists COMMENT Reviewed Absent Mixed, because presence differs too

An untouched mixed row preserves every file's own values. It is not a request to clear the field. Editing its values instead supplies one new value list to every selected file. For example, entering one ALBUMARTIST value can deliberately standardize the selection, while editing TITLE would replace each track's distinct title.

A mixed state compares whole value lists, including their order. Two files with the same names in a different value order can therefore be mixed. Choose a smaller selection to investigate a difference rather than typing over it merely to make the indication disappear.

docs.title: Separate values and multiline text
docs.text:
Use ＋ Add value to add another value to a field. Each value has its own textarea and remove × control. Enter within a textarea starts another line in that value. Two lines in one lyrics/comment value are different from two ARTIST values.

For a duet credit, keep Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg as two value boxes when the format/workflow supports separate artists. The multi-value explanation shows why typing a semicolon into one box does not necessarily create two stored values.

Remove field removes the whole row from the intended result. Removing all its value boxes also requests field removal. A remaining value box containing empty text is a different input; the target tag format determines how an empty text value survives saving. Inspect the saved result.

docs.title: Rename a field while retaining each file's values
docs.text:
Edit the FIELD name without changing its value boxes. A name-only edit uses each file's original values, even when the row is mixed. For example, rename a custom SESSION_NOTE field to SESSIONNOTES:

File SESSION_NOTE before Rename to SESSIONNOTES after 01.flac Early take SESSIONNOTES Early take 02.flac Final take SESSIONNOTES Final take

The old field is removed from each file, and its own value becomes the new field's value. If the values are edited as well, the edited list replaces the originals instead. Do not rename into a field already listed in the dialog: duplicate field identities are rejected for review.

Field identities use case-insensitive ASCII names, so a second artist row is not another independent field beside ARTIST. Native field spelling can remain specific to each file. Field names and mapping explain how names reach tag formats; a visible custom name is not a promise that every player will display it.

docs.title: Copy, cut and paste fields
docs.text:
Right-click a field row outside a value textarea, or focus the row and use Shift+F10. Copy field retains the field name and its separate values in OpenTag's field clipboard. Cut field additionally marks the original row for removal. Paste replaces a matching field's values, or adds a row when the field is absent.

Copy/Cut are unavailable for a mixed row because no single common value list represents all selected files. Inspect one file or make an intentional common value first. The field clipboard is separate from copying all tags, ordinary selected text and image clipboard contents. See context menus for the controls.

docs.title: Step through individual files
docs.text:
The << and >> buttons appear when one file is being edited. They move to the previous/next row in current file-list order and change the main selection to that file. A filtered or sorted view changes that sequence; the buttons are disabled at its ends.

The treatment of changed fields follows Options → Tags → Save mode at extended tag dialog:

Mode When navigating away from a changed file Keep changes pending Default. Stage the current field edits and move to the neighboring file. Save them later from the main window. Ask Choose Save, Don't save, or cancel the question to stay on the current file. Ignore changes Leave the current dialog edits unapplied and move on. Save changes Stage and write the current changed fields before moving; a reported save error keeps the issue visible.

The separate Save tags when using arrow-keys/single mouse click preference can also write pending changes as selection changes. Check both settings before relying on navigation as a read-only inspection workflow.

Closing the dialog does not undo edits already kept by an earlier navigation or written by a save mode. To discard unsaved work, inspect the main window's pending changes. To reverse a recorded disk operation, inspect its Undo label. Neither is a substitute for an original copy.

docs.title: Covers use a different confirmation path
docs.text:
The cover section offers Add cover…, Remove cover, Extract cover… and its ⋯/right-click menu. It uses the same selection summary as the tag panel. Cover actions can write immediately; field Keep changes is not a general confirmation or rollback for artwork operations.

Working with covers explains direct cover commands versus the Manage covers… dialog's OK write step. Supported image-file drops onto the dialog's cover area target that area; dropping elsewhere can have a different meaning. Extraction creates an external image instead of removing the embedded one.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Confirm the heading and selected-file count before replacing a shared field.
  • Leave mixed rows untouched to preserve differences; a blank-looking mixed indication is not an empty text value to fill automatically.
  • A field rename and a value replacement have distinct effects. Start with copied files when reorganizing custom field names.
  • A formula typed into a value textarea is ordinary metadata text; this dialog is not the Tag → Tag format-string evaluator.
  • Unsupported tag fields, provider access or format limits can prevent a later write. Check actual saved tags and errors, not only the dialog view.

docs.title: The file list
docs.text: The file list is the workspace's ordered set of loaded audio rows. It shows field values and technical information, lets you select the scope of an operation, and supplies the processing order for tasks such as numbering and positional text import. The order on screen is separate from filenames and track tags on disk.

docs.title: Read the list and selection information
docs.text:
Each row represents a loaded file or a supported chapter/subsong row. Columns can show editable fields, filenames or measured properties. A column's label and displayed expression are configurable, so a column named Artist is not proof of its actual configured field.

The information line summarizes selected-file duration/size, listed versus loaded totals, and the active file's available codec, bitrate, sample rate and channels. For example, 3 of 8 files means the current view shows three rows from eight loaded files; it does not mean five files were deleted. An unavailable technical property is not supplied by guessing from the suffix.

A filter changes what is visible. It does not remove files from disk or rewrite tags. After changing a filter, explicitly choose the intended selection and inspect the selected count before running a batch command. Use filtering to learn queries and their application timing.

docs.title: Select the intended files
docs.text:
Click a row to select it alone. Use Command-click on macOS or Ctrl-click on Windows/Linux to toggle individual rows. Shift-click selects the range from the selection anchor to the clicked row. The row checkbox also toggles its selection. With a row focused, arrow keys, Home/End and Page Up/Down move through the visible list; modifiers can extend the selection.

Task Shortcut Effect Select all Cmd+A / Ctrl+A Select the visible file-list rows when focus is outside a text editor. Invert selection Cmd+Shift+A / Ctrl+Shift+A Select visible rows that were not selected. Unselect all Cmd+U / Ctrl+U Clear the selection. Select next file Cmd+N / Ctrl+N Select the row after the last selected row, or the first row when nothing is selected. At the end it stays on the last row. Select similar files Cmd+G / Ctrl+G Select visible rows with the same current sort-value key as the active file. Select next similar files Cmd+Shift+G / Ctrl+Shift+G Find the next different key after the last selected row, then select visible rows with that key.

Similarity uses all active sort criteria, ignoring letter case. For an album-wide selection, sort only by Album first. If Track is a secondary criterion, the key includes Track too, so it does not group every track merely because ALBUM is equal. With no active sort, filename supplies the comparison key.

Right-clicking an unselected row first selects that row alone. Right-clicking a selected row preserves the multi-file selection. The row context menu can therefore act on several files even though the pointer is over only one.

docs.title: Sort with one or several columns
docs.text:
Click a column header to sort ascending by that column. Click the same primary header again to reverse it. Shift-click another header to add a secondary criterion; shift-clicking an existing criterion reverses that criterion without replacing the rest. The header arrows and priority numbers show which rules apply.

For an artist/album collection:

  1. Click Artist.
  2. Shift-click Album.
  3. Shift-click Track.
  4. Inspect a few boundaries between artists, albums and discs.

A configured numeric column compares the leading number, so tracks 2 and 10 can sort numerically. A custom column can instead have a separate sort format. Equal keys retain their prior order. Inspect mixed/empty values and numbered disc groups; sorting cannot infer a release's intended track order.

Choose View → Unsorted (load and playlist order) to remove active sort criteria. This returns to the underlying workspace order, which may already have been manually rearranged. It does not reconstruct an earlier order after shuffling or manual moves.

docs.title: Move rows into a manual order
docs.text:
Select rows, focus the file list, then use:

Key Manual move Alt+Up One row earlier Alt+Down One row later Alt+Page Up Gather at the beginning Alt+Page Down Gather at the end

Alt is ⌥ Option on macOS. Alt-dragging selected rows shows an insertion line and moves the rows to that position. Dragging an unselected row first selects it alone. Selected rows retain their relative order; an individual row already at a boundary cannot move beyond it.

For this example, start again with 01.mp3, 02.mp3, 03.mp3, 04.mp3 before each move and select 02.mp3 plus 04.mp3:

Move Resulting file-list order up 02.mp3, 01.mp3, 04.mp3, 03.mp3 down 01.mp3, 03.mp3, 02.mp3, 04.mp3 top 02.mp3, 04.mp3, 01.mp3, 03.mp3 bottom 01.mp3, 03.mp3, 02.mp3, 04.mp3

Making a real manual move in a sorted view clears its active sort and uses the displayed order as the starting point. With a filter, visible rows are rearranged within the positions held by those rows; hidden rows keep their places. No audio file is moved to another disk folder.

Click the file-icon column header to shuffle the shown rows. Shuffling also makes a manual order, and subsequent numbering/playlists use that order. Keep a playlist or other deliberate order record before experimenting when the sequence must be restored later. Manual order lasts while the files stay listed; it does not write track tags automatically.

docs.title: Edit a cell
docs.text:
Choose Edit → Edit in file list or F2. This starts the first selected file's editable filename column when one exists, otherwise its first editable column. It does not bulk-fill every selected row.

To edit a particular tag cell, select one file, then make a separate delayed second click on that editable cell. A fast double-click normally opens Extended tags, or a configured default external tool. Technical/read-only columns cannot be made writable merely by clicking them.

Key in the cell editor Effect Enter Accept the value; the General option can advance to the next file in the same column. Escape Cancel the current cell edit. Tab Accept and move to the next editable cell, wrapping to the next row. Shift+Tab Accept and move backward through editable cells/rows.

Ordinary field edits become pending changes. Save tags explicitly, or use the configured save-on-selection-change behavior, when they must reach disk. For multiple separate values or multiline text, Extended tags offers dedicated controls.

A filename cell is different: accepting it requests an immediate filesystem rename. Keep the existing audio extension in a filename-with-extension column. Path separators are not accepted there; use Tag → Filename for a reviewed folder layout. A title field edit does not rename the file, and a filename edit does not automatically change TITLE.

docs.title: Show, size and arrange columns
docs.text:
Right-click a column header to show/hide columns or choose column customization. Keep at least one column visible. Drag column headers to rearrange them, or drag their dividers to set widths. A hidden column's metadata is still present in files.

View → Auto-size columns or Command+numeric-keypad + / Ctrl+numeric-keypad + fits columns to measured contents within width limits. The shortcut requires the numeric keypad plus key. Very long lists are sampled from the top, so a later unusually long value can still need manual widening. View menu describes the column controls.

docs.title: Remove rows, refresh or delete files
docs.text:
• Remove from list (Delete; the Mac Backspace/delete key is also supported) removes selected rows from the workspace. The files remain on disk. Pending edits for removed rows are discarded after the configured confirmation.
  • File → Clear list removes all loaded rows and their workspace state.
  • View → Refresh (F5) rescans the loaded roots under the current subfolder preference. Review its pending-change warning before proceeding.
  • Reload tags rereads selected files' tags; it is a different task from rebuilding the loaded file list.
  • Delete files… and Delete files permanently… are actual filesystem operations. Read their confirmations; they are not substitutes for hiding unwanted rows from the current batch.

Check the Edit menu for deletion and transfer commands, and keep their scope separate from the filter and selection.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Arrange the list before numbering or positional text import. A sorted preview is not evidence that tags on disk already contain those numbers.
  • Moving rows does not create an undoable tag edit or restore an earlier shuffle through the Unsorted item.
  • Text focus changes shortcut meaning. Ctrl/Command+A in an editor selects text, not every loaded file.
  • A rendered column can use an expression, while its editable Field targets a particular tag name. Inspect the column definition when a displayed value and its editor seem different.
  • Save-on-moving-selection and tag-panel defaults can create or write pending edits during navigation; inspect their Options before assuming selection is only a visual action.

docs.title: Copy, move and delete files
docs.text: File operations change where audio files exist, rather than changing their metadata. Start with copied practice files and a separate destination folder. Check the selected-file count: a filter can hide selected rows without removing them from the operation.

docs.title: Choose the operation by its effect
docs.text:
Goal Command Disk and list effect Make another file in a folder Edit → Copy files to… Create a destination copy; retain the source and its listed row Relocate the file Edit → Move files to… Move the file and update its listed path; it may then leave the list Stop showing selected rows Edit → Remove from list Remove rows and their pending edits; keep the files on disk Empty the workspace File → Clear list Remove every listed row, including hidden rows; keep files on disk Delete through the system trash Edit → Delete files… Send successfully deleted files to the desktop trash and remove their rows Delete without the trash Edit → Delete files permanently… Remove successfully deleted files directly from disk and the list

Copy tags, Cut tags and Paste tags are different commands. They transfer metadata, not the audio files. Removing a tag also leaves the audio file in place.

docs.title: Copy one album file to a practice folder
docs.text:
Suppose the original is /Music/Juniper Vale/03 - Paper Boats.flac and the existing destination folder is /Practice/Harbour Lights.

  1. Save intended pending tag edits, or deliberately discard them. Copy/move commands require the selected files' pending changes to be resolved.
  2. Select the ordinary file row. Clear an old selection first if necessary; do not use the number of visible rows as the target count.
  3. Choose Edit → Copy files to… (Cmd+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+C).
  4. Choose the existing destination folder. Read the confirmation's destination, file count and shortened name list before accepting.
  5. Check the result and any file errors. The intended destination is /Practice/Harbour Lights/03 - Paper Boats.flac.
  6. Use Add files… or Add directory… to inspect the new copy. Copying does not automatically add its destination row to the file list.

The confirmation abbreviates long name lists; it is not a per-file rename preview. Check the full selection and destination yourself before accepting.

The command retains the filename and extension. It places selected files directly in the chosen folder; it does not recreate the source folder tree. To create a metadata-derived folder layout, use Tag → Filename on practice files instead.

docs.title: When a copy or move is rejected
docs.text:
The transfer planner checks the complete selection before starting. An ordinary existing destination name, two selected sources with the same basename, a source already in the destination folder, an unreadable source, or an invalid destination can reject the plan. Selected basenames are also compared without letter case, so Song.flac and song.flac are treated as a selection conflict even on a volume that can store both.

For example, selecting both /Set A/03 - Paper Boats.flac and /Set B/03 - Paper Boats.flac for one destination does not merge them or invent a suffix. Choose separate destination folders or deliberately rename copies before transferring them.

These checks are useful safeguards, not a universal filesystem alias or collision guarantee. Links, case rules, network volumes and changes made by another process have their own limits. A clean empty practice destination makes the intended result easier to inspect. Do not approve an operation on the assumption that it will resolve every ambiguous name for you.

Planning failure leaves that plan unstarted. A failure during execution is different: successful earlier transfers can remain. Read each error and inspect both folders before retrying; the batch is not one rollback transaction.

docs.title: Move files and understand disappearing rows
docs.text:
Use Edit → Move files to… (Cmd+Shift+V / Ctrl+Shift+V) with the same selection/destination checks. The destination filename is unchanged. A move can succeed even if reading the destination's metadata afterward fails, so an error does not always mean the file stayed at its old path.

Options → General → Keep moved files in the file list controls whether files moved outside the listed folders remain visible. With that option off, a successfully moved file can disappear from the list. That disappearance is not deletion. Inspect the reported destination in the file manager or open the destination folder in OpenTag.

Copy/move commands do not create a session tag-Undo step. To reverse a move, inspect the destination first, then deliberately move the file back when its original name/location is available. To remove an unwanted copy, identify the copy rather than deleting the original. Do not treat an older Undo Save tags menu item as an undo of the more recent file transfer.

docs.title: Remove rows while retaining files
docs.text:
1. Select the rows to stop showing.
  2. Choose Edit → Remove from list. With the file list focused, Delete performs this list removal; macOS also uses Backspace.
  3. If those rows have pending edits, read the discard confirmation. Accepting removes their unsaved field/artwork intent along with the rows.
  4. Reopen the file or its folder when needed. The disk still contains the last saved metadata, not the discarded pending values.

File → Clear list applies to the entire workspace, rather than only the selection. It can include rows outside the current filter. Neither operation is recorded as an Undo action for list membership. Opening files again is not a recovery of discarded edits. Resolve edits first when keeping them matters.

docs.title: Delete through the trash or delete permanently
docs.text:
For ordinary local files, Delete files… requests the desktop system's Recycle Bin/trash. The normal confirmation describes the selected names and count. Options → Messages → at deleting files controls whether that confirmation appears; a missing prompt does not mean that the command is a list-only operation.

After the operation, successful files leave the list and failures remain reported. A locked or unavailable file can fail while another is deleted. Do not repeat the whole selection without checking what already happened. If recovery is needed, inspect the system trash and use its restore command, then reopen the restored files. Trash behavior and recoverability depend on the OS, volume and permissions; this guide does not qualify a native trash round-trip on your machine.

Permanent deletion bypasses the trash

Delete files permanently… does not create an OpenTag Undo step or a trash copy. Keep a separate backup before using it. Its confirmation can also be suppressed by the deletion-message preference. Use the menu label deliberately instead of experimenting with modifier keys on real files.

The inspected backend accepts regular files for transfer/deletion and rejects folders and symbolic-link entries. This is not a recursive folder-deletion command. File operations require desktop/local filesystem access. Chapter rows are not separate audio files: copy/move/delete are unavailable for such rows. Turn off List chapters as separate files and reload the directory to work with the parent file. Provider documents have separate access and publication rules; do not substitute these desktop instructions for them.

docs.title: Reveal or play without changing metadata
docs.text:
File → Open in Finder/Explorer/file manager reveals selected files. With no selection, it can open the current working folder. Alt+Enter provides the file-list reveal route. For filesystem properties, reveal the file and use the file manager's properties/info command.

File → Play (F4 with the file list focused) asks the desktop to open files with their default application. More than ten selected rows triggers a confirmation; the backend limits the distinct resolved playback files to 100. Chapter/CUE playback resolves the referenced audio file, not an independent new file per displayed row. Starting an application is not proof that it played every track or understood chapter positions.

Reveal and Play do not save pending tag edits. A player reads the saved file, which can differ from what OpenTag currently shows as pending. Configured external tools have their own per-file and argument rules; they are not the same as default playback.

docs.title: Gotchas and recovery
docs.text:
Keep the result message, destination and per-file errors until the state is clear. If a copy/move partially completes, compare the original and destination folders before choosing the smaller remaining selection. If deletion partly completes, inspect the trash or backup before doing anything permanent.

Close or pause other programs that are rewriting the same files. Pending tag edits, session Undo and an external application's changes are three different states; none replaces an independent audio-file backup.

docs.title: Filtering the file list
docs.text: Use the Filter to show files that need attention: tracks without an album artist, files above a bitrate, or titles containing a particular phrase. Filtering changes the view; it does not remove files or edit tags.

docs.title: Start with a text search
docs.text:
1. Open a folder or add files to the list.
  2. Show View → Show filter with F3 if the Filter is hidden.
  3. Type Juniper Harbour into the Filter.

In the installed app, ordinary search requires every space-separated word to occur somewhere in the tags or filename. The words can occur in different fields. Juniper Harbour can therefore find ARTIST=Juniper Vale with ALBUM=Harbour Lights, regardless of case or word order.

The search does not require complete words: harb can match Harbour. An asterisk is literal text here, not a wildcard. To search only a particular field, switch to an expression.

docs.title: Ask a more precise question
docs.text:
Goal Enter Find an artist exactly, including one value of a multi-artist field ARTIST IS "Juniper Vale" Find titles containing Live TITLE HAS Live Find missing album artists ALBUMARTIST MISSING Find tracks numbered above 8 TRACK GREATER 8 Find Folk tracks except live recordings GENRE IS Folk AND NOT TITLE HAS Live Find a numbered track/total pair TRACK MATCHES "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$"

Write keywords such as IS, HAS, and AND in uppercase. Field names and compared text are case-insensitive. Quote a multiword value as one operand; the quotes group the filter text and are not part of the wanted tag value.

HAS asks about contained words. IS asks whether a complete stored value equals the text. MATCHES runs a regular expression. These are different questions: TITLE IS "Live*" looks for the literal asterisk, while TITLE MATCHES "^Live" finds a value beginning with Live.

The complete filter syntax reference covers all operators, missing versus empty fields, quoting, numeric rules, and format-string selectors.

docs.title: Choose automatic or manual application
docs.text:
Open the helper menu beside the Filter, or focus the field and press Ctrl+Space. Control is used on every platform; Ctrl+Alt+Space is also available on macOS when the system reserves Control+Space.

Auto-apply filter defaults to enabled. Results update while typing after a short delay. Turn it off to compose an expression without filtering at each partial word, then press Enter to apply it. The text being edited and the currently applied query can differ in manual mode.

Enabling Auto-apply while unapplied text exists applies that text. The helper also offers fields, information fields, functions, and history/favorites. Inserted placeholders still need the surrounding filter syntax: a function by itself is not an operator.

docs.title: Clear, hide, and restore the filter
docs.text:
Erase the text to show the original loaded list again; in manual mode, press Enter to apply the empty query. View → Hide filter or F3 also shows all loaded files. OpenTag remembers the hidden text during the session and restores it when the Filter is shown again. If the hidden text was still being edited in manual mode, showing it restores that text as the applied filter.

A filtered-out file remains loaded. The selection count is separate from the visible count, so a hidden selected file can still be selected. Review the selected count and selection before a write, rename, or removal. Use Unselect all and deliberately select the intended visible rows when a batch must be limited to the result set.

docs.title: Position the Filter
docs.text: Use View → Filter position to choose Above the file list, Left of the toolbars, or Right of the toolbars. The default is above the list. Compact layouts keep the Filter with the list and omit the position menu.

docs.title: If the result looks wrong
docs.text:
Filtering files… means the current query is still being evaluated. No matching files is a successful query with no matches. Invalid filter is an error: read the message, correct the query, or clear it. A syntax error does not mean that the files disappeared from disk.

Start with a simple field query and add one condition at a time. Check these common mistakes:

  • Write MATCHES, not MATCH.
  • Use integer thresholds such as TRACK GREATER 8; 3.5 and 3:30 are not valid numeric operands.
  • Use %_path% or another explicit information field for a folder/path search. Plain search does not search every technical field.
  • Distinguish a missing field from a present value containing empty text.
  • Avoid double quotes inside a quoted literal. Use the regex or $char(34) techniques in the reference.

The browser preview has a simpler substring search over its displayed data and paths. The full expression parser described here belongs to the installed app's backend. Do not use browser-preview matches as proof of installed filter behavior.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Filter syntax and tested examples
  • Field names
  • Regular expressions
  • Information placeholders

docs.title: Find text in the file list
docs.text:
Use Edit → Find… (Cmd+F / Ctrl+F) to list matching filenames and tag values, then select the files behind those results. Find leaves the file list's contents in place. To reduce the visible list, use Filter instead.

The search runs on the currently listed, visible files, including their pending field values. A filename means its leaf name with extension, not its whole folder path. Technical information fields are not part of this tag-value search; use the filter's information placeholders for those.

docs.title: Find a title and select its file
docs.text:
1. Load copied practice files, wait for any active filter to finish, and choose Edit → Find….
  2. Enter Pier, leave Strategy at Contains, and leave Case sensitive off.
  3. Choose Find or press Enter in the search input.
  4. Look for the result whose Field is TITLE and whose Match is North Pier.
  5. Click that row. The corresponding audio file becomes selected in the main window. Close Find when ready to edit it.

Find is a non-modal window: the main workspace can remain available while results are shown. A result selects a file; it is not an editable tag value or a replacement instruction. Check the main selection before applying a batch action.

docs.title: Choose a matching strategy
docs.text:
Ordinary strategies treat the criteria as literal text. A dot or bracket has special meaning only when Regular expression is chosen. The default is Contains, with case ignored.

Strategy Criteria Value being searched Result Contains Pier North Pier Match Matches word Pier North Pier Match Matches content Pier North Pier No match Begins with North North Pier Match Ends with Pier North Pier Match Regular expression ^North\s+Pier$ North Pier Match Matches word Pier North Pier-West Match Matches word Pier North Pier_West No match

Matches word requires boundaries around the whole criteria. Letters, numbers and underscore count as word characters for this strategy; a hyphen separates words. Matches content requires equality with one complete field value or filename. For a filename, the extension is part of that value, so North Pier is not the complete content of 04 - North Pier.flac.

Enable Case sensitive when Pier must differ from pier. Spaces at the start/end of the criteria are literal search characters; an entirely empty criteria reports Enter text to find rather than listing every file.

docs.title: Read match counts correctly
docs.text:
One file can have several result rows. A filename, TITLE and COMMENT can all match the same criteria. One matching field value creates one row, even if that value contains the searched text several times.

For example, use Contains with boats, ignoring case, on this practice selection:

Filename TITLE COMMENT 03 - Paper Boats.flac Paper Boats (absent) 04 - North Pier.flac North Pier Notes about boats

Expect 3 matches in 2 files: the first filename, its TITLE, and the second file's COMMENT. Select all results selects the two distinct files, not three copies of a file. A second ARTIST value can likewise supply its own result independently of the field's first value.

docs.title: Sort and navigate results
docs.text:
Click the Filename, Field or Match column header to sort those result rows. Clicking the active header again reverses that sort. Result sorting does not reorder the main file list or change tag values.

Click a row, or focus it and press Enter/Space, to select its file in the main list. Up/Down moves through result rows and selects their files. The current result control offers individual-row navigation or Select all results; it does not provide a separate Command/Ctrl-click range selection of arbitrary result rows. For a subset, close Find and adjust the selected files in the main list.

The table displays at most the first 2,000 matching rows. The status reports the full count, and Select all results considers all matching files, including ones represented only by unshown rows. Refine the query when every match must be inspected before acting.

docs.title: Refresh an outdated result set
docs.text:
The result table is a snapshot from the last Find operation. Edit tags, change a filter or remove files, then run Find again to refresh it. Clicking a result whose file is no longer visible reports that it is no longer listed. Select all results also excludes files that are no longer in the current visible list.

Selecting results changes the main selection. Configured tag-panel defaults can stage values for a multi-file selection; inspect pending changes before saving them. Running a search is not itself a metadata-replacement operation.

docs.title: Regular expressions use the Find dialect
docs.text:
Find uses JavaScript Unicode regular expressions, controlled by its Case sensitive checkbox. Enter the raw pattern without the apostrophe quoting used inside a $regexp(...) format string. An invalid expression is shown as an error and clears the result table for that run.

Do not assume every advanced pattern from an action or filter is accepted. For example, unscoped (?i) is invalid here; use the checkbox instead. Find does not add the shared core's multiline/dot-all defaults. The regex reference provides actual case-control and invalid-pattern examples. Find has no replacement box: use an action or converter when matching should lead to an edit.

docs.title: Reuse or remove criteria
docs.text:
The input's drop-down history remembers used criteria through the normal helper-list mechanism. The ► helper offers Remove from history and Remove all from history… for this input. Removing history does not remove tags or files. Physical Control+Space opens the focused helper; Shift+Delete removes the current remembered value.

Reopening an already open Find window selects its input for a new query. After closing and opening a new window, check the strategy and case option: the new dialog starts with Contains and case sensitivity off. A remembered criteria string does not carry those options with it.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Check whether a filter has hidden files that should participate in the search. Find searches this view, not every file elsewhere in the library.
  • The result's Field names metadata; the file list's configurable column labels do not rename those fields.
  • Several matching rows can refer to one file, while one field can contain several separately searched values. Read both the match and file counts.
  • Close Find before relying on workspace keyboard shortcuts whose routing changes while a dialog is open.
