docs.title: OpenTag on Windows
docs.text: Install the published desktop package, distinguish WebView2 startup problems from audio-file errors, and choose explicit paths and encodings for a small practice set. Windows uses Ctrl for the shared Primary shortcuts.

docs.title: Choose and verify the installer
docs.text:
The published v0.2.13 release contains this Windows package:

Scroll the download table sideways on a narrow screen to read complete filenames.

Processor build Asset x64 / 64-bit Intel or AMD OpenTag-v0.2.13-windows-x64-setup.exe

This release has no separate Windows ARM64, 32-bit, portable ZIP or Store package. Check a newer release's own assets before choosing it. A framework's ability to build another target is not evidence that OpenTag published or qualified that target.

Download SHA256SUMS from the same release and compare the full hash of the installer. In PowerShell, from the download folder:

Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath '.\OpenTag-v0.2.13-windows-x64-setup.exe'

-LiteralPath means the filename is used as written rather than as a wildcard. A matching hash is an integrity check against that release; it does not substitute for trusting the source. The v0.2.13 installer has no Authenticode publisher signature, so the guide cannot give a verified publisher identity to expect in an unknown-publisher warning. Review the download and your organization's policy before running it.

docs.title: Install and start with WebView2 available
docs.text:
1. Run the verified -setup.exe and follow its installation choices.
  2. Open OpenTag from the installed shortcut.
  3. If startup fails before the editor appears, record the exact message and check its runtime requirements before trying any audio operations.

OpenTag's Windows interface uses Microsoft Edge WebView2. The current installer configuration leaves Tauri's default runtime bootstrapper mode in place: if WebView2 is missing, obtaining it can require internet access. An offline machine or restricted download policy can therefore need runtime provisioning through its administrator. See the official Tauri Windows installer documentation. That is separate from Rust/Node build tooling, which a user does not need to install merely to run this desktop download.

The published package and runtime setting do not establish support for every Windows version or policy configuration. Keep the OS version and failure stage in a report rather than treating every startup error as a bad MP3. Use the shared installation checklist for download and update decisions.

docs.title: Open files from Explorer or the File menu
docs.text:
Use File → Change directory… for a copied album, or Add files… and Add directory… for additions. You can also drop copied files/folders into the app. A plain drop replaces the current list; holding Ctrl adds to it. Finish pending edits before replacing a working list.

File → Open in Explorer reveals selected files or the working folder. Play opens audio through the system's default association. The installer configuration does not automatically register OpenTag as the default audio handler or add a custom Explorer context-menu command. Use the File menu or window drop if a file-manager launch is not configured.

A shortcut or script can pass file/folder arguments to the installed executable. In PowerShell, & invokes a quoted executable path. This is an example, with both paths to replace with your own locations:

& 'C:\Path\To\opentag.exe' '/fp:C:\Music\Practice Album'

The /fp: argument opens that folder; it does not run a tagging action. A second recognized launch is forwarded to the existing instance. For append requests and quoting, use the command-line reference. Do not infer that a requested folder loaded merely because a process started; inspect the actual file list and any pending-edit decision.

docs.title: Shortcut focus and the notification area
docs.text:
Click the file list for selection commands. Text fields retain their text editing behavior, and Ctrl+Alt/AltGr combinations can be character entry. Use menu commands if a desktop utility intercepts a chord.

Chord Focus OpenTag result Ctrl+D File list Change directory Alt+T Text field Extended tags Ctrl+Alt+T Text field Text entry Ctrl+Tab File list Next pane Delete File list Remove rows from list Ctrl+Delete File list Move files to Recycle Bin or trash

Removing a row keeps its disk file. A trash command changes the filesystem; permanent deletion is a separate command. Read the command label rather than using Delete as a general “clear this” key. Ctrl+S saves selected pending tag changes; actions and renames have their own immediate Apply/write steps.

Under Options → General → Notification area, Always show icon in notification area and Minimize to notification area both start off. The first keeps an icon available; the second can hide a minimized window and its taskbar entry. Click its tray icon or choose Show OpenTag to restore it. The tray menu's Quit OpenTag follows the window-close route, including the pending-work decision. Minimizing is not saving pending tags.

docs.title: Paths and older text encodings
docs.text:
Quote paths with spaces in scripts. Literal folder separators typed into an OpenTag filename format create folders; slashes inside a tag value are data and use the configured replacement. Preview the entire destination and retain enough track/disc information to keep names distinct.

For a long-path or destination error, try a copied album in a shorter, clearly writable location and inspect that actual result. A character-cleaning expression does not establish full-path validity or support by another program. See portable names for the scope of $validate, Unicode counts and explicit truncation policies.

A Windows ANSI codepage is not synonymous with UTF-8 or Windows-1252. OpenTag uses the system ANSI codepage for applicable legacy operations. New text should use Unicode where possible. In Text File → Tag, the legacy fallback is used only after BOM/valid-UTF-8 detection.

These practice bytes illustrate choosing a known explicit fallback, not guessing the codepage of every Windows computer:

Source bytes in hex Legacy fallback Decoded text 43 61 66 C3 A9 windows-1252 Café 43 61 66 E9 windows-1252 Café

The first row is valid UTF-8 and does not use the fallback. The second is legacy text under the stated codepage. Inspect accents before applying an import. Changing a filename extension or changing Windows' display language does not repair already garbled field text; follow the encoding guide for the relevant operation.

docs.title: Credentials, settings and updates
docs.text:
The optional system-keychain choice uses Windows Credential Manager for the Discogs token. If the credential operation fails, check its status and error before repeating it. The secret is not included in a normal configuration backup or returned as visible token text.

Use File → Open configuration folder to find this user's saved settings; do not substitute another editor's configuration path. Save configuration… saves supported configuration, not pending tags or audio backups. Finish pending work and close the old app before updating with a newer verified package. An update check can open a release page; it is not an automatic in-place updater.

docs.title: If Windows-specific behavior differs
docs.text: Include the exact release asset, Windows version, architecture and message, and state whether the problem occurs during installer/runtime startup, opening a file, writing a tag, or using a tray/shortcut action. Start with one copied local file. Read-only package inspection and source/model tests do not prove installation, WebView2 download or every Windows filesystem behavior on your machine.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Use the reference to look up exact field names, syntax, storage mappings, and supported file formats. For a complete filtering task, start with the filtering guide.

Reference Look up Field names Editable metadata vocabulary, custom fields, and special action selectors. Tag mapping table The native ID3 frames, MP4 atoms, ASF attributes, Matroska target levels, and RIFF identifiers used for fields. Supported file formats Recognized extensions, tag read/write/remove capabilities, artwork, chapters, and limitations. Filter syntax Plain search, every filter operator, quoting, precedence, and worked examples. Format strings Placeholders, functions, and rules for constructing a value. Placeholders File information and other values available inside format strings. Regular expressions Pattern syntax, replacements, escaping, and Boost-specific behavior. Command line Open or append files/folders with platform-specific shell examples. Keyboard shortcuts Focus-sensitive commands, platform modifiers and dialog keys. Menu reference Visible commands, their input scope and write behavior.

docs.title: Choose the right kind of name
docs.text:
ARTIST is an editable field name. %artist% reads its value in a format string. TPE1 is the ID3v2 frame used to store that field. ARTIST IS "Juniper Vale" is a filter expression. These names participate in different layers; a native frame identifier is not automatically an editable field or placeholder.

Technical information such as duration describes a file; editing a similarly named custom field does not change the audio's measured duration. Check Field names before creating a field intended to control a player or an action.

docs.title: Scope of the reference
docs.text:
These pages describe the inspected OpenTag source and executable documentation examples. Recognition of an extension does not establish playback, DRM support, or compatibility with every application that reads that format. Native/runtime checks and release availability are separate from source inspection.

Additional context-menu, options and automation references are published as their checked pages become available. Unfinished pages remain outside the public navigation and search.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Launch OpenTag with a folder or file to open it in the desktop file list. Use /add when a launch should append to the existing list. These switches open the interactive application; they do not provide unattended tag editing, action execution or export commands.

docs.title: Supported arguments
docs.text:
Argument What it requests /fp:<folder> Load a folder and use it as the working directory when replacing the list /fn:<file> Load a file and use its parent folder as the working directory when replacing the list /add Append the requested files/folders instead of replacing the list; preserve the existing working directory

Switch names ignore case. A - prefix is also accepted, for example -fn:/home/you/Music/track.flac. If the value after fp: or fn: is empty, the next argument supplies it. Prefer the complete colon form above, with the whole argument quoted when it contains spaces.

Bare paths are accepted too: existing folders become folder requests and other paths become file requests. Relative paths are resolved against the launching process's working directory, not the shell's script location or the folder currently displayed in an already-open OpenTag window. Use absolute paths for shortcuts and scripts that can start from different directories.

Multiple file/folder arguments are allowed. The first requested directory, or the first file's parent when there are no directories, supplies the working directory for a replacement request. /add alone has nothing to load. Unrecognized switches can be ignored; they are not an alternate batch API.

docs.title: Windows: PowerShell
docs.text:
Replace the executable path below with the location of your installed opentag.exe. PowerShell's & invokes a quoted executable path. Each quoted argument is passed as one item, including its spaces.

Open a practice album folder:

& 'C:\Path\To\opentag.exe' '/fp:C:\Music\Juniper Vale\Harbour Lights'

Open one file instead:

& 'C:\Path\To\opentag.exe' '/fn:C:\Music\Juniper Vale\Harbour Lights\01 - Paper Boats.flac'

Append another file without replacing the current list:

& 'C:\Path\To\opentag.exe' '/add' '/fn:C:\Music\Juniper Vale\Harbour Lights\02 - Lanterns on the Water.flac'

The single quotes here belong to PowerShell; they are not part of the path OpenTag receives. In Command Prompt, use double quotes around arguments with spaces instead. A Windows shortcut can put the switches after its quoted executable path in Target.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
For an app installed in /Applications, invoke the bundle's executable when passing explicit switches:

'/Applications/OpenTag.app/Contents/MacOS/opentag' '/fp:/Users/you/Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights'

To append a file:

'/Applications/OpenTag.app/Contents/MacOS/opentag' '/add' '/fn:/Users/you/Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/02 - Lanterns on the Water.flac'

Finder Open With, dropping files on the Dock icon, and the ordinary open -a OpenTag <paths> document-opening route use macOS open-document events. They request a replacement list, rather than /add. Do not assume that open --args sends new arguments to an already-running application; use the direct executable route when you need the switches.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
Use the executable you installed or extracted. For example:

/path/to/opentag '/fp:/home/you/Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights'

/path/to/opentag '/add' '/fn:/home/you/Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/02 - Lanterns on the Water.flac'

The shell quotes preserve spaces as one argument. A bare absolute Unix path also remains a path; the leading / is not automatically treated as an unknown Windows-style switch.

docs.title: Existing windows, ordering and troubleshooting
docs.text:
Desktop launch handling forwards recognized opening requests to an existing instance and brings its main window forward. Requests wait while another operation is busy. Replacing the list can require a pending-edit decision; launching the program does not silently save those edits.

Appended files join the loaded list. An active sort can change their visible placement. Choose View → Unsorted (load and playlist order) when you need to inspect load order; /add is not a command to sort or renumber the files.

If nothing appears, check the executable path, the audio path and shell quoting. Check OpenTag's file errors for unreadable or unsupported files. The folder-recursion preference still governs scans of supplied directories. Opening a second process is not evidence that the requested file loaded: inspect the resulting file list before continuing.

See File menu for interactive opening commands and keyboard shortcuts for working with the loaded list.

docs.title: Field names
docs.text:
A field name identifies a piece of editable metadata, such as ARTIST. Its values are text shown in the tag panel, file-list columns, or Extended tags…. A mapping translates that logical name to the format's native storage.

New to this?

Keep ARTIST for the performer and ALBUMARTIST for the release credit. Use TITLE for the track name. Those distinctions make a mixed collection easier to sort and rename.

docs.title: Names, values, and placeholders
docs.text:
To inspect or add fields, select files and open View → Extended tags…. Frequently used fields can be added to the tag panel, and fields can be displayed through custom file-list columns. A field named MOOD is read as %mood% in a format string. A field with a space, such as RATING WMP, uses %rating wmp%; in filters quote the field name: "RATING WMP" PRESENT.

Lookups are generally case-insensitive, and the panel configuration normalizes names to uppercase. Vorbis Comments and APE retain their native field names unless a user mapping changes the displayed name. Thus a FLAC DATE is not automatically renamed to YEAR merely because an MP3 date appears as YEAR.

Multiple values belong to one field; they are not necessarily one text string joined with punctuation. For example, ARTIST can contain Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg separately. A player may combine them for display. Use the app's separate-value editing rather than inserting a semicolon and assuming every format will split it.

docs.title: Field vocabulary
docs.text: The tables cover all 118 named entries in OpenTag's fixed native mapping vocabulary. The meaning describes the metadata, not a promise that every format has a dedicated native location or every player displays it. The mapping tables and format capabilities explain storage and limits.

docs.title: Core description
docs.text: Field Meaning TITLE Name of this track or item. ARTIST Track performer; supports more than one value where the format allows it. ALBUM Release or collection title. ALBUMARTIST Artist credited for the album as a whole, which may differ from a track’s performer. YEAR Recording/release date text in the format’s mapped date field; it can contain more than four digits. DATE A separate date field, including ID3v2.3 TDAT; do not assume it is the same native field as YEAR. TRACK Track number, often with a total such as ⅜. DISCNUMBER Disc number, often with a total such as ½; Matroska video uses different episode semantics. GENRE Style or category text; old ID3v1 has a fixed indexed vocabulary. COMMENT Comment text; ID3v2 descriptions are addressed separately. DESCRIPTION Short description with a dedicated MP4 desc mapping; distinct from COMMENT. SUBTITLE Subtitle for the item. SETSUBTITLE Subtitle describing a disc/set rather than the individual track. CONTENTGROUP Content-group description, mapped to TIT1 in ID3v2. GROUPING Grouping field mapped to GRP1 in ID3v2; do not interchange with CONTENTGROUP automatically. COMPILATION Compilation flag: write 1 or remove the field in the constrained ID3/MP4 representations. COPYRIGHT Copyright notice. LANGUAGE Language of the content; it does not choose the interface language. LENGTH Stored length metadata, not the measured duration information placeholder. BPM Beats per minute; MP4 uses an integer representation. INITIALKEY Musical key text. MOOD Mood description. MEDIATYPE Original source medium/type description; distinct from the MP4 ITUNESMEDIATYPE enumeration. FILETYPE Stored file-type description; editing it does not transcode the audio.

docs.title: People and credits
docs.text: Field Meaning COMPOSER Composer credit. CONDUCTOR Conductor credit. LYRICIST Writer of the words. MIXARTIST Remixer or mix artist. NARRATOR Narration credit. INVOLVEDPEOPLE Role/person pairs in ID3v2 IPLS/TIPL; see the structured syntax below. MUSICIANCREDITS Musician role/person pairs; ID3v2.4 uses TMCL. PUBLISHER Publisher label/name. ENCODEDBY Person or organization credited with encoding. ENCODERSETTINGS Description of encoder settings; it does not reconfigure an encoder. FILEOWNER Owner/purchaser metadata; it does not change filesystem ownership.

docs.title: Sorting and classical works
docs.text: Field Meaning ALBUMSORT Alternate sort text for album title. ALBUMARTISTSORT Alternate sort text for the album artist. ARTISTSORT Alternate sort text for track artist. COMPOSERSORT Alternate sort text for composer. TITLESORT Alternate sort text for title. MOVEMENTNAME Movement title. MOVEMENT Movement number. MOVEMENTTOTAL Number of movements; shares ID3v2 MVIN with MOVEMENT. WORK Name of the larger work, with a dedicated MP4 atom. SHOWMOVEMENT MP4 flag to request movement-oriented presentation: 1 or deletion.

docs.title: Identifiers and dates
docs.text: Field Meaning ACOUSTID_ID AcoustID identifier text. ACOUSTID_FINGERPRINT Stored acoustic fingerprint text; editing it does not calculate a fingerprint. BARCODE Release barcode. The baseline MusicBrainz and Discogs importers can supply it. CATALOGNUMBER Label/catalog identifier. The baseline MusicBrainz and Discogs importers can supply it. ISRC International Standard Recording Code for the recording. UNIQUEFILEID ID3v2 owner/identifier pair for text identifiers; MusicBrainz recording IDs use their dedicated field. ENCODINGTIME Time the content was encoded. RELEASETIME Release date/time. TAGGINGTIME Time associated with tagging. ORIGYEAR Original recording/release year or date representation. ORIGALBUM Original album title. ORIGARTIST Original performer credit. ORIGFILENAME Original filename stored as metadata; changing it does not rename the file. ORIGLYRICIST Original lyricist credit.

docs.title: MusicBrainz identifiers
docs.text: Field Meaning MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMARTISTID MusicBrainz artist ID(s) for the release credit. MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMID MusicBrainz release ID. MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMRELEASECOUNTRY Release country from MusicBrainz. MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMSTATUS Release status, for example official. MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMTYPE Release-group type information. MUSICBRAINZ_ARTISTID MusicBrainz artist ID(s) for the track credit. MUSICBRAINZ_DISCID MusicBrainz disc ID, distinct from a CDDB/freedb disc ID. MUSICBRAINZ_ORIGINALALBUMID Legacy/original album identifier field. MUSICBRAINZ_ORIGINALARTISTID Legacy/original artist identifier field. MUSICBRAINZ_RELEASEGROUPID MusicBrainz release-group ID, which groups related editions. MUSICBRAINZ_RELEASETRACKID MusicBrainz release-track ID, identifying the track on a particular release. MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID MusicBrainz recording ID; do not confuse it with RELEASETRACKID. MUSICBRAINZ_TRMID Legacy MusicBrainz TRM identifier. MUSICBRAINZ_WORKID MusicBrainz work ID(s).

docs.title: Ratings, lyrics, podcasts, and links
docs.text: Field Meaning POPULARIMETER ID3v2 raw rating-owner/counter representation. RATING MM MediaMonkey-style ID3v2 rating convenience field. RATING WMP Windows Media Player-style rating convenience field, also mapped in ASF. UNSYNCEDLYRICS Unsynchronized lyrics; ID3v2 uses language PODCAST Podcast flag; 1 or deletion in constrained native representations. PODCASTCATEGORY Podcast category. PODCASTDESC Podcast description. PODCASTID Podcast identifier. PODCASTKEYWORDS Podcast keywords. PODCASTURL Podcast feed/location URL. NETRADIOOWNER Internet radio owner information. NETRADIOSTATION Internet radio station name. WWW General user URL. WWWARTIST Artist URL. WWWAUDIOFILE URL for the audio file. WWWAUDIOSOURCE URL for its source. WWWCOMMERCIALINFO Commercial/purchase information URL. WWWCOPYRIGHT Copyright-information URL. WWWPAYMENT Payment URL. WWWPUBLISHER Publisher URL. WWWRADIOPAGE Radio station page URL.

docs.title: MP4 store, video, and totals
docs.text: Field Meaning DIRECTOR Director credit with a dedicated MP4 atom. ITUNESACCOUNT Store account identifier. ITUNESADVISORY Content advisory: 0 none, 1 explicit, 2 clean. ITUNESALBUMID Store album ID; MP4 accepts an unsigned 64-bit integer. ITUNESARTISTID Store artist ID. ITUNESCATALOGID Store catalog/content ID. ITUNESCOMPOSERID Store composer ID. ITUNESCOUNTRYID Store country/storefront ID. ITUNESGAPLESS Gapless-album flag: 1 or deletion; it does not re-encode audio. ITUNESGENREID Store genre ID. ITUNESHDVIDEO HD-video flag: 0 or 1. ITUNESMEDIATYPE Named MP4 media-type enumeration, listed below. ITUNESOWNER Store owner metadata. ITUNESPURCHASEDATE Purchase date text. RATE MP4 native rating integer, separate from ID3 POPM convenience fields. STOREDESCRIPTION Store description. TOTALDISCS MP4 total in the disk pair, separate from its current-disc component. TOTALTRACKS MP4 total in the trkn pair, separate from its current-track component. TVEPISODE Episode number; MP4 tves or Matroska video target type 50 PART_NUMBER. TVEPISODEID Episode identifier text. TVNETWORK Television network text. TVSEASON Season number; MP4 tvsn or Matroska video target type 60 PART_NUMBER. TVSHOW Show title. TVSHOWSORT Alternate sort text for the show.

docs.title: Flags and MP4 media types
docs.text:
For COMPILATION, PODCAST, ITUNESGAPLESS, and SHOWMOVEMENT in their constrained ID3/MP4 mappings, use 1 to enable or remove the field to disable. The writer rejects other values in those paths. ITUNESHDVIDEO separately accepts 0 or 1; ITUNESADVISORY accepts 0 (none), 1 (explicit), or 2 (clean).

ITUNESMEDIATYPE accepts these names, ignoring case: Normal, Audiobook, Bookmark, Music Video, Movie, TV Show, Booklet, Ringtone, Podcast, and iTunes U. This is a metadata classification; it does not convert the codec or container.

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
ID3v2 INVOLVEDPEOPLE and MUSICIANCREDITS use semicolon-separated role/person pairs, with a colon between role and person:

Drums:Mira Solberg;Bass:Kofi Reed;

Do not substitute an unstructured list of names when the role relationships matter. INVOLVEDPEOPLE maps to IPLS in v2.3 and TIPL in v2.4. MUSICIANCREDITS has the dedicated TMCL frame in v2.4; a field without a dedicated frame in the selected revision can use custom text storage instead.

docs.title: Ratings
docs.text:
POPULARIMETER represents ID3v2 POPM as owner|rating|counter. The counter is optional and defaults to 0. The historical documented rating range runs from 1 (lowest) to 255 (highest); OpenTag additionally accepts 0. Its parser accepts an unsigned byte for rating and an unsigned 64-bit counter.

listener@example.test|196|12

That is a raw byte rating, not a number of stars. With Options → Tags → Advanced → Always display POPULARIMETER values for ID3v2 ratings enabled, these raw values replace the app-specific convenience view after tags are reloaded.

RATING MM uses the MediaMonkey owner convention and accepts numeric star values or * for a star and - for a half star; **- means 2.5. RATING WMP accepts whole star values or * characters; **** means 4. In the documented star interpretation, 1 is the lowest and 5 the highest. Both writers accept 0–5, with half steps only for MM. Each convenience field allows one rating for its owner and preserves the existing counter when changing the rating.

These mappings describe OpenTag's stored representations. They do not establish current playback/display behavior in MediaMonkey or Windows Media Player. The MP4 RATE field is a separate native integer, not automatically the same rating scale.

docs.title: Lyrics, comments, and identifiers
docs.text:
For ID3v2 UNSYNCEDLYRICS, prefix the text with a three-letter ISO-639-2 language code and two vertical bars:

eng||Lanterns drift across the bay.

The example is invented text. ID3v2 stores one lyrics value per language and description. UNSYNCEDLYRICS Translation addresses a frame with description Translation; COMMENT Session similarly addresses a described comment. Editing plain COMMENT affects its undescribed frame, rather than deleting all described comments. A single ID3 comment description holds one value; use separate descriptions for separate comments. The language||text prefix is an ID3v2 representation, not a universal requirement for every lyrics field in every format.

For ID3v2 UNIQUEFILEID, use owner|identifier, with one text identifier per owner and at most 64 identifier bytes. The MusicBrainz owner http://musicbrainz.org belongs in MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID instead. Binary identifiers can remain preserved without being exposed as editable text.

docs.title: Numbers and dates
docs.text:
A native MP4 track/disc atom contains a number and total together. A TRACK value such as 3/8 supplies both. TOTALTRACKS or TOTALDISCS can address the total separately; inconsistent simultaneous totals are rejected. The native pair uses unsigned 16-bit values. Do not assume these MP4 total fields are universally split out of an ID3 track string.

MOVEMENT and MOVEMENTTOTAL share ID3v2 MVIN as number/total. ID3v2.4 timestamp fields such as YEAR, RELEASETIME, ENCODINGTIME, and TAGGINGTIME require a timestamp the native writer can parse. A field-name change alone does not turn arbitrary date text into that representation.

docs.title: Custom fields
docs.text:
The fixed vocabulary is not the complete set of editable fields. Add a descriptive custom name such as LISTENING_CONTEXT when a supported format allows it. ID3v2 normally uses user-text frames, MP4 uses freeform atoms, APE/Vorbis retain their own names, and ASF keeps attributes. RIFF INFO has stricter four-character identifiers; arbitrary long custom names do not automatically gain an INFO entry.

Names must be nonempty and cannot contain NUL or line breaks. Vorbis names also cannot contain =. Values cannot contain NUL. The tag-panel editor applies its own additional validation and does not offer arbitrary technical _ fields as editable metadata.

An empty-looking field and a missing field can filter differently before saving; see Filter presence rules. Removing a field is the reliable way to request absence where a boolean convention requires deletion.

docs.title: Special action targets versus information fields
docs.text:
Some action types interpret these names as selectors or rename requests. They are not ordinary custom text fields, and not every action supports every selector.

Target Meaning in supporting actions _TAG Apply to metadata field values. This is separate from %_tag%, which reports tag-format information. _ALL Apply to tag values and the filename in text-transform actions that support that combination. It is not a promise to transform directories or binary covers. _FILENAME Request a filename transformation. Extension handling depends on the action type; inspect its preview/result before applying. _DIRECTORY Request a directory transformation. In the tag panel this special control instead acts as a folder switcher. _FIELDNAME Transform field names, only for APE/Vorbis-style names. The result must remain nonempty and cannot collide case-insensitively with another field.

Technical placeholders such as %_length%, %_bitrate%, and %_path% describe the file or application context. They are covered in Placeholders. Creating a custom LENGTH tag changes stored metadata, not the actual duration.

OpenTag also exposes CHAPTERS for supported MP4/Matroska chapter editing and CUESHEET for embedded cue-sheet content. These require their specific syntax and supported format; a custom field with that name is not automatically a chapter implementation in another container.

docs.title: Supported file formats
docs.text:
OpenTag reads and edits metadata in the formats below. The audio codec describes how samples are encoded; the container holds that stream and its tags. AAC and ALAC inside an MP4/M4A file therefore use MP4 metadata, while a raw .aac stream uses the ID3/APE policy.

New to this?

Identify the file's actual format and tag type before choosing fields or compatibility settings. Renaming .flac to .mp3 does not convert the audio or its metadata.

docs.title: Read, write, and remove capabilities
docs.text:
Read describes exposed metadata. Write describes supported tag output, not a request to create every listed tag type. Remove describes types the applicable removal policy can strip. MPEG and APE-family policies under Options → Tags choose the actual read/write/remove sets.

Format Folder-scan extensions Read Write Remove AAC, raw ADTS .aac ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 AIFF / AIFC .aif, .aiff, .aifc ID3v2 ID3v2 ID3v2 Monkey's Audio .ape ID3v1, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 DSF .dsf ID3v2 ID3v2 ID3v2 DSDIFF, an OpenTag addition .dff ID3v2 plus available DIIN artist/title ID3v2; synchronize existing DIIN artist/title ID3v2 and supported DIIN tag text FLAC .flac Vorbis Comments Vorbis Comments Vorbis Comments and prepended ID3v2 Matroska audio/video .mka, .mkv Matroska tags, supported chapters, image attachments Same supported structures Global tags, supported chapter structures/tags, image attachments; see limits below MPEG audio .mp1, .mp2, .mp3 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 MP4 family, including AAC/ALAC audio .mp4, .m4a, .m4b, .m4v, .m4p MP4/iTunes metadata; supported chapters separately MP4/iTunes metadata; supported chapter editing MP4/iTunes metadata; use the chapter operation for explicit chapter removal Musepack .mpc, .mp+, .mpp ID3v1, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 Ogg Vorbis .ogg, .oga Vorbis Comments Vorbis Comments Vorbis Comments Opus .opus Vorbis-style comments Vorbis-style comments Vorbis-style comments OptimFROG / DualStream .ofr, .ofs ID3v1, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 Speex .spx Vorbis-style comments Vorbis-style comments Vorbis-style comments TAK .tak ID3v1, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 True Audio .tta ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 WAV .wav, .wave RIFF INFO and ID3v2 RIFF INFO and ID3v2 RIFF INFO and ID3v2 WavPack .wv ID3v1, APEv1/v2 ID3v1, APEv2 ID3v1, ID3v2, APEv1/v2 Windows Media / ASF .wma, .asf ASF/Windows Media attributes ASF/Windows Media attributes Non-stream-specific editable attributes and cover metadata; stream-specific attributes can remain WebM .webm Matroska-family tags, supported chapters, image attachments Same supported structures Same Matroska-family removal behavior

ALAC is Apple Lossless audio carried in the MP4 family, not a second tag format requiring a standalone .alac scan extension. Likewise, a video track inside MP4, Matroska, or WebM does not turn this into a video-editing or transcoding application.

The table includes every extension admitted by the baseline's default folder scanner. Explicitly adding a file or changing the incoming extension restriction can attempt other suffixes, but does not add a parser for a different format. .wmv, for example, is not scanned by default; an explicitly added file with actual ASF content can use the ASF reader. File contents are checked, so a permitted extension alone is insufficient.

docs.title: Tag families and priorities
docs.text:
The Mpeg policy serves MPEG audio, raw AAC, and TTA. When several enabled tags are present, APE takes priority over ID3v2, then ID3v1. OpenTag displays one type rather than merging values from every block.

The Ape, Mpc policy serves Monkey's Audio, Musepack, WavPack, TAK, and OptimFROG. APE takes priority over ID3v1. An ID3v2 prefix in these files can remain physically present even though this reading policy does not display it; choose its removal explicitly if needed.

Saving can synchronize written types from the displayed values and remove a type selected for removal but not writing. Keep a copy before changing policies on files that intentionally contain conflicting tag blocks. ID3v1 is especially limited: it cannot preserve arbitrary long text, custom fields, multiple values, or embedded images. APEv1 reading does not mean new writes stay APEv1; the writer normally emits APEv2.

ID3v2.3 UTF-16 is the default MPEG write representation, with v2.4 UTF-8 and legacy v2.3 Latin-1 available. An existing ID3v2 tag in non-MPEG containers follows that format's preservation rules rather than being blindly converted by the MPEG checkbox. DSF/DFF preserve an existing revision; a new tag uses the configured revision. Test the actual player/device before choosing a non-Unicode representation.

docs.title: Artwork
docs.text:
Metadata family Artwork behavior ID3v2 Embedded picture frames; available in supported MPEG, AIFF, DSF/DFF, WAV, and other ID3 paths. ID3v1 No embedded artwork capacity. Enable a richer write type when adding covers. APEv2 Embedded APE cover items. FLAC / Vorbis-style comments Format-specific embedded picture representation. MP4 covr artwork. ASF WM/Picture attributes. Matroska / WebM Attachments with an image MIME type; non-image attachments such as fonts are separate. RIFF INFO No arbitrary embedded-cover field; a WAV can carry artwork in ID3v2.

A picture displayed from the containing folder is not evidence of an embedded image. The tag-panel fallback can show a local image when the file has no cover. Import or embed it explicitly if it must travel inside the audio file.

docs.title: Chapters and cue sheets
docs.text:
Supported MP4 and Matroska chapters appear through CHAPTERS and chapter information. Enable Options → Tags → Advanced → List chapters as separate files, then reload the directory, to show supported subsongs as rows. At least two chapters are needed for row expansion in the inspected implementation. These rows reference one parent file; they are not split audio files.

Supported sources also include ID3v2 CHAP frames and embedded CUESHEET content. Loading a standalone cue sheet can list its tracks. %_subsong% is the zero-based index and %_subsong_count% the count. Metadata common to every chapter row can be stored at file level; differing values use supported per-chapter storage.

MP4 reads Nero and QuickTime chapter representations, preferring Nero when both exist. Tools → Strip chapters MP4… explicitly removes supported chapter references/structures. This is separate from removing ordinary MP4 tag atoms; unreferenced chapter text bytes can remain in media storage after stripping, so it is not a secure-erasure operation.

For supported MP4/Matroska chapter-list edits, a CHAPTERS value has a time and title, such as 00:00:00.000 Opening. Other containers do not gain chapter support by adding arbitrary text called CHAPTERS.

docs.title: Technical information
docs.text:
OpenTag reports available format, codec, duration, bitrate, sample rate, channels/mode, file size, and tag information. Bit depth is meaningful where the stream provides it; a lossy codec does not acquire a valid PCM bit-depth measurement merely because a custom tag contains a number. Video/container-specific information is supplied where the reader can measure it.

Metadata fields such as LENGTH, FILETYPE, or ENCODERSETTINGS do not change the measured stream properties. Use information placeholders when filtering or exporting actual measurements. Missing or unavailable properties should remain unknown rather than being inferred from an extension.

docs.title: FLAC with prepended ID3v2
docs.text: OpenTag reads the native Vorbis Comments and hides an unexpected prepended ID3v2 tag. A subsequent FLAC metadata write strips that prefix while preserving the FLAC stream through the supported write path. Hidden ID3 information is therefore not guaranteed to remain after an unrelated edit. Back up a nonstandard file before normalizing it.

docs.title: Raw streams and unusual tag layouts
docs.text:
Raw .aac detection accepts up to 64 KiB of padding or junk after leading ID3v2 tags, followed by three consecutive compatible ADTS frames. This search applies only to .aac and stops at an MPEG audio frame. Recognized streams use the applicable APE/ID3v1 options and retain the intervening bytes. Malformed headers or data outside that bound can still be refused.

TAK and OptimFROG tag paths do not decode/re-encode the audio. Existing tests use specification-built streams and independent probes; real original-encoder/device qualification is separate. OptimFROG DualStream uses the same recognized OFR header and codec label in this implementation.

Footer-only APEv2 tags are read without treating the preceding 32 audio bytes as a header; an internal TAG sequence is not an ID3v1 tag. APE tags left untouched by the selected write policy retain their bytes. Some other unusual APE footer/header layouts and compressed/encrypted ID3 frames have additional restrictions. Unsupported encrypted-frame revision conversion is refused to keep the original file. A successful read is not a promise that every malformed or encrypted structure can be rewritten.

docs.title: MP4 metadata preservation
docs.text:
MP4 iTunes fields take precedence over Nero metadata; Nero supplies missing values. Editing or deleting a mapped field also updates or removes its existing Nero copy. OpenTag does not add newly created fields to the Nero set. For a file without chapters, an edited value too long for its existing Nero space is written to iTunes only; the older Nero value remains hidden by iTunes precedence.

Nero artwork is displayed when iTunes artwork is absent. A cover edit writes the result to iTunes artwork and removes the Nero copy, even if it was hidden. Ordinary text-field edits preserve that artwork copy. Unrelated udta/indx data is retained but is not exposed for editing.

Nonstandard plID items survive unrelated edits. Values of 1–8 bytes can appear as ITUNESALBUMID; editing that field writes the standard 8-byte representation. These constructed-fixture checks do not certify every original Nero or Mp3tag version’s output. Keep copies of unusual files and inspect saved tags in the receiving application.

docs.title: DSD
docs.text: DSF metadata uses its terminal ID3v2 area. DSF and DSDIFF can preserve unedited compressed or opaque encrypted ID3v2 frames byte for byte. That does not decrypt them; unsynchronization, extended headers, footers and merged duplicate frames still limit preservation. DSDIFF can additionally supply DIIN artist/title when ID3 lacks them. Duplicate DSDIFF ID3 chunks are refused for field/cover writes instead of being silently merged; removal can still handle them. A DST index can prevent edits that would move indexed sound data. These are container restrictions, not a request to decode DSD audio to PCM.

docs.title: Matroska and WebM
docs.text:
Tag target levels matter: the same native name can represent a track, album, disc, or episode depending on its target. Use recommended mapping for Matroska video changes that interpretation when an actual video track exists. The mapping reference details the levels.

Global tags, supported chapter tags, and image attachments can be edited without treating unrelated track/edition metadata or fonts as disposable. Remove tag preserves non-image attachments and unrelated scoped metadata while removing supported global/chapter metadata and images. The Segment Info Title is a different structure from a mapped TITLE tag and is not exposed as that field by this baseline.

Live/unknown-sized cluster layouts can be read through their metadata index but are refused for writing. A SeekHead without space for the updated metadata index can also make a write fail with the original preserved. Uninterpreted edition/segment chapter relationships are not a promise of full authoring support for every Matroska feature.

docs.title: ASF and protected files
docs.text:
ASF can contain attributes with binary types, language/stream scope, and values larger than 64 KiB. OpenTag preserves opaque structures it cannot expose as text; Remove tag intentionally does not mean erasing every ASF object. Older consuming readers may omit large Metadata Library values even when the file remains valid. Test long lyrics or large covers in the target player.

An extension such as .m4p, or encryption objects in ASF, does not establish DRM support. Editing a container's visible metadata cannot remove protection or guarantee protected playback. Damaged metadata, unsupported encrypted layouts, read-only sources, and access-provider restrictions can prevent a write even when the general family is listed.

docs.title: Platform and verification scope
docs.text:
The portable metadata core uses the same family parsers across supported builds. Access to a file is a separate requirement: mobile document providers can lack ordinary filesystem paths or permissions used by desktop folder, rename, and external-tool workflows. Consult the installed app's source-access message rather than assuming desktop filesystem operations apply to a provider URI.

This table is checked against the baseline source and relevant format tests, not a claim that every listed format has been exercised on every released platform or compared with the original Mp3tag executable. Tag editing does not establish playback support; OpenTag can delegate playback to another application.

docs.title: Filter syntax
docs.text:
The installed OpenTag app evaluates these expressions in the Filter. A query selects matching rows from the loaded file list; it does not edit metadata or scan folders that have not been loaded.

New to this?

Follow Filtering the file list for showing the Filter, applying a query, restoring all rows, and interpreting errors.

docs.title: Ordinary text search
docs.text:
An empty query matches every loaded file. A nonempty query without uppercase filter keywords is a plain search. Each word, separated by the ordinary space character, must occur as a substring in some tag value or the filename. Matching ignores case. Words may occur in different fields or in different values of a multi-value field.

Juniper Harbour can match an artist containing Juniper and an album containing Harbour. The same words in another order have the same all-words requirement. Punctuation is literal in plain search, including parentheses, brackets, and *; a regular expression is used only with MATCHES.

Plain search includes metadata values plus the filename with extension. It excludes other technical values such as bitrate and full folder path. * HAS text searches tag values only, so it can differ from plain search when the text occurs only in the filename.

docs.title: Expression grammar
docs.text:
Form Question answered field HAS text Does every word in text occur somewhere among this field's values? field IS text Does at least one complete value equal text? field MATCHES regexp Does at least one value match the regular expression? field GREATER integer Is a value's leading integer greater than the threshold? field LESS integer Is a value's leading integer smaller than the threshold? field EQUAL integer Is a value's leading integer equal to the threshold? field PRESENT Does the field supply at least one value, including an empty string? field MISSING Does the field supply no values? field ABSENT Alias of MISSING. NOT expression Invert the result. expression AND expression Require both results. expression OR expression Require either result. (expression) Group conditions explicitly.

Keywords must be uppercase. Field names and text comparisons ignore case. The all-tag-fields selector * is supported only with HAS and MATCHES; * IS x and * PRESENT are invalid. It excludes technical names beginning with _ and does not add the filename.

IS compares individual values. If ARTIST has Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg, ARTIST IS "Juniper Vale" succeeds. It does not compare a separator-joined display string. HAS can find its different words across those values.

docs.title: Boolean precedence
docs.text:
The order is NOT, then AND, then OR. Parentheses override it.

GENRE IS Ambient OR GENRE IS Folk AND TITLE HAS Live

This means Ambient files, plus Folk files whose title contains Live. To require Live for both genres, write:

(GENRE IS Ambient OR GENRE IS Folk) AND TITLE HAS Live

An uppercase boolean word occurring as data must be quoted: TITLE IS "AND OR NOT". Lowercase and is ordinary text, not an alternate spelling of the operator.

docs.title: Quote operands
docs.text:
Use one pair of double quotes around a field name or text containing spaces, such as "RATING WMP" PRESENT or ARTIST IS "Juniper Vale". Unquoted simple multiword operands are accepted in some positions, but quoting avoids accidental interpretation of uppercase keywords and grouping punctuation. Quote the complete operand, rather than combining quoted and unquoted fragments.

The filter's quoted strings have no escape sequence for an embedded double quote. A backslash inside a quoted string does not turn the next quote into literal data. To find a quotation mark in a field, use an unquoted regex operand:

TITLE MATCHES \"

Or build the character through a quoted format string:

"$ifgreater($strstr(%title%,$char(34)),0,yes,no)" IS yes

The outer quotes belong to the filter. $char(34) produces the quotation mark inside the evaluated format string. Apostrophes inside scripting expressions have the scripting language's own rules; they do not replace the Filter's double-quote grouping.

docs.title: Format strings on the left
docs.text:
For HAS, IS, GREATER, LESS, EQUAL, or MATCHES, an operand containing $ or % is evaluated as a format string instead of a literal field name. Enclose it in double quotes:

"%_bitrate%" GREATER 300

The selector can combine placeholders and scripting functions. Its result is one comparison value, which can behave differently from comparing a multi-value field directly. Missing placeholders normally evaluate to empty text, so "%albumartist%" IS "" can match a missing field even though ALBUMARTIST IS "" does not.

Presence tests require a field name, not a calculation. A simple %albumartist% MISSING spelling is accepted as a field reference; $len(...) PRESENT is invalid. Prefer the clearer ALBUMARTIST MISSING.

Evaluated selectors do more work per file than a direct field comparison. Use a direct field when it expresses the same question, especially on a large loaded collection. Available information fields and context-dependent functions are described in Placeholders and Format strings.

docs.title: Numeric comparisons
docs.text:
The threshold is a signed 64-bit integer. Decimal or duration syntax such as 3.5 or 3:30 is rejected. The field value is interpreted by its leading signed integer after leading whitespace; subsequent text is ignored:

Stored value Numeric part 03/08 3 2024-03-15 2024 128.6 128 -6 dB -6 B2 None; it does not satisfy a numeric comparison.

This differs from comparing complete text with IS. TRACK EQUAL 3 can match 03/08, while TRACK IS 3 does not. It does not extract the total 8. An excessively long digit run in a stored value saturates to the positive/negative numeric bound; it does not wrap around. A threshold outside the signed 64-bit range is invalid.

docs.title: Presence, missing values, and empty text
docs.text:
Field snapshot FIELD PRESENT FIELD MISSING FIELD IS "" No field No Yes No Field with no values No Yes No One value containing empty text Yes No Yes One nonempty value Yes No No

The app's save paths can remove empty metadata rather than preserving this exact in-memory distinction. Inspect the values being filtered, including pending edits, before assuming an empty-looking control proves a missing on-disk field.

docs.title: Regular expressions
docs.text:
MATCHES uses the same Boost-based engine as OpenTag scripting, with case-insensitive matching by default. It finds a match anywhere unless anchors such as ^ and $ constrain it. Quote a complete pattern when it contains spaces or filter grouping syntax. The word MATCH is rejected, rather than treated as another regex operator.

TRACK MATCHES "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$"

This finds a track/total pair of digits. A plain \d/\d searches for that shape anywhere and can also match a fragment of a longer value. Consult the regex reference for escaping, grouping, assertions, and engine limits.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
The examples below use four invented snapshots. Missing means no field; empty means one empty string. The display names A–D are for explaining results, not field values.

Row ARTIST values TITLE GENRE TRACK YEAR ALBUMARTIST Bitrate Filename A Juniper Vale Harbour Lights Indie Folk 01/08 2024 Missing 320 01 - Harbour Lights.flac B Juniper Vale Paper Boats (Live) Folk 2/8 2024-03-15 Juniper Vale 256 02 - Paper Boats.mp3 C Mira Solberg; Juniper Vale North "Wind" Ambient 10 2023 Mira Solberg 1411 10 - North Wind.flac D The Lanterns Low Tide Folk B2 Empty Missing 128 bonus.flac

A and B also have ALBUM=Harbour Lights; C has ALBUM=Night Harbour. D has no ALBUM.

Query Matching rows Why harbour vale A, B, C All words can be found across fields/values. flac A, C, D Ordinary search includes the filename extension. * HAS flac None These tag values do not contain flac. ARTIST HAS Juniper Vale A, B, C Both words occur among artist values. ARTIST IS "Juniper Vale" A, B, C One complete artist value is enough. TITLE IS "Harbour Lights" A Compare the complete value. GENRE IS Folk AND NOT TITLE HAS Live D Exclude the live Folk title. GENRE IS Ambient OR GENRE IS Folk AND TITLE HAS Live B, C AND binds more tightly than OR. (GENRE IS Ambient OR GENRE IS Folk) AND TITLE HAS Live B Grouping changes which files must be live. TRACK GREATER 8 C 10 exceeds 8; B2 has no leading integer. TRACK LESS 3 A, B The leading track numbers are 1 and 2. TRACK EQUAL 2 B 2/8 compares numerically as 2. YEAR EQUAL 2024 A, B The leading year of a full date is 2024. "%_bitrate%" GREATER 300 A, C Evaluate a technical placeholder before comparing. ALBUMARTIST MISSING A, D No values exist for this field. ALBUMARTIST ABSENT A, D ABSENT has the same result as MISSING. ALBUMARTIST PRESENT B, C An artist value is present. YEAR PRESENT A, B, C, D Even the explicit empty string is a value. YEAR IS "" D Only D has a present, empty year value. ALBUMARTIST IS "" None Missing is not a stored empty value. "%albumartist%" IS "" A, D A missing placeholder evaluates to empty text. TRACK MATCHES "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$" A, B Require the whole value to be digits/digits. TITLE MATCHES \" C Find a literal quotation mark. "$ifgreater($strstr(%title%,$char(34)),0,yes,no)" IS yes C Compute whether the title contains a quotation mark.

docs.title: Errors and limits
docs.text:
Invalid syntax, an invalid regular expression, or an unavailable scripting context is reported as a filter error. Correct it rather than interpreting the empty view as a valid no-match result. The parser also rejects overly large queries (more than 1 MiB), more than 8,192 tokens, or excessive nesting (depth limit 128). Regex evaluation has its own limits.

These are OpenTag source-verified rules. They do not establish identical corner-case results in the original Mp3tag executable, in another regex engine, or in OpenTag's simplified browser preview.

docs.title: Format strings
docs.text:
A format string is a line of text with blanks in it. For each file, OpenTag fills the blanks with that file's values: %artist% - %title% becomes Juniper Vale - Low Tide for one file and Juniper Vale - Paper Boats for the next.

You write format strings to rename files, to build new tag values from old ones, to define columns, to name exports and playlists, and in many other places. This page is the complete reference for the language: every character with a special meaning, how conditions decide, and how file and folder names are made safe.

New to this?

Start with Your first tagging session to try a naming pattern on a practice album. Use this reference when you need a syntax detail.

All examples on this page use track 2 of the guide's example album, unless a row says otherwise:

Field Value TITLE Lanterns on the Water ARTIST, ALBUMARTIST Juniper Vale ALBUM Harbour Lights YEAR 2024 TRACK 2/8 GENRE Indie Folk DISCNUMBER (not set)

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Syntax Meaning Example Result plain text Copied as it is Live at Live at %field% The field's value (placeholder) %artist% Juniper Vale %_name% Information about the file %_extension% mp3 $function(…) A scripting function $upper(%album%) HARBOUR LIGHTS […] Optional section: dropped when its fields are empty %album%[ (%year%)] Harbour Lights (2024) '…' Quoted text: everything inside is literal '%artist%' %artist% '' One apostrophe %artist%''s best Juniper Vale's best \ or / A folder level (only where the result is a file name) %artist%\%album% folder Juniper Vale, then Harbour Lights

docs.title: Where you use format strings
docs.text:
The same language works everywhere. Only what happens to the result differs.

Where The result becomes Tag → Filename The new file name, and folders if it contains \ Tag → Tag and the Format value action The new value of a field, or a new file or folder name for _FILENAME and _DIRECTORY Columns (Value) The text shown in that column Copy as Text One line per file on the clipboard Export, playlists Output file names, partitions and extended playlist info Cover actions (import, export), Import text file, Text File → Tag The name of the file to read or write Guess values (source) The text that the guessing pattern takes apart External tools (parameter) The argument passed to the tool Filter (left side of an operator) The value that is compared

Two more places look similar but work the other way round: Filename → Tag and Guess values read values out of text with a pattern. See Patterns at the end of this page.

docs.title: Plain text
docs.text: Anything that isn't one of the special characters % $ [ ] ' is copied unchanged, spaces included. Inside a function's brackets, , and ) are special too (see Special characters).

docs.title: Placeholders: %field%
docs.text:
%name% is replaced by the value of the field called name:

  • Any field works. There is no fixed list: %mood%, %catalognumber%, %my own field% all work if the file has that field.
  • Case doesn't matter. %Artist%, %ARTIST% and %artist% are the same.
  • A missing field gives empty text. %discnumber% on a file without a disc number gives nothing, not an error and not the text %discnumber%.
  • Multi-value fields give their first value. A file with two artists, Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg, gives Juniper Vale for %artist%. Use $meta to get all of them.
  • Names starting with _ are information about the file, not tag fields: %_filename%, %_bitrate%, %_length%, %_covers% and about sixty more. They are all listed on the Placeholders page.

%% (an empty name) and an unclosed %title are errors.

docs.title: Scripting functions: $name(…)
docs.text:
A function takes arguments, separated by commas, and returns text:

$left(%title%,8)

gives Lanterns. Functions nest. Each argument is itself a format string:

$upper($left(%title%,8))

gives LANTERNS.

  • Function names are not case-sensitive: $cutLeft and $cutleft are the same.
  • Arguments are not trimmed. In $replace(%title%, on, at) the search text is ·on (with a leading space). Write $replace(%title%,on,at) unless you mean the spaces.
  • An unknown function name, or the wrong number of arguments, is an error that the preview shows before anything is changed.

Scripting functions cover text, case, numbers, dates, conditions, regular expressions and multi-value fields. The examples below show common uses.

docs.title: Optional sections: […]
docs.text:
Square brackets mark a part that should disappear when it has nothing to say. A section is kept when at least one placeholder inside it has a value, and dropped completely, with its text, when none has:

Format string With these values Result %album%[ (%year%)] YEAR = 2024 Harbour Lights (2024) %album%[ (%year%)] YEAR not set Harbour Lights [CD%discnumber% - ]%title% DISCNUMBER not set Lanterns on the Water [CD%discnumber% - ]%title% DISCNUMBER = 2 CD2 - Lanterns on the Water [%artist% & %albumartist%] ARTIST set, ALBUMARTIST not set Juniper Vale & [(live)] anything (empty)

Things to know:

  • "Has a value" means a placeholder inside produced text. In the fifth row, ARTIST is enough to keep the section. Its text is kept even though ALBUMARTIST is empty. To require both, use $and with $if.
  • A section with only plain text is always dropped, because no placeholder in it has a value. Write plain text outside brackets.
  • Functions count through their arguments. [CD$num(%discnumber%,1)] is dropped when DISCNUMBER is empty, even though $num would have returned 0.
  • Sections can be nested: [%album%[ (%year%)] - ]%title%.
  • Commas and brackets inside a section that sits in a function argument are plain text: in $upper([%year%, ]%album%) the comma does not end the argument.

docs.title: Quoted text: '…'
docs.text:
Text between apostrophes is copied exactly, special characters included:

Format string Result '[%year%]' [%year%] '['%year%'] '%album% [2024] Harbour Lights '100% '%genre% 100% Indie Folk %artist%''s favourites Juniper Vale's favourites 'Rock ''n'' roll' Rock 'n' roll

'' (two apostrophes) gives one apostrophe, both inside and outside a quoted part. An apostrophe that is never closed is an error ("Unterminated quoted literal").

Gotcha: apostrophes in plain text

A single ' in your text starts a quoted part. %artist%'s best is an error, because the quote never closes. Write %artist%''s best. Values that contain apostrophes, such as a title The Keeper's Song, are fine: only what you type in the format string is parsed.

docs.title: Special characters
docs.text:
These characters mean something. To get them as plain text, quote them.

Character Special meaning Write it literally as % Starts and ends a placeholder '%' $ Starts a function '$' [ ] Optional section '[' ']' ' Starts and ends quoted text '' , Separates function arguments (only inside a function's brackets) ',' ) Ends a function (only inside a function's brackets) ')' ( Nothing: always plain text ( \ / A folder level, when the result is a file name _ or another character (see file names)

Backslash is not an escape character in format strings. \% is a backslash followed by the start of a placeholder.

Gotcha: ) and , inside function arguments

$replace(%title%, (Interlude),) doesn't do what it looks like: the ) after Interlude ends the function early, and OpenTag reports the wrong number of arguments. Quote the text that contains it:

$replace(%title%,' (Interlude)',)

Fog Horn (Interlude) becomes Fog Horn. The same applies to commas: $replace(%artist%,' & ',', ') turns Kofi & the Tidewater Band into Kofi, the Tidewater Band.

docs.title: True and false: how conditions decide
docs.text:
Functions such as $if, $if2, $and, $or and $not test whether something is true. OpenTag doesn't treat text like 1 or yes as true. Truth comes from where a value came from:

  • A placeholder is true when the field has a value, and false when it is missing or empty.
  • Plain text is never true, not even 1.
  • Comparison functions are true or false by their answer: $eql, $neql, $grtr, $geql, $less, $leql, $strcmp, $stricmp, $and, $or, $not, $odd, $isdigit.
  • Most other functions are true when any of their arguments is, so $upper(%title%) is true when TITLE has a value.
Format string With these values Result $if(%year%,%year%,unknown year) YEAR = 2024 2024 $if(%year%,%year%,unknown year) YEAR not set unknown year $if(1,yes,no) anything no $if($eql(%year%,2024),this year,older) YEAR = 2024 this year $if2(%albumartist%,%artist%) ALBUMARTIST not set Juniper Vale (from ARTIST) $if($and(%artist%,%discnumber%),both,not both) DISCNUMBER not set not both

Gotcha: search functions return positions, not true or false

$strstr(%title%,Water) returns the position where Water starts (17), or 0 when it isn't found. Because %title% has a value, $if($strstr(%title%,Snow),yes,no) is true even though Snow isn't in the title. Compare the position instead:

$if($grtr($strstr(%title%,Snow),0),yes,no)

docs.title: Multi-value fields
docs.text:
A field can hold several values, for example two artists. A plain placeholder only gives the first one. These functions give you the rest:

Format string With ARTIST = Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg Result %artist% Juniper Vale $meta(artist) Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg $meta(artist,1) (counting starts at 0) Mira Solberg $meta_sep(artist,' & ') Juniper Vale & Mira Solberg

Note that $meta takes the field name, without %. In the tag panel and the file list, OpenTag shows multiple values joined with \\. A bare placeholder does not add that display separator; choose a join explicitly with $meta_sep when needed. Storage of multiple values depends on the tag format.

docs.title: Write separate values with Format Value or Tag → Tag
docs.text:
When writing an ordinary metadata field, Format Value and Convert → Tag → Tag… split their evaluated result at two consecutive backslashes (\\). Each component is trimmed and empty components are dropped. If no values remain, the destination field is removed. Without that delimiter, a nonempty result stays one value with its surrounding whitespace intact. A single backslash is ordinary text.

For example, Rock\\Pop stores two values, Rock and Pop. $meta_sep(artist,\\) preserves separate existing artists in this writing context; $meta_sep(artist,' & ') creates one joined value. These are output rules for those metadata-writing commands, not a general change to what scripting functions return. Filename and directory destinations use their path rules instead. See the Format Value examples for delimiter, whitespace and empty-result cases.

docs.title: Numbers inside text
docs.text:
Numeric functions skip leading whitespace, read a signed integer prefix, and ignore the rest. TRACK = 2/8 counts as 2, a year of 2024-05-01 counts as 2024, and -3 remains negative. Text without a leading integer, such as B2, counts as 0. These functions use integer arithmetic; a decimal such as 2.9 contributes 2.

Format string With these values Result $num(%track%,2) TRACK = 2/8 02 $num(%track%,3) TRACK = 2/8 002 $add(%track%,10) TRACK = 2/8 12 $num(%track%,2) TRACK = B2 (a vinyl side) 00 $num(-3,3) anything -03 $num(' 3/8',2) anything 03

Use $num for padding and arithmetic functions such as $add for calculations.

docs.title: File and folder names
docs.text:
When the result of a format string is a file name (in Tag → Filename, and in Format value or Tag → Tag on _FILENAME or _DIRECTORY), OpenTag applies three extra rules.

1. \ and / that you type make folders. Both work on every platform, and OpenTag uses the right one for your system. The path is relative to the file's current folder, unless it starts at the root of a drive.

%artist%\%album%\$num(%track%,2) - %title%

moves track 2 into Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/ under its current folder, as 02 - Lanterns on the Water.mp3.

2. \ and / from ordinary metadata values are replaced, so an artist or album value does not create a folder by accident. The replacement is _ unless changed under Options → Files → Replace folder separator in tag values with. Native path placeholders are exceptions: %_path%, %_folderpath% and %_workingpath% can supply folder components in filename mode. A selected conditional branch retains that path provenance too; other derived function results still follow the ordinary value-cleaning rule. Action filenames preserve native path characters from those placeholders, including a literal backslash inside a Unix folder name. Tag → Filename normalizes separators across its final generated path instead; that same backslash is treated as a folder boundary there.

3. Characters that file systems reject are replaced with _. These are : * ? " < > | and control characters, and the rule applies to values only. Characters you type yourself are kept.

Format string With these values Result %artist%\%title% ARTIST = AC/DC, TITLE = Live: Encore AC_DC\Live_ Encore $replace(%artist%,/,-)\%title% ARTIST = AC/DC AC-DC\… %genre%\%artist% Replace folder separator set to - , GENRE = Folk/Rock Folk - Rock\Juniper Vale [CD$num(%discnumber%,1)\]%title% DISCNUMBER = 2 CD2\Lanterns on the Water [CD$num(%discnumber%,1)\]%title% DISCNUMBER not set Lanterns on the Water $if(%discnumber%,CD%discnumber%\,)%title% DISCNUMBER = 2 CD2\Lanterns on the Water $upper('a/b') anything A_B

A few more details:

  • Conditions keep your folders. The branch that $if, $if2, $ifgreater or $iflonger returns keeps the \ you typed in it, as the sixth row shows. Other functions treat their result as a value, so in the last row the / inside $upper(…) becomes _.
  • The extension is kept. OpenTag adds the file's extension, unless your result already ends with it, so %title%.mp3 doesn't become .mp3.mp3.
  • An empty result is an error. Nothing is renamed.

Coming from Mp3tag

Mp3tag on Windows uses \ for folders. OpenTag accepts \ and / on macOS, Linux and Windows alike, so action groups and format strings you bring along keep working.

docs.title: Patterns: reading values out of text
docs.text:
Filename → Tag and Guess values use format strings in reverse. You describe what the text looks like, and OpenTag works out the values.

%track% - %artist% - %title%

applied to the file name 03 - Juniper Vale - Paper Boats.mp3 sets TRACK to 03, ARTIST to Juniper Vale and TITLE to Paper Boats.

Patterns have their own, simpler rules:

  • Only placeholders and plain text. Functions, […] and quotes have no special meaning in a pattern.
  • The whole name must match, from start to end. If it doesn't, the file is reported and left unchanged.
  • %dummy% matches text that you want to skip.
  • Each placeholder matches as little as possible. With %artist% - %title%, the name Juniper Vale - Salt - Cedar gives ARTIST = Juniper Vale and TITLE = Salt - Cedar.
  • Two placeholders right next to each other (%track%%title%) are an error, because OpenTag can't know where one ends.
  • The same placeholder twice adds a second value: %artist% feat. %artist% gives a multi-value ARTIST.

Filename → Tag adds two rules for file names, which Guess values doesn't need:

  • The extension is left out, unless your pattern ends with it.
  • \ in a pattern matches folder levels: %artist%\%album%\%track% %title% reads the two folders above the file too. Use \ here on every platform.

For a worked folder pattern, see Tags from folder and file names.

docs.title: The ► helper menu and history
docs.text: Wherever you can type a format string, a ► button sits next to the input. Its menu inserts placeholders, technical fields and functions at the cursor, and remembers the format strings you used before. Open it from the keyboard with Ctrl+Space (Control on every platform; on a Mac, Ctrl+Option+Space also works). In the history list, Shift+Del removes the highlighted entry.

docs.title: Errors and limits
docs.text:
A format string that can't be read is reported when you preview it, and nothing is changed. The messages are:

Message Cause Fix Unterminated field placeholder A % without its closing % Close it, or write '%' for a percent sign Empty field placeholder %% Write '%' Unterminated quoted literal An odd number of ' Close the quote, or write '' for an apostrophe Unterminated optional section / Unexpected closing optional bracket Unbalanced [ ] Balance them, or quote them: '[' Expected function call after $… A $ not followed by a name and ( Write '$' for a dollar sign Unsupported scripting function: $… A misspelt or unknown function Check the function name in the ► helper menu $… expects n..=m arguments Too many or too few arguments, often from an unquoted , or ) Quote commas and brackets in arguments $replace requires complete search/replacement pairs An odd number of search and replace arguments Add the missing replacement (it may be empty)

Format strings can nest up to 128 levels deep and produce at most 1 MiB of text per file. You'll only reach these limits by accident, for example with a runaway $repeat.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Track number and title, with the disc number for multi-disc albums 
[$num(%discnumber%,1)-]$num(%track%,2) %title%
With these values Result DISCNUMBER not set, TRACK = 2/8 02 Lanterns on the Water DISCNUMBER = 2, TRACK = 5 2-05 Salt & Cedar Album artist folder with a fallback to the artist 
$if2(%albumartist%,%artist%)\%album%[ (%year%)]\$num(%track%,2) - %title%

Files without an album artist are filed under their artist; the year is added only when it is known. Track 2 becomes Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights (2024)/02 - Lanterns on the Water.mp3.

A-to-Z folders by the first letter of the artist 
$upper($left(%artist%,1))\%artist%\%album%

gives J/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights.

A column that flags tracks longer than five minutes

Use this as the Value of a custom column:

$ifgreater(%_length_seconds%,300,long,)

Harbour Lights (5:01) shows long; every other track shows nothing.
