  • Menus overview

docs.title: Tag Sources menu
docs.text: Tag sources propose release metadata and artwork for selected audio files. Select the files of one album, save pending edits, then choose a provider. A search result is a candidate: review the release, enabled fields and track matching before importing it.

docs.title: Built-in source commands
docs.text:
Item Purpose MusicBrainz… Search or look up a MusicBrainz release and review its fields/tracks Discogs… Search or look up a Discogs release Discogs Release ID… Open a specific release using its ID/address rather than a broad search freedb… Query the configured server by selected-file track layout, or search gnudb by artist and album freedb (local)… Search a configured local freedb database/index; Primary+L Covers: freedb (gnudb)… Search gnudb artwork without importing tag fields Covers: MusicBrainz… Look up artwork without importing tag fields Covers: Discogs… Look up artwork without importing tag fields Discogs access token… Configure the token used by the Discogs connection Options… Open the Tag Sources preferences

The remote freedb dialog offers Track layout of the selected files and Artist and album. Text and artwork searches require a recognized gnudb host. OpenTag asks for matches before reading the chosen entry; it does not read a remote entry from a typed disc ID.

The local database supports a disc ID derived from the selected files or typed directly, plus Artist and album words through its text index. These are lookups from files/identifiers; the dialog does not expose a physical-CD-drive selector.

Configure provider/server and local-index settings under Options → Tag Sources, freedb and Local freedb. Server availability, authentication and network policy still affect whether a live query succeeds. These menu entries do not certify that a remote service accepts every saved configuration.

docs.title: Last used source and quick search
docs.text:
Primary+I reopens the last used source, including an installed web source. The corresponding menu entry can show that shortcut. Primary+Shift+I requests a quick search for built-in sources using the selected album/artist or disc information. If the search returns one result, it can open that release without the result-list step. Review/import remains a separate decision; quick search is not a command to trust an arbitrary match.

An installed web script has its own search fields and is not the same quick built-in-provider route. Use its visible dialog when search details need editing. Primary means Ctrl on Windows/Linux and Command on macOS.

docs.title: Installed web sources
docs.text:
On desktop platforms with folder access, Install tag sources… copies supported source files into the configuration's sources folder. Open sources folder reveals it. Installed scripts and settings can create submenus; # in a source filename separates menu levels, and & marks an access key.

A source normally searches a page/API, lists releases, then parses the chosen release for review. It does not run page JavaScript as a browser would. Companion include/settings files can be required. Inspect the source's origin, configuration and output before using it on important tags. A script created for another application can need adaptation.

The original documentation's web-source archive provides further resource pointers. A listed script or provider is not a compatibility or availability guarantee for OpenTag.

docs.title: Match files before applying
docs.text:
For example, if two selected files are Paper Boats and Lanterns on the Water, choosing a release with the same album title is not enough. Check its edition, track count and order, and match those two file rows to the intended source tracks. Moving rows in source review changes matching, not file paths.

The enabled field set determines which proposed values are imported. Field selection and enabled state are separate. A covers-only command deliberately leaves tag fields alone. Read the Apply result and any per-file errors before assuming the entire selected album was updated.

Source review supports F2 to edit a field, Space to toggle enabled fields, Primary+A/Primary+Shift+A for selection and Primary+E/D to enable/disable all. Alt+Up/Down or Alt+Page Up/Down moves file rows for matching. See keyboard shortcuts for the complete focus rules.

docs.title: Tools menu
docs.text:
The Tools menu contains built-in metadata/container utilities, the tool configuration command and any external programs you have defined. A built-in utility writes through OpenTag's supported file path; a named external tool starts another program with its own behavior and completion rules.

Choose a workflow first

Use built-in utilities for stored tag/layout cleanup, or external tools for executable paths, parameters and selection scope. Neither route is an audio repair guarantee.

docs.title: Fixed menu items
docs.text:
The current built-in items appear in this order:

Item Result Scope and timing Remove tag types… Choose ID3v1, ID3v2 and/or APEv2 blocks to remove Writes selected supported local files when Remove is chosen; explicit types are independent of Options' Remove switches Strip chapters MP4… Remove the applicable MP4 chapter structure Whole-file immediate operation; normally confirms file/chapter count and leaves freed boxes Remove unsupported fields… Remove ID3v2 frames OpenTag does not display MP3/AAC/AIFF/WAV applicability; dialog explains applicable/skipped counts Optimize… Normalize FLAC padding or reorganize MP4 layout FLAC/MP4 applicability; writes only when a change is needed Configure tools… Open the Tools Options editor Saves definitions/preferences through the Options dialog; opening it does not launch a program

The four built-in utilities have no dedicated shortcuts displayed in this menu. The file-list context menu also groups them under Utils. Context placement does not turn them into actions or change their write/recovery scope.

Read tag removal before erasing a metadata block. Remove unsupported fields… is not a command to delete every custom field, and Optimize… does not re-encode audio or promise every player will read it. Chapters explains why stripping a parent file's chapters is different from editing one displayed chapter title.

docs.title: Configured program entries
docs.text:
Saved tool definitions are appended after the fixed items, separated from them. Each displays its saved Name and launches that definition. With no definitions, the menu explains that none exist and points to Configure tools…. Removing or reordering a definition changes this generated part of the menu; it does not install/uninstall the executable.

The first ten definitions display Cmd+1 through Cmd+0 on macOS or Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+0 on Windows/Linux. The tenth uses 0. Later tools remain available by menu selection without a displayed digit shortcut. Reordering changes which definition owns each numbered slot. These are tools' shortcuts, not the Alt-digit converter shortcuts.

For example, with a saved tool named Inspect track, choose Tools → Inspect track to run it. Its Path, Parameter and per-file checkbox determine what is prepared; the menu name is not a shell command. A custom toolbar may reference the same saved name while displaying a different button label. Distinct tool names make those references easier to maintain.

The Default tool (double-click in the file list) setting is separate from menu ordering. A chosen definition follows its current-selection/per-file rules on a row double-click. No action currently falls back to Extended tags in OpenTag; it does not make double-click inert. See tool configuration for that deliberate distinction.

docs.title: Selection and availability
docs.text:
Utilities require an applicable selection and supported mutation access. Selected pending edits must be resolved first; the unavailable-command reason can say Save pending changes first. Mixed-format utility selections may skip formats outside that utility's list. An applicable count is not a count of successfully rewritten files.

Chapter rows are not independent audio files. Supported whole-file utilities can act once on their underlying parent, while cue-sheet track rows have narrower field-editing scope. Provider documents and restricted sources follow additional access/mutation rules. Do not use the presence of a familiar menu label as proof that every desktop operation is supported there.

Named external tools require the desktop/local launch route and a selection. Their disabled entries can show a reason. Unlike built-in cleanup, a tool launch does not save pending tag-panel values first. If the other application should read those changes, save deliberately before running it. A hidden selected row can still be a target; review selection before batch launching.

With per-file launching off, the tool runs once for the first selected file. With it on, it prepares one launch per selected file, asks above ten targets and rejects a per-file request above 100. The 99-definition limit is different from that runtime target limit. Program launch and final task success are also different: Started does not report final exit status or prove that another program opened one window per file.

docs.title: Error and recovery scope
docs.text:
Built-in utilities can partially complete and can have limited/unavailable session Undo. Check their result, errors and current history notice. An external program's edits and outputs are outside OpenTag's general Undo contract. Canceling or closing an Options dialog does not reverse a program that already started.

Use copied files for a new definition and retain independent backups before removing data. The Undo guide distinguishes recorded local writes, side images, pending edits, unrecorded file operations and external outputs.

docs.title: View menu
docs.text: View changes how loaded information is displayed. Hiding a panel or a column does not remove the corresponding metadata from audio files.

docs.title: Panels, fields and filtering
docs.text:
Item Result Refresh Rescan loaded folders and reload file information; F5 Show tag panel / Hide tag panel Toggle the editor panel; physical Control+Q Extended tags… Inspect and edit fields and embedded artwork beyond the visible tag panel; Alt+T Show filter / Hide filter Toggle the filter bar; F3 Default values in input fields Stage configured tag-panel defaults; Save tags writes those pending values Customize tag panel… Configure panel fields and their display/default behavior Field values… Manage the panel's custom-value lists

Refresh is different from reloading only the selected tags. Resolve pending edits before a refresh that would replace loaded information. A filtered-out file remains loaded. Hiding the filter shows all loaded files, while remembering its text for restoration when the filter is shown again. See filtering for manual application, hidden selections and invalid queries.

For example, configure a default genre, then choose Default values in input fields. The value is staged in the panel; it is not an immediate rewrite of every file. This differs from Discard pending changes, which removes unsaved edits rather than applying defaults.

docs.title: Sort and columns
docs.text:
Item Result Sort by Choose a displayed column as the primary sort; choosing it again reverses direction Unsorted (load and playlist order) Remove active sort criteria and show the maintained load/manual order Customize columns… Edit column visibility, names, values and editable fields Auto-size columns Fit displayed widths to content; Primary+Num + Column visibility choices Show/hide individual columns without deleting fields

A column's sort value can differ from its displayed value. Sorting a numeric track column as text can produce a different order from a padded numeric key. Headers and the sort indicator show the active criteria. Multi-column header sorting and the Sort by primary choice serve different needs; inspect the current arrows before using similar-file selection or generating a playlist.

To restore input order after sorting by artist, choose Unsorted (load and playlist order). Manual Alt+arrow or Alt+drag ordering starts from the current displayed order and leaves the sorted view. Neither sorting nor reordering moves audio files between folders.

docs.title: Toolbars and positions
docs.text:
Toolbars contains Main toolbar, Custom toolbar, Customize main toolbar… and Customize custom toolbar…. A hidden toolbar can be restored from this menu. The custom toolbar can include configured tools and action groups; an unavailable or removed target still needs attention before it runs.

Tag panel position offers Left, Right, Top, Bottom and Floating. The title bar can also be dragged to dock it. Double-clicking the title bar toggles a floating/docked position. Size and position are layout settings, not changes to the tag data.

Filter position offers Above the file list, Left of the toolbars and Right of the toolbars. Compact layouts omit these position menus and keep the filter with the list. Do not interpret a missing layout menu on a narrow/mobile view as loss of the underlying fields.

docs.title: Keyboard access
docs.text: Physical Control+Tab cycles through available tag-panel, filter and file-list panes; Control+Shift+Tab reverses that order. Hidden panes are skipped. On a Mac these are Control chords, not Command+Tab. See keyboard shortcuts for focus-dependent editing, Alt/Option behavior and dialog keys.

docs.title: Options reference
docs.text:
Open File → Options… with Cmd+O / Ctrl+O to change how OpenTag reads files, presents fields, writes tags, and contacts online services. These pages explain each setting and the consequences of changing it.

New to this?

Start with General, Files, and Tags. Keep automatic saving disabled while learning: selecting another file then leaves a chance to review pending edits before writing them.

docs.title: Choose and save a page
docs.text:
Select a page in the tree on the left. The arrow keys move between pages; Home and End select the first and last pages. On a narrow window the tree becomes an Options page list. Moving between pages retains the changes being edited.

OK validates and saves the settings across pages. If a value is invalid, OpenTag selects the affected page and shows the problem. Cancel or Escape closes the dialog without saving its ordinary settings. Restore page defaults resets the controls of the selected page in the dialog; press OK to save the reset. It does not reset every page at once.

Some buttons open an independent editor or carry out an operation immediately. In particular, Tag Panel and Field Values save through their own OK buttons; Library cleanup/clear, building a local freedb index, and exporting a configuration or value list perform work when clicked. Canceling the outer Options dialog does not undo that work.

Changing tag read options can change which metadata is displayed. On OK, OpenTag reloads loaded local files that have no pending edits when tag settings change. Files with pending edits retain those edits; save or discard them before reloading. Changing settings alone is not a request to rewrite the music library.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page Configure General Sorting, selection, completion, moved files, and notification area. Messages Confirmations, completion messages, and cover preservation. Files Folder scan extensions, safe names, and modification timestamps. Directories Subfolders, favorites, startup, and image-picker location. Appearance Color mode, scaling, and row/grid display. Library Persistent metadata cache and maintenance. Language Not available in this guide’s source baseline; the language reference is held until integration. Tags Selection-change saving, Extended tags, and folder images. Tags → Mpeg ID3v1, ID3v2, and APE policies for MPEG-family files. Tags → Ape, Mpc Tag policies for APE-family files. Tags → Mapping Field names shared across tag formats. Tags → Advanced Ratings, chapters, comment language, and storage compatibility. Tag Panel Fields, layout, and default editing values. Field Values Custom choices and genres. Networking Request timeout and proxy. Updates Version checks, beta releases, and release notes. Tag Sources Cover output, MusicBrainz sizes, and source diagnostics. Tag Sources → freedb Remote CDDB servers and disc IDs. Tag Sources → Local freedb Historical local databases and search indexes. Export Export dialogs, folders, and byte-order marks. Playlist Paths, naming, encoding, and automatic playlists. Tools External programs and double-click behavior.

docs.title: Where settings live
docs.text:
Use File → Open configuration folder to locate the active desktop profile. Ordinary options are versioned JSON in the app's configuration directory; other editors have their own configuration files. Color mode is remembered on the device separately. Use the app's configuration save/load commands for supported backups rather than guessing a platform-specific path or editing a running app's files.

The reference describes settings found in the guide’s source baseline. Availability in a downloaded build depends on which features that build includes; a source check does not establish release availability or runtime parity with Mp3tag. A missing page should be checked against the installed build before following instructions for it.

docs.text:
• General
  • Tags
  • Library

docs.title: Appearance options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Appearance to change color mode, control size, and separation between file-list rows.

New to this?

Enlarge the whole interface when text is hard to read. Enlarge only the toolbar when its buttons are the problem.

docs.title: Color mode
docs.text:
System is the default and follows the operating system's light/dark preference. Light and Dark fix the app to the selected mode. The title-bar color-mode control offers the same preference; it is remembered on the device.

The setting changes presentation, not artwork or exported files. Mp3tag's documented Windows-version restriction is not an OpenTag requirement; OpenTag uses its own interface theme.

docs.title: Symbols
docs.text: OpenTag does not provide Mp3tag's Standard versus Original icon-set switch. Its toolbar uses OpenTag's own symbols. Choosing a color mode or changing scale does not load a historical Mp3tag icon set.

docs.title: Toolbar scaling
docs.text: Toolbar scaling defaults to 100%. Available values are 100%, 110%, 125%, 150%, 175%, and 200%. Increase it to enlarge toolbar icons and buttons without enlarging the rest of the interface.

docs.title: User interface scaling
docs.text: User interface scaling has the same choices and defaults to 100%. It zooms the whole interface, including the toolbar. Toolbar scaling remains an additional toolbar-specific factor, so raising both makes toolbar controls grow more than other controls. If the toolbar becomes too large, return its own scale to 100% before adjusting the overall scale.

docs.title: Display grid lines in file view
docs.text:
Choice Effect Off Default. No added grid or alternating row treatment. Alternate row colors Shade adjacent rows differently to help follow a wide row. Grid lines Draw boundaries between file-list cells. Useful with many columns.

OpenTag uses explicit choices. Mp3tag's three-state checkbox encodes these appearances differently; a grayed checkbox in that application is not an extra OpenTag mode.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• General options
  • Options overview
  • Tag-panel layout

docs.title: Directories options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Directories for folder scanning and the starting folder of the cover-image picker. Its Startup child page controls what opens on launch.

New to this?

Start with one album folder. Enabling subfolders for a music-library root can add many more files than expected; the Files extension restriction can narrow the scan.

docs.title: Subfolders
docs.text: Read subfolders defaults to on. Folder operations then include nested folders. Turn it off to work only with audio directly inside the selected folder. It controls discovery, not whether an already loaded file can be edited.

docs.title: Favorite directory
docs.text:
OpenTag keeps an ordered list of favorites through File → Favorite directories… rather than a single favorite-path input on this page. Add the folders used frequently and put the preferred one first. File → Favorite directory or Ctrl+M opens the first favorite. Control is used on every platform, including macOS.

Managing favorites is separate from choosing a startup mode. Adding a favorite does not automatically load it every time the app starts.

docs.title: Startup directory
docs.text:
Choose Directories → Startup → Startup directory:

Choice Result Empty file list Default. Start without reopening a folder. Previous directory Open the most recent folder from the saved directory history. First favorite directory Open the first folder in the favorites list.

If there is no matching recent/favorite entry, there is no folder to restore. Files or directories supplied as launch requests take precedence over the normal startup folder. Startup restoration also depends on folder access being available on the platform; a file-picker-only environment cannot provide the same folder workflow.

docs.title: Cover art directory
docs.text:
Default folder for Add cover defaults to empty. It sets the starting location of the Add cover… picker; it does not automatically import or embed images.

Accepted forms include a full path, a path relative to the selected audio file's folder, and a format string using its fields. For example, Artwork points to an Artwork subfolder of the selected file's folder; %artist% can supply a component of a configured image archive path.

If the configured location is empty or cannot be opened, OpenTag tries the first selected file's folder when that folder contains an image. Otherwise it uses a valid working folder, falling back to the selected file’s folder when no valid working folder is available. Select the intended file before opening the picker, since the initial location derives from the selection.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Files and extension restrictions
  • General selection settings
  • Tags and folder-image display

docs.title: Export options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Export for output-file behavior shared by export configurations. A configuration's format, filename, and template are edited in the Export… dialog itself.

New to this?

Leave the selection dialog enabled while building a template. Check both the active configuration and destination before running a batch export.

docs.title: Show selection dialog
docs.text:
Defaults to on. File → Export… opens the configuration selector, where an output configuration can be chosen and edited. With the setting off, the command immediately runs the active configuration. This is useful for a repeated report but makes the remembered selection important.

Holding Shift with the export command, Cmd+Shift+E / Ctrl+Shift+E, requests an export per folder. That partitioning is separate from creating directories.

docs.title: Don't create directories
docs.text: Defaults to off, allowing parent folders needed by the export destination to be created. Enable it when a misspelled or unexpected path should fail rather than produce a new folder tree. Existing output directories can still be used. The option does not prohibit writing files inside them.

docs.title: Write BOM
docs.text: Defaults to off. Write BOM (UTF-8 and UTF-16 exports) adds a byte-order mark for those encodings. Some spreadsheet/text applications use a BOM to detect Unicode correctly; other consumers prefer files without it. Match the requirements of the program that reads the output. A BOM changes the start of the output bytes, not the exported field values.

docs.title: Open the result
docs.text:
Messages controls whether OpenTag offers to open the written export through the operating system's associated application. Disabling that message leaves the output on disk and does not disable export itself.

These settings do not define CSV quoting, HTML structure, sorting, or which fields a template includes. Those belong to the export configuration/template. A playlist has its own Playlist options, including its own BOM setting.

docs.title: Field Values options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Field Values, then Edit field values…, to maintain reusable choices for any editable tag field. The same editor is available through View → Field values….

New to this?

Use a custom list for consistent spellings such as Indie Folk, Instrumental, and Live. The list suggests values; it does not forbid other text or automatically retag existing files.

docs.title: Choose a field and enter values
docs.text:
Enter an uppercase field name in Field, or select a field under Fields with custom values. Put one choice per line in Custom field values. Field names are normalized to uppercase; technical information fields beginning with _ cannot receive editable custom lists.

The editor trims leading/trailing whitespace, drops empty lines and exact duplicates, and preserves the order entered. Sort A–Z sorts the current list. A field supports up to 5,000 custom choices. Multiline text belongs in metadata fields, not inside one list entry.

Press the editor's own OK to save. Cancel abandons its unsaved list edits. Once that OK has saved the list, canceling the outer Options dialog does not reverse it.

docs.title: Where choices appear
docs.text:
The tag-panel drop-down can include special keep/blank choices, values already present in the selection, the field's custom list, and standard genre choices for GENRE. In-place file-list and Extended tags editing also receive completion candidates from field values. General → Auto-completion controls inline completion, independently of storing these choices.

Prefer values from tags in list at tag panel defaults to off. Enable it to show only the selection's existing values, alongside applicable keep/blank choices, when the selection already supplies values. If a field is empty, its custom choices remain available. This preference can make a large collection's current spellings easier to review without mixing in the whole custom list.

docs.title: Genres
docs.text:
Show only user-defined genres defaults to off. Enable it to omit the standard genre list from the panel's choices and use the custom GENRE list instead. Existing selected values still appear. In OpenTag the saved list preferences apply without requiring the Mp3tag restart described in the original reference.

A custom genre is still text. ID3v1 supports a fixed indexed genre list and cannot preserve arbitrary new genre names. Use a richer tag type such as ID3v2 or APEv2 when saving user-defined genres; changing this UI list does not extend ID3v1.

docs.title: Import, export, and quick addition
docs.text:
Import… reads a text list with one value per line and merges it into the current field's list, removing exact duplicates. It does not replace every field's lists. Export… writes the current field's list for backup or sharing. Export writes a file immediately, even if the editor is later canceled.

While editing a single-line value in the tag panel, Shift+Enter adds that field's current text to its custom list. Empty or multiline values are rejected, and an exact duplicate is not added again. This stores a suggestion; it is not a separate command to save pending audio-file edits.

docs.title: Files options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Files to restrict folder scans, control separators inside tag-derived names, and preserve file modification times.

New to this?

A tag value is data; a separator typed into a filename format string is a request to create a folder. This page keeps those two uses separate.

docs.title: Read files
docs.text:
Restrict incoming files to defaults to empty, meaning all supported formats. Enter extensions to limit files discovered while scanning a folder:

*.mp3;*.flac

mp3, .mp3, and *.mp3 are accepted forms. Separate entries with semicolons, commas, or whitespace. Matching is case-insensitive, and repeated extensions are ignored. This is an extension list, not a general filename pattern: album*.mp3 is invalid. An allowed extension must still be a format OpenTag can read.

The restriction applies to folders. Files explicitly added individually are still read. To inspect a single M4A alongside an MP3-only folder scan, add that file directly. Changing the restriction does not itself remove already loaded rows; rescan the folder to use the new choice.

docs.title: Rename files from tags
docs.text:
Replace folder separator in tag values with defaults to _. OpenTag replaces both backslashes and forward slashes inside tag values used for file renaming. This applies to Tag → Filename and filename-changing Format Value, Guess Values, and Tag → Tag operations.

ALBUM value Replacement Tag-derived name component Harbour/Live _ Harbour_Live Harbour/Live - Harbour - Live Harbour/Live Empty HarbourLive

The replacement may contain up to 16 characters. It cannot itself contain \ / : * ? " < > | or control characters. Leaving it empty removes separators; it does not leave them unchanged.

Separators deliberately typed into the format string still form folders. With %artist%\%album%\%title%, the two typed backslashes request artist and album folders; a slash inside an actual album value is replaced. Preview the complete path before applying a rename, especially after changing this setting.

docs.title: Write files
docs.text:
Preserve timestamps of modified files defaults to off. Enable to restore the original modification time after writing or removing tags. It preserves that filesystem timestamp; it does not preserve the complete file bytes or prevent metadata changes.

A backup or sync tool that relies only on modification times may overlook an edit when this is enabled. The Library also uses modification time and size to recognize external changes. If an external editor preserves both, use Reload tags to force a fresh read.

docs.title: General options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → General to control everyday selection, sorting, and typing behavior. These settings affect the editor rather than the contents of saved tags.

New to this?

Leave automatic saving off until the difference between selecting a file, editing a field, and saving tags is familiar. Automatic selection and automatic saving are separate settings.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect and when to use it Show current directory in window title On Add the working folder to the title, for example OpenTag — /Music/Juniper Vale. Useful with several windows or similar album folders. With no folder loaded, the title remains OpenTag. Automatically select next file when editing in file view Off After committing an edit in a file-list cell, move the selection to the next file. Enable for entering a sequence of titles down a column; disable when several fields on one file need attention. Auto-completion at selection boxes On Complete typed prefixes using available values in tag-panel fields and file-list cells. The added suffix is selected, so further typing replaces it. Disable if suggestions interfere with free typing. Use natural sorting (1, 2, 11, …) On Treat digit sequences numerically: Track 2 precedes Track 11. With it off, textual sorting can place Track 11 before Track 2. This changes list order, not track fields or filenames. Select files automatically when they are added to the list Off Select incoming files after adding them. Useful for adding one album and immediately editing it; check the resulting selection before a batch command. Keep moved files in the file list On Retain files moved outside a listed folder. With it off, those files leave the list after a move unless they have pending changes. This does not delete the moved files.

Completion matches prefixes without regard to case and retains the characters already typed. If a candidate is Juniper Vale and the typed text is ju, the suggested text starts ju and completes the rest. Empty input is not filled automatically, and pasting does not trigger this inline completion. The candidates depend on the field's custom value lists and current selection.

Even with automatic selection off, loading files into an empty, unselected list selects an initial file for inspection. The setting controls selecting the incoming batch, not a guarantee that the list will have no selected row.

docs.title: Notification area
docs.text:
Both controls default to off. Always show icon in notification area keeps a tray icon available. Minimize to notification area hides the minimized window and its taskbar entry; click the tray icon or choose Show OpenTag from its menu to return.

These controls are for Windows and Linux. Linux requires notification-area support, including libayatana-appindicator. On macOS the controls are unavailable; minimized windows use the Dock. Do not look for a Windows-style tray setting to recover a minimized Mac window.

docs.title: Library options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Library to keep previously read metadata between sessions. The Library is a cache of file information, not a second collection of audio files.

New to this?

Enable it when repeatedly opening a large collection. A first load still has to read the files; later loads provide the opportunity for a cache hit.

docs.title: Enable Library
docs.text:
Enable Library defaults to off. With it off, files are read from disk when loaded. With it on, metadata is stored in a database in the configuration folder and reused on later loads when the path, modification time, size, and reading-settings fingerprint still match.

OpenTag updates the cache when it saves, renames, moves, or deletes files. File → Reload tags forces selected files to be read again and refreshes their entries. A change to tag-reading settings or reader version prevents reuse of an entry interpreted with the older settings.

The status reports whether the database exists, the cached file count and size, and how many files in the last load came from the Library versus disk. A high disk-read count after enabling the Library is expected for the first load or changed files.

Coming from Mp3tag

OpenTag caches metadata and image descriptors. It reads image bytes from the audio file when needed; it does not move embedded images or other binary payloads into the Library database. Do not expect the binary-storage or memory behavior described for Mp3tag's Library.

docs.title: Only include these directories
docs.text:
This restriction defaults to off. Turn it on, choose Add…, and select the folders whose files should be cached. Remove removes the selected inclusion entry. Files outside the included folders can still be loaded and edited; they are read from disk each time and are not added to the persistent cache.

With the restriction enabled and no folders listed, nothing is cached. Add an album's parent folder if all its descendant albums should be included. This list controls caching, not the file-list contents and not an automatic background scan.

docs.title: Cleanup Library
docs.text:
Cleanup Library checks cached paths and removes entries for files no longer accessible, including files moved or deleted outside OpenTag. With a directory restriction, it also removes entries outside the included folders. It uses the restriction currently displayed in the dialog.

Progress and checked/removed counts appear on the page. Cancel stops further cleanup; entries already removed stay removed. Cleanup does not delete music files. Reconnect removable or network drives before cleanup if their entries should remain cached: an inaccessible path can be treated as an orphan.

docs.title: Clear Library
docs.text: Clear Library… asks whether to remove every cache entry. Choose Clear to do so or Keep to cancel. The audio files remain where they are; their next load reads metadata from disk. Clearing is useful when deliberately rebuilding the cache, and is performed immediately rather than waiting for the outer Options OK.

docs.title: Performance and stale values
docs.text:
Place the active configuration on reliable, fast storage when practical. The Library still performs file-stat checks and database writes, so a slow portable drive or network filesystem can limit improvement. Compare the status counts before attributing loading time to tag parsing.

Mp3tag's original troubleshooting mentions excluding its process from Windows Defender. OpenTag provides no equivalent antivirus setting; those instructions name a different executable and should not be applied as an OpenTag prerequisite. Investigate actual I/O or scanning delays under the computer's existing policy.

If another program changes metadata while preserving both file size and modification time, an old cache entry can remain valid by those checks. Use Reload tags after that kind of external edit.

docs.title: Messages options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Messages to choose which completion messages and confirmations appear around editing operations.

New to this?

Keep confirmations for tag removal, file deletion, and unsaved changes enabled while learning. A completion message and a confirmation serve different purposes: one reports what happened, the other asks before proceeding.

docs.title: Completion notifications
docs.text:
All three default to off.

Setting When it reports after saving tags After an explicit tag save. It is not a dialog for every directly edited file-list cell. after actions, converters that write files, and Tag → Tag After operations that change file information through those paths. Pending auto-numbering edits remain subject to saving. after removing tags or tag types After tag removal. It does not refer to deleting the audio file.

The file list and status/error area still provide operational feedback when optional completion dialogs are disabled.

docs.title: Confirmations and warnings
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect at removing tags On Ask before removing configured tag types. Review read/write/remove policies, since tag removal can affect hidden metadata. at cutting tags Off Ask before cutting tag information. Cutting involves removal, unlike copying. at pasting tags Off Ask before applying the tag clipboard to the selection. Enable when frequent copying makes an accidental paste costly. at exporting and creating playlists (offers to open the written file) Off Offer to open a completed output file using its associated application. This controls a post-write offer, not whether the file may be overwritten. at deleting files On Ask before filesystem deletion. Normal deletion uses Trash/Recycle Bin even with this confirmation off. Permanent deletion remains a distinct operation. at warnings from Actions (file errors of the last action or action groups) On Show errors from the last action run. With it off, errors are still listed beneath the file list. at unsaved changes (closing, reloading, refreshing or discarding pending edits) On Ask when an operation would discard pending edits. With it off, those edits can be discarded without that prompt. at importing covers (when files already have cover art) On Ask whether existing embedded images should be preserved during a tag-source import.

The unsaved-changes message is not an automatic-save mode. Use Tags to configure selection-change saving. Avoid disabling the prompt merely to silence a workflow whose save behavior is not yet understood.

docs.title: Existing artwork without a question
docs.text:
When at importing covers is disabled, Without asking, existing cover art is becomes available:

  • Preserved keeps existing embedded artwork.
  • Replaced or added to, as chosen in the import follows the cover operation selected in the import. This is the default remembered choice.

The tag-source prompt can remember its answer through Don't show this message again; later imports then reuse that choice. Re-enable the message here to review each import again. Preserving existing art and saving a downloaded image alongside an album are separate decisions.

Discarding edits

Turning off at unsaved changes removes a chance to recover unsaved work. Save tags before closing, reloading, or using a command that discards pending changes.

docs.title: Networking options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Networking to configure requests to online tag sources and the update service.

New to this?

Keep the system proxy choice unless the network requires a different route. A longer timeout helps a slow server finish; it does not fix an incorrect address or an authentication failure.

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text: Timeout defaults to 30 seconds. Enter a whole number from 5 to 300. A request that takes too long is abandoned and reported as a failure. This is a request timeout, not a promise that a multi-request search will finish within that total time. Establishing the connection has a separate ceiling of 10 seconds, or the chosen timeout if shorter.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
Choice Behavior Use the system proxy settings Default. Let the HTTP client use system/environment proxy configuration, including applicable HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY values. No proxy Make a direct connection through the client's no-proxy mode. Use when inherited proxy settings are inappropriate. Use this HTTP proxy Use the address entered below for the app's HTTP requests.

For Proxy address, enter a host and port such as proxy.example.test:8080, or an HTTP/HTTPS URL such as http://proxy.example.test:8080. A missing scheme is interpreted as http://. Paths beyond /, query strings, unsupported schemes, and embedded user names/passwords are rejected.

Proxy authentication is not supported. Ordinary options can be stored and exported as plain text, so do not attempt to insert credentials into the address. Ask the network administrator for an appropriate system-proxy route if authentication is required.

These settings govern OpenTag's HTTP client; a web browser or external tool has its own network configuration. Choosing a proxy here does not change the operating system's settings.

docs.text:
• Tag Sources
  • Updates
  • Tools

docs.title: Playlist options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Playlist to configure Playlist (all files), Playlist (selected files), and Generate playlists…. A playlist stores references to audio files; creating one does not copy or transcode the music.

New to this?

Use .m3u8 and relative entries for a Unicode playlist that can move with its album folder. Keep the filename-confirmation dialog enabled until destinations are predictable.

docs.title: Write extended info
docs.text:
Defaults to on. Extended info supplies a duration and display label in addition to the file path. The default Extended info format string is:

%artist% - %title%

For ARTIST=Juniper Vale, TITLE=Harbour Lights, the label is Juniper Vale - Harbour Lights. A player may use this label without rereading tags. If tags later change, regenerate the playlist to update stored labels. Disable extended info for a consumer that expects paths alone; the consumer decides how it uses optional labels.

docs.title: Relative entries
docs.text:
Entries relative to working directory (if possible) defaults to on. OpenTag attempts relative paths instead of full machine-specific paths. For a playlist beside an album's files, 01 - Harbour Lights.flac is easier to move than /Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/01 - Harbour Lights.flac.

The actual output location and common filesystem roots determine whether relative paths are possible. Paths across different Windows drives cannot always be represented relatively. Test a generated playlist after moving its folder as a unit; a relative playlist still breaks if its audio files are moved independently.

docs.title: Automatic playlists
docs.text:
Create playlist automatically after saving tags or renaming files defaults to off. Enable to regenerate the configured playlist after those operations. Automatic creation uses the saved configuration without asking for a filename each time.

Use a stable filename and confirm the selection/list scope before relying on this for a collection. A tag edit can otherwise have the extra effect of rewriting a playlist. Errors in automatic creation are reported separately; a successful tag write is not proof that the playlist also succeeded.

docs.title: Filename of playlist
docs.text:
Defaults to %_directory%.m3u8. The value is a filename format string, and may include a relative or absolute path. Relative output names are placed under the working directory. A folder called Harbour Lights therefore supplies Harbour Lights.m3u8 with the default.

Loaded-playlist placeholders can reuse its name/location:

Placeholder Meaning %_playlist_filename% Loaded playlist's filename without extension. %_playlist_filename_ext% Loaded playlist's filename including extension. %_playlist_folderpath% Loaded playlist's containing folder path.

These describe a loaded playlist, not whichever audio file is selected. Without that context, choose a filename that does not depend on them.

docs.title: Encoding and extension
docs.text:
Extension Output .m3u8 UTF-8 M3U, suitable for Unicode names. .m3u M3U using the Windows ANSI codepage on Windows. On macOS/Linux, Windows-1252 is used only when OpenTag can read it back unchanged; otherwise UTF-8 is used. .pls PLS playlist.

For example, a filename containing Â© would become the Windows-1252 bytes C2 A9, which also form valid UTF-8 for the different text ©. OpenTag uses UTF-8 for that case and for characters outside Windows-1252. .m3u8 always uses UTF-8. Check the receiving player as well as loading the playlist back into OpenTag.

Write BOM for UTF-8 playlists (.m3u8, .pls) defaults to off. Enable only when the target reader needs a byte-order mark for encoding detection. This setting is independent of Export's BOM option.

docs.title: Confirm the filename
docs.text:
Show confirm filename dialog defaults to on. OpenTag first evaluates the configured filename format string, then shows the proposed path. Text entered into this confirmation dialog is a literal filename: new placeholders typed there are not evaluated.

For example, change the configured format string to %album%.m3u8 if the album should supply the name. Typing that same expression into the confirmation field instead asks for a name containing those literal characters. Automatic playlist creation bypasses this dialog.

docs.title: Don't create directories
docs.text: Defaults to off. Relative and absolute playlist output paths can create parent folders. Enable Don't create directories to require the destination folders to exist already. This prevents unexpected folder creation; it does not disable writing into an existing folder or turn a playlist into an audio copy.

docs.title: Tag Panel options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tag Panel, then Customize tag panel…, to choose the fields shown beside the file list. View → Customize tag panel… opens the same editor.

New to this?

Add a field for metadata edited frequently, such as MOOD. Hiding a control removes it from the panel, not from the audio files.

docs.title: Field list
docs.text:
New inserts a field after the selected entry. Select a row to edit it; Move up and Move down change order. Uncheck its box to hide it without removing its configuration. Remove deletes the control definition. Restore defaults restores the standard layout in this editor; the editor's OK saves the result.

Up/Down selects entries. Alt+Up/Down moves the selected entry, and Space toggles its visibility. The inspected implementation allows at most 100 entries. Ordinary fields cannot appear twice; separator entries can.

The initial panel contains Title, Artist, Album, Year, Track, Genre, Comment, Album Artist, Composer, Discnumber, and Directory, with cover art displayed. Most defaults keep each file's existing value.

docs.title: Field controls
docs.text:
Control Meaning Name Visible label. An & before a letter makes it an Alt mnemonic; && displays a literal ampersand. Field Metadata field identifier, such as TITLE or MOOD. OpenTag normalizes it to uppercase. It is independent of the label. Default value The value staged by default-value workflows; see below. Type Text, Check, or Multiline. Choose Multiline for comments or lyrics. Size of field Layout width: Full, Larger, Large, Medium, Normal, Small, Smaller, or Tiny. Consecutive fields share a row where their widths fit. Rows Height of a Multiline control, from 1 to 20. Unavailable for other types.

A label such as &Mood gives Alt+M when that mnemonic is available. Alt is Option on macOS. The label is not the saved field name: a label Mood with Field MOOD still writes MOOD.

_DIRECTORY adds a folder switcher rather than an editable metadata field. _SEPARATOR starts a new layout row, or a new column when the panel is docked above/below the file list. Other technical fields beginning with _ are not editable panel fields.

docs.title: Default values
docs.text:
< keep > leaves each file's existing value alone. < blank > requests an empty field. Any other default is literal text. Defaults can be staged when multiple files are selected and through View → Default values in input fields. A field that already has a pending edit is not overwritten by automatic defaults.

For example, a default MOOD=Reflective is useful during a deliberate classification session, but can stage that value when later selecting another batch. Restore < keep > when finished. Default text is not a format-string evaluation engine.

A Check control treats empty text and 0, false, or no as off, and other nonempty text as on. A mixed selection can have an indeterminate state. Inspect the target field's conventions before using a checkbox for arbitrary text.

docs.title: Covers and saved configurations
docs.text:
Display cover art controls whether the panel shows its artwork area. Tags separately controls whether a folder image can stand in for missing embedded artwork.

Save configuration… exports the layout currently being edited. Load configuration… loads an OpenTag layout for review. Import Mp3tag configuration… reads a selected supported Mp3tag panel configuration, reports skipped entries, and places imported controls in the editor. Review that report before the editor's OK makes the layout active. Importing a layout does not import the audio collection or tag values.

The editor saves independently of its parent Options dialog. Canceling it discards unsaved layout edits, but does not remove an already exported configuration file.

docs.title: Tag Sources → freedb
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tag Sources → freedb to configure a CDDB server for album metadata. The historical freedb service ended; the saved defaults point to gnudb, and a compatible alternative server can be entered.

New to this?

A server address, application acceptance, and an album match are three separate conditions. If the server refuses OpenTag, changing the disc ID will not fix that refusal. A local snapshot avoids dependence on a remote CDDB server.

docs.title: Server list
docs.text:
Select the server to use from FREEDB SERVER. New adds a configuration; Delete removes the selected one while leaving at least one entry. Changing the selected entry changes which server is used after Options OK.

OpenTag ships HTTPS and HTTP gnudb entries, with HTTPS selected initially. Current list of freedb servers restores that shipped list and selects its first entry, replacing edits in the dialog. Unlike the remote-list retrieval described for Mp3tag, this button does not fetch a fresh list from a server. Restore page defaults also restores the page's saved-default choices for later OK.

docs.title: Server fields
docs.text:
Field Meaning and default NAME Label used in the server selector; the initial HTTPS entry is gnudb (HTTPS). It is not the network address. PROTOCOL HTTPS or HTTP. Default HTTPS encrypts the request in transit when the server supports it. ADDRESS Hostname only, initially gnudb.gnudb.org. Do not paste a whole URL here. PATH Server endpoint, initially /~cddb/cddb.cgi. Keep it separate from the hostname. PORT Optional number from 1 to 65535. Empty uses the protocol's default port. Your email address (sent to the freedb server) Optional configured identity sent in the CDDB handshake, not a login password. Defaults to empty.

The default endpoint is https://gnudb.gnudb.org/~cddb/cddb.cgi. HTTPS encrypts the connection; HTTP does not. Choose a protocol the selected server supports.

docs.title: Email and application identity
docs.text:
An address entered here must look like name@example.org. Every request sends its user/domain components with OpenTagAudioTagEditor and the application version. Empty email sends the developer contact john@neerdael.nl. Use an address intended to be shared with the selected server. This identifies the client; it is not a password or account sign-in.

gnudb may accept only applications registered by its operator and may reply 500 Unknown application otherwise. Changing the email address does not register OpenTag, and saving valid settings does not establish live registration. A refusal message is a service/application registration issue, not evidence that the endpoint settings were saved incorrectly. Choose a compatible server or local database when appropriate. Ordinary timeout/proxy behavior is configured under Networking.

docs.title: Disc ID fields
docs.text:
Both switches default to off:

  • Copy disc ID to COMMENT field includes the source disc ID in the imported comment data. Review the comment in the import before applying it if it already holds notes worth keeping.
  • Copy disc ID to DISCID field imports the disc ID into its dedicated DISCID field, keeping that identity separate from human-readable comments.

The entry's own freedb DISCID is used when present, falling back to the listed ID. It can differ from the gnudb Entry ID shown in results.

These govern metadata imported from freedb; they do not change the audio or make a server accept the client. The disc ID is not a MusicBrainz release identifier, a barcode, or a filesystem path.

docs.title: Search methods
docs.text:
Use remote freedb lookup by track layout or artist and album. Typed disc-ID lookup is available only for a local snapshot. OpenTag asks the server for matches before reading the chosen entry.

Artist/album and artwork search are restricted to recognized gnudb hosts (gnudb.org or its subdomains). Other configured CDDB servers use track-layout lookup, even if they implement similar text commands. If the server answers 429 Too Many Requests, wait before searching again; OpenTag does not automatically repeat that rejected request.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Local freedb
  • Tag Sources cover settings
  • Networking

docs.title: Tag Sources → Local freedb
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tag Sources → Local freedb to use an extracted historical freedb database on disk. This is a source of album metadata, separate from OpenTag's own Library cache.

New to this?

Select the database root containing category subfolders, not an individual album file. A local snapshot reflects the date it was created; it does not receive current server updates.

docs.title: Local freedb folder
docs.text:
The folder defaults to empty. Type its full path or use Choose folder…. The reader supports category folders such as blues, classical, and rock, with either one xmcd file per disc or the Windows xxtoyy range-file layout.

Extract the snapshot before selecting it; a downloaded compressed archive is not the database folder. A nonexistent path or unreadable category data cannot provide matches. Store it somewhere the app can continue to access.

Local lookup by disc ID reads that snapshot. The historical Mp3tag documentation says audio-file-based lookup is unavailable locally. Do not transfer that restriction to OpenTag unchanged: its local reader supports disc-ID lookup, and its tag-source workflow can derive a disc ID from a suitable ordered track layout. That is metadata matching, not an acoustic fingerprint of the music.

docs.title: Text index
docs.text:
To search by artist/album words, choose Build index. The page reports whether an index exists, its disc count, and whether it belongs to the currently entered folder. Building has progress reporting; Cancel requests cancellation. An unfinished build does not replace the previous completed index.

An index for another folder is not a valid index for this folder. Rebuild after replacing the snapshot or changing the configured root; changes to database files are not indexed automatically. An empty root must be set before building can start. In environments without the index backend, the button is unavailable and the page states that text indexing is not available there.

Building an index performs work immediately using the entered folder. Saving Options chooses which folder later searches use; canceling the outer dialog does not undo a completed index build. No local index is needed for a direct disc-ID lookup.

docs.title: Lookup methods
docs.text:
SEARCH BY Input Text index needed? Disc ID of the selected files ID derived from file-list order and durations No freedb disc ID Existing freedb disc ID entered in DISC ID No Artist and album words Words in indexed artist/album titles Yes

For selected-file lookup, use one complete disc in track order with known durations and at most 99 files. A local disc ID is distinct from gnudb's listed Entry ID, a barcode or a MusicBrainz identifier. The database is not updated from gnudb and does not receive corrections when tags are saved.

docs.title: No matching album
docs.text: Confirm the selected files belong to one complete disc, their list order and durations are appropriate, and the snapshot actually contains the release. A title search needs an index; a missing disc cannot be recovered by rebuilding the same snapshot's index. A newer edition may require another source. See Search a local freedb snapshot for the three lookup methods and import review.

docs.title: Tag Sources options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tag Sources or Tag Sources → Options… for source lookups, cover-image output and diagnostics. Server settings are under freedb; historical offline databases are under Local freedb.

New to this?

Saving an image beside an album and embedding it in audio files are separate actions. This page supplies the external image's name; the import review determines what is actually saved.

docs.title: Default file name for cover art
docs.text:
Defaults to folder. Save image to file in a tag-source dialog uses this name/format string, fills placeholders from the first written audio file of each destination folder, and adds an extension for the image type.

For example, %albumartist% - %album% can produce Juniper Vale - Harbour Lights.jpg when those fields are present and the chosen image is JPEG. The exact extension follows the downloaded image, so do not assume a JPEG result for every source. A shared album image is named once per folder, not once per track title.

The format also has the app’s working-folder context (%_workingdir%, %_workingpath%) and active File List column functions. For example, a $columnValues column based on %ALBUM% uses the newly imported album when the external image is saved. Review the resulting path and any file errors. This names a separate image; it does not rename audio or choose an embedded picture type.

Save image to file replaces an existing image of the resulting name and extension. The review's Replace existing artwork choice applies to embedded covers, not this external image file.

This setting does not search for local images and does not choose the starting folder of Add cover…; that is Directories → Cover art directory.

docs.title: MusicBrainz cover size
docs.text:
Choose 250 pixels, 500 pixels (default), 1200 pixels, or Original size. The choice is used for MusicBrainz artwork from the Cover Art Archive, including its cover-source workflows, and for Cover Art Archive images listed by gnudb.

Smaller images reduce transfer and storage requirements. Choose 1200 or Original when a high-resolution image is needed, accepting that the original can be much larger. This requests the source's image variant; it is not a local resizer for covers already embedded in files.

docs.title: Write debug output for web sources
docs.text:
Defaults to off. This traces .src scripts, not built-in provider lookups. Enable to write downloaded pages and a step-by-step parser trace for .src web-source searches and album lookups. Find the debug folder through Tag Sources → Open sources folder.

Use the trace to identify whether a source's page structure or parsing steps have changed. Disable it when finished to avoid accumulating downloaded responses. A response or trace can contain search text and service data; inspect it before sharing it in an issue.

docs.title: Online services
docs.text:
Setting Choices and default API keys… Open the AcoustID, Last.fm and fanart.tv key dialog; storage is separate from ordinary Options. iTunes Store country (two letters) For example US (default) or NL; an empty value uses US. iTunes Cover size 600, 1200 (default) or 3000 pixels Deezer Cover size 500 or 1000 (default) pixels Write synchronized lyrics (LRC time stamps) when available Off by default; enable to prefer available LRC text in UNSYNCEDLYRICS. Last.fm Tags written to GENRE The top 1 (default), 2, 3 or 5 usable tags fpcalc program Full executable path for AcoustID; empty for automatic discovery. Does not install fpcalc.

Cover sizes request provider image variants without guaranteeing availability or detail. Last.fm has no cover size option; its supplied images are generally smaller.

Choose OK to save Options. API keys have their own Save button and do not wait for Options OK. Use Tag Sources → Discogs access token… for its separate credential and optional keychain setting.

The freedb and Local freedb subpages configure a CDDB server and local database folder. They do not choose servers for the other online services.

docs.title: Tags → Advanced
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tags → Advanced for format-specific interoperability choices. Change one setting at a time when investigating a particular player's behavior.

New to this?

These are storage and interpretation choices. Keep a copy of a representative file and check it in the program that motivated the change; OpenTag source checks do not establish that program's compatibility.

docs.title: ID3v2 comment language code
docs.text:
ID3v2 comment language code (ISO-639-2) defaults to eng. Enter a three-letter alphabetic code, such as deu for German. OpenTag normalizes the stored language code to lower case when writing new comment frames. A two-letter interface locale such as de is not valid here.

This is an identifier in an ID3v2 comment frame, not an automatic translation of the comment text or the app interface. Some readers choose comments by language identifier. The original Mp3tag compatibility guidance says localized Windows Explorer or Windows Media Player may need the Windows language’s three-letter code, such as deu, while iTunes requires eng and can ignore comments with another code. Those are the documented historical reader distinctions; this guide does not verify those programs’ current behavior. Keep eng unless there is a tested reason to change it, then confirm the target reader displays the comment.

docs.title: Always display POPULARIMETER values for ID3v2 ratings
docs.text:
Defaults to off. Normally supported player-specific rating frames can appear through convenience fields such as RATING MM or RATING WMP. Enable this to expose ID3v2 POPM values as POPULARIMETER instead.

The raw field includes an owner identifier, rating byte, and play counter in owner|rating|counter form. It is not the same text representation as a star rating. For example, changing display mode does not mean a raw value of 128 is a 128-star score. Reload tags to inspect the new field view before editing or filtering ratings.

docs.title: List chapters as separate files
docs.text:
Defaults to off. Enable and reload the directory to list supported chapters as individual rows. Supported source paths include MP4 chapters, Matroska chapters, ID3v2 CHAP, and embedded cue sheets. This is useful for editing chapter titles; disable it when working with the file's global tags as one row.

A chapter row refers to part of its parent media file. It is not a newly split audio file. %_subsong_count% identifies the count of subsongs/chapters and %_subsong% their zero-based index, useful when adding diagnostic file-list columns. Reload the directory after changing the option so row expansion can be rebuilt.

docs.title: Use recommended mapping for Matroska video
docs.text:
Defaults to on. Matroska tags can target different semantic levels. The same native name can mean different things at different levels: for example, PART_NUMBER can represent a track at target type 30 or a disc at target type 50.

For files containing video, this option uses the recommended video mapping, including title at target type 50, album at 60, and episode/season semantics. Disable only when a particular consumer expects an older mapping such as title at target type 30. Reload tags after changing the choice. Changing the view alone does not rewrite all existing Matroska tags.

docs.title: Use single MP4 atom for multiple values
docs.text:
Defaults to on. Store a field's multiple values as several data entries inside one field atom. With it off, use a separate field atom per value. The conceptual field still has several values; this changes their container arrangement.

For example, two artist values can be represented under one artist atom with two data entries, or two artist atoms. Different players may interpret these arrangements differently. Test with the actual consumer rather than joining distinct artists into one string merely to work around a display issue.

docs.title: Reuse unmodified MP4 atoms
docs.text:
Defaults to off. With reuse enabled, an unchanged existing field can stay in its original storage rather than being remapped on a save. This matters for user-defined atoms whose field name has a documented standard atom: the existing atom remains until the value changes. A changed value is written through the normal mapping.

Leave it off when normalizing such fields to the documented representation is desired. Enable when an established collection or legacy reader relies on the existing arrangement. This is a field-storage preservation policy, not a guarantee that the complete MP4 file remains byte-for-byte unchanged after editing another field.

docs.title: Reuse unmodified ID3v2 frames
docs.text:
Defaults to off. The equivalent ID3v2 policy can preserve an unchanged user-defined TXXX frame when that field also has a documented native frame mapping. Without reuse, saving can normalize it to the mapped frame even though its text was not edited. With reuse, changing the field's value triggers writing through its normal mapping.

The option does not change the meanings of user-defined field aliases. It determines whether an unchanged native representation should be reused while a tag is being written.

docs.title: Tags → Ape, Mpc
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tags → Ape, Mpc for formats whose normal metadata is APE: Monkey's Audio, Musepack, WavPack, TAK, and OptimFROG.

New to this?

Keep APEv2 writing enabled for these formats unless a specific player requires another choice. ID3v1 cannot hold the same field set, artwork, or full Unicode text.

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
Both switches default to on:

Switch Effect ID3v1 Allow an existing legacy ID3v1 tag to be displayed. APE Allow an existing APEv1/APEv2 tag to be displayed.

APE takes priority over ID3v1 when both are enabled and present. The view uses one tag type rather than merging the fields of both. Disable APE reading temporarily to inspect an otherwise hidden ID3v1 value, then restore the intended reading policy. Reading switches do not delete either tag.

docs.title: Write
docs.text:
ID3v1 defaults to off. Enable only when the consuming software requires it, accepting its limited text lengths, genre list, fields, and character repertoire.

APEv2 (also updates an existing ID3v1 tag) defaults to on. It writes APEv2 and upgrades APEv1. An existing ID3v1 tag is updated as well, even if the explicit ID3v1 write switch is off. Leaving the explicit switch off therefore avoids requesting a new ID3v1 tag; it does not freeze one already present.

At least one write type must remain enabled. Written types receive values based on the displayed tag. Back up files that intentionally contain differing tag blocks before a save that synchronizes them.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
Switch Default Effect ID3v1 On Remove an existing ID3v1 tag when removal is requested; ordinary saving removes it when it is not being written. ID3v2 Off Remove an existing ID3v2 block. That block is not displayed by this family's reading policy, so it can otherwise remain hidden. APE On Remove existing APEv1/APEv2 when requested; ordinary saving strips it when APEv2 writing is off.

Remove tag… uses these switches. All Remove switches off produces a no-types-selected error. A checked Remove switch does not override writing the same supported type during Save: a written type is updated rather than removed. In particular, APEv2 writing's update of an existing ID3v1 tag counts as writing that tag.

The Mpeg page has a conditional-ID3v2 control and an ID3v2 encoding choice; this page does not. Choosing an ID3v2 version there does not turn this family into an ID3v2-writing policy.

docs.text:

docs.title: Tags → Mapping
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tags → Mapping to give a format's fields the names used throughout OpenTag. A mapping changes the field name exposed to the editor and format strings; it does not translate its text or calculate a new value.

New to this?

Use a mapping when two formats store the same concept under different field names. Do not use it to extract a year from a full date: that requires a value transformation.

docs.title: Add and edit a rule
docs.text:
Choose New, then set:

Control Meaning Tag type The format family the rule applies to: APEv2, ID3v2, MP4, Vorbis Comments, or WMA. Source The field name OpenTag otherwise shows for this format. Target The preferred field name to show and use in OpenTag.

Select an existing row to edit it. Move up and Move down change list order; Remove removes the selected rule. The default list is empty. Press OK to save the rules. Clean local files are reloaded; files with pending edits require deliberate saving/discarding and reloading before inspecting their new mapped view.

Source and target must be nonempty names without line breaks. Matching is case-insensitive for validation, and one source in a tag type cannot map to several different targets. Multiple sources may map to the same target.

docs.title: Reading mapped fields
docs.text:
Suppose FLAC files contain DATE=2024-03-15, while the collection's column and format strings use YEAR. Add Vorbis Comments, Source DATE, Target YEAR.

Stage Field and value Stored in FLAC DATE=2024-03-15 Shown after mapping/reload YEAR=2024-03-15 Format string %year% 2024-03-15

The value is still a date, even though the displayed name is YEAR. A field-name rule does not validate or shorten it. An ID3v2 rule does not affect the FLAC, because the tag-type choice is part of the rule.

docs.title: Saving mapped fields
docs.text:
Writing reverses the mapping. Editing YEAR in the example writes the value to the native DATE field. If both DATE and RELEASE map to YEAR, a write of that target fans out to both source names.

This makes many-to-one mapping useful for harmonizing a collection, but it also means saving can write more than one underlying field. Avoid merging distinct concepts into one target unless they are intended to receive the same value. Test rules on a copy and inspect the result after reload.

docs.title: Field names versus native identifiers
docs.text:
ID3v2 and MP4 already have built-in mappings from native frame/atom identifiers to readable field names. Use the readable OpenTag field name as Source, such as COMPOSER, rather than entering an ID3 frame identifier or MP4 atom code. This page adds aliases above that mapping layer; it does not replace the built-in identifier-to-field table.

With reuse of unmodified frames/atoms enabled, an unchanged field may retain its prior physical representation. Changing the mapping view is therefore distinct from deliberately rewriting a value into a new native location.

docs.title: Tags → Mpeg
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tags → Mpeg to control ID3v1, ID3v2, and APE tags in MPEG-family audio. This policy also serves raw AAC and TTA through OpenTag's format adapters. An AAC stream inside an MP4/M4A container instead uses MP4 tags.

New to this?

A file can hold several independent tag blocks with conflicting values. Check what is read before choosing what to write or remove. Try a copied file before changing a library-wide policy.

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
All three reading switches default to on. OpenTag displays one enabled, present tag type, in this priority order:

Priority Switch Reads 1 APE APEv1 or APEv2. 2 ID3v2 ID3v2 metadata. 3 ID3v1 The older fixed-size tag.

If a higher-priority enabled type is absent, the next present type is used. Contents are not assembled field by field from all three. For example, a file with an APE title and a different ID3v2 title shows the APE title while APE reading is enabled. Disabling APE reading reveals the ID3v2 view; it does not remove APE from the file.

The file's technical tag information identifies present/read tag types. When diagnosing another player's different result, inspect that information rather than assuming the visible value is the only stored value.

docs.title: Write
docs.text:
Setting Default Effect ID3v1 On Write the limited legacy tag. Long text, extra fields, Unicode outside its character repertoire, multiple values, and artwork cannot all be represented. ID3v2 On Write the richer ID3v2 tag using the selected revision/encoding. ID3v2 only if ID3v1 too small Off When both ID3v1 and ID3v2 writing are enabled, create ID3v2 only if needed. An existing ID3v2 tag is still updated. APEv2 (also updates an existing ID3v1 tag) Off Write APEv2, upgrading an existing APEv1 tag. If an ID3v1 tag already exists it is updated too, even when the explicit ID3v1 writing switch is off.

At least one write type must remain enabled. Saving synchronizes written types from the displayed field set, so enabling a second type is not a promise to preserve a conflicting hidden tag independently.

docs.title: When ID3v1 is too small
docs.text:
OpenTag checks more than text length. Artwork, custom fields, multiple values, a user-defined genre, and characters outside Latin-1 require ID3v2. In the inspected implementation, title/artist/album fit only within 30 characters; comment space is 28 characters when a track is present, otherwise 30; year must be four digits; a track must fit its legacy positive byte value. A TRACK value containing a total, such as 3/8, needs ID3v2 to preserve that text.

Metadata in a file without ID3v2 With conditional ID3v2 writing Short title, artist, album, four-digit year, standard genre ID3v1 may suffice. Same fields plus embedded front cover ID3v2 is needed. Same fields plus MOOD=Reflective ID3v2 is needed. Existing ID3v2, even if values would fit ID3v1 Existing ID3v2 is updated.

docs.title: ID3v2 version and encoding
docs.text:
Choice Use and tradeoff ID3v2.4 UTF-8 Unicode in ID3v2.4. Choose when all consuming players support this revision. ID3v2.3 UTF-16 Default. Unicode in ID3v2.3; a practical compatibility choice for older consumers that support Unicode but not v2.4. ID3v2.3 ISO-8859-1 Legacy non-Unicode output for a device that specifically requires it. Characters outside Latin-1 are written as ?, so names in other scripts can lose information.

Changing this setting affects future writes; it does not convert every loaded file immediately. Keep Unicode unless a known consuming device requires another format, then test its actual display on a copy.

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
ID3v1, ID3v2, and APE removal all default to on. File → Remove tag… removes the selected types that exist. Saving also removes a checked type when it is not written. Thus disabling Write APEv2 while leaving Remove APE enabled can remove an existing APE tag during an ordinary save.

If every Remove switch is off, the remove command reports that no types are selected. Disabling Read alone never requests deletion. A type left unread and unwritten is retained only if the removal policy also leaves it alone.

Mp3tag's original reference specifically couples ID3v1 removal with removal of a dependent Lyrics3 tag. OpenTag has Lyrics3-aware raw-stream layout handling, but this guide has no verified equivalent guarantee for every MPEG removal path. Do not use the ID3v1 checkbox as a general Lyrics3-cleanup promise.
