docs.title: Tags options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tags to choose when edits are saved and which images the tag panel displays. The child pages configure Mpeg, Ape, Mpc, Mapping, and Advanced behavior.

New to this?

An edited field can be pending in OpenTag while the audio file on disk is unchanged. Keep the default pending mode to review a batch before using Save tags.

docs.title: Save tags when changing selection
docs.text:
Save tags when using arrow keys or a single mouse click defaults to off. Enable it to write pending tag-panel edits when selecting another file with the mouse, moving the file-list selection with arrow keys, or choosing Select next file. Clicking an empty area of the file list or choosing Unselect all also leaves the current selection and can save its pending tags. Moving selection can therefore modify files without a separate Save command. Select next file also has Cmd+N / Ctrl+N and can keep focus in the tag panel. This automatic-save path applies to local desktop files; provider-backed documents are excluded.

With it off, selection changes do not provide this automatic write. Review pending changes and choose Save tags deliberately. Messages → at unsaved changes controls prompts when other commands would discard edits; disabling that message is not a way to enable saving.

docs.title: Save mode at extended tag dialog
docs.text:
This controls changed fields when << or >> moves between files in Extended tags…:

Mode Result Keep changes pending Default. Keep the edits in OpenTag for a later Save tags. Ask Ask how to handle the changed fields before moving. Ignore changes Discard the dialog's changes for the file being left. Save changes Write changes when moving to the other file. A save failure must be resolved rather than treated as a successful move.

Keep changes in the editor stages the changes; pending mode does not mean the file has already been saved. Review the selection and pending state before writing. OpenTag's explicit pending mode is an addition to Mp3tag's documented ask/ignore/save choices.

docs.title: Folder images in the tag panel
docs.text:
Don't display first image from file directory as cover art defaults to off. When a selected file has no embedded cover, OpenTag may show an image from its folder. This is a display fallback: seeing the picture does not mean it is stored in the audio file.

Enable the option when auditing which files actually contain embedded artwork. It hides the fallback without deleting image files. Import a cover explicitly if the audio file should carry it when copied elsewhere.

docs.title: Read, write, and remove policies
docs.text:
The format pages separate three decisions:

  • Read chooses which existing tag is displayed.
  • Write chooses which tag types receive saved values.
  • Remove chooses tag types stripped by Remove tag; saving also strips a selected type when it is not being written.

Read selection is not a merge of every stored tag. Two programs can show different values when they prioritize different blocks in the same file. Changes to the policy can also affect more metadata than the single field edited: written tag types are synchronized from the displayed values.

The Mpeg policy includes MPEG audio, raw AAC, and TTA. Ape, Mpc includes Monkey's Audio, Musepack, WavPack, TAK, and OptimFROG. Other formats follow their native storage rather than these switches; Remove tag uses their own supported removal path.

docs.title: Tools options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Tools to configure external programs for selected local audio files. Saved tools appear in the Tools menu and file-list context menu. The default tool can also run on a file double-click.

New to this?

Start with a player or inspection program and one copied file. A tool is a separate application: it can change files independently of OpenTag, so its changes are not automatically an OpenTag undo step.

docs.title: Add, edit, and reorder
docs.text:
New adds a tool; select it to edit its fields. Remove, Move up, and Move down manage the list. At most 99 tools are allowed. The initial list is empty.

The first ten entries have Cmd+1 through Cmd+0 on macOS, or Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+0 on Windows/Linux. The tenth entry uses 0. Reordering changes the corresponding shortcut positions. Shortcuts do not run a tool while typing into an ordinary text field.

docs.title: Name, Path, and Parameter
docs.text:
Field Use Name Nonempty label shown in the menus. Path Full path of the executable. Use Browse… to select it. A command name found only through a shell's search path is insufficient. On macOS an application bundle path ending in .app is also accepted. Parameter Optional argument text containing supported placeholders. Empty parameters pass the selected file's full path as one argument.

For a program that accepts a file path, use:

"%_path%"

Arguments are separated by whitespace, and double quotes keep an argument together. An unmatched quote is an error. Placeholder values are inserted into the parsed arguments; a file path containing spaces remains one argument when the placeholder occupies one quoted argument.

OpenTag starts the program directly, without a shell. Redirection, pipes, command substitution, and shell wildcard expansion are not performed. Enter the executable in Path and its arguments in Parameter, rather than a complete shell command in either field.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text:
For a file /Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/03 - Tidepool.flac, a single listed root /Music, and its containing folder:

Placeholder Meaning Illustrative value %_path% Complete file path. /Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/03 - Tidepool.flac %_filename_ext% Filename including extension. 03 - Tidepool.flac %_filename% Filename without extension. 03 - Tidepool %_filename_rel% File path relative to the list root, where available. Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/03 - Tidepool.flac %_directory% Containing folder's name. Harbour Lights %_folderpath% Complete containing folder path, with trailing separator. /Music/Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/ %_folderpath_rel% Relative containing folder path, with trailing separator. Juniper Vale/Harbour Lights/

Relative placeholders depend on the root context. With several roots or a file outside the chosen root, do not assume the same relative result; use %_path% when the external program needs an unambiguous file location. Path separators follow the platform.

docs.title: For all selected files
docs.text:
A new tool enables for all selected files (otherwise only the first selected file). Enabled means launch one process per selected file. Disabled means run once for the first selected file; it does not collect every selected path into one argument list.

OpenTag asks before launching a per-file tool for more than ten files. The backend limits one per-file invocation request to 100 selected files. Save pending changes first so an external program reads the intended on-disk data. Tool availability is limited to supported local-file contexts; a provider-backed document is not automatically an executable filesystem path.

docs.title: Default tool
docs.text:
Default tool (double-click in the file list) defaults to No action. Select a configured tool to launch it on a file double-click. No action disables the external-tool action; it does not remove explicit tools from menus. OpenTag’s file-list double-click falls back to Extended tags… when no default tool is selected. This differs from Mp3tag’s documented no-action behavior.

If another program modifies tags, use Reload tags to read its changes. Keep the Library timestamp/size cache rules in mind when an external editor preserves those attributes.

  • Library and external changes

docs.title: Updates options
docs.text:
Open File → Options… → Updates to control checks against OpenTag releases on GitHub. Checking reports available versions; OpenTag does not automatically download or install them.

New to this?

Use Check now… for a deliberate check. Review the release notes and choose the package for the platform before replacing an installed build.

docs.title: Check for updates on startup
docs.text: Defaults to off. When enabled, OpenTag checks its version on launch. Network failures do not mean that the installed version is current; they mean the check could not establish that fact.

docs.title: Also include development builds (beta)
docs.text: Defaults to off. Enable to include prereleases in the comparison. This changes which releases are reported, not the app's current features and not an installation channel. Disable it to compare against stable releases only. A beta may be published even when there is no newer stable release.

docs.title: Display release notes for new versions
docs.text: Defaults to on. After a previously used profile starts a different app version, OpenTag opens that version's GitHub release page in the default browser. A fresh profile does not have a previous version to compare. The setting is independent of startup update checking.

docs.title: Check now
docs.text:
Check now… performs a manual version check. It uses the saved settings: changing the beta or network controls in the open Options dialog does not save them. Press OK, then reopen the page if the check must use those new values.

Results distinguish a newer available release, an installed version already at the newest applicable release, and no applicable releases. Follow the release link to obtain a build. These are OpenTag releases; Mp3tag's version numbers and update channel do not apply.

docs.title: Scripting functions
docs.text:
Scripting functions calculate text inside a format string. They can read tags, transform a value, compare inputs or choose an output. This index covers all 64 built-in functions in OpenTag's format-string engine, including both forms of $meta through its optional index argument.

New to this?

Start with Format strings from zero and Regular expressions from zero. The family pages below explain every argument and provide worked examples.

docs.title: Choose a family
docs.text: Goal Reference Change spelling, capitalization or character ranges Text and case Find a substring or compare two strings Search and compare Select an output or combine conditions Conditions and logic Calculate integers or pad a number Numbers and maths Display a timestamp or elapsed time Dates and durations Read multiple values, columns or application context Lists, metadata and environment Match varying text with a pattern Regular expressions

docs.title: Read a function signature
docs.text:
$name(x,y) means two arguments separated by a comma. A signature such as $mid(x,start[,n]) has an optional final argument; the square brackets in this reference notation are not characters to type. Repeated arguments are shown with an ellipsis, for example $add(x,y[,z…]).

Function names ignore case, so $cutLeft and $cutleft are equivalent. Argument text can still be case-sensitive: the MM and mm date tokens, for example, mean different things.

Ordinary spaces in arguments are text. Quote a pattern or replacement when its commas, parentheses, brackets or dollar signs would otherwise become format-string syntax. An empty argument is written by leaving that position empty. '' supplies an apostrophe; it is not an empty string.

docs.title: Alphabetical index
docs.text: Function Use it to $add Add integers $and Require every condition flag $ansi Represent text in the system ANSI encoding $caps Capitalize words and lowercase their remaining letters $caps2 Capitalize words while preserving their remaining letters $caps3 Capitalize the first character and characters after explicit triggers $char Create a Unicode character from its code point $columnnames Format the configured file-list column names $columnvalues Format the current file's rendered column values $cutleft Remove characters from the beginning $cutright Remove characters from the end $dedup Keep the first distinct delimited segments $distance Count insertions, deletions and substitutions $div Divide integers in order $eql Compare numeric or case-insensitive string equality $fmtdate Format a calendar timestamp $fmtduration Format elapsed minutes, seconds and milliseconds $fmtnum Format a grouped integer for the numeric locale $folderdepth Count folder components in path text $geql Test greater than or equal $getenv Read environment or application directory context $grtr Test greater than $if Choose from two results using a flag $if2 Choose a field or expression fallback using its flag $ifgreater Choose based on integer magnitude $iflonger Choose based on character count $isdigit Test whether the first character is an ASCII digit $left Read the first characters $len Count characters $leql Test less than or equal $less Test less than $list Format raw tag-field names and values $lower Lowercase text $meta Read all field values or one indexed value $meta_sep Join field values with a chosen separator $mid Read characters from a position $mod Calculate integer remainders $mul Multiply integers $neql Test inequality $not Invert a flag $num Zero-pad a leading integer $odd Test integer oddness $or Accept any true condition flag $ord Read the first character's code point up to U+FFFF $rand Generate an integer from 0 through 32767 $regexp Replace pattern matches and reuse captures $repeat Repeat text $replace Apply ordered literal replacements $reverse Reverse character order $right Read the final characters $sort Sort literal-delimited segments $strchr Find the first occurrence of a character $strcmp Test exact string equality $stricmp Test string equality after lowercasing $strrchr Find the final occurrence of a character $strrstr Find the final occurrence of a substring $strstr Find the first occurrence of a substring $sub Subtract integers in order $trim Trim both ends $trimleft Trim the beginning $trimright Trim the end $upper Uppercase text $uuid Generate a version-4 UUID $validate Replace a defined set of forbidden filename characters

docs.title: Distinguish visible text, field availability and truth
docs.text:
A function can return the text 0 while retaining a true flag inherited from a present source field. Conversely, literal 1 has no true flag. Read the condition rules when using $if, $if2, $and, $or or $not. Comparisons such as $grtr produce explicit boolean flags.

Optional sections […] use field availability, which is a separate part of evaluation. Removing all text from a present field does not necessarily make its enclosing optional section behave like a missing field. Keep presence tests close to field placeholders; use explicit comparisons for questions about calculated text.

docs.title: Diagnose an expression error
docs.text:
Symptom Check Unknown function Check this index and the function name; export-template commands such as $loop use a separate context Wrong argument count Check the signature, commas and any unquoted comma inside the intended text Unterminated literal or function Balance single quotes and closing parentheses; build the expression from the inside out Valid expression, unexpected output Check missing fields, case rules, leading-integer conversion, and condition flags Context required Functions such as $columnvalues and $getenv(MP3TAGAPP) need the application's supplied context Output/work limit Reduce repetition, padding, comparison size or nesting rather than repeating the same oversized expression

A valid expression that finds no regex match normally returns its input unchanged. A missing field normally produces empty text. Those are results, not syntax errors. In a field-writing converter, an empty output can remove the destination field; preview before applying.

Each family page describes its own errors. Supplying too few or too many arguments reports an error rather than guessing which argument was intended. All function arguments are evaluated, including an unused conditional branch.

docs.title: Conditions and logic
docs.text:
Use conditions to choose between results, test values and combine questions. The format-string language tracks a truth flag alongside the visible text. That flag controls $if, $if2, $and, $or and $not.

New to this?

Follow Format strings from zero for a worked field fallback before using this reference.

docs.title: Understand what counts as true
docs.text:
Input to a condition Flag A placeholder with a nonempty first value True A missing or empty placeholder False A comparison that succeeds True; displayed text is 1 A comparison that fails False; displayed text is 0 Literal text, including 1, 0 and yes False

Most text and numeric functions inherit flags from their arguments. They do not recompute truth from their output. For example, searching a present title can return the position text 0 while still carrying a true flag. Test that position with $grtr(position,0).

All function arguments are evaluated before a result is chosen. A branch that is not selected can still report an error. Do not hide an invalid expression or division by zero in the unused branch of $if.

Examples use ARTIST = Juniper Vale, TITLE = Paper Boats, TRACK = 3/8, YEAR = 2024, with ALBUMARTIST and MISSING absent.

docs.title: $if(condition,yes,no)
docs.text:
Returns yes when the condition flag is true, otherwise no.

Argument Meaning condition A field-presence test or boolean expression yes, no Results for the two cases; either can be empty Format string With these values Result $if(%year%,dated,undated) YEAR = 2024 dated $if(1,yes,no) Any file no $if($eql(%year%,2024),current,other) YEAR = 2024 current

The result inherits the chosen branch's flag. Choosing literal yes displays that word but does not make it true if passed into another condition. Related: $if2.

docs.title: $if2(x,fallback)
docs.text:
Returns x when its flag is true, otherwise fallback.

Argument Meaning x Preferred expression, often a field placeholder fallback Expression to use when x is false Format string With these values Result $if2(%albumartist%,%artist%) ALBUMARTIST absent; ARTIST = Juniper Vale Juniper Vale $if2(ready,fallback) Any file fallback $if2($upper(%title%),unknown) TITLE = Paper Boats PAPER BOATS

This is a reliable missing-field fallback when the first argument is a placeholder. It is not a general nonempty-string test: literal ready is false, and a transformed present field can retain a true flag even when its output becomes empty. Related: $iflonger.

docs.title: $ifgreater(x,y,yes,no)
docs.text:
Returns yes if the leading integer in x is greater than the one in y, otherwise no.

Argument Meaning x, y Numeric inputs, interpreted with the leading-integer rule yes, no Results to select Format string With these values Result $ifgreater(%track%,2,later,early) TRACK = 3/8 later $ifgreater(B2,0,positive,zero or negative) Any file zero or negative $ifgreater($len(%title%),10,long,short) TITLE = Paper Boats long

Equal inputs take the no branch. Nonnumeric input becomes 0 rather than causing an error. Related: $grtr, numeric rules.

docs.title: $iflonger(x,n,yes,no)
docs.text:
Returns yes when x contains more than n characters, otherwise no.

Argument Meaning x Text whose character count is tested n Threshold; negative values become 0 yes, no Results to select Format string With these values Result $iflonger(%title%,10,long,short) TITLE = Paper Boats long $iflonger(abc,3,long,short) Any file short $iflonger($trim(' '),0,present,empty) Any file empty

Length counts Unicode characters, not UTF-8 bytes. This provides an explicit nonempty-text check when n is 0, independently of inherited truth flags. Related: $if2, text functions.

docs.title: Equality
docs.text: $eql and $neql compare integers when both complete input strings parse as integers. Otherwise they compare lowercase text. Unlike relational functions, they do not discard a suffix such as /8 for integer equality. Use $strcmp for exact string equality including case and zero padding.

docs.title: $eql(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when the values are equal under the rule above, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y The two values to compare Format string With these values Result $eql(03,3) Any file 1 $eql(3/8,3) Any file 0 $if($eql($lower(%title%),paper boats),same,different) TITLE = Paper Boats same

$eql(A,a) is true because fallback string equality ignores case. Related: $neql, $strcmp.

docs.title: $neql(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns the inverse of $eql: true (1) when unequal, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y The two values to compare Format string With these values Result $neql(3,4) Any file 1 $neql(A,a) Any file 0 $if($neql($num(%track%,1),3),other,third) TRACK = 3/8 third

This does not mean "different after trimming"; surrounding whitespace can change string comparison. Related: $eql.

docs.title: Relational comparisons
docs.text: The following four functions compare leading integers. A missing or nonnumeric argument counts as 0. They are numeric comparisons, not alphabetical sorting rules.

docs.title: $grtr(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when x is greater than y, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y Leading-integer inputs to compare Format string With these values Result $grtr(4,3) Any file 1 $grtr(B2,0) Any file 0 $if($grtr($strstr(%title%,Boats),0),found,missing) TITLE = Paper Boats found

Equal values are false. Related: $geql.

docs.title: $geql(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when x is greater than or equal to y, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y Leading-integer inputs to compare Format string With these values Result $geql(3,3) Any file 1 $geql(-1,0) Any file 0 $if($geql($len(%title%),11),long enough,short) TITLE = Paper Boats long enough

The first example includes equality, which distinguishes it from $grtr. Related: $leql.

docs.title: $less(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when x is less than y, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y Leading-integer inputs to compare Format string With these values Result $less(2,3) Any file 1 $less(3,3) Any file 0 $if($less($num(%track%,1),4),first three,later) TRACK = 3/8 first three

Equal values are false. Related: $leql.

docs.title: $leql(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when x is less than or equal to y, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y Leading-integer inputs to compare Format string With these values Result $leql(3,3) Any file 1 $leql(4,3) Any file 0 $if($leql($len(%title%),11),fits,too long) TITLE = Paper Boats fits

The equality case is included. Related: $less.

docs.title: $and(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns true (1) only when every argument's flag is true. Accepts 2–63 arguments.

Argument Meaning x, y, later arguments Presence checks or boolean expressions Format string With these values Result $and($eql(1,1),$grtr(3,1)) Any file 1 $and(1,1) Any file 0 $if($and(%artist%,%year%),complete,incomplete) ARTIST and YEAR present complete

Literal 1 is not a boolean true value. All arguments are evaluated; this is not a short-circuit error guard. Related: $or.

docs.title: $or(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when at least one argument's flag is true. Accepts 2–63 arguments.

Argument Meaning x, y, later arguments Presence checks or boolean expressions Format string With these values Result $or(%missing%,%artist%) MISSING absent; ARTIST present 1 $or(yes,1) Any file 0 $if($or(%artist%,%albumartist%),credited,unknown) ARTIST present; ALBUMARTIST absent credited

Use $if2 when the goal is to return one field's actual text rather than ask whether either field is available. Related: $and.

docs.title: $not(x)
docs.text:
Returns the opposite of x's flag: false becomes true (1), and true becomes false (0).

Argument Meaning x Flag to invert Format string With these values Result $not(%missing%) MISSING absent 1 $not(1) Any file 1 $if($not($eql(%year%,2024)),other,year 2024) YEAR = 2024 year 2024

The second example follows the literal-text rule: literal 1 starts false, so negating it is true. Related: $eql.

docs.title: $odd(x)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when the leading integer is odd, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x Leading-integer input to test Format string With these values Result $odd(3) Any file 1 $odd(B2) Any file 0 $if($odd($num(%track%,1)),odd track,even track) TRACK = 3/8 odd track

Negative odd numbers are also true. A nonnumeric value becomes 0 and is therefore even under this rule. Related: numbers and maths.

docs.title: Dates and durations
docs.text:
Use $fmtdate for calendar timestamps and $fmtduration for elapsed time. A duration is not a date: 90061 seconds can display as 25:01:01 without referring to a particular day.

New to this?

Read Format strings from zero for argument syntax and nested expressions.

Function names are case-insensitive: $fmtDate and $fmtdate call the same function. Tokens inside a date pattern are case-sensitive.

docs.title: $fmtdate(pattern[,timestamp])
docs.text:
Returns a calendar date/time formatted with pattern. Supply an integer Unix timestamp in seconds, or omit it to use the current time.

Argument Meaning pattern Date tokens and literal text, described below timestamp Optional whole seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC; an explicitly empty argument means 0

The timestamp selects an instant. The application's timezone determines its displayed local calendar date and time. Month and weekday names use the date locale. The examples below explicitly assume UTC and en-US, with timestamp 1704164645 = 2024-01-02 03:04:05 UTC.

Format string With these values Result $fmtdate('yyyy-MM-dd',1704164645) UTC, en-US 2024-01-02 $fmtdate('yyyy-MM-dd',) UTC, en-US 1970-01-01 $upper($fmtdate(MMM,1704164645)) UTC, en-US JAN $fmtdate('yyyy-MM-dd ''day'' HH:mm',1704164645) UTC, en-US 2024-01-02 day 03:04

To format a file timestamp, use a raw timestamp placeholder, for example $fmtdate('yyyy-MM-dd',%_file_mod_datetime_raw%). A human-readable date string is not an integer timestamp. Invalid integers, unsupported named locales and timestamps outside the supported calendar range report errors.

docs.title: Every date token
docs.text:
Results in this table use the same UTC/en-US instant:

Token Meaning Example result yyyy Four-digit year 2024 yy Two-digit year 24 MMMM Full month name January MMM Abbreviated month name Jan MM Two-digit month 01 M Month without leading zero 1 dddd Full weekday name Tuesday EEEE Alias for full weekday name Tuesday ddd Abbreviated weekday name Tue EE Alias for abbreviated weekday name Tue dd Two-digit day of month 02 d Day of month without leading zero 2 HH Two-digit 24-hour clock hour 03 H 24-hour clock hour without leading zero 3 hh Two-digit 12-hour clock hour 03 h 12-hour clock hour without leading zero 3 mm Two-digit minute 04 m Minute without leading zero 4 ss Two-digit second 05 s Second without leading zero 5

Use MM for a month and mm for minutes. Neither %Y-%m-%d nor an arbitrary platform date-format language is substituted for this token set. Text not recognized as a token is copied, but a token embedded in an ordinary word is still interpreted.

docs.title: Quote literal date text
docs.text:
There are two parsing layers. First the format-string parser reads the function argument. Then the date formatter reads tokens within that argument.

In the last expression above, the outer quotes group the pattern as one argument. Each doubled apostrophe inside those quotes passes one apostrophe to the date formatter, which sees:

yyyy-MM-dd 'day' HH:mm

The date formatter copies day literally. Without its own quotes, the d in day would become the day-of-month token. Within a date pattern, two apostrophes represent one literal apostrophe. An unclosed date literal is an error.

docs.title: $fmtduration(x[,unit[,hours[,milliseconds]]])
docs.text:
Returns elapsed time in minutes/seconds, optionally including hours and milliseconds. It accepts a finite decimal number.

Argument Meaning x Duration value; a missing or empty value means zero unit s for seconds, m for minutes, or ms for milliseconds; omitted/empty means seconds hours Literal 1 requests HH:MM:SS; other values leave total minutes as M:SS milliseconds Literal 1 appends .mmm; omitted/other values do not Format string With these values Result $fmtduration(61) Any file 1:01 $fmtduration(-1.25,s,0,1) Any file -0:01.250 $fmtduration($add(3600,61),s,1) Any file 01:01:01 $fmtduration(1.5,m) Any file 1:30 $fmtduration(61234,ms,0,1) Any file 1:01.234 $fmtduration(90061,s,1) Any file 25:01:01

Hours can exceed 23 because this is a duration. The function does not insert day units. The hours and milliseconds options compare their text to 1; they are not the typed condition flags used by $if.

Fractional precision beyond milliseconds is truncated, not rounded. Units must be lowercase m, s or ms. Scientific notation, NaN, infinity, malformed decimal text and arithmetic overflow report errors. The integer arithmetic functions use a different leading-integer rule; do not pass a decimal through $add if its fractional part must survive.

docs.title: Lists, metadata and environment
docs.text:
Use these functions to read multiple field values, inspect the file-list columns, transform delimited lists and access application context.

New to this?

A bare %artist% reads the first artist value. Follow Format strings from zero, then use $meta or $meta_sep when the remaining values matter.

Unless a row says otherwise, examples on this page use only these tag fields: ARTIST has two values, Juniper Vale and Mira Solberg, and TITLE has one value, Paper Boats. The example file-list columns are Title = Paper Boats, then Artist = Juniper Vale.

docs.title: $meta(field[,index])
docs.text:
Returns all values of a field joined with comma-space when index is omitted, or one value at the zero-based index when it is supplied.

Argument Meaning field Field name such as artist, without percent signs index Optional zero-based value index: 0 is first, 1 is second Format string With these values Result $meta(artist) Two artist values from the example Juniper Vale, Mira Solberg $meta(artist,9) Two artist values from the example (empty) $upper($meta(artist,1)) Two artist values from the example MIRA SOLBERG $meta(artist,-1) Two artist values from the example Juniper Vale

A missing field or out-of-range index returns empty text. Use $meta(artist), not $meta(%artist%): the latter treats the artist's value as a field name. The index uses a nonnegative leading-integer count; negative or nonnumeric input becomes 0, as the last example shows. Related: $meta_sep.

docs.title: $meta_sep(field,separator)
docs.text:
Returns all values of a field joined with the chosen separator.

Argument Meaning field Field name without percent signs separator Literal text to put between values; may be empty Format string With these values Result $meta_sep(artist,' & ') Two artist values from the example Juniper Vale & Mira Solberg $meta_sep(missing,'; ') MISSING absent (empty) $upper($meta_sep(artist,/)) Two artist values from the example JUNIPER VALE/MIRA SOLBERG

Joining produces one string; it does not create separate destination values. Use a field-splitting action for that structural change. Related: $meta.

docs.title: $list(prefix,separator,suffix[,value_separator])
docs.text:
Returns a formatted entry for each raw tag field, joining the entries without an additional delimiter.

Argument Meaning prefix Text before each field name separator Text between the name and its values suffix Text after each field's values value_separator Text between that field's values; defaults to a comma Format string With these values Result $list('<',=,'>') Only example ARTIST and TITLE fields <ARTIST=Juniper Vale,Mira Solberg><TITLE=Paper Boats> $list('<',=,'>',';') Only example ARTIST and TITLE fields <ARTIST=Juniper Vale;Mira Solberg><TITLE=Paper Boats> $upper($list(,=,';',' & ')) Only example ARTIST and TITLE fields ARTIST=JUNIPER VALE & MIRA SOLBERG;TITLE=PAPER BOATS;

The field names and values come from the raw tag-field map, not visible column names or all information placeholders. The examples show the map's field-name order. Quoting the < and > here makes the intended literal text explicit; if the result is used in HTML, escape its data for that output format rather than assuming this function performs HTML escaping. Related: $columnnames, $meta_sep.

docs.title: $sort(x,delimiter)
docs.text:
Returns the segments of x sorted lexicographically and rejoined with the same literal delimiter.

Argument Meaning x Text containing segments delimiter Nonempty literal separator; may contain several characters Format string With these values Result $sort(b;a;c,;) Any file a;b;c $sort(10;2,;) Any file 10;2 $upper($sort(b;a,;)) Any file A;B

Sorting is case-sensitive, does not trim segments, and is not a numeric or locale-aware natural sort. Empty segments participate too. An empty delimiter reports an error. Related: $dedup.

docs.title: $dedup(x,delimiter[,ignore_case])
docs.text:
Returns the first occurrence of each distinct segment, preserving the original order and spelling.

Argument Meaning x Text containing segments delimiter Nonempty literal separator ignore_case Optional literal 1 ignores case; omitted/other text compares exactly Format string With these values Result $dedup(a;b;a,;) Any file a;b $dedup(A;a;B;A,;,1) Any file A;B $upper($dedup(a;b;a,;)) Any file A;B

Segments are not trimmed. A and A differ even with case ignored. The optional setting compares its text to 1; it does not use a typed condition flag. Empty delimiters are rejected. Related: $sort.

docs.title: $columnnames(prefix,suffix)
docs.text:
Returns each file-list column's name wrapped in the prefix and suffix, in configured column order.

Argument Meaning prefix Text before every name suffix Text after every name; also useful as a separator Format string With these values Result $columnnames('[',']') Columns Title, Artist [Title][Artist] $columnnames(,';') No columns in supplied context (empty) $upper($columnnames(,';')) Columns Title, Artist TITLE;ARTIST;

This function requires the application's column context. An empty column list returns empty text; unavailable context reports an error. A trailing separator in the last example comes from the suffix after the final column. The Value expression of a file-list column does not itself receive that column context, so this function cannot be used there to list its peers. Related: $columnvalues.

docs.title: $columnvalues(prefix,suffix)
docs.text:
Returns the current file's rendered values for the file-list columns, wrapped individually and kept in configured column order.

Argument Meaning prefix Text before every rendered value suffix Text after every rendered value Format string With these values Result $columnvalues('[',']') Example Title and Artist columns [Paper Boats][Juniper Vale] $columnvalues(,';') No columns in supplied context (empty) $lower($columnvalues(,';')) Example Title and Artist columns paper boats;juniper vale;

These are display results from column definitions, which can differ from raw tag values. Missing column context reports an error. Do not assume a standalone expression evaluator has an application's rendered columns. The Value expression inside a column is evaluated without that context; it cannot call this function to read the other columns' rendered results. Related: $columnnames, $list.

docs.title: $folderdepth(path)
docs.text:
Returns the number of folder components, excluding a drive or UNC server/share prefix and excluding the last component when it looks like a file path without a trailing separator.

Argument Meaning path Path text using slash or backslash separators Format string With these values Result $folderdepth('C:\Music\Album\03.mp3') Any file 2 $folderdepth('\\server\share\Album\03.mp3') Any file 1 $add($folderdepth('C:\Music\Album\03.mp3'),1) Any file 3 $folderdepth('Music\Album\') Any file 2

The function inspects text; it does not check the filesystem. A folder path without its trailing separator can have its last component treated as a filename. Related: Path placeholders.

docs.title: $getenv(name)
docs.text:
Returns the named environment value. A missing ordinary variable gives empty text. The two compatibility names below read application context.

Argument Meaning name Environment-variable name, or MP3TAGAPP / MP3TAGAPPDATA

These examples supply GUIDE_READER=listener, application directory /opt/OpenTag, and configuration directory /home/listener/.config/opentag:

Format string With these values Result $getenv(GUIDE_READER) Supplied example environment listener $getenv(GUIDE_MISSING_VARIABLE) Variable absent (empty) $upper($getenv(GUIDE_READER)) Supplied example environment LISTENER $getenv(MP3TAGAPP) Supplied application directory /opt/OpenTag $getenv(MP3TAGAPPDATA) Supplied configuration directory /home/listener/.config/opentag

MP3TAGAPP and MP3TAGAPPDATA are compatibility identifiers in OpenTag; their names do not refer to another running program. They require the corresponding application context or report an error. Ordinary variable names follow the host environment's naming rules. Related: $folderdepth.

docs.title: $uuid()
docs.text:
Returns a newly generated version-4 UUID in hyphenated lowercase form. There are no arguments; retain the empty parentheses.

Format string With these values Result $uuid() Any file A UUID in 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form $len($uuid()) Any file 36 $upper($uuid()) Any file A UUID in uppercase 8-4-4-4-12 form

Each call generates a value. Re-evaluating the expression can therefore change it. Store a generated value once when later operations must reuse that same identifier; do not assume two $uuid() calls agree. Related: $rand.

docs.title: Numbers and maths
docs.text:
Use these functions to pad track numbers, calculate integers and format readable counts. They return text for the enclosing format string.

New to this?

Start with Format strings from zero. The format-string reference explains nesting and quoting.

docs.title: Read the numeric rules first
docs.text:
Arithmetic uses signed integers, not decimal arithmetic. A leading integer is read after any initial whitespace. Text after that integer is ignored: 3/8 means 3, 12px means 12, and 2.9 means 2. Text without a leading integer, such as B2, means 0. Do not apply these functions to vinyl sides or decimal measurements without first deciding how to represent them.

Operations run from left to right. Overflow and division by zero report errors. Numeric output does not automatically become a true condition; use comparison functions when testing a result.

docs.title: $num(x,n)
docs.text:
Returns the leading integer from x, padded with zeros to at least n characters. Use it for a predictable filename width.

Argument Meaning x Numeric text or a field such as %track% n Minimum width; a negative value is treated as zero Format string With these values Result $num(%track%,2) TRACK = 3/8 03 $num(B2,2) Any file 00 $num($add(%track%,10),3) TRACK = 3/8 013

The total after / is not retained. Width is a minimum, so $num(123,2) remains 123. Excessive padding is rejected by the output limit. Related: Auto-numbering recipe.

docs.title: $add(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns the sum of 2–64 integer arguments.

Argument Meaning x, y, later arguments Integers or text with a leading integer Format string With these values Result $add(3,4) Any file 7 $add(B2,4) Any file 4 $num($add(%track%,8),2) TRACK = 3/8 11

$add(1.9,2.9) calculates 1 + 2, not a decimal sum. A missing field contributes 0. Related: $sub, $num.

docs.title: $sub(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns the result of subtracting each later argument from the running value. Accepts 2–64 arguments.

Argument Meaning x Initial value y, later arguments Values to subtract in sequence Format string With these values Result $sub(10,3,2) Any file 5 $sub(2,5) Any file -3 $num($sub(%track%,1),2) TRACK = 3/8 02

The first example means (10 - 3) - 2. Negative results are allowed; they do not indicate a parsing error. Related: $add.

docs.title: $mul(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns the product of 2–64 integer arguments.

Argument Meaning x, y, later arguments Factors multiplied in order Format string With these values Result $mul(2,3,4) Any file 24 $mul(5,%missing%) MISSING absent 0 $add($mul(%track%,10),1) TRACK = 3/8 31

One missing or nonnumeric argument can turn the entire product into 0. Large products can overflow and report an error. Related: $div.

docs.title: $div(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns sequential integer division, discarding each fractional part toward zero. Accepts 2–64 arguments.

Argument Meaning x Initial dividend y, later arguments Divisors applied from left to right Format string With these values Result $div(17,5) Any file 3 $div(-17,5) Any file -3 $add($div(125,60),1) Any file 3

Division by 0, including a missing field used as divisor, is an error. Use $fmtduration for a formatted time rather than trying to build time text with rounded decimal division. Related: $mod, dates and durations.

docs.title: $mod(x,y[,z…])
docs.text:
Returns the remainder after each integer division, from left to right. Accepts 2–64 arguments.

Argument Meaning x Initial dividend y, later arguments Divisors for successive remainder operations Format string With these values Result $mod(17,5) Any file 2 $mod(-17,5) Any file -2 $num($mod(125,60),2) Any file 05

A negative dividend can produce a negative remainder. This is a remainder operation, not a guarantee of a positive mathematical modulo. A zero divisor is an error. Related: $div.

docs.title: $fmtnum(x)
docs.text:
Returns a grouped integer using the application's numeric locale or system number-format settings. Use it for display, not identifiers.

Argument Meaning x Text interpreted with the leading-integer rule

These examples use an en-US numeric format:

Format string With these values Result $fmtnum(1234567) Numeric locale en-US 1,234,567 $fmtnum(B2) Numeric locale en-US 0 $fmtnum($mul(1250,8)) Numeric locale en-US 10,000

Another locale can use different group separators or grouping widths. An unsupported locale or invalid custom grouping reports an error. Use $num for zero padding without locale grouping.

docs.title: $rand()
docs.text:
Returns a newly generated integer from 0 through 32767 inclusive. There are no arguments, but the empty parentheses are required.

Format string With these values Result $rand() Any file An integer from 0 through 32767 $num($rand(),5) Any file Five decimal digits, for example 00123 $mod($rand(),10) Any file An integer from 0 through 9

The examples describe ranges, not fixed outputs. Each call can return a different value, including two calls in one expression. Random numbers are not unique IDs and can collide; do not use a single random value as the only distinguishing part of a filename. Related: $uuid.

docs.title: Search and compare
docs.text:
Use these functions to locate text, compare values or check a naming rule. Search positions start at 1; 0 means no match. Boolean comparisons return text 1 or 0 with a corresponding condition flag.

New to this?

Work through Format strings from zero before building a nested search condition.

Examples use TITLE = Paper Boats. Searches are case-sensitive and count Unicode characters rather than UTF-8 bytes. A search result inherits its input's truth flag; test the returned position with $grtr(position,0) instead of passing the position directly to $if.

docs.title: $strstr(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns the first position of the whole substring y in x, or 0.

Argument Meaning x Text to search y Exact substring to find Format string With these values Result $strstr(%title%,Boats) TITLE = Paper Boats 7 $strstr(%title%,boats) TITLE = Paper Boats 0 $if($grtr($strstr(%title%,Boats),0),found,missing) TITLE = Paper Boats found

An empty search string returns 0. To search without case sensitivity, normalize both inputs with $lower first. Related: $strrstr.

docs.title: $strrstr(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns the last starting position of substring y in x, or 0.

Argument Meaning x Text to search y Exact substring to locate from the right Format string With these values Result $strrstr(la-la-la,la) Any file 7 $strrstr(Paper Boats,xyz) Any file 0 $if($grtr($strrstr(%title%,a),0),has a,no a) TITLE = Paper Boats has a

The returned number is still measured from the left. It is not a count of characters from the end. Related: $strstr.

docs.title: $strchr(x,c)
docs.text:
Returns the first position of the first character in c, or 0.

Argument Meaning x Text to search c Character to find; only its first character is used Format string With these values Result $strchr(%title%,a) TITLE = Paper Boats 2 $strchr(%title%,Bo) TITLE = Paper Boats 7 $if($grtr($strchr(%title%,z),0),found,missing) TITLE = Paper Boats missing

The second example searches for B, not for either B or o, and not for the complete string Bo. An empty c returns 0. Related: $strrchr, $strstr.

docs.title: $strrchr(x,c)
docs.text:
Returns the last position of the first character in c, or 0.

Argument Meaning x Text to search c Character whose last occurrence is wanted Format string With these values Result $strrchr(%title%,a) TITLE = Paper Boats 9 $strrchr(%title%,) TITLE = Paper Boats 0 $if($grtr($strrchr(%title%,a),5),late,early) TITLE = Paper Boats late

Only the first character of c participates, even when more text is supplied. Related: $strchr, $strrstr.

docs.title: $strcmp(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when both strings are exactly equal, otherwise false (0). This is an equality test, not a sorting comparator.

Argument Meaning x, y Strings to compare, including their case and spaces Format string With these values Result $strcmp(%title%,Paper Boats) TITLE = Paper Boats 1 $strcmp(03,3) Any file 0 $if($strcmp($lower(%title%),paper boats),same,different) TITLE = Paper Boats same

03 and 3 differ as strings. Use $eql when integer equality is the intended rule. Related: $stricmp, conditions and logic.

docs.title: $stricmp(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when the strings are equal after lowercase conversion, otherwise false (0).

Argument Meaning x, y Strings to compare without letter-case differences Format string With these values Result $stricmp(%title%,PAPER BOATS) TITLE = Paper Boats 1 $stricmp('Paper Boats ','Paper Boats') Any file 0 $if($stricmp($trim(' Paper Boats '),PAPER BOATS),same,different) Any file same

Whitespace still matters. Lowercase conversion is not a general language-aware equivalence or accent-removal rule. Related: $strcmp.

docs.title: $distance(x,y)
docs.text:
Returns the Levenshtein edit distance: the fewest single-character insertions, deletions or substitutions needed to turn x into y.

Argument Meaning x, y The two strings to compare Format string With these values Result $distance(%title%,Paper Boat) TITLE = Paper Boats 1 $distance(,abc) Any file 3 $if($eql($distance(%title%,Paper Boats),0),exact,changed) TITLE = Paper Boats exact

Case differences count as changes. The result measures spelling differences, not whether two titles refer to the same recording. Very large comparisons are rejected by a work limit. Related: $stricmp.

docs.title: $validate(x,repl)
docs.text:
Returns x with each of / ? * " < > | : replaced by repl. Use it to clean a component under that specific rule.

Argument Meaning x Text to clean repl Literal replacement for each forbidden character; may be empty Format string With these values Result $validate('Paper: Boats?',_) Any file Paper_ Boats_ $validate('A/B',) Any file AB $upper($validate('a:b',-)) Any file A-B

This function does not create a path, remove all platform-specific invalid names, or check whether a destination exists. Backslashes are not in this function's replacement set. Filename evaluation has additional rules; see file and folder names.

docs.title: $isdigit(x)
docs.text:
Returns true (1) when the first character is an ASCII digit 0–9, otherwise false (0). It does not validate the entire string as a number.

Argument Meaning x Text whose first character is checked Format string With these values Result $isdigit(3/8) Any file 1 $isdigit(-3) Any file 0 $if($isdigit($trim(' 3/8')),numeric prefix,other) Any file numeric prefix

12x is true, while an empty string or one beginning with whitespace is false. To require a complete numeric form, use a suitable anchored regular expression. Related: Regular expressions.

docs.title: Text and case
docs.text:
Use these functions to transform text, select characters and control capitalization. Functions read values and return text; they do not change a source tag until the surrounding converter or action writes the result.

New to this?

Follow Format strings from zero, then return here for individual argument rules.

Examples using %title% assume TITLE = Paper Boats. A middle dot · in a result marks a significant space; type an actual space when reproducing it. Character counts and positions use Unicode scalar values. Combining characters can therefore count separately from the character they decorate.

docs.title: $lower(x)
docs.text:
Returns x with lowercase letters.

Argument Meaning x Text to transform. Format string With these values Result $lower(%title%) TITLE = Paper Boats paper boats $lower(ÉTÉ) Any file été $lower($left(%title%,5)) TITLE = Paper Boats paper

Case conversion can change a name's intended spelling. It does not remove accents.

Related: $upper.

docs.title: $upper(x)
docs.text:
Returns x with uppercase letters.

Argument Meaning x Text to transform. Format string With these values Result $upper(%title%) TITLE = Paper Boats PAPER BOATS $upper(été) Any file ÉTÉ $upper($left(%title%,5)) TITLE = Paper Boats PAPER

Unicode uppercasing can change the number of characters; do not assume it preserves string length.

Related: $lower.

docs.title: $caps(x[,separators])
docs.text:
Returns text with each word's first character uppercased and its remaining characters lowercased.

Argument Meaning x Text to transform. separators Optional additional characters that start the next word; whitespace always does. Format string With these values Result $caps(PAPER BOATS) Any file Paper Boats $caps(DJ NIMBUS) Any file Dj Nimbus $caps($replace(low_tide,_,' ')) Any file Low Tide

This is mechanical capitalization, not a language-aware title style. DJ becomes Dj. The separator argument is a set of characters, not a regex.

Related: $caps2.

docs.title: $caps2(x[,separators])
docs.text:
Returns text with each word's first character uppercased and its remaining characters preserved as written.

Argument Meaning x Text to transform. separators Optional extra word-boundary characters; whitespace always starts a word. Format string With these values Result $caps2(pAPER bOATS) Any file PAPER BOATS $caps2(DJ NIMBUS) Any file DJ NIMBUS $caps2($lower(%title%)) TITLE = Paper Boats Paper Boats

This does not repair arbitrary uppercase text: existing uppercase letters after the first character remain uppercase.

Related: $caps.

docs.title: $caps3(x[,triggers])
docs.text:
Returns text with the first character uppercased, subsequent characters lowercased, and another uppercase character immediately after each trigger.

Argument Meaning x Text to transform. triggers Optional characters after which the very next character is uppercased. Format string With these values Result $caps3(PAPER BOATS) Any file Paper boats $caps3('FIRST. SECOND',.) Any file First. second $caps3($upper(%title%)) TITLE = Paper Boats Paper boats

A trigger affects the next character, even when that character is a space. This is not sentence recognition; in the second example the period triggers the space, and second remains lowercase.

Related: $caps.

docs.title: $len(x)
docs.text:
Returns the number of Unicode characters in x.

Argument Meaning x Text to count. Format string With these values Result $len(%title%) TITLE = Paper Boats 11 $len(é猫🙂) Any file 3 $ifgreater($len(%title%),10,long,short) TITLE = Paper Boats long

The count uses Unicode scalar values, not bytes or user-perceived grapheme clusters. A combining accent can count separately.

Related: $left.

docs.title: $left(x,n)
docs.text:
Returns at most the first n characters of x.

Argument Meaning x Text to read. n Character count; zero or negative means none. Format string With these values Result $left(%title%,5) TITLE = Paper Boats Paper $left(abc,0) Any file (empty) $upper($left(%title%,5)) TITLE = Paper Boats PAPER

Asking for more characters than exist returns the available text. It does not pad the result.

Related: $right.

docs.title: $right(x,n)
docs.text:
Returns at most the final n characters of x.

Argument Meaning x Text to read. n Character count; zero or negative means none. Format string With these values Result $right(%title%,5) TITLE = Paper Boats Boats $right(abc,9) Any file abc $lower($right(%title%,5)) TITLE = Paper Boats boats

The count is in Unicode characters. For a known prefix to discard, $cutleft often states the intent more clearly.

Related: $cutleft.

docs.title: $mid(x,start[,n])
docs.text:
Returns characters beginning at position start, counting from 1. If n is omitted, return one character.

Argument Meaning x Text to read. start First position, starting at 1; zero or negative produces empty text. n Optional maximum character count, initially 1. Format string With these values Result $mid(%title%,7,5) TITLE = Paper Boats Boats $mid(abc,0,2) Any file (empty) $upper($mid(%title%,7)) TITLE = Paper Boats B

Omitting the length does not mean the rest of the string. Positions beyond the end return empty text.

Related: $len.

docs.title: $cutleft(x,n)
docs.text:
Returns x after removing up to n characters from its beginning.

Argument Meaning x Text to shorten. n Number of initial characters to remove. Format string With these values Result $cutleft(%title%,6) TITLE = Paper Boats Boats $cutleft(abc,9) Any file (empty) $upper($cutleft(%title%,6)) TITLE = Paper Boats BOATS

A count beyond the text's length removes everything. A zero or negative count leaves it unchanged.

Related: $cutright.

docs.title: $cutright(x,n)
docs.text:
Returns x after removing up to n characters from its end.

Argument Meaning x Text to shorten. n Number of final characters to remove. Format string With these values Result $cutright(%title%,6) TITLE = Paper Boats Paper $cutright(abc,0) Any file abc $lower($cutright(%title%,6)) TITLE = Paper Boats paper

The function counts characters, not suffix words. Use a regex if the suffix varies in length or should be checked before removal.

Related: $cutleft.

docs.title: $trim(x[,chars])
docs.text:
Returns x with matching characters removed from both ends.

Argument Meaning x Text to trim. chars Optional set of characters to remove; otherwise trim whitespace. Format string With these values Result $trim(' Paper Boats ') Any file Paper Boats $trim('--Title--',-) Any file Title $upper($trim(' Paper Boats ')) Any file PAPER BOATS

The optional argument is a character set, not a substring. An explicitly empty set removes nothing; interior whitespace is not collapsed.

Related: $trimleft.

docs.title: $trimleft(x[,chars])
docs.text:
Returns x with matching characters removed only from its beginning.

Argument Meaning x Text to trim. chars Optional trim-character set; otherwise whitespace. Format string With these values Result $trimleft(' Paper Boats ') Any file Paper Boats·· $trimleft('--Title--',-) Any file Title-- $upper($trimleft(' Paper Boats ')) Any file PAPER BOATS·

Trailing text and spaces remain, as the first result shows. The optional set is not a literal prefix to remove once.

Related: $trimright.

docs.title: $trimright(x[,chars])
docs.text:
Returns x with matching characters removed only from its end.

Argument Meaning x Text to trim. chars Optional trim-character set; otherwise whitespace. Format string With these values Result $trimright(' Paper Boats ') Any file ··Paper Boats $trimright('--Title--',-) Any file --Title $upper($trimright(' Paper Boats ')) Any file ·PAPER BOATS

Leading spaces remain. Use $trim when both ends should be cleaned.

Related: $trim.

docs.title: $repeat(x,n)
docs.text:
Returns x repeated n times.

Argument Meaning x Text to repeat. n Repeat count; zero or negative produces empty text. Format string With these values Result $repeat(la,3) Any file lalala $repeat(x,0) Any file (empty) $upper($repeat(la,2)) Any file LALA

The function adds no separators. Excessively large results report an output-limit error.

Related: $replace.

docs.title: $reverse(x)
docs.text:
Returns x with its character order reversed.

Argument Meaning x Text to reverse. Format string With these values Result $reverse(%title%) TITLE = Paper Boats staoB repaP $reverse(%missing%) MISSING absent (empty) $upper($reverse(ab)) Any file BA

Reversal works on Unicode scalar values, so combining sequences and other grapheme clusters may be split.

Related: $len.

docs.title: $replace(x,from,to[,from,to…])
docs.text:
Returns x with every exact occurrence of each search string replaced, processing the pairs in order.

Argument Meaning x Original text. from Nonempty literal search string; matching is case-sensitive. to Literal replacement; an empty argument deletes matches. Format string With these values Result $replace(%title%,Boats,Ships) TITLE = Paper Boats Paper Ships $replace(aaa,a,b,b,c) Any file ccc $upper($replace(%title%,' ',_)) TITLE = Paper Boats PAPER_BOATS

Later pairs see earlier replacements. This is not regex replacement: $1 is literal text here. Supply complete search/replacement pairs, with 3–63 arguments in total; an empty search string is an error.

Related: $trim.

docs.title: $char(n)
docs.text:
Returns the Unicode character at numeric code point n.

Argument Meaning n A valid Unicode scalar value interpreted as an integer. Format string With these values Result $char(65) Any file A $char(233) Any file é $lower($char(65)) Any file a

Negative, surrogate or out-of-range code points report errors. Although $char supports supplementary characters, $ord is limited to U+FFFF.

Related: $ord.

docs.title: $ord(x)
docs.text:
Returns the numeric code point of the first character, limited to U+0000–U+FFFF. An empty input returns 0.

Argument Meaning x Text whose first character is inspected. Format string With these values Result $ord(A) Any file 65 $ord(%missing%) MISSING absent 0 $add($ord(a),1) Any file 98

Later characters are ignored. A first character above U+FFFF, such as many emoji, reports an error rather than returning its full code point.

Related: $char.

docs.title: $ansi(x)
docs.text:
Returns text retaining characters representable in the application's ANSI codepage, with unrepresentable characters replaced by ?.

Argument Meaning x Unicode text to round-trip through the system ANSI encoding. Format string With these values Result $ansi(Café) ANSI codepage windows-1252 Café $ansi(猫) ANSI codepage windows-1252 ? $upper($ansi(Café)) ANSI codepage windows-1252 CAFÉ

These examples assume Windows-1252. In a UTF-8 context the text is preserved. This operation can lose characters; it is not a repair for already-misdecoded legacy bytes. Missing or unsupported codepage context reports an error.

Related: $replace.

docs.title: Tag sources
docs.text: Tag sources look up metadata, lyrics and artwork for selected files. Choose a result, check its fields and file-to-track matches, then save the changes.

docs.title: Choose a source
docs.text:
Source Use it for Setup MusicBrainz Release metadata and Cover Art Archive artwork No key Discogs Releases, catalog numbers and artwork Optional personal token; some builds include an application key iTunes Store album metadata and artwork No key; choose the store country in Options Deezer Album metadata, ISRCs and artwork No key LRCLIB Lyrics matched to each selected file No key AcoustID Recordings identified by audio fingerprint API key and separately installed fpcalc; desktop only Last.fm Album metadata and listener tags for GENRE API key fanart.tv Album covers and disc artwork API key; covers only freedb / freedb (local) Disc metadata from a CDDB server or local database folder Configure the server or local folder in Options

Covers: MusicBrainz…, Covers: Discogs…, Covers: iTunes…, Covers: Deezer… and Covers: fanart.tv… write artwork without changing text fields. A provider may have no result for your edition.

docs.title: Search, review and save
docs.text:
1. Select the files for one album. Check their order and existing tags.
  2. Choose a source from Tag Sources, choose a search type, enter the identifying information and select Search or Look up for an ID.
  3. Select a search result and choose Next. An ID lookup opens the review directly. Preview opens the source's page in your browser without writing tags.
  4. In Fields, uncheck values to keep unchanged and edit proposed values where needed. Missing source values do not clear existing fields.
  5. Check Tracks and files. Use Auto-match, Selection order or Suggest sorting, then drag files or use row arrows to correct matches. AcoustID retains fingerprint pairs; LRCLIB's per-file result keeps file order.
  6. Choose whether to write artwork and replace existing covers. Save image to file also saves it beside the written files, using the configured cover file name.
  7. Select Save tags to … files or Save cover to … files. Its count shows how many files will be written.

Saving writes immediately. Unmatched files and files with no checked source values or selected cover are skipped. A successful import is one undo step; use Edit → Undo to undo it. Cancel leaves proposed tag changes unwritten. Save cover as… saves the displayed image separately when requested; canceling the tagging dialog does not cancel that separate save.

Save image to file replaces an existing image with the same name and extension. Replace existing artwork controls embedded covers; it does not protect an existing external image from that replacement.

Repeat the last source with Cmd+I / Ctrl+I. Add Shift (Cmd+Shift+I / Ctrl+Shift+I) to start its search immediately when the required input is available.

docs.title: Set up API keys
docs.text:
Open Tag Sources → API keys… for AcoustID, Last.fm and fanart.tv. Each section says whether this build includes a key. Without a built-in or saved key, the corresponding source stays unavailable.

Enter your key and choose Save. An empty box keeps the saved key; Remove the saved key deletes it. Saved keys are not displayed again. Your AcoustID or Last.fm key takes precedence over a built-in key. For fanart.tv, your personal key accompanies a built-in project key; without a project key, your key is used as the project key.

The dialog provides registration addresses. Availability depends on the installed build and provider; do not assume every downloaded or locally compiled build includes working keys.

docs.title: Last.fm
docs.text:
Choose Tag Sources → Last.fm…. Artist and album looks up that album directly; Album title words searches by album title. MusicBrainz release ID accepts a release MBID for a direct lookup.

The review offers available album and track metadata, cover art and filtered, title-cased listener tags as GENRE. Choose the genre count in Options → Tag Sources → Online services. Personal collection tags and bare numbers are filtered, but review the remaining genres. Artwork is limited to the images Last.fm supplies, typically up to 300 pixels.

docs.title: fanart.tv
docs.text:
Choose Tag Sources → Covers: fanart.tv…. Search by artist and album or free text, or enter a MusicBrainz release group ID or address. A release group collects editions of an album; an individual release address is refused.

Search results come from MusicBrainz; artwork comes from fanart.tv. Front covers are ordered by likes, followed by disc artwork. Choose the image to write to all selected files. This source supplies no text metadata.

docs.title: Network access and privacy
docs.text:
Online searches need a network connection. They send search terms and identifiers to providers; per-file lyrics lookups send track metadata and duration. AcoustID sends a locally computed fingerprint and duration, not the audio file. Preview also contacts the source in your browser. There is no downloaded offline mirror of these online catalogs. A configured local freedb folder can supply disc metadata without a server lookup.

Personal API keys live in tag-sources.json in OpenTag's configuration folder, separately from ordinary Options. They are text with restricted file permissions where supported, not encrypted by OpenTag. Keep this file out of shared configuration copies. Discogs also offers an optional system keychain location. Built-in application keys are part of the installed binary; they cannot keep an individual's secret confidential from someone inspecting that binary.

OpenTag avoids putting credentials in displayed errors. Authentication still sends the required credential to its provider over HTTPS; Last.fm uses a request URL parameter. Consult provider terms before redistributing data or artwork.

Requests are spaced separately by service. iTunes pauses several seconds between requests; many per-file lookups or album pages take longer. Correct missing-key errors, and wait before retrying quota or server errors. Starting a newer source request supersedes older work without resetting provider quotas.
