docs.title: AcoustID fingerprints
docs.text: AcoustID identifies recordings from the sound of your files. OpenTag computes a fingerprint locally, asks AcoustID for matches, then retrieves the chosen release's metadata and artwork from MusicBrainz.

docs.title: Set up fingerprinting
docs.text:
1. Use a desktop build on macOS, Windows or Linux. This source is not offered on Android or iOS.
  2. Install Chromaprint's fpcalc separately. OpenTag does not bundle it. Obtain it from the Chromaprint project or your package manager.
  3. If OpenTag cannot find it, enter the executable's full path in Options → Tag Sources → Online services → fpcalc program. Leave the setting empty for automatic discovery on the executable search path and common Unix installation locations.
  4. Open Tag Sources → API keys…. If this build has no AcoustID key, add your application's key using the registration address shown there.

Enter an executable path in fpcalc program, not a shell command or extra arguments. Files must be accessible and decodable by that fpcalc installation. A fingerprint process taking more than 2 minutes is stopped and reported.

docs.title: Identify and review
docs.text:
1. Select the album's files and choose Tag Sources → AcoustID (fingerprints)….
  2. Select Search. OpenTag fingerprints each file and ranks releases by the number of selected files matched, then match score.
  3. Select the correct release and choose Next. Compare the edition, track list, matches and artwork, then save.

Identified files are paired with their matched MusicBrainz recordings, including across discs. If files have overlapping candidate recordings, OpenTag reassigns compatible pairs when necessary to keep the greatest number of compatible fingerprint assignments. A direct free track keeps earlier assignments stable; this does not globally optimize match scores. Auto-match, Selection order and Suggest sorting arrange remaining files without replacing those fingerprint pairs. You can still move files manually; inspect the resulting assignments.

ACOUSTID_ID is offered per file only when that file was identified as the recording of its assigned track. Moving it onto another recording does not copy another file's AcoustID. If only ACOUSTID_ID is checked and no ID applies or cover is selected, the file is skipped.

docs.title: Limits and privacy
docs.text:
A match identifies a recording, not necessarily your exact edition. Several releases can contain it, so the highest-ranked result still needs review. Files without a usable match do not gain an inferred AcoustID.

OpenTag sends fingerprints and durations, not audio files. It performs lookups only and does not submit new fingerprints. AcoustID requests are spaced about 350 milliseconds apart; MusicBrainz lookups use a separate spacing of about 1.1 seconds. Local fingerprinting adds to the time needed.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• API key setup
  • Search, review and save
  • Tag Sources options

docs.title: Deezer
docs.text: Use Tag Sources → Deezer… for album metadata, track ISRCs and artwork. The public lookup needs no account or API key.

docs.title: Find an album
docs.text:
1. Select the album's files and choose Deezer….
  2. Choose Artist and album, Free text, Album ID or address, or Barcode (UPC). An album ID is numeric; a deezer.com album address also works.
  3. Select Search, select the edition and choose Next. In album ID mode, Look up opens the review directly.
  4. Check file-to-track matches and fields, then use the shared review to save.

Artist and album searches send plain words. Results can match other fields too; a title match alone does not establish the correct edition.

docs.title: Fields and artwork
docs.text:
Album fields include ALBUM, ALBUMARTIST, YEAR, GENRE, PUBLISHER and BARCODE. Track fields include TITLE, ARTIST, ISRC, TRACK and DISCNUMBER, when supplied by Deezer.

Track pages are collected before the review opens. Track totals are calculated per disc, and disc totals come from the returned tracks. A failed later page produces an error instead of a partial album. Lookups exceeding 10,000 returned tracks are refused. This does not guarantee the provider's catalog is complete.

Choose 1000 pixel artwork (the default) or 500 pixels in Options → Tag Sources → Online services. Choose Covers: Deezer… for artwork only.

docs.title: Lookup errors
docs.text: OpenTag spaces Deezer requests about 120 milliseconds apart. Deezer can report an error inside a successful HTTP response; OpenTag displays quota and missing-release messages rather than treating those as empty albums. Wait after a quota error. Check the album ID, barcode or search words after a missing result. OpenTag retrieves no Deezer streams or audio previews.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Search, review and save
  • Tag Sources options
  • iTunes / Apple Music

docs.title: Discogs
docs.text: Use Tag Sources → Discogs… for release metadata and artwork. An exact release helps distinguish editions with different tracks, catalog numbers or covers.

docs.title: Find a release
docs.text:
Select the album's files and choose Discogs…. Search by Artist and album, Free text, Barcode or Catalog number, or use Release ID or address. Tag Sources → Discogs Release ID… opens the direct lookup.

Use a numeric release ID or an address containing /release/. A Discogs master groups editions; choose the individual release rather than its master ID. Select a search result and choose Next, or use Look up for a direct release lookup. Then check the fields, artwork and file matches.

Covers: Discogs… writes artwork without changing text fields. Available images and thumbnails depend on authentication and what Discogs supplies.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Open Tag Sources → Discogs access token… to see this build's setup. Requests use your personal token first, then a built-in application key if available, or otherwise anonymous access. Not every build includes an application key.

Create a personal access token in your Discogs account's Settings → Developers, enter it in OpenTag and choose Save. An empty input keeps the saved token; Remove the saved token deletes it. The stored token is not displayed again.

When offered, Keep the token in the system keychain moves it to macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or the Linux Secret Service. Otherwise it stays in the private configuration file. Mobile builds use the file. The token moves when you save the dialog; keychain failures are reported rather than silently deleting the token.

Anonymous requests are spaced about 2.5 seconds apart; authenticated requests about 1.1 seconds apart and can supply search thumbnails. Check or replace a rejected token. A quota error may still require waiting. OpenTag uses release lookups, not account collection management or an OAuth sign-in flow.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Search, review and save
  • Network access and privacy
  • Tag Sources options

docs.title: Find album tags with freedb and gnudb
docs.text: Use Tag Sources → freedb… to find album metadata by artist and title or by the track layout of selected files. The original freedb service ended; OpenTag's default server is gnudb. Treat a result as a suggestion: check its edition, track order and values before writing tags.

docs.title: Search by artist and album
docs.text:
1. Save pending edits and select copied files from one disc.
  2. Choose Tag Sources → freedb…, then SEARCH BY → Artist and album.
  3. Enter the artist and album, such as Juniper Vale and Harbour Lights. Choose Search. The selected-file count helps narrow the request when it is between 1 and 99.
  4. Compare the artist, album title, category and Entry ID shown in the results. Select a result and choose Next, or double-click its row, to load that entry into the import review. Year and track count are not supplied in this artist/album result list.

OpenTag offers artist/album and artwork search only for recognized gnudb servers (gnudb.org or its subdomains). Use track-layout lookup for other configured CDDB servers, even if they implement similar search commands. Choose the server under Options → Tag Sources → freedb.

docs.title: Search from the selected tracks
docs.text:
Choose Track layout of the selected files. OpenTag derives a disc layout from file-list order and durations. Select one complete disc in track order, with known durations for every file and at most 99 files. Exclude tracks from other discs and unrelated bonus files.

This does not listen to the music or read a physical CD. Missing tracks, different durations, another order or a different pressing can prevent a match. Try artist/album search when layout lookup finds nothing.

Remote results show Entry ID, gnudb's identifier for a listed entry. OpenTag asks for matches first and reads the entry you choose. Typed disc-ID lookup is available only in a local freedb database.

docs.title: Review before writing
docs.text:
After the entry loads, check its year when provided and compare its source track list with the selected files. The review pairs those source tracks with your files. Check the first and last track, as well as tracks with similar titles.

  • Use Auto-match, Selection order, or Suggest sorting → Title or Length to help arrange files. A suggested match still needs inspection.
  • Drag a file to another row, use its arrow buttons, or press Alt+Up or Alt+Down. A duration difference over ten seconds is highlighted.
  • Enable only the fields you want to import. Edit album values or choose Edit per track to correct a track field before saving.
  • Check Write cover art independently. Replace existing artwork affects embedded covers; Save image to file writes an external image beside the affected audio files.

Choose Save tags to … files after checking the plan. Inspect the saved files and any reported per-file errors before continuing. OpenTag does not submit corrections to the database.

docs.title: Find cover art only
docs.text:
Choose Tag Sources → Covers: freedb (gnudb)… to search by artist/album or selected track layout. Inspect the artwork, then choose Save cover to … files. This workflow selects artwork rather than album tag fields.

gnudb can list Cover Art Archive images in an entry or through a separate artwork search. Album metadata does not guarantee an image. MusicBrainz cover size under Options → Tag Sources also controls the image variant requested here; it does not resize covers already embedded in files.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
Result Next step No album match Check the selected disc; try artist/album search or another source 500 Unknown application The server may not have registered OpenTag; use a compatible server or a local snapshot 429 Too Many Requests Wait before searching again; OpenTag does not automatically repeat the rejected request Text/artwork search unavailable on a custom server Select a recognized gnudb server for those searches, or use track-layout lookup Incorrect database values Choose another entry or edit the review; saving tags does not update gnudb

Each server request includes OpenTag's application identity/version and a handshake email identity. Configure your own address or use the documented developer-contact fallback in the server options. Saving valid settings does not establish live service registration.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Server settings and disc-ID fields
  • Search a local freedb snapshot

docs.title: iTunes / Apple Music
docs.text: Use Tag Sources → iTunes… for album metadata and store artwork. No Apple account or API key is needed for the lookup.

docs.title: Find an album
docs.text:
1. Select the album's files and open iTunes….
  2. Choose Artist and album, Free text, Album ID or Apple Music address, or Barcode (UPC). For an ID lookup, use the album's numeric collection ID or its Apple Music / iTunes album address.
  3. Select Search, choose the edition and select Next. In album ID mode, Look up opens the review directly.
  4. Check the country, fields, artwork and file-to-track matches before saving.

iTunes returns up to 50 album search results; there is no further result-page lookup. Narrow the words or use an album ID if the edition is missing.

docs.title: Country and artwork
docs.text:
Set Store country (two letters) in Options → Tag Sources → Online services, for example US (the default) or NL. Store catalogs can differ, so changing country can change which editions are found.

The same page selects 600, 1200 or 3000 pixel artwork; 1200 is the default. Covers: iTunes… uses artwork without changing text fields. The selected size requests Apple's image variant; availability and quality depend on the store.

docs.title: Fields and limits
docs.text:
The review can offer album, album artist, year, genre and copyright; song titles, artists, track and disc numbers; and iTunes album, artist and catalog identifiers. Advisory information appears only when supplied. The release lookup requests a limited response (limit=200). If Apple returns fewer album songs than its stated positive track count, OpenTag reports an incomplete album before opening the review or saving. A response at the limit without a usable album total is also refused. Smaller responses without a total show the available songs, whose completeness cannot be confirmed.

OpenTag makes no continuation request for this album lookup. Large or incomplete albums can therefore be unavailable, including in Covers: iTunes…, which uses the same lookup. Try another edition, store country or source rather than saving a partial listing as the complete album.

OpenTag spaces iTunes requests about 3.1 seconds apart, so a search followed by a release lookup can pause. It retrieves metadata and artwork, not music, audio previews or an Apple Music subscription library.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Search, review and save
  • Tag Sources options
  • Deezer

docs.title: Search a local freedb snapshot
docs.text: A local freedb database is an extracted collection of historical album entries. Use it when you already have a snapshot and want lookup without a remote CDDB server. It reflects the snapshot's date; building a text index does not add newer albums.

docs.title: Choose the database folder
docs.text:
1. Extract the snapshot into a folder the app can read.
  2. Open File → Options… → Tag Sources → Local freedb.
  3. Use Choose folder…, or type the full path, to select the root containing category folders such as rock, classical and blues.
  4. Choose OK to save that folder for later searches.

OpenTag reads one-xmcd-file-per-disc snapshots and Windows xxtoyy range files. Select their database root, not a category or individual entry. If an entry is below D:\Databases\freedb\rock, choose D:\Databases\freedb. A compressed download is not itself the database folder.

docs.title: Choose a lookup method
docs.text:
Select files from one disc and open Tag Sources → freedb (local)….

SEARCH BY Input Text index needed? Disc ID of the selected files ID derived from file-list order and durations No freedb disc ID An existing freedb disc ID entered in DISC ID No Artist and album words Words in indexed artist/album titles Yes

For selected-file lookup, select one complete disc in track order, with known durations and at most 99 files. This is layout matching, not acoustic fingerprinting. OpenTag supports deriving this local ID; the historical Mp3tag restriction on local audio-based lookup does not describe its reader.

A freedb disc ID is different from gnudb's listed Entry ID, a barcode or a MusicBrainz release identifier. If you do not know the ID, try the selected files or build the text index.

docs.title: Build and use the text index
docs.text:
Open Options → Tag Sources → Local freedb, check LOCAL FREEDB FOLDER, and choose Build index. Wait for the status to show a disc count for that folder. Large snapshots take time; Cancel requests cancellation. An unfinished build does not replace the previously completed index.

Building starts immediately with the entered folder, before Options OK. Cancelling the outer Options dialog does not undo a completed build. Save Options if later searches should use this same folder.

Now choose Artist and album words in freedb (local)…. For an indexed entry Juniper Vale / Harbour Lights, try juniper harbour. All query words must match artist/title text. Case and accents are normalized; a partial word can match a longer word. This searches database entries, not your audio.

Rebuild after changing the root or replacing snapshot contents. An index records its root, so one built for another folder is rejected. Changes to database files are not indexed automatically. If the current environment does not provide indexing, the page reports it and disables the control.

docs.title: Review and troubleshoot
docs.text:
Choose a result and Next. Compare source tracks with your files, correct the pairing and select fields to write. The import review lets you edit values before choosing Save tags to … files.

  • No text results: check that the completed index belongs to this folder, then try fewer artist/title words.
  • No disc-ID result: check order, durations and whether this snapshot contains the release. Rebuilding an unchanged snapshot cannot add a missing disc.
  • Wrong folder: select the database root, with category subfolders inside it.

These lookups read the local database. They do not upload corrections or update it from gnudb, and the database is separate from OpenTag's music cache.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Local freedb options
  • Remote freedb and gnudb

docs.title: LRCLIB lyrics
docs.text: Use Tag Sources → Lyrics: LRCLIB… to find lyrics for selected files. No API key is needed. Lyrics are proposed in UNSYNCEDLYRICS for review before writing.

docs.title: Look up the selected files
docs.text:
1. Check the files' title, artist, album and duration. Correct misleading tags before searching.
  2. Open Lyrics: LRCLIB… and keep Each selected file (title, artist, album, length) selected.
  3. Select Search. The combined result opens the review for the files.
  4. Inspect the proposed lyrics and save the checked field. Files without lyrics are left unchanged.

The lookup first uses metadata and duration. If it returns no usable lyrics, OpenTag searches by title and artist. With a known, positive file duration, the fallback accepts only a result within 3 seconds. Without a usable duration, it takes the first result containing lyrics, so review that match especially carefully. Similar metadata can still identify the wrong version; check live, instrumental and edited recordings.

A lookup failure is reported without discarding the other files' results. The combined result keeps one track per file in file list order. Instrumental records supply no lyrics to write.

docs.title: Search for one record
docs.text: Choose Free text to browse lyrics records, or Lyrics record ID to open a numeric LRCLIB record directly. Check the file-to-track pairing before saving an individually selected record.

docs.title: Plain or synchronized lyrics
docs.text:
The default is plain text. Enable Write synchronized lyrics (LRC time stamps) when available in Options → Tag Sources → Online services to keep LRC timestamps. Both choices write text to UNSYNCEDLYRICS; this option does not create an ID3 synchronized-lyrics frame. Player support varies.

When only synchronized lyrics are available and the option is off, OpenTag removes timestamps and LRC metadata lines. LRCLIB supplies no language; ID3 lyrics use the unknown-language code XXX. Literal text, including ||, is retained rather than interpreted as a language prefix.

Requests are spaced about 200 milliseconds apart; a busy-server response is retried once. Each selected file needs a lookup, and a fallback can add another.

docs.text:

  • Tag Sources options

docs.title: Web source script reference
docs.text:
A source has two languages: header values describe requests and parser sections read the returned text. Format strings appear only in the places that accept them, such as SearchBy defaults, SayFormat and UseFormat. A parser command is not a $function(...) call.

Start with the local JSON lesson for a complete source and installation guide for menus/settings. This page covers every header in the canonical source format and all 59 commands accepted by the checked OpenTag parser. Examples inspect parser output directly; they do not certify a provider, track matching or an audio-file write.

docs.title: Description headers
docs.text:
Write [Key]=value on one line. Header names ignore case. A parser section starts with [ParserScriptAlbum]=... or [ParserScriptIndex]=... and continues until the next header. UTF-8 is the preferred source-file encoding; a BOM is recognized and non-UTF-8 legacy text falls back to Windows-1252.

Header Meaning and important boundary [Name] Descriptive source name; the filename still determines its menu path [BasedOn] Original site/source metadata; use the actual request/base headers below rather than relying on this as URL resolution [IndexUrl] Search address containing %s, replaced with the assembled query [AlbumUrl] Album base for a result's relative address, or the direct-lookup address when there is no index stage [WordSeparator] String placed between separately encoded search words; absent/empty defaults to %20 [IndexFormat] Pipe-separated result fields; %_url% is required for a result list [SearchBy] Up to three labelled search fields with defaults and URL fragments [Encoding] Encoding/escaping policy for search words in URLs; separate from source-file encoding [UserAgent] 1 requests OpenTag's own name/version user agent; otherwise the web-source browser-style agent is used [ParserScriptIndex] Script that emits the result list into the unnamed output [ParserScriptAlbum] Required script that emits release and track fields [Include] Plain companion filename whose keys replace this file's keys [MinAppVersionWin] Upstream Windows minimum-version declaration, retained as source metadata; not an OpenTag compatibility certificate [MinAppVersionMac] Equivalent upstream Mac declaration; check OpenTag commands independently [Settings] Plain .settings schema filename used by this source's configuration variables

A source needs an album parser and at least an index or album URL. A missing index URL or index parser makes it a direct lookup. Avoid adding an incomplete index stage when a known release identifier is all that is needed.

The old misspelling WordSeperator is accepted as a fallback, but use WordSeparator in new sources. Unknown headers can be retained diagnostically; they do not automatically add a feature. In particular, do not infer a source-order guarantee from an unverified header in an imported script.

docs.title: Search fields and URL encoding
docs.text:
A SearchBy entry has Label||default format||URL fragment. Separate entries with $$. For example, Artist||%artist%||artist=%s$$Album||%album%||&album=%s creates two fields. Defaults use the first selected file. Entered text is split into words, encoded according to Encoding, joined with WordSeparator, inserted into each fragment, then assembled into the IndexUrl/AlbumUrl %s position.

With WordSeparator=+, the words Juniper Vale become Juniper+Vale. Characters inside each word, such as &, are encoded rather than becoming a new query parameter. Repeated whitespace between words is normalized by this word-splitting step. If a URL template lacks %s, the query is appended; an explicit substitution point is clearer.

Encoding value Current search-word behavior url-utf-8 Default: percent-encode UTF-8 bytes, retaining unreserved URL characters url Percent-encode ISO-8859-1 bytes; unrepresentable characters become ? before escaping utf-8 Keep more ASCII punctuation while escaping address delimiters/control characters and non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes iso-8859-1 The corresponding Latin-1 byte policy ansi The web-source query implementation uses Windows-1252 with that ASCII escaping policy

The ansi row concerns this URL builder. It is not a statement that every OpenTag ANSI operation uses the same platform codepage. Prefer url-utf-8 for a UTF-8 API unless its actual requirements say otherwise.

docs.title: Index results
docs.text:
The index script writes to OutputTo "", the unnamed buffer. Finish each result with SayNewline. Separate its values with | in the order defined by IndexFormat. The field names beginning with _ are internal rather than visible result columns:

  • %_url%: album address; an empty/invalid result address is not a usable row.
  • %_coverurl%: optional thumbnail address for the result. Use a reasonably small image, about 250 × 250 pixels or less, rather than a full-size cover.
  • %_preview%: optional address for previewing the result.
  • Other named fields, such as %Album% and %Year%, become visible columns.

An absolute album URL is used directly. Otherwise AlbumUrl is prefixed when provided, and the resulting address is resolved against the downloaded page. Do not duplicate a path prefix in both the base and emitted result. Cover and preview addresses resolve against the page too. Only accepted web addresses are used by the request workflow.

docs.title: Album and track outputs
docs.text:
OutputTo chooses a named buffer. An album value such as ALBUM applies to the release. Track-valued buffers contain |-separated entries, conventionally ending with |, as in Paper Boats|Lanterns on the Water|. A single track also needs its separator to distinguish a track list from one album value.

TITLE establishes the track count when available; otherwise another track-valued output supplies it. Keep TRACK, TITLE, per-track ARTIST and other track lists aligned. COVERURL/_COVERURL supplies image addresses. _LENGTH can supply per-track duration text in seconds, m:ss or hss form. Other underscore-prefixed buffers are internal and are not written as ordinary tags. Double backslashes separate multiple values within a field, as in Juniper Vale\\Mira Solberg.

For a pipe that belongs inside a value, use $verticalBar() in a SayFormat or UseFormat expression. It emits a protected marker that the release/result conversion restores to a literal pipe after splitting. A raw | would split the output instead.

This parser-level description does not establish later duration-unit handling or automatic file-order suggestions. Check titles/positions and review the mapping manually where needed; parser output, release conversion and matching are separate stages.

docs.title: Includes and settings
docs.text:
Include resolution happens after reading this file's own keys. Included keys replace local keys regardless of where the Include line appeared. With several includes, later includes can replace earlier included keys. Keep source-specific values out of shared includes unless that override is intended. Avoid cycles; the checked loader permits at most eight nested include levels.

A settings schema needs a nonempty root key and a settings array. Give each entry a stable key, a useful title, optional description and a correctly typed default where it holds a value:

Type Control/value string Text input, or a dropdown when choices supplies strings number Numeric input; saved values must be numeric bool Checkbox with a boolean value heading Heading only; no stored value separator Separator with optional explanatory text; no stored value

Saved values live under the schema's root key in the shared sources settings.json. A saved value of the wrong type falls back to a default. Absent bool/number/string defaults fall back to false/0/empty text. Adding a new key can therefore work with an old saved settings file. Different schema root keys keep sources' values separate.

Optional localizations map two-letter ISO-639-1 codes to entries identified by those same keys. The root key localizes the dialog title; entry keys localize titles/descriptions. In the checked baseline, the settings dialog uses the system/browser language code and falls back to unlocalized text when no entry matches. A schema is not an automatic translation of arbitrary parser output.

IfVar/IfNotVar compare configured values and SayVar emits one. Booleans reach the parser as true/false, numbers as text and strings as themselves. Variable keys are exact; value comparisons ignore ASCII case. These settings are separate from named outputs and selected-file metadata.

docs.title: Choose a command family
docs.text: Task Commands to start with Locate data FindLine, FindInLine, GotoLine, MoveChar Read or emit SayRest, SayUntil, SayFormat, SayOutput Change working state Set, OutputTo, Use, UseFormat Branch or repeat If, IfVar, Do, While Clean text Replace, RegexpReplace, KillTag, Trim Inspect execution Debug, DebugWriteInput Read JSON json, json_select, json_foreach

docs.title: Read a command example
docs.text:
Each example below states its input, script and expected output buffer, using the marked visible-space notation where applicable. They run in a fresh parser context, with page URL https://catalogue.example.invalid/release/harbour. That address is context text for the examples; no request to it is needed. A Settings line supplies only the named example variable. Debug files are additional in-memory parser results; the app writes them under its sources/debug folder.

Commands ignore case. Double quotes delimit parser string parameters; \" puts a quote inside one. Other backslashes remain literal, so a regex \d needs one backslash at this layer. # outside quotes starts a comment.

Ordinary string parameters substitute existing %output% values. Unknown output references can remain literal text, and bare %20 is not a field. SayFormat and UseFormat instead evaluate their first argument as a format string with %_current% and, unless restricted, named outputs as fields. Use that language's apostrophe quoting for literal parentheses, brackets, commas or dollar signs inside expressions. See format strings and regular expressions. The case-sensitive parser regex commands below differ from the default case policy of the $regexp(...) formatting function.

Character/line positions are one-based; relative moves can be negative. Counts, positions and loop limits require whole numbers. Read trimming is on by default and applies to the documented read commands, not every emitted string. Code blocks retain significant spaces. Examples labelled Visible spaces use ␠ to show one ASCII space in input/output, so edge spaces can be seen; substitute a real space when constructing that input. Their scripts remain literal commands. Examples labelled CRLF make output line endings explicit.

docs.title: FindLine
docs.text:
Syntax: FindLine "text" [occurrence] [optional]

Find the next matching line from the current position and move to its first character. The occurrence counts matching lines, not several copies on one line. Use a third parameter of 1 to leave a missing match nonfatal; the cursor then stays where it was.

Input

Header
Album: Old Harbour
Album: Harbour Lights

Script

FindLine "Album:" 2
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Album: Harbour Lights

docs.title: FindLineNoCase
docs.text:
Syntax: FindLineNoCase "text" [occurrence] [optional]

Use the same matching-line navigation without case sensitivity. Finding a line does not skip the label within it: use FindInLine next when the value starts after a marker.

Input

header
ALBUM: Harbour Lights

Script

FindLineNoCase "album:"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

ALBUM: Harbour Lights

docs.title: FindInLine
docs.text:
Syntax: FindInLine "text" [occurrence] [optional]

Search the current line from the cursor and place it after the chosen occurrence. A missing match is an error unless the third parameter is 1. It does not search later lines.

Input

Title: old; Title: Paper Boats

Script

FindInLine "Title: " 2
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: GotoChar
docs.text:
Syntax: GotoChar position

Choose a one-based character position in the current line. Characters are Unicode characters, not UTF-8 bytes. Positions before 1 clamp to 1, and positions beyond the line stop at its end.

Input

Álbum: Lanterns

Script

GotoChar 8
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Lanterns

docs.title: GotoLine
docs.text:
Syntax: GotoLine line

Choose a one-based input line and reset the character cursor to its start. A line beyond the input is an error. This is useful for a known fixed format; marker searches survive inserted lines better.

Input

Header
Paper Boats

Script

GotoLine 2
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: MoveChar
docs.text:
Syntax: MoveChar distance

Move relative to the current character position. Negative values move left. Movement stays on the current line and clamps at its ends.

Input

XXPaper Boats

Script

MoveChar 5
MoveChar -3
SayNChars 5

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper

docs.title: MoveLine
docs.text:
Syntax: MoveLine distance [optional]

Move relative to the current input line and reset its character position. Negative values move up. With the optional parameter 1, out-of-range movement clamps at an edge instead of failing.

Input

Header
Notes
Paper Boats

Script

MoveLine 2
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: Say
docs.text:
Syntax: Say "text"

Append the parameter text to the chosen output. This does not consume input. Ordinary parameters expand existing %output% references; they do not automatically evaluate scripting functions. Use SayFormat for a format string.

Input

Ignored input

Script

Say "Juniper Vale"

Output buffer: unnamed

Juniper Vale

docs.title: SayUntil
docs.text:
Syntax: SayUntil "delimiter"

Append input up to the delimiter on this line, leaving the cursor at the delimiter. A missing delimiter reads to the line end. The default Trim setting trims the extracted text; the delimiter itself is not consumed.

Input

Paper Boats|next

Script

SayUntil "|"

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: SayUntilML
docs.text:
Syntax: SayUntilML "delimiter"

Read across lines until the delimiter or input end. Joined output lines use CRLF. The cursor stops at the delimiter; advance it before repeating the same extraction.

Line endings: CRLF

Input

Paper
Boats</title>

Script

SayUntilML "</title>"

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper
Boats

docs.title: SayRest
docs.text:
Syntax: SayRest

Append the remaining current line and consume it. Read text is trimmed by default; Trim "off" retains its edge whitespace. Later lines are not included.

Input

Title: Paper Boats

Script

FindInLine "Title: "
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: SayNChars
docs.text:
Syntax: SayNChars count

Copy and consume this many Unicode characters from the cursor, stopping at line end. This direct character copy retains spaces; it is not affected by automatic read trimming.

Visible spaces: ␠

Input

␠␠Paper

Script

SayNChars 2

Output buffer: unnamed

␠␠

docs.title: SayNextNumber
docs.text:
Syntax: SayNextNumber

Find the next ASCII numeric value and emit it, advancing past it. An optional minus and decimal fraction are retained. This is not a localized thousands/decimal-number parser.

Input

Take -03.5 bonus

Script

SayNextNumber

Output buffer: unnamed

-03.5

docs.title: SayNextWord
docs.text:
Syntax: SayNextWord

Skip leading whitespace, then copy the next non-whitespace run. Punctuation belongs to that run. The cursor advances past the emitted text.

Input

   Paper, Boats

Script

SayNextWord

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper,

docs.title: SayOutput
docs.text:
Syntax: SayOutput "buffer"

Append an existing output without consuming input. Names ignore case. CurrentUrl is supplied by the request context and can be read the same way.

Input

Script

Set "ALBUM" "Harbour Lights"
SayOutput "album"
Say " @ "
SayOutput "CurrentUrl"

Output buffer: unnamed

Harbour Lights @ https://catalogue.example.invalid/release/harbour

docs.title: SayNewline
docs.text:
Syntax: SayNewline

Append a CRLF pair. It does not move the input cursor. Index scripts use this to finish a result row; it is different from a pipe separating columns.

Line endings: CRLF

Input

Script

Say "Paper"
SayNewline
Say "Boats"

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper
Boats

docs.title: SayDate
docs.text:
Syntax: SayDate [unit]

Consume a number at the cursor and emit its UTC calendar date. The default unit is seconds since 1970-01-01; "ms" selects milliseconds. The output uses YYYY-MM-DD.

Input

1704067200000

Script

SayDate "ms"

Output buffer: unnamed

2024-01-01

docs.title: SayDuration
docs.text:
Syntax: SayDuration [unit] [hours] [milliseconds]

Consume a numeric interval. Use seconds by default, "ms" for milliseconds or "m" for minutes. Set the next flag to 1 for hss and the final flag to 1 for a .mmm suffix; otherwise minutes can exceed 59.

Input

62005

Script

SayDuration "ms" 1 1

Output buffer: unnamed

0:01:02.005

docs.title: SayRegexp
docs.text:
Syntax: SayRegexp "pattern" ["separator"] ["stop text"]

Find every full regex match in the current remainder, joining them with a space by default. Omit the third parameter to search the entire current remainder. A supplied third parameter restricts matching to text before that stop text’s first occurrence; if the supplied stop text is absent from the input, this command emits nothing and leaves the cursor unchanged. After a successful search, the cursor advances to the end of that region and leaves any stop marker for later. A missing stop marker leaves the cursor unchanged. Matching is case-sensitive here; use an inline regex option when another policy is intended.

Input

item2 item7; item9

Script

SayRegexp "item\d" ", " ";"

Output buffer: unnamed

item2, item7

docs.title: SayFormat
docs.text:
Syntax: SayFormat "format string" [current-only]

Evaluate a format string and append it. %_current% is the entire current input, not only the cursor remainder. Named outputs are available as fields unless the second parameter is 1. Quote format-language punctuation inside the format string as usual. This command does not consume the input cursor.

Input

paper boats

Script

Set "ARTIST" "Juniper Vale"
SayFormat "$upper(%_current%) — %ARTIST%"

Output buffer: unnamed

PAPER BOATS — Juniper Vale

docs.title: SayVar
docs.text:
Syntax: SayVar "key"

Append a configured setting as text. The key matches the schema key exactly; a missing key gives empty text. This is a setting value, not an output buffer or selected audio tag.

Settings: edition=deluxe

Input

Script

SayVar "edition"

Output buffer: unnamed

deluxe

docs.title: Set
docs.text:
Syntax: Set "buffer" ["value"]

Replace the named buffer with a value. Omit the second parameter to remove that buffer. Unlike OutputTo, this does not switch the destination of later Say commands.

Input

Script

Set "NOTE" "old"
Set "NOTE"
IfNotOutput "NOTE"
Say "cleared"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

cleared

docs.title: OutputTo
docs.text:
Syntax: OutputTo "buffer"

Choose the output used by later Say commands. Text is appended there; it does not clear an earlier value. Use an empty name for the unnamed index-result output.

Input

Album: Harbour Lights

Script

OutputTo "ALBUM"
FindInLine "Album: "
SayRest

Output buffer: ALBUM

Harbour Lights

docs.title: SkipChars
docs.text:
Syntax: SkipChars "characters"

Skip a prefix made from any characters in the supplied set. Stop at the first other character; the string is a set, not a literal word to find.

Input

 _-Paper Boats

Script

SkipChars " _-"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: Insert
docs.text:
Syntax: Insert "text"

Insert text at the current input cursor without consuming it. Reading afterward starts at that inserted text. This edits the parser input, not the downloaded website or audio file.

Input

Boats

Script

Insert "Paper "
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
Syntax: Use "text"

Replace the entire current input and reset the cursor. Use %buffer% to supply an output value; a bare buffer name is just literal text. The original downloaded input remains available to json "on".

Input

Ignored input

Script

Set "ALBUM" "Harbour Lights"
Use "%ALBUM%"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Harbour Lights

docs.title: UseFormat
docs.text:
Syntax: UseFormat "format string" [current-only]

Evaluate a format string, replace current input with its result and reset the cursor. The second parameter 1 excludes named outputs while keeping %_current% available.

Input

paper boats

Script

UseFormat "$upper(%_current%)"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

PAPER BOATS

docs.title: If
docs.text:
Syntax: If "prefix"

Test whether the current remainder starts with this case-sensitive prefix. This is not a search over the whole line. A false branch jumps to Else or Endif without consuming input.

Input

Album: Harbour Lights

Script

If "Album:"
Say "album found"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

album found

docs.title: IfNot
docs.text:
Syntax: IfNot "prefix"

Take the branch when the current remainder does not start with the prefix. The condition itself does not move the cursor.

Input

Paper Boats

Script

IfNot "#"
SayRest
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: IfOutput
docs.text:
Syntax: IfOutput "buffer"

Test whether the named output exists and contains nonempty text. A buffer containing only spaces is still nonempty. This does not inspect an audio tag unless the script placed that value in the buffer.

Input

Script

Set "ARTIST" "Juniper Vale"
IfOutput "ARTIST"
Say "present"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

present

docs.title: IfNotOutput
docs.text:
Syntax: IfNotOutput "buffer"

Take the branch when an output is absent or empty. Buffer names are case-insensitive.

Input

Script

IfNotOutput "COMMENT"
Say "no comment"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

no comment

docs.title: IfGreater
docs.text:
Syntax: IfGreater number

Compare a numeric value at the cursor with the threshold, without consuming it. No number at the cursor makes the condition false. This does not search ahead for a later number.

Input

12 tracks

Script

IfGreater 10
Say "large"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

large

docs.title: IfLess
docs.text:
Syntax: IfLess number

Use the same cursor-based numeric comparison for a lower threshold. The threshold can be a decimal value; movement/count parameters elsewhere still require whole numbers.

Input

2.5 tracks

Script

IfLess 3
Say "small"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

small

docs.title: IfVar
docs.text:
Syntax: IfVar "key" "value"

Compare a configured setting with the supplied text, ignoring ASCII case in the values. Keys remain exact. An absent setting reads as empty text; provide a schema/default for meaningful choices.

Settings: edition=deluxe

Input

Script

IfVar "edition" "DELUXE"
Say "extra tracks"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

extra tracks

docs.title: IfNotVar
docs.text:
Syntax: IfNotVar "key" "value"

Take the branch when the configured value differs. It uses the same setting/key rules as IfVar.

Settings: edition=deluxe

Input

Script

IfNotVar "edition" "standard"
Say "alternate edition"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

alternate edition

docs.title: Else
docs.text:
Syntax: Else

Separate the true and false parts of one condition. At most one Else belongs to a condition; nested blocks must close in order.

Input

Live

Script

If "Studio"
Say "studio"
Else
Say "other"
Endif

Output buffer: unnamed

other

docs.title: Endif
docs.text:
Syntax: Endif

Close an If-family condition. Execution resumes after it whether the condition was true or false; a missing or unmatched Endif is a compile error.

Input

Paper

Script

If "Paper"
Say "matched"
Endif
Say "."

Output buffer: unnamed

matched.

docs.title: Do
docs.text:
Syntax: Do

Start a body that runs at least once. While closes the body and checks whether it repeats. Advance input or provide a useful limit; finding the same marker repeatedly does not make progress.

Input

xxxstop

Script

Do
SayNChars 1
While "x" 3

Output buffer: unnamed

xxx

docs.title: While
docs.text:
Syntax: While "prefix" [maximum]

Repeat from the matching Do while the current remainder starts with the prefix. A supplied maximum bounds body executions. Use positive limits and keep Do/While loops unnested for portability to other implementations.

Input

AAA

Script

Do
SayNChars 1
While "A" 2

Output buffer: unnamed

AA

docs.title: Replace
docs.text:
Syntax: Replace "from" "to"

Replace literal matches in the entire current input. The old cursor location is kept and clamped, so reposition after length-changing transformations when needed. An empty search performs no replacement.

Input

Paper_Boats

Script

Replace "_" " "
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: RegexpReplace
docs.text:
Syntax: RegexpReplace "pattern" "replacement"

Replace regex matches in the entire current input, using case-sensitive matching and Boost replacement captures. These are parser parameters; dollar captures here are not an unquoted $regexp format-string call. Like Replace, it retains/clamps the old cursor position; relocate it deliberately after length changes.

Input

03_Paper Boats

Script

RegexpReplace "^([0-9]+)_(.*)$" "$2 [$1]"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats [03]

docs.title: JoinUntil
docs.text:
Syntax: JoinUntil "text"

Join the current line through the line containing the next marker, or through input end if absent. If the marker is already in the current remainder, no join is needed. No separator is inserted. Existing spaces at line boundaries determine whether words stay separated.

Input

<title>Paper
 Boats</title>

Script

JoinUntil "</title>"
FindInLine ">"
SayUntil "</title>"

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: JoinLines
docs.text:
Syntax: JoinLines count

Join this line with the next count lines, without adding spaces. -1 or a count beyond the remaining range joins all remaining lines. It does not mean a total of count lines including this one.

Visible spaces: ␠

Input

Paper␠
Boats

Script

JoinLines 1
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper␠Boats

docs.title: KillTag
docs.text:
Syntax: KillTag "tag" ["replacement"]

Remove matching opening/closing/self-closing tags on the current line, ignoring case in tag names. Use * for any tag and an optional replacement instead of removal. This is a text helper, not a complete HTML parser or entity decoder.

Input

<em>Paper</em> Boats

Script

KillTag "em"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: Trim
docs.text:
Syntax: Trim "on"|"off"

Control automatic edge-whitespace trimming for SayRest, SayUntil and SayUntilML. The default is on. Direct Say/SayNChars copies are not implicitly trimmed. The example keeps two spaces on each side.

Visible spaces: ␠

Input

␠␠Paper␠␠

Script

Trim "off"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

␠␠Paper␠␠

docs.title: Unspace
docs.text:
Syntax: Unspace

Remove whitespace at the beginning/end of the current input line and adjust the cursor. Internal whitespace is unchanged. This edits input, unlike changing the Trim read policy.

Visible spaces: ␠

Input

␠␠Paper␠␠

Script

Unspace
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
Syntax: Debug "on"|"off" ["filename"] [megabytes]

Start/stop a command trace. The default name is debug.out and the default cap is 10 MB; a positive whole-number cap changes it. A trace forced by Options keeps its own filename and cannot be switched off by the script.

Debug file: trace.out

Input

Paper Boats

Script

Debug "on" "trace.out"
SayRest
Debug "off"

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: DebugWriteInput
docs.text:
Syntax: DebugWriteInput ["filename"]

Capture the entire current, possibly transformed input. The default name is debug-input.out. In the application, debug filenames are reduced to safe plain names under the sources/debug folder.

Debug file: snapshot.txt

Input

Paper_Boats

Script

Replace "_" " "
DebugWriteInput "snapshot.txt"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: json
docs.text:
Syntax: json "on"|"off" ["current"]

Enable JSON mode from the original downloaded text. Add "current" to parse transformed input instead; "off" leaves JSON mode. JSON selection writes a value to text input so a later Say command can emit it. Turning JSON mode off leaves that current text in place.

Input

prefix:{"title":"Paper Boats"}

Script

Replace "prefix:" ""
json "on" "current"
json_select "title"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats

docs.title: json_foreach
docs.text:
Syntax: json_foreach "array"

Enter each array item in its original order. The input initially contains the array size; select the item/field before reading it. An empty/missing array skips the body. Close with json_foreach_end.

Input

{"tracks":["Paper Boats","Lanterns"]}

Script

json "on"
json_foreach "tracks"
json_select ""
SayRest
Say "|"
json_foreach_end

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats|Lanterns|

docs.title: json_foreach_reverse
docs.text:
Syntax: json_foreach_reverse "array"

Iterate the same array in reverse order. The loop counter still starts at 1 for the first emitted item; it is not the original array index.

Input

{"tracks":["Paper Boats","Lanterns"]}

Script

json "on"
json_foreach_reverse "tracks"
json_select ""
SayRest
Say "|"
json_foreach_end

Output buffer: unnamed

Lanterns|Paper Boats|

docs.title: json_foreach_counter
docs.text:
Syntax: json_foreach_counter [digits]

Put the current one-based loop counter on text input, with optional leading-zero width. It emits nothing until a Say command reads it. Calling it outside an active array loop is an error.

Input

{"tracks":["Paper Boats","Lanterns"]}

Script

json "on"
json_foreach "tracks"
json_foreach_counter 2
SayRest
Say "|"
json_foreach_end

Output buffer: unnamed

01|02|

docs.title: json_foreach_end
docs.text:
Syntax: json_foreach_end

Close the last JSON array loop, advance to its next item or leave it. Object selections made inside the iteration are unwound before the next item. Nested JSON loops must close in order.

Input

{"tracks":["Paper","Boats"]}

Script

json "on"
json_foreach "tracks"
json_select ""
SayRest
json_foreach_end

Output buffer: unnamed

PaperBoats

docs.title: json_select_object
docs.text:
Syntax: json_select_object "key"

Enter an object context. When an object is found, its key becomes text input; otherwise input is empty. Leave that selected context with json_unselect_object before reading the parent again.

Input

{"release":{"title":"Harbour Lights"}}

Script

json "on"
json_select_object "release"
json_select "title"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Harbour Lights

docs.title: json_unselect_object
docs.text:
Syntax: json_unselect_object

Return to the preceding JSON context. This does not replace current text input by itself: select another value after returning. It cannot pop an active loop item as though it were a selected object.

Input

{"title":"root","release":{"title":"inner"}}

Script

json "on"
json_select_object "release"
json_select "title"
SayRest
Say "/"
json_unselect_object
json_select "title"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

inner/root

docs.title: json_select
docs.text:
Syntax: json_select "key"

Select a value into text input. Strings lose JSON quotes; numbers/booleans become text; null/missing values become empty. An empty key selects the current value. Dotted paths are supported after checking for a literal key of that name.

Input

{"artist":{"name":"Juniper Vale"}}

Script

json "on"
json_select "artist.name"
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Juniper Vale

docs.title: json_select_array
docs.text:
Syntax: json_select_array "array" index ["separator"]

Select a one-based array element, or -1 for all elements joined by the supplied separator. An out-of-range index becomes empty. Without a separator, all-element mode concatenates the values. This one-based index differs from a numeric component in a dotted JSON path.

Input

{"tracks":["Paper Boats","Lanterns"]}

Script

json "on"
json_select_array "tracks" -1 " / "
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Paper Boats / Lanterns

docs.title: json_select_many
docs.text:
Syntax: json_select_many "array" "field" ["separator"] ["last separator"] [maximum] [include-empty]

Extract one field from many array objects. The default separator is comma-space; a last separator can join the final pair differently. A positive maximum truncates selected values after empty filtering. Set the final flag to 1 to keep empty/missing field values as empty slots.

Input

{"artists":[{"name":"Juniper Vale"},{"name":"Mira Solberg"},{"name":"Kofi"}]}

Script

json "on"
json_select_many "artists" "name" ", " " & " 2
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

Juniper Vale & Mira Solberg

docs.title: json_select_many_count
docs.text:
Syntax: json_select_many_count "array" ["field"] [include-empty]

Count array items, optionally requiring a named field. With a field, empty values are excluded unless the last flag is 1; missing keys remain excluded even with that flag. The count is put on input, not directly in output.

Input

{"artists":[{"name":"Juniper"},{"name":""},{},{"name":"Mira"}]}

Script

json "on"
json_select_many_count "artists" "name" 1
SayRest

Output buffer: unnamed

3

docs.title: Troubleshoot and bound the work
docs.text:
Start with the saved input and one field. Verify a Find/Goto step, inspect its cursor, then add one Say operation. Add a loop only after one iteration works. Missing markers, an unexpected JSON shape, a changed URL or a login/error page need different corrections; moving the cursor farther is not a general fix.

An unknown command, wrong argument count or unbalanced block fails compilation with a source line. Runtime failures can name the command/input position. DebugWriteInput captures transformed input; a forced Options trace also retains the downloaded input. File names are sanitized and kept under sources/debug. Check those files before changing an extraction pattern blindly.

The checked engine stops after 2,000,000 command steps and checks appended output against a 16 MB cumulative byte budget. Debug traces have a default 10 MB cap. These guardrails do not certify that a source handles every response size, provider rule or future page layout. Keep requests and scripts small while developing, preserve a working copy and inspect the final review/import outcome.

docs.title: Web sources (.src)
docs.text:
A web source describes how to search a site/API and turn its response into proposed tags. It is a text-based parser, not a browser that runs a website's JavaScript. Prefer a documented JSON/XML API or stable server-rendered text when one is available.

A search usually has two stages: parse a result list, then parse the selected release. A direct source can skip the result-list stage and look up one release identifier. Both routes lead to review: a fetched album is not automatically the right edition or track mapping for your selected files.

docs.title: Install the complete source
docs.text:
1. Obtain the source's .src file and any companion .inc and .settings files. Keep them together and inspect what they are intended to query.
  2. Choose Tag Sources → Install tag sources… on a desktop with folder access. Select all required files, not just the .src.
  3. Read the installation result. A copied file can still have a missing include, invalid schema or unsupported syntax.
  4. Open Tag Sources and choose the installed entry.

The supported installer accepts individual local .src, .inc and .settings files up to 4 MB each. It copies them by filename into the sources folder; an existing file with that name can be replaced. Back up a customized source before installing another version with the same filenames.

Tag Sources → Open sources folder opens data/sources inside OpenTag's configuration folder. File → Open configuration folder is another way to find it. Files can be copied there manually; returning focus to OpenTag refreshes the source list. Keep includes and schemas in that same folder. An include is a plain filename, not an arbitrary path outside the source folder.

Save new source files as UTF-8. Unicode BOMs are recognized; otherwise valid UTF-8 is used, with Windows-1252 as the legacy fallback. If characters are wrong, inspect the actual saved bytes and response encoding before changing field text to compensate.

docs.title: Organize menu entries
docs.text:
The filename determines the menu path. For example, Practice#&Harbour.src makes a Practice → Harbour… entry, with H as an access key. # separates submenu levels; & marks a mnemonic character. The source's [Name] supplies descriptive source information, not a different filesystem location.

A schema named Practice#Settings.settings can create a separate Practice → Settings… item. Source entries and settings entries are separated in the menu. Source-list problems are reported there too; inspect the problem text when an expected entry is absent.

docs.title: Search, review and apply
docs.text:
Save pending tag edits and select one album's practice files. Open the source, inspect its search fields and run the search. Their labels, initial values and URL construction come from [SearchBy] and the source headers.

For a result list, verify the visible release details and choose the intended row. A thumbnail can help identify an edition, but it is not a match guarantee. A preview address can open more release information. A direct source instead uses the entered identifier to reach the album page.

At review, check proposed fields, enabled states, artwork and the mapping between local files and source tracks. A parser's track order is not a promise that automatic matching or ordering suggestions preserved the intended local order. Match by known titles/positions when needed. Apply only the fields and artwork you intend to change, then read the reported result and file errors.

The source parser does not interpret arbitrary tag fields in its command arguments as selected-file data. Its named outputs and special contexts have separate rules; see the script reference. The writing lesson builds a small source from local JSON so the parsing steps can be understood before adapting a live site.

docs.title: Configure a source
docs.text:
Open its settings menu item when it supplies a .settings schema. String fields can be free text or choices, number fields hold numbers, and booleans use checkboxes. Headings and separators organize the dialog without holding values. Save stores the chosen settings; Cancel leaves them alone.

Schemas provide defaults. Saved values override those defaults when their value types match. Newly added settings can therefore use a default without requiring an old settings file to be edited manually. A source's root schema key identifies its section in the shared data/sources/settings.json file; settings with a different root key remain separate.

IfVar, IfNotVar and SayVar read the configured values. These are not the same as output buffers or editable audio tags. A source can use a setting to include an optional COMMENT or choose a response language, but only if its script actually implements that choice.

docs.title: Debug the downloaded text
docs.text:
Options → Tag Sources can enable web-source debug output. It retains the downloaded input and a parser trace under the sources folder's debug subfolder. A script can also request Debug or DebugWriteInput; the reference explains filenames, caps and the difference between original and transformed input.

Read a failure in this order:

  1. Check the source file and parser section named in the error.
  2. Check the line/command and the input near its cursor.
  3. Verify that the downloaded text actually contains the expected data.
  4. Simplify to one field, then add navigation and loops one step at a time.

If the site returns a sign-in page, rate-limit response or JavaScript shell, changing FindLine offsets will not create the missing album data. Check the provider's API/authentication requirements. A web source does not inherit an unrelated browser's login session merely because the site works there.

docs.title: Compatibility and limits
docs.text:
A third-party source can rely on headers, parser details or remote behavior that differs in OpenTag. Minimum-version declarations written for another application do not certify OpenTag compatibility. Check the actual command reference and test a small copied selection.

Keep unsupported headers and matching assumptions visible while adapting a source. In particular, do not infer ordering guarantees or duration-matching accuracy from successful parser output alone. Those belong to release conversion and review/matching as well. The examples in this guide establish specified pure parser results, not every provider or native-platform workflow.

Only web addresses accepted by the source workflow can be fetched. A release address must come from the current search/lookup, so if it becomes stale, search again rather than trying to reuse an old internal result. Offline fixtures and a successful HTTP response are different from a verified live provider import.

docs.title: Further resources
docs.text: The official Mp3tag Community has Web Sources Scripts for contributed sources and Web Sources Discussion for authoring questions. Treat examples there as source material to inspect, adapt and test against OpenTag's current commands and request behavior; community publication does not establish unchanged compatibility here.

docs.title: Write a web source from local JSON
docs.text:
Build a source that reads an album and two track titles from JSON you control. This lesson takes about 25 minutes. It keeps network data predictable while you learn source headers, JSON selection, output buffers and settings.

  • OpenTag desktop app with source installation/folder access available.
  • Two copied practice audio files selected in this order: Paper Boats, then Lanterns on the Water; save pending edits first.
  • Python available to serve a separate practice-data folder on localhost.
  • A plain-text editor that can save UTF-8 without changing file extensions.

The local server serves only the practice folder and binds to 127.0.0.1. It is part of this exercise, not an instruction to run the source against a personal music directory. The parser examples are also checked directly by tests without launching OpenTag or making network requests.

docs.title: 1. Create one predictable response
docs.text:
Make a practice folder with a release subfolder. Save the following as release/harbour.json:

{
  "album": "Harbour Lights",
  "artist": "Juniper Vale",
  "year": 2024,
  "tracks": [
    {"title": "Paper Boats"},
    {"title": "Lanterns on the Water"}
  ]
}

In a terminal, serve that practice folder. Replace its path below. On Windows PowerShell:

python -m http.server 8766 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory 'C:\PracticeCatalogue'

On macOS/Linux:

python3 -m http.server 8766 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$HOME/PracticeCatalogue"

Open http://127.0.0.1:8766/release/harbour.json in a browser. It must show the JSON above. Keep the terminal open; the server runs until stopped with Ctrl+C. If the address fails, resolve the path/port problem before involving OpenTag.

docs.title: 2. Write the source description
docs.text:
Save this UTF-8 text as Practice#&Harbour.src, keeping its .src extension:

[Name]=Practice catalogue
[AlbumUrl]=http://127.0.0.1:8766/release/%s.json
[SearchBy]=Release ID||harbour||%s
[Encoding]=url-utf-8
[Settings]=Practice#Settings.settings

[ParserScriptAlbum]=...
json "on"
OutputTo "ALBUM"
json_select "album"
SayRest
OutputTo "ARTIST"
json_select "artist"
SayRest
IfVar "includeYear" "true"
OutputTo "YEAR"
json_select "year"
SayRest
Endif
json_foreach "tracks"
OutputTo "TITLE"
json_select "title"
SayRest
Say "|"
OutputTo "TRACK"
json_foreach_counter
SayRest
Say "|"
json_foreach_end

There is no index URL/script, so this is a direct lookup. The Release ID field starts as the literal harbour. Its value replaces %s in [AlbumUrl]. That %s belongs to URL construction; %artist% in a normal format string has a different job.

[ParserScriptAlbum]=... begins a multiline command section. json "on" parses the response. json_select puts a selected value on the parser's text input, and SayRest appends that text to the current output buffer. OutputTo "ALBUM" chooses that buffer; it does not write an audio tag yet.

The array loop changes the JSON context to each track. TITLE and TRACK collect per-track values, each followed by |. The final pipe matters: it marks a track-valued output rather than a single album-wide value. The counter command puts its number on the input; SayRest is still needed to copy it to output.

docs.title: 3. Give the optional year a setting
docs.text:
Save this JSON as Practice#Settings.settings:

{
  "key": "practiceCatalogue",
  "title": "Practice catalogue settings",
  "settings": [
    {
      "type": "bool",
      "key": "includeYear",
      "title": "Import the release year",
      "description": "Include YEAR from the local response.",
      "default": false
    }
  ]
}

The root key identifies this source's saved settings. includeYear names one setting. The schema stores a boolean; the parser receives it as true or false text. IfVar compares that configured value and either fills YEAR or skips that branch. The script does not depend on a field named includeYear in the selected audio files.

docs.title: 4. Install and inspect the lookup
docs.text:
Choose Tag Sources → Install tag sources… and install both files. Open Tag Sources → Practice → Settings…, leave the checkbox off and choose Save. Then choose Tag Sources → Practice → Harbour….

Confirm Release ID is harbour, then run the lookup. It uses the local response directly. In the parser, the expected buffers are:

  • ALBUM: Harbour Lights
  • ARTIST: Juniper Vale
  • TITLE: Paper Boats|Lanterns on the Water|
  • TRACK: 1|2|

YEAR is absent with the default setting. At review, check that the two local files map to the matching source titles in the order intended. Select only the proposed fields you want to apply. Do not rely on automatic duration or ordering suggestions for this exercise; its response deliberately contains no duration data.

After applying, inspect the tags and the result/errors. Successful parsing and successful writing are separate checks. Keep the original audio untouched elsewhere so a practice result can be compared safely.

docs.title: 5. Change one thing and observe the difference
docs.text:
Open Practice → Settings…, enable Import the release year, save and repeat the lookup. The YEAR output should now be 2024. The title/track buffers remain the same. This change demonstrates a setting-controlled branch without changing the response or the selected files.

To inspect the loop progressively, temporarily give the response's tracks array one item, then restore the second item. Confirm that TITLE/TRACK gain one aligned entry each. If an error names a command line, use its input/cursor context rather than guessing at a different JSON field.

docs.title: Go further: a search list
docs.text:
A search-and-select source adds [IndexUrl], [IndexFormat] and [ParserScriptIndex]. The index script emits one line per result, with pipe separators matching IndexFormat. %_url% identifies the album address; %_coverurl% can provide a thumbnail and %_preview% a preview address. The selected album then passes through the same album-parser stage.

Build the index separately from a known response before combining both stages. For a runnable extension to this local exercise, save search.json at the root of the practice folder:

{
  "releases": [
    {"path": "/release/harbour.json", "album": "Harbour Lights", "year": 2024}
  ]
}

Remove the old AlbumUrl and SearchBy header lines from the working source, keep its album parser/settings, then append this block:

[AlbumUrl]=http://127.0.0.1:8766
[IndexUrl]=http://127.0.0.1:8766/search.json?q=%s
[IndexFormat]=%_url%|%Album%|%Year%
[SearchBy]=Album||Harbour Lights||%s

[ParserScriptIndex]=...
OutputTo ""
json "on"
json_foreach "releases"
json_select "path"
SayRest
Say "|"
json_select "album"
SayRest
Say "|"
json_select "year"
SayRest
SayNewline
json_foreach_end

Index row: /release/harbour.json|Harbour Lights|2024

The row ends with CRLF from SayNewline. AlbumUrl plus the relative path points to the same local album response used earlier. The search URL accepts the encoded query; this small static fixture returns the same search.json for any query. It demonstrates request/parsing structure rather than a real search algorithm.

Reinstall the changed source and repeat the exercise. There is now a result-list stage with Album and Year columns. Choose Harbour Lights to reach the existing album parser. A year displayed in a search column is not itself an instruction to import YEAR: the album parser's includeYear setting still controls that output.

The reference explains the headers, commands, URL encoding and contexts used by both stages.

docs.title: What you learned
docs.text:
• Headers describe the source; parser commands process its downloaded text.
  • JSON selection changes text input without immediately importing a tag.
  • Output buffers distinguish album values from pipe-delimited track values.
  • Settings are separate typed configuration, read by explicit commands.
  • Review, track matching and writing require checks after the parser succeeds.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Install sources, settings and debug output
  • Header and parser-command reference
  • Format-string quoting and functions

Stop the practice HTTP server with Ctrl+C when finished. Keep a working copy of the source before adapting its URL or parser for another response.
